rules.quote: This chapter does not apply to a work or operation on one undertaking or project by one or more contracts if the aggregate contract price for labor, materials, and all other items is less than one thousand dollars ($1,000), that work or operation being considered of casual, minor, or inconsequential nature, and the work or operation does not require a building permit.
rules.notes: Only the section title appears in this chunk (Sections Affected table); the dollar threshold and conditions are NOT stated here. Do not hard-code a number from this source.
rules.correction: threshold_usd was null. B&P 7048 sets the minor-work exemption at an aggregate contract price below $1,000 (labor, materials and all other items, one project by one or more contracts), and only if the work needs no building permit. The exemption is lost if the work is part of a larger operation or split to evade, or if the person advertises as a contractor or employs anyone. Parameters and quote filled from the statute.

rules.title: Holder of inactive license may not contract (B&P 7076.5 amended)
rules.plain_english: A contractor holding an inactive license certificate is not entitled to practice contracting until reinstated; this section was amended in 2025.
rules.applies_to: Contractors with inactive licenses; owners verifying license status
rules.quote: Inactive license certificate; 7076.5 Reinstatement; Holder not entitled Amended 592 297 to practice
rules.notes: Derived from section title in the Sections Affected table; substantive changes not described in this chunk.

rules.title: CSLB fee schedule (B&P 7137) amended in 2025
rules.plain_english: CSLB's fee schedule was amended by 2025 legislation; license, renewal and registration fees should be checked against the current schedule.

parameters.delinquency_fee: 50% of the renewal fee if renewed after expiration (7137(a)(5))
parameters.veteran_reduction: 50% of initial license and registration fees (7137(a)(3)(D))

rules.applies_to: Contractors paying CSLB fees
rules.citation: B&P 7137 (amended Stats 2025 ch 592, SB 861); 16 CCR 811 (current fee amounts)
rules.source: 2026 CSLB Law Book, PDF page 16 (table); PDF pages 374-377 (B&P 7137); PDF pages 451-452 (16 CCR 811)
rules.quote: 7137 Fee schedule Amended 592 351

rules.title: Definition of incidental and supplemental work (16 CCR 831) amended
rules.plain_english: The regulation defining 'incidental and supplemental' work (work outside your classification that you may still perform) was amended in 2025.
rules.applies_to: Specialty contractors performing work outside their classification
rules.quote: 831 Incidental and Supplemental Defined Amended 2025-26 436
rules.notes: Definition text not in this chunk (Chapter 9). Effective date of the regulatory amendment not stated.

rules.title: Extension of time to correct under an order of correction (16 CCR 883) amended
rules.plain_english: The regulation on getting more time to comply with a CSLB order of correction was amended in 2025.

parameters.request_deadline: before expiration of the time allowed in the order of correction
parameters.grounds: unable to complete despite substantial efforts and reasonable diligence because of conditions beyond the cited person's control
parameters.consequence_if_late: failure to correct within the time allowed is a violation of the order whether or not good cause existed
parameters.amendment_2025: change without regulatory effect filed 6-26-2025 (1 CCR 100)

rules.source: 2026 CSLB Law Book, PDF page 17 (table); PDF page 539 (16 CCR 883 text); PDF page 558 (history)
rules.quote: Such request must be made in writing, and must be made prior to the expiration of the time allowed in the order of correction. An extension may be granted upon showing of good cause which determination is within the discretion of the Registrar. If a request for extension of time is not made prior to the expiration of time allowed in the order of correction, failure to correct within the time allowed shall constitute a violation of the order of correction whether or not good cause for an extension of time existed.

Grounds: inability to finish despite substantial efforts because of conditions beyond the person's control, granted for good cause at the registrar's discretion. A late request makes failure to correct a violation even if good cause existed. No fixed extension length (extension_days stays null). The 2025 amendment was a change without regulatory effect. Parameters and quote filled.

rules.title: Partnership license canceled when a general partner leaves or is added
rules.plain_english: If your license is issued to a general partnership, the license is canceled when any general partner leaves or a new general partner is added.

cancel_triggers: general partner leaves for any reason

rules.applies_to: Contractors licensed as general partnerships
rules.citation: B&P (partnership license cancellation; section not cited on this page)
rules.quote: when a contractor’s license is issued to a general partnership and a ... general partner leaves for any reason or the partnership wants to add another general partner, the license is canceled.
rules.notes: Partners may be personally liable for partnership debts and other partners' negligence. Also: a general partnership requires registration of the business name (PDF pages 39-40).

rules.title: LLC: file Articles of Organization (LLC-1); keep operating agreement on site
rules.plain_english: To form an LLC, file Articles of Organization (Form LLC-1) with the Secretary of State; the LLC must also have a members' operating agreement kept at its records office (not filed with the state).

parameters.operating_agreement_kept_at: office where LLC records are kept

rules.applies_to: Contractors organized as California LLCs
rules.citation: California LLC law (section not cited on this page)
rules.quote: In addition to filing the applicable documents with the Secretary of State, an operating agreement among the members as to the affairs of the LLC and the conduct of its business is required. The LLC does not file the operating agreement with the Secretary of State but maintains it at the office where the LLC’s records are kept.
rules.notes: Form text: 'To form an LLC in California, Articles of Organization (Form LLC-1) must be filed with the California Secretary of State’s office.' LLC licensees also need the $100,000 wage bond and liability insurance (see related rules).

rules.title: Corporations begin by filing articles of incorporation
rules.plain_english: To incorporate, file articles of incorporation with the California Secretary of State.
rules.applies_to: Contractors forming corporations
rules.citation: California Corporations Code (not cited on this page)
rules.quote: You can begin the process of incorporation by filing articles of incorporation with the Secretary of State.
rules.notes: Corporate officers may be personally liable even though stockholders usually are not.

rules.title: Sole owners and partnerships pay estimated taxes quarterly
rules.plain_english: If the business is a sole proprietorship or partnership, estimated federal and state income taxes must be prepaid or paid quarterly.
rules.applies_to: Sole proprietor and partnership contractors
rules.citation: Federal/state tax law (not cited on this page)
rules.quote: If the business is a sole ownership or partnership, estimated federal and state income taxes must be prepaid or paid quarterly.
rules.notes: Specific quarterly due dates are not stated in this source.
rules.correction: Quote matches PDF p.41, but federal and California income tax law is not reproduced in the law book. The "quarterly" schedule cannot be checked against primary text.

rules.title: Get a federal EIN; deposit withheld payroll taxes on schedule
rules.plain_english: Employers must get a federal Employer Identification Number from the IRS and pay withheld federal income and Social Security taxes quarterly, monthly or semimonthly as required.
rules.applies_to: Contractors with employees
rules.citation: Federal tax law (not cited on this page)
rules.quote: A federal Employer Identification Number (EIN) must be requested from the Internal Revenue Service, and the federal income and Social Security taxes withheld from employee wages must be paid quarterly, monthly, or semimonthly, as required.
rules.notes: Which deposit frequency applies is set by IRS rules, not stated here.

rules.title: Register with EDD; pay state payroll taxes for employees earning over $100/quarter
rules.plain_english: Register with California's EDD, get a state employer number, and pay state payroll and unemployment insurance taxes for any employee who earns more than $100 in a calendar quarter.
rules.applies_to: Contractors with employees in California
rules.citation: California Unemployment Insurance Code (not cited on this page)
rules.quote: The contractor must register with the Employment Development Department, obtain a state EIN, and pay state payroll and unemployment insurance taxes for employees who earn over $100 in a calendar quarter.
rules.correction: Quote matches PDF p.41, but the Unemployment Insurance Code is not reproduced in the law book, so the $100-per-quarter trigger cannot be checked against primary text.

rules.title: Seller's permit, possible 6-month sales tax deposit, collect sales tax
rules.plain_english: Businesses selling tangible personal property need a California Seller's Permit, may be required to deposit six months of estimated sales tax, and must collect sales tax from customers unless tax on materials was paid at purchase.

parameters.trigger: selling tangible personal property
parameters.possible_security_deposit: estimated sales tax for first 6 months
parameters.collect_sales_tax_unless: tax on materials already paid at purchase

rules.applies_to: Contractors that sell tangible personal property (e.g., fixtures/materials sold to customers)
rules.citation: California sales and use tax law (not cited on this page)
rules.quote: California requires a Seller’s Permit for businesses that sell tangible personal property. The State Board of Equalization can require a deposit of the estimated sales tax for the first six months. The contractor must collect the required sales tax from the customer unless the tax on materials is already paid at the time of purchase.
rules.notes: Book names the State Board of Equalization; seller's permit administration has since moved to the California Department of Tax and Fee Administration (CDTFA) - verify current agency.

rules.title: Determine city/county permits before starting a job
rules.plain_english: Before starting any job, find out whether city or county permits are required, and know the applicable zoning laws and building codes.

parameters.timing: before starting a job

rules.applies_to: All contractors
rules.citation: Local ordinances / building codes (not cited on this page)
rules.quote: Before starting a job, determine if city or county permits are required. In addition, the contractor must be familiar with zoning laws and building codes.
rules.notes: Ties to the HIC requirement to describe permits and state who pays for them.

rules.title: Project bond cost typically 1-2% of contract price
rules.plain_english: Performance/payment bonds usually cost about 1 to 2 percent of the contract price; include that cost in your bid.
rules.applies_to: Contractors bidding bonded projects (often lender-financed or commercial)
rules.quote: Bonds can be obtained from bonding companies for a percentage of the contract price, usually in the one to two percent range. This requirement is the cost of doing business that should be recognized when the bid is submitted.
rules.notes: Industry guidance, not a legal requirement. Bonding is 'generally mandatory for large jobs financed by institutional lenders'. Verified: quote matches PDF p.42. This is CSLB business guidance, not a statutory requirement; the book itself is the source.

rules.title: Performance, payment and contract bonds; surety liability capped at face amount
rules.plain_english: Performance bonds guarantee completion, payment bonds protect against labor/material liens, contract bonds do both; the surety generally pays no more than the bond's face amount unless it took over completion.

bond_types.performance_bond: guarantees completion per plans and specs
bond_types.payment_bond: assures owner no liens for labor and materials

parameters.surety_max_liability: face amount of bond (unless surety assumed completion)

rules.applies_to: Contractors and owners on bonded projects
rules.quote: In general, unless the bonding company has taken responsibility for completing the project, the bonding company will not have to pay more than the face amount of the bond.
rules.notes: Project bonds are distinct from the contractor license bond.

rules.title: Contractor license bond $25,000; qualifying individual bond $25,000
rules.plain_english: Every licensed contractor must carry a $25,000 contractor license bond; a qualifying individual's bond is also $25,000.

parameters.scope: any project the contractor agrees to perform

rules.applies_to: All licensed contractors; qualifying individuals where required
rules.citation: B&P contractor bond provisions (section not cited on this page; commonly B&P 7071.6 and 7071.9)
rules.quote: Each licensed contractor is required to carry a contractor bond. ... The contractor license bond amount is $25,000. The bond for qualifying individuals is $25,000.
rules.notes: Cash deposit may be filed in lieu of bond (AB 521, PDF page 12). When a qualifying-individual bond is required is not specified in this chunk. Verified: 7071.6(a) $25,000 contractor bond as condition of issuance/reinstatement/reactivation/renewal/continued maintenance; not required while license inactive (7071.6(c)); board may require double ($50,000) for applicants with unlicensed-contracting conviction/final citation causing substantial injury (7071.6(d)); surety aggregate liability for non-wage claimants capped at $7,500 (7071.6(b)). Qualifying individual bond $25,000 is required only when the qualifier is neither the proprietor, a general partner, nor a joint licensee (7071.9(a)(1)).

rules.title: LLC licensees need an additional $100,000 employee/worker bond
rules.plain_english: An LLC contractor must carry a $100,000 surety bond for workers, on top of the $25,000 license bond, to issue, reissue, reinstate, reactivate or renew the license.

parameters.beneficiaries: employees/workers damaged by failure to pay wages, interest on wages, fringe benefits, other contributions

rules.applies_to: Contractors licensed as limited liability companies
rules.quote: A $100,000 surety bond (in addition to the $25,000 contractor bond) is required for the issuance, reissuance, reinstatement, reactivation, and renewal of an LLC license for the benefit of any employee or worker damaged by the LLC’s failure to pay wages, interest on wages, or fringe benefits, as well as other contributions.
rules.notes: Total bonding for an LLC licensee: $125,000 (25,000 + 100,000). Verified: 7071.6.5(a) $100,000 surety bond for issuance, reissuance, reinstatement, reactivation, renewal or continued valid use of an LLC license; for employees damaged by failure to pay wages, interest on wages or fringe benefits; also covers welfare, pension and apprentice contributions if party to a collective bargaining agreement (7071.6.5(d)); not applicable while inactive (7071.6.5(e)).

rules.title: CGL insurance not required by license law except for LLCs
rules.plain_english: California license law doesn't require general liability insurance unless your business is an LLC, though commercial owners commonly require it by contract.
rules.applies_to: All contractors
rules.quote: Contractors State License Law does not require contractors to carry CGL insurance unless their business entity is a limited liability company (see below).
rules.notes: Home improvement contractors must still disclose CGL status in writing (16 CCR 872(a)). Verified: 7071.19(a) requires LLC licensees to maintain liability insurance "in addition to any bond"; no comparable license-law requirement for other entity types appears in the book. HIC contracts must still state CGL status (B&P 7159(e)(1); 16 CCR 872).

rules.title: Home improvement contractors must disclose CGL insurance status in writing
rules.plain_english: Home improvement contractors must tell the homeowner in writing whether they carry general liability insurance, and if so, give the insurer's name and phone number in writing.

parameters.format: 16 CCR 872(a) prescribed form with contractor-name checkboxes (does not carry / carries CGL), insurer name and phone
must_accompany: every estimate (bid) intended to result in a home improvement contract
contract_notice_7159e1_options: (Name) does not carry commercial general liability insurance.
(Name) carries commercial general liability insurance written by (insurer). You may call (insurer) at ___ to check the contractor’s insurance coverage.

(Name) is a limited liability company that carries liability insurance or maintains other security as required by law. You may call (insurer/trust company/bank) at ___ to check on the contractor’s insurance coverage or security.

rules.applies_to: Home improvement contractors
rules.source: 2026 CSLB Law Book, PDF page 43 (summary); PDF pages 401, 535-536 (statutory/regulatory text)
rules.quote: The following statement, must accompany every estimate (bid) intended to result in a home improvement contract and every home improvement contract. The heading shall be printed in at least 14-point type, the questions in at least 12-point type, and the comments in italics of at least 11-point type.
rules.notes: Corresponds to the 'Commercial General Liability Insurance' notice in the HIC required-notices list.
rules.correction: Rule said only "disclose in writing". 16 CCR 872(a) requires a prescribed form ("Information About Commercial General Liability Insurance") with every estimate or bid intended to lead to an HIC and with every HIC. Type sizes: heading at least 14-pt, questions 12-pt, comments 11-pt italics. Separately, the contract needs the 7159(e)(1) CGL notice with one of four statutory statements. Citation, quote and parameters updated.

rules.title: LLC liability insurance: $1M aggregate + $100K per personnel over 5, max $5M
rules.plain_english: An LLC contractor must carry liability insurance with at least a $1 million aggregate limit if it has five or fewer personnel of record, plus $100,000 for each additional person, up to $5 million.
rules.applies_to: Contractors licensed as LLCs
rules.quote: Liability insurance with the aggregate limit of $1 million for licensees with five or fewer people listed as members of the personnel of record is required for a limited liability company; plus, an additional $100,000 in insurance is required for each additional member of the personnel of record, not to exceed $5 million total.
rules.notes: Cap reached at 45 personnel of record (1,000,000 + 40 * 100,000 = 5,000,000). Verified with a caveat: statute 7071.19(b)(2) literally says "an additional one hundred thousand dollars ($100,000) of insurance shall be obtained for each person listed on the personnel of record" for LLCs with more than five persons; CSLB (book p.43) reads it as each ADDITIONAL person beyond five, which the formula follows. A more conservative literal reading would be 1,000,000 + 100,000 * personnel_of_record (still capped at 5,000,000). Cap is per designated period (policy year, max 12 months), less amounts paid on claims; limit must be reinstated by the next designated period or the license is suspended by operation of law (7071.19(d)).

rules.title: Workers' comp required with one or more employees (even part-time)
rules.plain_english: If you have even one employee, including part-time and employed relatives, you must carry workers' compensation coverage.
rules.applies_to: All employer-contractors
rules.citation: Labor Code 3700; see Labor Code 2750.5 (owner-operators/independent contractors)
rules.quote: If the employer has one or more employees, even part-time, they are required to insure for workers’ compensation claims.

rules.title: Three ways to secure workers' comp coverage

self-insurer permit from Director of Department of Industrial Relations (Labor Code 3700)
collectively bargained ADR program recognized by Division of Workers’ Compensation (Labor Code 3201.5)

rules.notes: Third method (Labor Code 3201.5 collectively bargained ADR program) follows on the same page.

rules.title: Workers' comp penalties the insurer does not absorb
rules.plain_english: Your WC insurer takes on your WC obligations, except penalties for your serious and willful misconduct, injury to an illegally employed worker under 16, or discriminating against an employee for filing a claim.

discrimination against employee for filing industrial injury claim

rules.title: Authorize medical treatment within 1 working day of claim form; $10,000 cap until decision
rules.plain_english: Within one working day after receiving an employee's workers' comp claim form, the employer must authorize medical treatment and keep providing it until the claim is accepted or rejected. rules.title: Serious and willful employer misconduct: compensation increased by one-half; not insurable
rules.plain_english: If an employee is hurt because of the serious or willful misconduct of the employer or its managers, the compensation is increased by one-half plus up to $250 in costs. The insurer is not liable for this increase and cannot cover it, so the contractor pays it directly.
rules.applies_to: Employer-contractors

The insurance company is not liable for the increase
rules.notes: Insurance Code 11661 bars the policy from covering this increase.

rules.title: Failing to secure workers' comp is a misdemeanor
rules.plain_english: Not carrying workers' compensation coverage (or approved self-insurance) when required is a crime (misdemeanor).

rules.title: No workers' comp: automatic license suspension (B&P 7125.2); discipline for willful violation (B&P 7110(c))
rules.plain_english: If you are required to carry workers' comp and you don't, or you let it lapse, your license is automatically suspended by law. The suspension starts on the lapse date, or on the date coverage was first required, and lasts until you prove coverage (B&P 7125.2). A willful or deliberate violation of the compensation insurance laws is also grounds for CSLB discipline, including revocation (B&P 7110(c)). Employing workers without coverage carries minimum civil penalties of $10,000 (sole owner) or $20,000 (partnership, corporation, LLC or tribal business) per violation (B&P 7125.4).

parameters.violation: failure to obtain or maintain workers' compensation coverage when required

automatic_suspension.effective_on: earlier of (1) date the WC coverage lapses or (2) date WC coverage was required to be obtained
automatic_suspension.reinstatement: any time, on proof of compliance per B&P 7125 and 7125.1

discretionary_discipline.mental_state: willful or deliberate disregard and violation of the compensation insurance laws

parameters.renewal_or_reinstatement_blocked_until: current and valid Certificate of WC Insurance or Certification of Self-Insurance in the licensee's business name (B&P 7125.4(c))

rules.applies_to: Licensed contractors with employees
rules.citation: B&P 7125.2 (automatic suspension); B&P 7110(c) (discipline for willful/deliberate violation); B&P 7125.4 (civil penalties)
rules.source: 2026 CSLB Law Book, PDF page 48 (summary); PDF page 351 (B&P 7110); PDF pages 369-370 (B&P 7125.2, 7125.4)
rules.quote: B&P 7125.2: "The failure of a licensee to obtain or maintain workers’ compensation insurance coverage, if required under this chapter, shall result in the automatic suspension of the license by operation of law ... (a) The license suspension imposed by this section is effective upon the earlier of either of the following: (1) On the date that the relevant workers’ compensation insurance coverage lapses. (2) On the date that workers’ compensation coverage is required to be obtained." | B&P 7110: "Willful or deliberate disregard and violation of ... (c) The safety laws or labor laws or compensation insurance laws or Unemployment Insurance Code of the state ... constitutes a cause for disciplinary action against a licensee."
rules.notes: Book summary (PDF p.48) reads: "A contractor’s license may be suspended or revoked by the registrar of contractors if the contractor fails to secure the payment of compensation (Business and Professions Code §7110)." Corrected against the statutory text in Ch. 8.
rules.correction: The book summary says the registrar "may" suspend or revoke for failure to secure compensation, and cites 7110. But B&P 7110(c) makes only a "willful or deliberate disregard and violation" of the compensation insurance laws a cause for discipline. The direct license consequence is B&P 7125.2: failing to obtain or maintain required WC coverage causes AUTOMATIC suspension by operation of law. It takes effect on the earlier of the coverage-lapse date or the date coverage was first required, and is lifted only on proof of compliance (7125, 7125.1). Also added the B&P 7125.4(a) civil penalties: at least $10,000 per violation for a sole owner and at least $20,000 for an entity, with subsequent violations up to $30,000 total per occurrence (as amended by SB 291, effective 1/1/2026). Title, plain_english, parameters, citation and quote updated.

rules.title: Willful safety violation causing death or prolonged impairment: fine and/or imprisonment
rules.plain_english: An employer, or a supervisor who directs other employees, who willfully violates a safety or health standard that causes an employee's death or prolonged bodily impairment can be fined and/or imprisoned on conviction.

rules.title: Keep records required by B&P 7111 and for audits/tax
rules.plain_english: Keep the business records that Contractors State License Law requires (B&P 7111) and that government agencies need for audits and tax reporting.
rules.applies_to: All licensed contractors
rules.quote: State and federal agencies frequently specify that certain records must be maintained and made available for government audits and to substantiate tax reporting. For a description of the records specifically required under Contractors State License Law, see Business and Professions Code section 7111.
rules.notes: The record types and retention period in B&P 7111 are not stated on this page; pull them from the Law Sections chunk.

rules.title: Accrual accounting required for federal tax when inventories used; cash basis not recommended
rules.plain_english: If your business uses inventories, federal tax rules require the accrual method. CSLB does not recommend cash-basis accounting for contractors because it does not match job income with job costs.

parameters.accrual_definition: revenue recognized when earned, expenses when incurred

rules.applies_to: Contractor bookkeeping/accounting
rules.citation: None cited (federal income tax rule described in CSLB guidance)
rules.quote: For federal income tax purposes, the accrual method is required when inventories are utilized. ... For these reasons, the cash basis of accounting is not recommended for contractors.
rules.notes: Federal tax rules have small-business exceptions that this book does not mention; check with a CPA.

rules.title: Percentage-of-completion revenue recognition
rules.plain_english: Under the percentage-of-completion method, you recognize revenue and profit in proportion to the work completed. For example, 50% of the work done means 50% of estimated revenue and profit is earned.
rules.applies_to: Contractors with qualifying long-term projects using accrual accounting
rules.quote: The percentage of completion method will report profits and losses regularly based on work accomplished on each job. For example, if the work performed each year is estimated to represent 50 percent of total performance under contract, then 50 percent of the total estimated revenue and profit is considered earned.
rules.notes: Accounting method, not a licensing requirement.

rules.title: Completed-contract revenue recognition
rules.plain_english: Under the completed-contract method, all gross income and related costs of a contract are reported in the year the contract is completed.
rules.applies_to: Contractors with qualifying long-term projects using accrual accounting
rules.quote: The completed contract method allows for the gross income and related costs for each contract to be reported in the year in which such a contract is completed.
rules.notes: Federal tax eligibility limits for this method are not stated here.

rules.title: Retention: usually 10% withheld from progress payments
rules.plain_english: Retention is an amount, usually 10%, held back from each progress payment until the project is satisfactorily completed and accepted. It is earned money, carried as a current asset.

parameters.released_upon: satisfactory completion and final acceptance of the project

rules.applies_to: Contractors and subcontractors receiving progress payments; owners withholding retention
rules.quote: Retention: A specified amount, usually 10 percent, withheld from progress payments to the contractor pending satisfactory completion and final acceptance of the project. You have already earned this amount even though you have not yet been paid.
rules.notes: 'Usually 10 percent' describes common practice, not a legal cap. These pages do not cover California's statutory retention limits and release deadlines (for example the public works retention caps in the Public Contract Code and the private works retention release rules in the Civil Code), so check those separately before setting a default.

rules.title: Current vs. long-term: one-year line
rules.plain_english: On the balance sheet, current assets are cash or items convertible to cash within one year. Current liabilities are debts due within one year. Long-term liabilities are due more than one year after the balance sheet date.
rules.applies_to: Contractor financial statements
rules.quote: These are the assets that are either cash or capable of being converted into cash in the normal course of business, generally within one year from the date of the balance sheet. ... Current Liabilities: This item includes debts of the company that are due within one year of the balance sheet date. ... Long-term liabilities are notes or mortgages due one year beyond the balance sheet date.
rules.notes: Each part of the quote comes from a different page (54, 55 and 56).

rules.title: Fixed assets valued at original cost less accumulated depreciation
rules.plain_english: Equipment, tools and other fixed assets are carried at their original cost minus accumulated depreciation, not at market value.
rules.applies_to: Contractor financial statements
rules.quote: Regardless of their current market value, fixed assets are valued at their original cost less accumulated depreciation.
rules.notes: Leased property is often shown with fixed assets, and lease payments with liabilities.

rules.title: Working capital = current assets - current liabilities
rules.plain_english: Working capital is total current assets minus total current liabilities.
rules.applies_to: Contractor financial analysis
rules.quote: The difference between the total current assets and the total current liabilities is called working capital.
rules.notes: This page gives no statutory minimum. The CSLB working-capital requirement for license applicants, if any, appears elsewhere in the law.

rules.title: Current ratio = current assets / current liabilities
rules.plain_english: The current ratio is total current assets divided by total current liabilities. In the book's example, $250,000 / $180,000 = 1.39.
rules.applies_to: Contractor financial analysis
rules.quote: To calculate the current ratio, divide total current assets by total current liabilities.
rules.notes: No target ratio is mandated.

rules.title: Quick ratio = (current assets - inventories) / current liabilities
rules.plain_english: The quick ratio uses quick assets (current assets minus inventories) divided by current liabilities. In the book's example, $140,000 / $180,000 = 0.78.
rules.applies_to: Contractor financial analysis
rules.quote: One simple method of determining the quick assets is total current assets minus inventories.

rules.title: Debt-to-net-worth and efficiency ratios
rules.plain_english: Lenders look at total liabilities divided by net worth. Efficiency is measured by net sales to net working capital, net sales to total assets, and net income to net worth.
rules.applies_to: Contractor financial analysis
rules.quote: The long-term creditors (banks or insurance companies) would be interested in the ratio of total liabilities to net worth. ... Net sales to net working capital, net sales to total assets, and net income to net worth are all measures of the efficiency of the company’s use of its resources.

rules.title: Typical payment structure: 3+ payments, 90% during construction, 10% retention
rules.plain_english: A typical custom-building or remodeling contract has three or more payments. 90% is paid during construction and the final 10% (retention) after completion and expiration of the lien period.

parameters.final_payment_trigger: completion and expiration of the lien period

rules.applies_to: Custom building and remodeling contracts (typical practice)
rules.quote: The typical contract provides for three or more payments, 90 percent during the construction phase and the final 10 percent upon completion and expiration of the lien period. This final 10 percent is the “retention.”
rules.notes: Describes typical practice, not a statutory schedule. Home improvement contracts carry their own statutory down payment and progress payment limits (B&P 7159), which are not restated here.

rules.title: Cannot collect more than the percentage of work completed
rules.plain_english: A contractor may not bill or collect more than the percentage of the work already completed.
rules.applies_to: Contractors receiving progress payments
rules.citation: None cited on this page (CSLB business guidance); related home improvement progress-payment rule in B&P 7159 (not cited here)
rules.quote: The contractor cannot ... collect more than the percentage already completed.
rules.notes: Stated generally in the business management chapter. For home improvement contracts the statutory rule is in B&P 7159; cross-check that chunk.

rules.title: Retention released only after whole project accepted
rules.plain_english: Retention is released only after the entire project is accepted, even if your own work finished early. Subcontractors who finish early may wait a long time, so plan cash flow (possibly borrowing).

parameters.risk: early-finishing subcontractors wait for project acceptance

rules.applies_to: Contractors and subcontractors with retention
rules.quote: Retention payments to the individual contractor may be held up through no fault of the contractor. The total project must be ... accepted before retentions are released.
rules.notes: These pages give no statutory deadlines for releasing retention after completion. California prompt payment and retention statutes are outside this chunk.

rules.title: Estimate must include sales tax, freight, burdened labor, direct and indirect costs
rules.plain_english: Bid estimates should include sales tax and freight on materials. Do not deduct cash discounts unless you are sure you can pay within the discount period. Labor must include payroll taxes, benefits, vacation and insurance, along with permits, financing costs, equipment and indirect costs.

parameters.exclude_cash_discounts_unless: funds certain to pay within discount period

rules.applies_to: Contractors preparing bids/estimates
rules.quote: It is important to include sales tax and freight costs. Cash discounts should not be included unless the contractor is certain that sufficient financial resources will be available so that accounts payable may be repaid during the discount period.
rules.notes: Best-practice guidance; useful as an estimating checklist.

rules.title: Add overhead and profit to every bid
rules.plain_english: After totaling job costs, add overhead (office rent, supplies, office wages, advertising, bad debts, storage, other admin costs) and then add profit. Omitting profit seriously jeopardizes the business.
rules.applies_to: Contractors preparing bids/estimates
rules.quote: The contractor also must identify the overhead expenses. Overhead normally includes such expenses as office rental, supplies and wages, advertising, bad debts, storage charges, and any other general administrative costs. When all the costs have been totaled, the contractor must add profit.
rules.notes: The pitfalls on page 65 (bidding without understanding the plans, overextension, bidding against competitors instead of the job) are also useful bid-review checks.

rules.title: Schedule with bar chart or critical path method
rules.plain_english: The estimate becomes the project budget and a schedule. A bar chart shows task start and finish dates. The critical path method links dependent tasks, and any delay on a critical-path task delays the whole project.

parameters.cpm_rule: delay on any critical-path task = delay of project completion

rules.applies_to: Contractor project scheduling
rules.quote: The critical path method (Figure 6.B) is a more complex tool that better interrelates the tasks. ... Any delay in one of these tasks will result in an overall delay of the project.
rules.notes: Figures 6.A and 6.B (pages 66-67) are images with no extractable text.

rules.title: Design an insurance package; review coverage yearly
rules.plain_english: Work with an agent or broker on an insurance package that can include workers' comp, fire, liability, auto, fidelity bonds, business interruption, employee health and life, and key-person coverage. Cover the largest exposure first, use deductibles to cut cost, and review property and liability coverage every year.
rules.applies_to: Contractor risk management
rules.quote: Insurance is a means of reducing the company’s exposure to risk. The contractor should consult an insurance agent or broker to design a comprehensive insurance package to meet the company’s specific needs. ... Reviewing coverage yearly to reflect changes in the business.
rules.notes: Of these coverages, only workers' comp (if you have employees) is legally mandatory per other sections. The rest is guidance.

rules.title: Four owner-builder contract types
rules.plain_english: Common owner-builder contract types are lump-sum, cost-plus, unit-price and guaranteed-maximum cost. Standard forms are available from trade associations, AIA and AGC, and an attorney should check contracts for regulatory compliance.

parameters.recommended_review: attorney check for compliance with regulatory agency requirements

rules.applies_to: Contractors and owners entering construction contracts
rules.quote: There are typically four types of contractual agreements between the builder and owner with which the contractor should be familiar. These are the lump-sum, the cost-plus, the unit-price, and the guaranteed-maximum cost contract.

rules.title: Put significant contracts in writing
rules.plain_english: Some contracts are legally required to be in writing, and any contract of significance should be written so the parties' rights and intent are clear if a dispute arises.

parameters.applies_when: statutorily required, and recommended for any contract of significance

rules.applies_to: Contractors and owners
rules.citation: None cited on this page (statutory writing requirements, e.g., home improvement contracts, appear elsewhere)
rules.quote: Besides the statutory requirement that certain contracts be in writing, it is extremely important that a contract of any ... significance at all be in writing.
rules.notes: Which contracts are statutorily required to be written is not specified on this page.

rules.title: Document changes and get a signed written change order
rules.plain_english: When the customer requests something different from the contract (more or less work), document it in writing, negotiate the cost and time impact right away, let the customer decide, and have both parties sign a written change order.

parameters.trigger: request differs from original agreement (more or less)
steps: immediately negotiate cost and time effect
inform customer and let customer decide
both parties sign written change order

rules.applies_to: Contractors and owners on any project with changes/extras
rules.citation: None cited on this page (CSLB guidance; home improvement extra-work rules appear in B&P 7159 elsewhere)
rules.quote: Once you determine that a request is different than what was agreed to (whether more or less), document that fact in writing. You should also immediately negotiate the effect of the change, such as cost and time. ... If you and your customer agree to the change, make sure both parties sign the written change order.
rules.notes: Statutory content requirements for change orders on home improvement contracts are in another chunk.

rules.title: Punch lists, end-of-job walk-through, regular invoicing
rules.plain_english: Use frequent punch lists, do a walk-through near the end of the job to list remaining items, fix deficiencies quickly, document progress, and invoice regularly to keep cash flowing and the customer informed.
rules.applies_to: Contractors (dispute prevention)
rules.quote: Frequent “punch lists” are a good idea. A walk-through near the end of the job to determine the items that are left to be completed is recommended. Correct any deficiencies quickly. ... By invoicing regularly, you will minimize your business’s cash demands while keeping your customer informed.
rules.notes: Best-practice guidance.

rules.title: Small claims monetary limit $12,500
rules.plain_english: You can sue for money owed in small claims court for up to $12,500. Cases are usually heard within one to two months at minimal cost.
rules.applies_to: Contractors (or customers) pursuing money claims
rules.quote: Although you cannot foreclose on a mechanics lien in small claims court, you may get a monetary judgment of up to $12,500 (see CCP §116.221).
rules.notes: CCP 116.221 sets the limit for natural persons. A lower limit for entity plaintiffs (CCP 116.220) is not stated in this source; verify before applying $12,500 to a corporation or LLC.
rules.correction: Quote matches PDF p.71. CCP 116.221 is not reproduced in the law book (the 2026 edition removed non-B&P code sections, PDF p.10); primary text not visible. B&P text on PDF p.306 only points to CCP 116.220 "in Appendix", and the 2026 edition has no appendix. The $12,500 limit cannot be checked against primary text. The extractor's caution stands: CCP 116.220 sets a lower limit for plaintiffs that are not natural persons (believed to be $6,250), so do not apply $12,500 to a corporation or LLC without checking.

rules.title: Mechanics lien cannot be foreclosed in small claims court
rules.plain_english: Small claims court can award money but cannot foreclose a mechanics lien; lien foreclosure must be filed in superior court.
rules.applies_to: Lien claimants
rules.quote: Although you cannot foreclose on a mechanics lien in small claims court, you may get a monetary judgment of up to $12,500 (see CCP §116.221).
rules.notes: Lien foreclosure deadlines are in the mechanics lien rules below. The 'superior court' venue is implied, not stated.

rules.title: No attorneys in small claims
rules.plain_english: In small claims court both you and your customer must represent yourselves. Neither side may be represented by an attorney.
rules.applies_to: Parties in small claims court
rules.citation: None cited on this page (CCP small claims provisions)
rules.quote: You and your customer must represent yourselves. Neither you nor your customer may be represented by an attorney.
rules.notes: Small-claims self-help: https://selfhelp.courts.ca.gov/small-claims-california

rules.title: Losing small claims defendant may appeal within 30 days
rules.plain_english: If the defendant loses in small claims court, they have an automatic right to appeal within 30 days of the ruling. Small claims judgments are otherwise as binding as other court judgments.

parameters.trigger: small claims ruling

rules.applies_to: Parties in small claims court
rules.citation: None cited on this page (CCP small claims provisions)
rules.quote: If the defendant loses in small claims court, there is an automatic right of appeal within 30 days of the ruling.
rules.notes: Calendar days assumed. The source does not say whether the 30 days run from the ruling date or from mailing of notice.
rules.correction: Quote matches PDF p.71. The CCP small-claims appeal provisions (CCP 116.710-116.795) is not reproduced in the law book (the 2026 edition removed non-B&P code sections, PDF p.10); primary text not visible. Caution (not verifiable here): CCP 116.750 is believed to run the 30 days from the clerk's mailing or delivery of notice of entry of judgment, not from the ruling date. The plaintiff also has no appeal on its own claim. Do not compute the deadline from the hearing date without checking.

rules.title: Residential (1-4 unit) arbitration clause: B&P 7191 title, type size and exact notice; bars CSLB arbitration
rules.plain_english: If a contract for work on residential property with four or fewer units has an arbitration clause, the clause must be titled 'ARBITRATION OF DISPUTES' and set in the required bold type (or in capitals if typed). The exact B&P 7191 notice and assent statement must come right after it, before the parties' initials. A clause that does not comply may not be enforceable against anyone but the contractor. If the parties agreed to private arbitration, the dispute cannot go to CSLB arbitration (B&P 7085(a)(6)).

parameters.applies_to_contracts: contracts for work on residential property with four or fewer units that contain a provision for arbitration of a dispute between the principals
parameters.format_if_printed: at least 10-point roman boldface type, or contrasting red print in at least 8-point roman boldface type
parameters.notice_placement: immediately following the arbitration provision and immediately before the line or space for the parties to indicate assent or nonassent (initials)
parameters.required_notice_text: NOTICE: BY INITIALING IN THE SPACE BELOW YOU ARE AGREEING TO HAVE ANY DISPUTE ARISING OUT OF THE MATTERS INCLUDED IN THE ‘ARBITRATION OF DISPUTES’ PROVISION DECIDED BY NEUTRAL ARBITRATION AS PROVIDED BY CALIFORNIA LAW AND YOU ARE GIVING UP ANY RIGHTS YOU MIGHT POSSESS TO HAVE THE DISPUTE LITIGATED IN A COURT OR JURY TRIAL. BY INITIALING IN THE SPACE BELOW YOU ARE GIVING UP YOUR JUDICIAL RIGHTS TO DISCOVERY AND APPEAL, UNLESS THOSE RIGHTS ARE SPECIFICALLY INCLUDED IN THE ‘ARBITRATION OF DISPUTES’ PROVISION. IF YOU REFUSE TO SUBMIT TO ARBITRATION AFTER AGREEING TO THIS PROVISION, YOU MAY BE COMPELLED TO ARBITRATE UNDER THE AUTHORITY OF THE BUSINESS AND PROFESSIONS CODE OR OTHER APPLICABLE LAWS. YOUR AGREEMENT TO THIS ARBITRATION PROVISION IS VOLUNTARY.
parameters.required_assent_statement: WE HAVE READ AND UNDERSTAND THE FOREGOING AND AGREE TO SUBMIT DISPUTES ARISING OUT OF THE MATTERS INCLUDED IN THE ‘ARBITRATION OF DISPUTES’ PROVISION TO NEUTRAL ARBITRATION.
parameters.notice_format_if_printed: at least 10-point roman boldface type, or contrasting red print in at least 8-point roman boldface type
parameters.consequence_of_noncompliance: provision may not be enforceable against any person other than the licensee (B&P 7191(c))
parameters.effect_on_cslb_arbitration: not eligible for CSLB arbitration if the parties previously agreed to private arbitration of the dispute pursuant to contract or otherwise (B&P 7085(a)(6); also a criterion for mandatory referral under 7085(b))
parameters.later_waiver_exception: stated only in CSLB narrative (PDF p.72); not in B&P 7085

rules.applies_to: Contractors using arbitration clauses in contracts for work on residential property with four or fewer units
rules.citation: B&P 7191 (clause title, type size, notice); B&P 7085(a)(6) (no CSLB arbitration after private arbitration agreement)
rules.source: 2026 CSLB Law Book, PDF page 72 (summary); PDF pages 439-440 (B&P 7191); PDF page 324 (B&P 7085)
rules.quote: (a) If a contract for work on residential property with four or fewer units contains a provision for arbitration of a dispute between the principals in the transaction, the provision shall be clearly titled “ARBITRATION OF DISPUTES.” ... (c) A provision for arbitration of a dispute between a principal in a contract for work on a residential property with four or fewer units that does not comply with this section may not be enforceable against any person other than the licensee.
rules.notes: Exact notice and assent text are in parameters.required_notice_text and required_assent_statement, checked character for character against PDF p.439. Original book summary (PDF p.72): "If you want potential disputes to be solved via private arbitration you must use the arbitration notice in Business and Professions Code section 7191 ... (unless both parties later sign a waiver of the contractual arbitration clause)."
rules.correction: The book summary says contractors "must use" the 7191 notice for any private arbitration clause. B&P 7191 actually covers only contracts for work on residential property with four or fewer units. For those, the provision must be titled "ARBITRATION OF DISPUTES" and set in at least 10-pt roman boldface (or contrasting red, at least 8-pt roman boldface) if printed, or in capitals if typed. The statutory NOTICE and assent statement must follow it immediately, before the initials line. A provision that does not comply may not be enforceable against anyone other than the licensee (7191(c)). Added the exact statutory notice and assent text. The bar on CSLB arbitration comes from B&P 7085(a)(6) ("The parties have not previously agreed to private arbitration of the dispute pursuant to contract or otherwise"). The "unless both parties later sign a waiver" exception appears only in the CSLB narrative (PDF p.72); B&P 7085 does not support it.

rules.title: CSLB arbitration: mandatory at or below $25,000 (bond amount); voluntary above $25,000 and under $50,000
rules.plain_english: CSLB must refer a qualifying complaint to arbitration when the contract price or the damages demanded is $25,000 or less, which is the amount of the contractor's bond. When damages are above $25,000 and below $50,000, CSLB may refer it to arbitration only if both the contractor and the complainant agree.

parameters.qualifying_complaints: verified complaint alleging violation of B&P 7107, 7109, 7110, 7113, 7119 or 7120, or any complaint arising from a contract involving works of improvement, where the registrar finds a possible violation
parameters.formula: tier = 'mandatory' if (contract_price <= 25000 or damages_demanded <= 25000) else ('voluntary' if 25000 < damages < 50000 and both_parties_agree else 'not_eligible')
parameters.cost: free (CSLB narrative, PDF p.72; not stated in statute)

rules.applies_to: Contractors subject to CSLB complaints; homeowners filing complaints
rules.source: 2026 CSLB Law Book, PDF page 72 (summary); PDF pages 324-325 (B&P 7085); PDF page 295 (B&P 7071.6)
rules.quote: For the purposes of paragraph (1), “material damages” means damages greater than the amount of the bond required under subdivision (a) of Section 7071.6, but less than fifty thousand dollars ($50,000). (b) In all cases in which a possible violation of the sections set forth in paragraph (1) of subdivision (a) exists and the contract price, or the demand for damages is equal to or less than the amount of the bond required under Section 7071.6, but, regardless of the contract price, the complaint shall be referred to arbitration, utilizing the criteria set forth in paragraphs (2) to (6), inclusive, of subdivision (a).
rules.notes: B&P 7071.6(a) (operative 1/1/2023) sets the bond at $25,000. If the bond amount changes, both tier boundaries move with it. Original book summary (PDF p.72): "a mandatory program for disputes involving alleged damages of less than $25,000, and a voluntary program for disputes involving alleged damages of between $25,000 and $50,000."
rules.correction: The statute sets the tier boundaries by reference to the contractor's bond, and the book gets the edges wrong. Mandatory referral (B&P 7085(b)) applies when the contract price OR the demand for damages is "equal to or less than" the B&P 7071.6 bond amount, which is $25,000 (PDF p.295). The complaint "shall be referred" with no party consent needed. So exactly $25,000 is mandatory, not voluntary, and a contract price at or under $25,000 also qualifies. Voluntary referral (7085(a)) needs the consent of both licensee and complainant and "material damages" above the bond amount but "less than" $50,000, so exactly $50,000 is out. Both tiers need a possible violation of B&P 7107, 7109, 7110, 7113, 7119 or 7120, or a complaint arising from a contract for a work of improvement. "Free" comes from the CSLB narrative only. The 7085(b) text as printed reads garbled ("but, regardless of the contract price, the complaint shall be referred"); the thresholds above follow its operative words.

rules.title: CSLB arbitration eligibility criteria (B&P 7085)
rules.plain_english: CSLB can send a dispute to its arbitration program only if all of these hold: the contractor's license was in good standing at the time of the alleged violation; the contractor has no history of repeated or similar violations and no outstanding disciplinary actions; the parties have not already agreed to private arbitration; and the registrar finds arbitration serves the public better than discipline. Voluntary cases also need evidence of material damages, and the parties must be told about Civil Code 2855.
rules.applies_to: Disputes filed with CSLB
rules.source: 2026 CSLB Law Book, PDF page 72 (summary); PDF pages 324-325 (B&P 7085)
rules.quote: (2) There are reasonable grounds for the registrar to believe that the public interest would be better served by arbitration than by disciplinary action. (3) The licensee does not have a history of repeated or similar violations. (4) The licensee was in good standing at the time of the alleged violation. (5) The licensee does not have any outstanding disciplinary actions filed against him or her. (6) The parties have not previously agreed to private arbitration of the dispute pursuant to contract or otherwise.
rules.notes: The book summary (PDF p.72) adds "(current and not under suspension)" to explain good standing. Original summary criterion: "The contractor cannot have a record of prior violations."
rules.correction: The book lists three criteria. B&P 7085(a) has seven, worded differently. "Cannot have a record of prior violations" overstates the statute, which only requires that the licensee "does not have a history of repeated or similar violations" ((a)(3)). Added the missing criteria: no outstanding disciplinary actions filed against the licensee ((a)(5)); a registrar finding that the public interest is better served by arbitration than by discipline ((a)(2)); and, for voluntary referrals, evidence of material damages ((a)(1)) and that the parties were advised of Civil Code 2855 ((a)(7)). Mandatory referrals (7085(b)) use criteria (a)(2)-(6).

rules.title: Lien remedies: preliminary notice, record lien, stop notice, foreclose
rules.plain_english: Anyone who improves property may have lien rights on the property and possibly on construction funds. Perfecting them is technical and deadlines are short: serve the preliminary notice, record the mechanics lien, file a stop notice, and sue to foreclose.
rules.applies_to: Contractors, subcontractors, laborers, material suppliers
rules.citation: None cited on this page (Cal. Civil Code mechanics lien law)
rules.quote: You should be thoroughly familiar with the manner and means of perfecting your lien rights, such as giving the preliminary notice, recording the mechanics lien, filing a stop notice, and filing suit to foreclose. These remedies can be utilized by anyone who improves the property.
rules.notes: The CSLB guide uses pre-2012 terminology. Under the current Civil Code (8000 et seq.) a 'stop notice' is a 'stop payment notice' and an 'original contractor' is a 'direct contractor'.

rules.title: Corporations/LLCs need an attorney outside small claims
rules.plain_english: A corporation or LLC cannot represent itself in court except in small claims and must hire an attorney. Sole proprietors and partners may represent themselves.
rules.applies_to: Contractor business entities filing suit
rules.quote: If you are a corporation or limited liability company, you cannot represent yourself in court other than small claims court and must obtain the services of an attorney. If you are a partner or a sole proprietor, you can represent yourself in court and are not required to have an attorney represent you.

rules.title: Breach-of-contract suit available even without lien rights
rules.plain_english: Even if you missed the mechanics lien deadlines, you can still sue for breach of contract or on any other legal theory to collect money owed.
rules.applies_to: Contractors owed money
rules.quote: Regardless of your mechanics lien rights, as with any other businessperson, you can file suit for breach of the construction contract if someone does not fulfill their obligation.
rules.notes: Page 74 repeats the point: 'even if you have not availed yourself of the mechanics lien rights, you still have alternative legal remedies.' Limitations periods for contract suits are not stated.

rules.title: Mechanics lien right is constitutional
rules.plain_english: The California Constitution gives mechanics, material suppliers, artisans and laborers a lien on the property they improved, for the value of their labor and materials. Statutes set how the lien is perfected.

parameters.lien_measure: value of labor done and material furnished

rules.applies_to: Contractors, subcontractors, laborers, material suppliers; property owners
rules.quote: Mechanics, persons furnishing materials, artisans, and laborers of every class, shall have a lien upon the property upon which they have bestowed labor or furnished material for the value of such labor done and material furnished
rules.notes: The source writes the citation as 'Article 14, Section 3'.

rules.title: Lien claimant needs a contract with owner or owner's agent
rules.plain_english: You don't need a contract directly with the owner to claim a lien, but you must have one with the owner or someone treated as the owner's agent (a contractor, subcontractor, architect, builder or other person in charge of the work).

contract_required_with: other person having charge of the work of improvement

rules.applies_to: Potential lien claimants
rules.citation: None cited (CSLB lien guide); Cal. Civil Code mechanics lien law
rules.quote: To file on mechanics liens does not mean that they must have a contract directly with the owner. However, they must have a contract with the agent of the owner and every contractor, subcontractor, architect, builder, or other person having charge of a work of improvement and held to be an agent of the owner.
rules.correction: Quote matches PDF p.73. The Civil Code mechanics lien law (Civ. Code 8000 et seq.) is not reproduced in the law book (the 2026 edition removed non-B&P code sections, PDF p.10); primary text not visible.

rules.title: A material supplier's supplier has no lien
rules.plain_english: A material supplier is not the owner's agent, so a company that sells to a material supplier (not to a contractor) has no mechanics lien right.

parameters.reason: material supplier is not agent of owner

rules.applies_to: Material suppliers and their vendors
rules.citation: None cited (CSLB lien guide); Cal. Civil Code mechanics lien law
rules.quote: A material supplier is not the agent of the owner and, therefore, a material supplier’s supplier is not entitled to a statutory lien.
rules.notes: Useful as an eligibility check: tier = supplier-to-supplier means no lien.

rules.title: Work/materials must be incorporated (installed) to perfect a lien
rules.plain_english: To perfect a mechanics lien, your work or materials must be incorporated into (installed in) the structure.
rules.applies_to: Lien claimants
rules.citation: None cited (CSLB lien guide); Cal. Civil Code mechanics lien law
rules.quote: Further, to perfect your lien, the work and/or materials, etc. must be incorporated into the structure. That is to say, it has to be installed.
rules.notes: This is a simplified statement; the Civil Code has nuances for materials furnished but not used. Verify before using it to deny a lien.
rules.correction: Quote matches PDF p.73. The Civil Code mechanics lien law is not reproduced in the law book (the 2026 edition removed non-B&P code sections, PDF p.10); primary text not visible. The extractor's caution about materials that were furnished but not installed stands.

rules.title: No mechanics lien on public works; use stop notice
rules.plain_english: A mechanics lien is a lien on property and a stop notice is a lien on construction funds; you may use either or both. On public works you cannot record a mechanics lien, so a stop notice may be your only remedy.
rules.applies_to: Contractors, subcontractors and suppliers on public and private works
rules.citation: None cited (CSLB lien guide); Cal. Civil Code mechanics lien law
rules.quote: A mechanics lien is a lien on property. A stop notice is a lien on funds. You may use one or the other, or both. However, it should be noted that in public works, you cannot file a mechanics lien; therefore, your only remedy may be a stop notice.
rules.notes: Current statutes call this a 'stop payment notice'. Public works payment bond claims are another remedy that this page does not cover.

rules.title: Gather property and party information before serving notices
rules.plain_english: Before serving lien notices, get the property's legal description and the owner's name and interest. Confirm who ordered the work and whether others (such as lenders) hold an interest, determine your role (prime, sub, laborer, supplier), identify the construction lender, and consider any bond or joint control.

checklist: owner name and extent of owner's interest
whether owner requested the improvement; interests of requester and others (e.g., lenders)
your role: prime contractor, subcontractor, laborer, or material supplier
effect of a bond or joint control

rules.applies_to: All potential lien and stop notice claimants
rules.citation: None cited (CSLB Mechanics Lien and Stop Notice Checklist, Part I)
rules.quote: Obtain the legal description of the property. ... Determine the name of the construction lender (if any). ... Consider the effect of a bond or joint control.
rules.notes: Good template for a job-intake form.

rules.title: Serve Preliminary 20-day Notice within 20 days of first furnishing
rules.plain_english: Subcontractors and material suppliers must serve a Preliminary 20-day Notice on the owner, the original (prime) contractor and the construction lender within 20 days after first furnishing labor or materials. Only one notice is needed per job, however many deliveries you make.

parameters.trigger: first furnishing of labor or materials

rules.applies_to: Subcontractors and material suppliers on private works
rules.citation: None cited (CSLB lien guide); Cal. Civil Code preliminary notice provisions (Civ. Code 8200-8216)
rules.quote: Within 20 days from first furnishing labor or materials, serve a “Preliminary 20-day Notice” on the owner, the original contractor, and construction lender. No matter how many deliveries you make, or the time span over which you furnish labor or materials, only one Preliminary Notice is required.
rules.notes: The Civil Code range is the extractor's cross-reference, not printed in the source. Two points also come from the extractor, not this source, and should be verified: under current law a late notice generally covers only work furnished within 20 days before service and after, and some direct contractors must also give notice to the construction lender.
rules.correction: Quote matches PDF p.75. Civil Code 8200-8216 are not reproduced in the law book. Partial support from B&P text in the book: the statutory Mechanics Lien Warning in B&P 7159(e)(4) (PDF p.402-403) says "The Preliminary Notice can be sent up to 20 days after the subcontractor starts work or the supplier provides material." It also says owners do not get preliminary notices from the prime contractor or laborers. That supports the 20-day figure. The service list (owner, original contractor, lender) and the effect of late service remain unchecked.

rules.title: Preliminary notice must include owner-responsibility wording
rules.plain_english: The preliminary notice must include specific statutory wording that tells the owner of their responsibility to notify everyone who served a preliminary notice (for example, when a Notice of Completion or Cessation is recorded).

parameters.required_content: statement informing owner of duty to notify those who served a Preliminary Notice

rules.applies_to: Subcontractors and material suppliers serving preliminary notices
rules.citation: None cited (CSLB lien guide); Cal. Civil Code preliminary notice content provisions
rules.quote: The notice must include specific wording to inform a property owner of a new responsibility to notify anyone else who served a Preliminary Notice.
rules.notes: The exact statutory wording is not reproduced in this source; take it from the Civil Code (preliminary notice form) before generating a notice.
rules.correction: Quote matches PDF p.75. The required statutory wording does not appear anywhere in the law book; the Civil Code preliminary-notice form is not included. The exact text must come from the Civil Code.

rules.title: Optional: file preliminary notice with county recorder to be alerted of NOC/NOCessation
rules.plain_english: You may also file your preliminary notice with the county recorder where the property is located. The recorder will then notify you when a Notice of Completion or Notice of Cessation is recorded, which shortens your lien deadline.

parameters.file_with: county recorder of county where property is located
parameters.benefit: recorder notifies you when Notice of Completion or Notice of Cessation is recorded

rules.applies_to: Subcontractors and material suppliers
rules.quote: NOTE: You may also file the Preliminary 20-day Notice with the county recorder in the county in which the property is located. The county recorder will then notify you when a Notice of Completion or Notice of Cessation is recorded on the property.

rules.title: How to serve the preliminary notice
rules.plain_english: Serve the preliminary notice by first-class certified or registered mail, return receipt requested, postage prepaid. Address it to the recipient's residence or business, the address on the building permit, or the address on a recorded mortgage or trust deed. Personal delivery, or leaving it with an adult in charge at the residence or business, also works. Keep the post office receipts as proof.

mail_methods: first class certified mail, return receipt requested, postage prepaid
first class registered mail, return receipt requested, postage prepaid
valid_addresses: residence or place of business of person served
address on recorded mortgage or trust deed
alternative_methods: leaving with adult person in charge at residence or place of business

rules.applies_to: Lien claimants serving preliminary notices
rules.citation: None cited (CSLB lien guide); Cal. Civil Code notice service provisions
rules.quote: The most common method for serving a notice is to use first class certified or registered mail, return receipt requested, postage prepaid, addressed to the residence or place of business of the person being served, or at the address shown by the building permit, or at an address contained on a recorded mortgage or trust deed.

rules.title: Stop work under the contract once a Notice of Completion is recorded
rules.plain_english: Once a Notice of Completion has been recorded (it requires the owner's or owner's agent's signature), do no additional work under that contract.

parameters.trigger: Notice of Completion recorded
parameters.action: do not perform additional work under the contract

rules.applies_to: Subcontractors, suppliers and prime contractors
rules.quote: If the owner records a Notice of Completion after completion of work of improvement (this requires signature of owner or owner’s agent), you should not do additional work under the contract.
rules.notes: Repeated for prime contractors on pages 76-77 ('Do not do additional work under the contract').

rules.title: Owner may record Notice of Cessation only after 30 days of no labor
rules.plain_english: An owner may record a Notice of Cessation only after labor on the job has stopped for at least 30 days.
rules.applies_to: Project owners; lien claimants tracking deadlines
rules.citation: None cited (CSLB lien guide); Cal. Civil Code notice of cessation provision
rules.source: 2026 CSLB Law Book, PDF pages 75 and 77
rules.quote: Labor must have ceased for at least 30 days before the owner is entitled to record a Notice of Cessation.
rules.notes: Current law refers to a continuous 30-day cessation (extractor's note; verify).
rules.correction: Quote matches PDF p.75 and p.77. The Civil Code notice-of-cessation provision is not reproduced in the law book (the 2026 edition removed non-B&P code sections, PDF p.10); primary text not visible.

rules.title: Subcontractor: record lien within 30 days after owner records NOC or Notice of Cessation
rules.plain_english: If the owner records a Notice of Completion or Notice of Cessation, a subcontractor or supplier must record its Claim of Lien with the county recorder within 30 days of that recording, and serve stop notices at the same time.

parameters.trigger: owner records Notice of Completion or Notice of Cessation

rules.applies_to: Subcontractors and material suppliers (non-prime claimants)
rules.citation: None cited (CSLB lien guide); Cal. Civil Code lien recording deadlines for claimants other than direct contractors
rules.quote: Within 30 days of the owner recording either a Notice of Cessation or Completion, the subcontractor must ... record a Claim of Lien with the county recorder. Also at this time, serve stop notices (see below).
rules.notes: Confirmed by the glossary on page 79 (30 days for a subcontractor if the NOC is recorded). The book frames the trigger as the date of recording.
rules.correction: Quote matches PDF p.75-76. The Civil Code lien-recording deadline for claimants other than direct contractors is not reproduced in the law book (the 2026 edition removed non-B&P code sections, PDF p.10); primary text not visible. It is consistent with the glossary on PDF p.79 (30 days for a subcontractor after an NOC).

rules.title: Owner must notify potential lien claimants within 10 days of recording NOC/NOCessation
rules.plain_english: An owner who records a Notice of Completion or Notice of Cessation must notify potential lien claimants within 10 days of recording, so they know their lien deadline was shortened. This does not apply to residential property with four or fewer units.

parameters.trigger: owner records Notice of Completion or Notice of Cessation
parameters.notify: potential lien claimants (those who gave preliminary notice)
parameters.exempt_if: residential property of four or fewer units

rules.applies_to: Project owners (other than residential 1-4 units)
rules.citation: None cited (CSLB lien guide); Cal. Civil Code owner notice provision
rules.quote: An owner who files a Notice of Cessation or a Notice of Completion must notify any potential lien claimants within 10 days of recording the notices. This notification is designed to let you, the potential lien claimant, know that the time for filing a Claim of Lien has been reduced. This provision does not apply to a residential property of four or fewer units.
rules.notes: The consequence of an owner's failure to notify is not stated here. Under the Civil Code, the shortened deadline may not apply to a claimant who was not notified (extractor's note; verify).
rules.correction: Quote matches PDF p.76. The Civil Code owner-notice provision is not reproduced in the law book (the 2026 edition removed non-B&P code sections, PDF p.10); primary text not visible. The 10-day duty and the exemption for residential property of four or fewer units cannot be checked against primary text.

rules.title: File lien foreclosure within 90 days of recording the lien; record lis pendens
rules.plain_english: Within 90 days after recording your Claim of Lien, file a lawsuit to foreclose it and record a lis pendens at the same time. If you served a stop notice, file suit on it then too. Otherwise the lien is lost.

parameters.trigger: recording of Claim of Lien
concurrent_actions: file action on stop notice (if applicable)

rules.applies_to: All mechanics lien claimants (prime contractors, subcontractors, suppliers)
rules.citation: None cited (CSLB lien guide); Cal. Civil Code lien foreclosure deadline
rules.quote: File Lien Foreclosure Action within 90 days of recording a Claim of Lien and record a lis pendens at the same time. You must also file an action on the stop notice at this time, if applicable.
rules.notes: Repeated for prime contractors on page 77. The source does not mention how an unenforced lien is released, or the statutory timing window for suit on a stop payment notice; verify the latter against the current Civil Code.
rules.correction: Quote matches PDF p.76-77. The Civil Code lien-foreclosure deadline is not reproduced in the law book (the 2026 edition removed non-B&P code sections, PDF p.10); primary text not visible. The phrase "Otherwise the lien is lost" in plain_english is the extractor's inference. The book does not state the consequence.

rules.title: No NOC/NOCessation recorded: record lien within 90 days of use+cessation or acceptance
rules.plain_english: If no Notice of Completion or Notice of Cessation is recorded, prime contractors, subcontractors and suppliers must record their Claim of Lien within 90 days after labor ceases and the owner uses the work, or after the owner accepts the work. Subs and suppliers should serve stop notices at the same time.

triggers: labor ceases and owner/agent uses the work of improvement
parameters.precondition: no Notice of Completion or Notice of Cessation recorded

rules.applies_to: Prime contractors, subcontractors and material suppliers on private works
rules.citation: None cited (CSLB lien guide); Cal. Civil Code lien recording deadlines
rules.quote: If no Notice of Completion or Notice of Cessation is recorded and either: (a) Labor ceases and the owner or agent uses work of improvement, or (b) The owner or agent accepts improvement, then: (1) Within 90 days of any of the above acts, record a Claim of Lien. Also, at this time, serve stop notices (see below).
rules.notes: Glossary page 79: 'If this notice is not filed in a timely manner, you have a 90-day period'. Under the current Civil Code, completion also includes actual completion and cessation of labor for a continuous 60 days (extractor's note, not in this source; verify).
rules.correction: Quote matches PDF p.76 (subs/suppliers) and p.77 (prime). The Civil Code completion and lien-recording provisions is not reproduced in the law book (the 2026 edition removed non-B&P code sections, PDF p.10); primary text not visible.

rules.title: Who to serve stop notices on; surety if payment bond recorded
rules.plain_english: Serve stop notices on the owner, bonded stop notices on the construction lender, or on anyone else holding construction funds. If no mechanics lien has been recorded and a surety payment bond has been recorded, serve the surety. File suit on the notice when you file the lien foreclosure.

parameters.surety_service_required_if: no mechanics lien recorded AND surety payment bond recorded
parameters.suit_timing: same time as lien foreclosure action

rules.applies_to: Subcontractors and material suppliers on private works
rules.citation: None cited (CSLB lien guide); Cal. Civil Code stop payment notice and payment bond provisions
rules.quote: Serve stop notices on the owner, bonded stop notices on the construction lender, or anyone holding funds. (b) If no mechanics lien has been recorded, and a surety payment bond has been recorded, then the notice must be served on the surety. (c) File suit on the notice at the same time that you file a Lien Foreclosure Action.
rules.notes: Current term: 'stop payment notice'.

rules.title: Prime contractor: Notice of Completion within 15 days after completion (owner signature)
rules.plain_english: Within 15 days after completion, a Notice of Completion may be recorded. It must be signed by the owner or owner's agent. After that, do no more work under the contract.
rules.applies_to: Prime contractors and owners
rules.citation: None cited (CSLB lien guide); Cal. Civil Code notice of completion provision
rules.quote: Within 15 days after completion, you may record a Notice of Completion. ... This notice requires the signature of the owner or the owner’s agent.
rules.notes: This conflicts with the glossary on page 79, which says the NOC must be recorded within 10 days after completion. Current law is believed to be 15 days (extractor's note; verify). See rule notice-of-completion-recording-deadline.
rules.correction: Quote matches PDF p.76-77. The Civil Code notice-of-completion provision is not reproduced in the law book (the 2026 edition removed non-B&P code sections, PDF p.10); primary text not visible. The book contradicts itself: 15 days here, 10 days in the glossary (PDF p.79). The book alone cannot settle which is current. 15 days is believed to be current law (Civ. Code 8182), but this was not checked against primary text.

rules.title: Prime contractor: record lien within 60 days after NOC or Notice of Cessation
rules.plain_english: If a Notice of Completion or Notice of Cessation is recorded, the prime (original) contractor must record its Claim of Lien within 60 days of that recording, then foreclose within 90 days of recording the lien.

parameters.trigger: recording of Notice of Completion or Notice of Cessation

rules.applies_to: Prime (original/direct) contractors
rules.citation: None cited (CSLB lien guide); Cal. Civil Code direct contractor lien deadline
rules.quote: Within 60 days of recording a Notice of Cessation or a Notice of Completion, the contractor must record a Claim of Lien.
rules.notes: Confirmed by the glossary on page 79 (60 days for a prime contractor).
rules.correction: Quote matches PDF p.77. The Civil Code direct-contractor lien deadline is not reproduced in the law book (the 2026 edition removed non-B&P code sections, PDF p.10); primary text not visible. It is consistent with the glossary on PDF p.79.

rules.title: 'Claim of lien' and 'mechanics lien' mean the same (AB 457)
rules.plain_english: Since AB 457 (effective 2011), 'claim of lien' and 'mechanics lien' have the same legal definition.
rules.applies_to: Lien claimants and owners
