rules.quote: NOTE: Per AB 457, which took effect in 2011, the definitions of “claim of lien” and “mechanics lien” are the same.

rules.title: Serve Notice of Mechanics Lien with signed proof of service affidavit or lien is unenforceable
rules.plain_english: When you record a mechanics lien, serve a Notice of Mechanics Lien on the owner (or reputed owner), or on the construction lender or original contractor. The person who served it must complete and sign a proof of service affidavit. Without service and the affidavit, the lien cannot be enforced.

serve_on: owner or person believed to be owner
parameters.required_document: proof of service affidavit signed by person serving

rules.applies_to: All mechanics lien claimants
rules.citation: AB 457 (2010); Cal. Civil Code mechanics lien content and service provision
rules.quote: Notice of Mechanics Lien be served on the owner or person believed to be the owner of the property or on the construction lender or original contractor, and that a “proof of service affidavit” ... be completed and signed by the person serving the Notice of Mechanics Lien. ... will cause the mechanics lien to be unenforceable.
rules.notes: Under the current Civil Code, service on the lender or original contractor is generally an alternative only when the owner cannot be served. The proof of service is attached to the lien when recorded (extractor's note; verify).
rules.correction: Quote matches PDF p.78. AB 457 and the Civil Code service provisions is not reproduced in the law book (the 2026 edition removed non-B&P code sections, PDF p.10); primary text not visible. The extractor's caution stands: service on the lender or original contractor is believed to be a fallback for when the owner cannot be served.

rules.title: Bonded stop notice to lender: bond = 1.25 x claim
rules.plain_english: To bind a construction lender, a stop notice must be accompanied by a bond equal to 1.25 times the claim, delivered in person or by certified or registered mail to whoever administers or holds the construction funds. If the claimant loses, it must pay the costs awarded to the owner, contractor or lender.

parameters.deliver_to: persons responsible for administering or holding construction funds
parameters.claimant_liability_if_loses: all costs awarded to owner, contractor, or construction lender

rules.applies_to: Stop notice claimants serving construction lenders (private works)
rules.citation: None cited (CSLB lien guide); Cal. Civil Code bonded stop payment notice provision
rules.source: 2026 CSLB Law Book, PDF pages 78 and 81
rules.quote: To bind a construction lender, the stop notice must be bonded. The bond that accompanies a stop notice to any construction lender must be in the sum equal to 1 ¼ times the amount of the claim. The bond must be delivered along with the stop notice in person or by certified or registered mail to the responsible parties for administering or holding the construction funds.
rules.notes: Also stated in the glossary entry 'Bonded Stop Notice' on page 78. Exceptions under current law (for example, a direct contractor's notice to a lender) are not stated here.
rules.correction: Quote matches PDF p.81 (and glossary entry, PDF p.78). The Civil Code bonded stop payment notice provision is not reproduced in the law book (the 2026 edition removed non-B&P code sections, PDF p.10); primary text not visible. The 1.25x bond multiplier cannot be checked against primary text.

rules.title: Claim of Lien: required contents (signed and verified)
rules.plain_english: A Claim of Lien must be signed and verified by the claimant or its agent and state the five items listed in the parameters, including the demand after credits and offsets and a site description sufficient for identification.

required_fields: amount of claimant's demand after deducting credits and offsets
name of owner or reputed owner, if known
kind of labor, services, equipment, or materials furnished
name of person who employed claimant or to whom claimant furnished labor/services/equipment/materials
description of the site sufficient for identification

rules.applies_to: All mechanics lien claimants
rules.citation: None cited (CSLB lien glossary); Cal. Civil Code mechanics lien content provision
rules.quote: Claim of Lien (mechanics lien) is a written statement signed and verified by the claimant or by the claimant’s agent that must state the following: 1. The amount of claimant’s demand (after deducting credits and offsets). 2. The name of the owner or reputed owner, if known. 3. The kind of labor, services, equipment, or materials furnished by the claimant.
rules.notes: Items 4 and 5 are in the parameters. Current law also requires the claimant's address, a Notice of Mechanics Lien statement and proof of service (see notice-of-mechanics-lien-service-and-proof); verify the full list before generating forms.

rules.title: Notice of Cessation: required contents (owner signed and verified)
rules.plain_english: A Notice of Cessation is signed and verified by the owner or agent and states the six items listed in the parameters, from the approximate date labor stopped to the original contractor's name.

required_fields: confirmation that no further labor has been performed since recording
nature of owner's interest or estate
street address of site or description sufficient for identification
name of original contractor, if any

rules.applies_to: Project owners recording a Notice of Cessation
rules.citation: None cited (CSLB lien glossary); Cal. Civil Code notice of cessation provision
rules.quote: Notice of Cessation is a written notice, signed and verified by the owner or their agent, stating: 1. Approximate date when labor on the job stopped. 2. Confirmation that no further labor has been performed since the recording of the notice. 3. Name and address of the owner. 4. Nature of the interest or estate of the owner.
rules.notes: Items 5 and 6 are in the parameters.

rules.title: Notice of Completion: required contents (owner signed and verified)
rules.plain_english: A Notice of Completion is signed and verified by the owner or agent and states the five items listed in the parameters, from the completion date to the original contractor for the completed work.

required_fields: nature of owner's interest or estate
street address of site or description sufficient for identification
name of original contractor, if any, for the contract covering the completed portion

rules.applies_to: Project owners recording a Notice of Completion
rules.citation: None cited (CSLB lien glossary); Cal. Civil Code notice of completion provision
rules.quote: Notice of Completion is a written notice, signed and verified by the owner or their agent, stating: 1. Date that the job was finished. 2. Name and address of the owner. 3. Nature of the interest or estate of the owner. 4. Street address of the site, if any, or a description of the site sufficient for identification.
rules.notes: Item 5 is in the parameters.

rules.title: Notice of Completion recording deadline (book states 10 days and 15 days)
rules.plain_english: The owner's Notice of Completion must be recorded with the county recorder in the county where the site is located, soon after completion. The glossary says within 10 days, but the checklist on page 76 says within 15 days. If it is recorded late, the shortened lien deadlines do not apply and claimants have 90 days.

parameters.record_with: county recorder of county where site is located
parameters.if_not_timely: claimants get the 90-day lien recording period

rules.applies_to: Project owners; lien claimants computing deadlines
rules.citation: None cited (CSLB lien glossary); Cal. Civil Code notice of completion provision
rules.source: 2026 CSLB Law Book, PDF page 79 (conflicts with PDF page 76)
rules.quote: The Notice of Completion must be recorded in the Office of the County Recorder of the county in which the site is located within 10 days after completion of the project.
rules.notes: Internal conflict in the source: 10 days (glossary, p.79) vs. 15 days (prime contractor checklist, p.76). The extractor believes 15 days is current law and 10 days comes from the pre-2012 statute; verify against the Civil Code before hard-coding.
rules.correction: Quote matches PDF p.79. The book does contradict itself, as the rule records: 10 days in the glossary (PDF p.79) and 15 days in the prime-contractor checklist (PDF p.76-77). The Civil Code notice-of-completion provision is not reproduced in the law book (the 2026 edition removed non-B&P code sections, PDF p.10); primary text not visible. Neither value can be checked. Keep the conflict flag and do not hard-code either value from this source.

rules.title: Lien recording deadline: 60 days (prime) / 30 days (sub) after NOC; else 90 days
rules.plain_english: If a valid Notice of Completion is recorded, a prime contractor has 60 days and a subcontractor 30 days to record a mechanics lien. If no timely notice is recorded, the deadline is 90 days.
rules.applies_to: All mechanics lien claimants on private works
rules.citation: None cited (CSLB lien glossary); Cal. Civil Code lien recording deadlines
rules.quote: If the Notice of Completion is recorded, then the time within which you must record your mechanics lien is 60 days if you are a prime contractor and 30 days if you are a subcontractor. If this notice is not filed in a timely manner, you have a 90-day period within which to record the claim.
rules.notes: This is the core lien deadline lookup. A Notice of Cessation shortens deadlines the same way (pages 75-77). The 90-day period runs from completion, which pages 76-77 describe as cessation plus use, or acceptance.
rules.correction: Quote matches PDF p.79. The Civil Code lien-recording deadlines is not reproduced in the law book (the 2026 edition removed non-B&P code sections, PDF p.10); primary text not visible. It is consistent with the checklists on PDF p.75-77 (30/60/90 days).

rules.title: Notice of Non-Responsibility: required contents
rules.plain_english: An owner or interest-holder who did not order the work (for example, a landlord whose tenant hired the contractor) can give a signed and verified Notice of Non-Responsibility. It must contain the four items listed in the parameters, ending with a statement that they will NOT be responsible for claims.

parameters.signed_and_verified_by: person owning/claiming interest who did not cause the work, or that person's agent
required_fields: description of site sufficient for identification
name and nature of title or interest of person giving notice
name of purchaser or lessee, if known
statement that person will NOT be responsible for claims arising from the work
parameters.typical_use: landlord whose tenant ordered the work

rules.applies_to: Property owners/landlords whose tenants or purchasers order work; contractors working for tenants
rules.citation: None cited (CSLB lien glossary); Cal. Civil Code notice of non-responsibility provision
rules.quote: This notice must contain: 1. Description of the site sufficient for identification. 2. Name and nature of the title or interest of the person giving the notice. 3. Name of the purchaser or person holding the lease (lessee), if known. 4. Statement by the person giving the notice that they will ... NOT be responsible for any claims arising from the work of improvement.
rules.notes: Contractors working for a tenant should check for a recorded notice. It can defeat a lien against the owner's interest.

rules.title: Notice of Non-Responsibility: post on site and record within 10 days of discovery
rules.plain_english: Within 10 days of discovering the work, the person asserting non-responsibility must post the notice in a conspicuous place on the site and record it with the county recorder.

parameters.trigger: discovery of the work of improvement
actions: post in conspicuous place on site
record with county recorder of county where site is located

rules.applies_to: Property owners/interest holders who did not cause the work
rules.citation: None cited (CSLB lien glossary); Cal. Civil Code notice of non-responsibility provision
rules.quote: Within 10 days of discovering the work of improvement, the person asserting non-responsibility must post this notice in a conspicuous place on the site and must record the notice in the Office of the County Recorder of the county in which the site is located.
rules.notes: Both posting and recording are required.
rules.correction: Quote matches PDF p.80. The Civil Code notice-of-non-responsibility provision is not reproduced in the law book (the 2026 edition removed non-B&P code sections, PDF p.10); primary text not visible.

rules.title: Definitions: original (prime) contractor; owner
rules.plain_english: The original or prime contractor (usually a general contractor) contracts directly with the owner. 'Owner' includes anyone with title or an interest in the real property.

parameters.owner_scope: any person having some title or interest in the parcel

rules.applies_to: Mechanics lien role classification
rules.quote: Original Contractor, also known as prime contractor, is usually a general contractor. Owner includes any person(s) having some title or interest in a parcel of real property.
rules.notes: Current Civil Code term: 'direct contractor'.

rules.title: Definition: subcontractor (no direct contract with owner)
rules.plain_english: A subcontractor is anyone without a direct contract with the owner who contracts with the prime contractor or another subcontractor. Subs are usually specialty contractors but can be general contractors. This role decides which lien deadlines apply.
rules.applies_to: Mechanics lien role classification
rules.quote: Subcontractor is any person who does not have a contract directly with an owner. The subcontractor has a contract with and from the prime contractor or another subcontractor. A subcontractor is usually a specialty contractor but can also be a general contractor.

rules.title: Definitions: lien foreclosure action; lis pendens
rules.plain_english: A lien foreclosure action is the lawsuit to enforce a mechanics lien. A lis pendens is a recorded notice that a pending lawsuit affects the real property, warning buyers they may be bound by the judgment.
rules.applies_to: Lien claimants and owners
rules.quote: Lien Foreclosure Action is a lawsuit to foreclose the mechanics lien. Lis Pendens is a notice that a lawsuit is pending, and that the lawsuit affects real property. It warns everyone who might acquire the property that they may be bound by an adverse judgment.

rules.title: Payment bond substitutes for the property as lien security
rules.plain_english: A payment bond, usually bought by the owner or contractor, is large enough to pay all claimants. Claimants can sue on the bond, which replaces the real property as security against mechanics liens.

parameters.amount: sufficient to pay all claims of claimants
parameters.effect: substitutes bond for real property as security

rules.applies_to: Owners, contractors and lien claimants
rules.quote: Payment Bond is a bond usually procured by the owner or contractor in an amount sufficient to pay all claims of claimants. The bond gives the claimant the right to recover in any suit brought on the bond. Usually, the bond is used to protect against mechanics liens and substitutes the bond as security instead of the real property.
rules.notes: Statutory bond amount percentages (for example for public works) are not stated here.

rules.title: Stop Notice: required contents (signed and verified)
rules.plain_english: A stop notice is a signed and verified notice telling a lender or other fund holder that money is owed. It must state the three items listed in the parameters, including the value of work already furnished and of the whole job.

required_fields: type of labor, services, equipment, or materials furnished or agreed to be furnished
name of person to or for whom furnished
amount (value as near as possible) of work/equipment already completed or furnished, and amount of whole work agreed

rules.applies_to: Stop notice claimants (private and public works)
rules.citation: None cited (CSLB lien glossary); Cal. Civil Code stop payment notice provisions
rules.quote: Stop Notice is a written notice, signed and verified by the claimant or the claimant’s agent, that puts a lender or anyone else holding construction funds on notice that there is money due and owed to the claimant. It must state the following: 1. Type of labor, services, equipment, or materials furnished or agreed to be furnished by the claimant.
rules.notes: Items 2 and 3 are in the parameters. Current term: 'stop payment notice'.

rules.title: Stop notice service on private works: owner/architect; lender branch manager
rules.plain_english: On private works, deliver the stop notice to the owner personally, leave it with a person in charge at their residence or business, or deliver it to their architect. For a lender with branches, deliver to the manager or responsible person at the branch holding the construction funds.

owner_service_options: left with person in charge at owner's residence or place of business
parameters.lender_service: manager or other responsible person at the office/branch administering or holding the construction funds
parameters.mail_alternative: registered or certified mail has same effect as personal service

rules.applies_to: Stop notice claimants on private works
rules.citation: None cited (CSLB lien glossary); Cal. Civil Code stop payment notice provisions
rules.quote: the notice must be delivered to the owner personally or left at their residence or place of business with a person in charge or delivered to their architect, if ... any; and, if the notice is served upon a construction lender holding construction funds and maintaining branch offices, it must be delivered to the manager
rules.notes: Quote truncated to fit 400 characters. It continues: 'or other responsible person at the office or branch administering or holding the construction funds.'

rules.title: Stop notice on public works: file with state department director or public disbursing officer
rules.plain_english: On state public works, file the stop notice with the director of the department that started the contract. On other public works, file it with the controller, auditor or other disbursing officer who pays under the contract, or with the body that awarded the contract.

parameters.state_public_work_file_with: director of the department that initiated the contract
other_public_work_file_with: other public disbursing officer responsible for contract payments
commissioners, managers, trustees, officers, board of supervisors, board of trustees, common council, or other awarding body

rules.applies_to: Subcontractors and suppliers on public works
rules.citation: None cited (CSLB lien glossary); Cal. Civil Code public works stop payment notice provisions
rules.quote: If involving any public work for the state, the notice must be filed with the director of the department that initiated the contract. If involving any other public work, the notice must be filed in the office of the controller, auditor, or other public disbursing officer whose duty it is to make payments under the provisions of the contract
rules.notes: Public works stop notice deadlines are not stated in this source.

rules.title: Stop notice may be served by registered or certified mail
rules.plain_english: Any stop notice may be served by registered or certified mail, which has the same effect as personal service.
rules.applies_to: Stop notice claimants
rules.quote: Any stop notice may be served by registered or certified mail with the same effect as personal service.

rules.title: Fund holder must withhold enough to cover the stop notice or be liable
rules.plain_english: A lender, owner or other party holding construction funds that receives a stop notice must withhold enough money to cover it. If it doesn't, it may be directly liable to the claimant.

parameters.obligation: withhold funds sufficient to satisfy stop notice amount
parameters.consequence_of_failure: fund holder may be directly liable to claimant
parameters.lender_bound_only_if: stop notice is bonded (1.25 x claim)

rules.applies_to: Owners, construction lenders, public agencies and others holding construction funds
rules.citation: None cited (CSLB lien glossary); Cal. Civil Code stop payment notice provisions
rules.quote: The stop notice obligates the person holding construction funds to withhold sufficient funds to satisfy the amount in the stop notice. If the person holding the funds does not withhold sufficient funds to satisfy the stop notice, then the lender or whoever else is holding the funds may be responsible to the claimant directly.
rules.notes: Category is 'required_notice' because a stop notice triggers the owner's or lender's withholding duty. It could also be read as a process_step.
rules.correction: Quote matches PDF p.81. The Civil Code stop payment notice provisions is not reproduced in the law book (the 2026 edition removed non-B&P code sections, PDF p.10); primary text not visible.

rules.title: Government bids may require steps toward minority, women and DVBE goals
rules.plain_english: Federal, state and local agencies, utilities and some private corporations may require bidders to take specific steps toward minority, women and disabled veteran business enterprise (DVBE) participation goals. For state contracts, check with the DGS Office of Small Business and DVBE Services.

parameters.state_contact: DGS Procurement Division, Office of Small Business and DVBE Services (OSDS), (916) 376-5000, OSDSHelp@dgs.ca.gov
parameters.federal_resource: U.S. Dept. of Commerce Minority Business Development Agency (www.mbda.gov)

rules.applies_to: Contractors bidding public/government contracts
rules.quote: Contractors bidding in California should know that there are a variety of federal, state, and local governmental agencies, as well as public utilities and private corporations, which may require a bidder to take specific steps to achieve established minority, women, and disabled veteran business enterprise (DVBE) goals.
rules.notes: Goal percentages and good-faith-effort steps are not stated here; they are set by each agency.

rules.title: Call 811 at least 2 working days, no more than 14 calendar days, before excavating
rules.plain_english: Anyone planning to excavate must contact the regional notification center (call 811, free) at least two working days, and no more than 14 calendar days, before starting. The center issues an inquiry (ticket) number confirming the call. Emergencies are excluded.
rules.applies_to: Any person or entity planning to excavate (contractors, subcontractors, owners) in California
rules.quote: California Government Code sections 4216-4216.9 require anyone planning to excavate to contact the appropriate regional notification center at least two working days (but not more than 14 calendar days) before beginning excavation. The center will issue an inquiry identification number to the excavator as confirmation of the call.
rules.notes: Page 85 repeats the rule with 'Excluding emergency situations'. The book cites the 4216-4216.9 range; the specific notice provision is believed to be Gov. Code 4216.2 (extractor's note).
rules.correction: Quote matches PDF p.84 (repeated on p.85 with "Excluding emergency situations"). Gov. Code 4216-4216.9 (B&P 7110(f), PDF p.351, only names the article) is not reproduced in the law book (the 2026 edition removed non-B&P code sections, PDF p.10); primary text not visible. The 2-working-day / 14-calendar-day window cannot be checked against primary text.

rules.title: Excavation permit invalid without USA identification number
rules.plain_english: An excavation permit is not valid unless you have the USA/811 inquiry identification number.
rules.applies_to: Excavators holding excavation permits
rules.quote: NOTE: An excavation permit is not valid without this identification number.

rules.title: USA applies to anyone disturbing the ground surface
rules.plain_english: Anyone who plans to disturb the ground by digging, drilling, boring or similar must comply with the 811 notification law.
rules.applies_to: Any person or entity
rules.quote: Any person or entity who plans to disturb the surface of the ground by digging, drilling, boring, etc.
rules.correction: Quote matches PDF p.85. Gov. Code 4216-4216.9 (B&P 7110(f), PDF p.351, only names the article) is not reproduced in the law book (the 2026 edition removed non-B&P code sections, PDF p.10); primary text not visible.

rules.title: USA exemptions for private property owners (no-permit work)
rules.plain_english: A private property owner is exempt from calling 811 when they hire a licensed contractor for excavation that needs no permit, or when they (not being a licensed contractor) improve their own principal residence with work that needs no permit. The licensed contractor is still responsible.

exempt_cases.who: private property owner who is not a licensed contractor

rules.applies_to: Private property owners
rules.quote: An owner of private property who contracts with a California state-licensed contractor or subcontractor for an excavation project that does not require an excavation permit. ... An owner of private property (who is not a licensed contractor or subcontractor) who, as a part of improving their principal residence, does work that does not require an excavation permit.
rules.notes: Combine with usa-own-ticket-per-contractor: the hired contractor must get its own ticket.
rules.correction: Quote matches PDF p.85. Gov. Code 4216-4216.9 (B&P 7110(f), PDF p.351, only names the article) is not reproduced in the law book (the 2026 edition removed non-B&P code sections, PDF p.10); primary text not visible.

rules.title: Excavating equipment rental agreements: required USA responsibility clause
rules.plain_english: A company that rents or leases power excavating or boring equipment to a licensed contractor is exempt from the 811 law only if the signed rental agreement contains the exact clause below, which shifts USA responsibility and liability to the renter.

parameters.applies_to_equipment: power-operated or power-driven excavating or boring equipment
parameters.lessee_must_be: contractor or subcontractor licensed under Contractors State License Law
parameters.required_clause_text: It is the sole responsibility of the lessee or renter to follow the requirements of the regional notification center law pursuant to Article 2 (commencing with Section 4216) of Chapter 3.1 of Division 5 of Title 1 of the Government Code. By signing this contract, the lessee or renter accepts all liabilities and responsibilities contained in the regional notification center law.

rules.applies_to: Equipment rental/leasing companies; licensed contractors renting excavation equipment
rules.quote: “It is the sole responsibility of the lessee or renter to follow the requirements of the regional notification center law pursuant to Article 2 (commencing with Section 4216) of Chapter 3.1 of Division 5 of Title 1 of the Government Code. By signing this contract, the lessee or renter accepts all liabilities and responsibilities contained in the regional notification center law.”
rules.notes: A contractor renting equipment who signs this clause takes on full USA compliance responsibility.
rules.correction: The clause text matches PDF p.85 word for word. Gov. Code 4216-4216.9 (B&P 7110(f), PDF p.351, only names the article) is not reproduced in the law book (the 2026 edition removed non-B&P code sections, PDF p.10); primary text not visible. The statutory wording cannot be checked against primary text. The clause is a condition of the lessor's exemption: the lessor is exempt only if the signed rental agreement contains it. It is not a clause the contractor must add on its own. The rule's plain_english says this correctly.

rules.title: Each excavating contractor/sub needs its own USA ticket
rules.plain_english: Every contractor and subcontractor excavating on a jobsite must have its own USA ticket number for its own excavation work. It cannot rely on the GC's or another sub's ticket.

parameters.ticket_per: each contractor or subcontractor performing excavation

rules.applies_to: All contractors and subcontractors excavating at a jobsite
rules.quote: Every contractor or subcontractor excavating at a jobsite must have their own Underground Service Alert (USA) identification (ticket) number for the excavation work they are performing.

rules.title: USA ticket valid 28 calendar days; revalidate before expiry
rules.plain_english: A USA ticket number is valid for 28 calendar days. If work will continue past that, contact the center to revalidate before the ticket expires.
rules.applies_to: Excavators holding USA tickets
rules.quote: Upon notification, the center will issue an identification (ticket) number. The ticket number will be valid for 28 calendar days. If work is to continue past 28 calendar days, the ticket number must be revalidated again by notifying the center before the ticket number expires.
rules.notes: Calculation: expiry_date = ticket_issue_date + 28 calendar days; send a revalidation alert before then.
rules.correction: Quote matches PDF p.85. Gov. Code 4216-4216.9 (B&P 7110(f), PDF p.351, only names the article) is not reproduced in the law book (the 2026 edition removed non-B&P code sections, PDF p.10); primary text not visible.

rules.title: Mark excavation boundaries (usually white paint) before operators mark
rules.plain_english: Before excavating, clearly mark the boundaries of the work area at the site, usually with white paint.
rules.applies_to: Excavators
rules.quote: At the site, excavators must clearly mark the boundaries of the work area, usually with white paint.

rules.title: Operators mark lines in color code or advise clearance
rules.plain_english: After notification, utility operators must give information about their facilities within your marked area and mark or stake their lines in the correct color, or tell you the area is clear. Operators answer only for facilities they own.

operator_actions: mark or stake lines using appropriate color code

rules.applies_to: Subsurface installation operators; excavators waiting for marks
rules.source: 2026 CSLB Law Book, PDF pages 84 and 86
rules.quote: Within these boundary markings, operators of underground installations must then provide information about their facilities, mark or stake the location of their lines clearly using the appropriate color to show what type of installation is present or advise of clearance.
rules.notes: Page 84: operators are only responsible for facilities they own.

rules.title: Request re-marking when marks are no longer visible
rules.plain_english: If utility markings become unreadable during the job, contact the notification center and ask that the operator re-mark the lines within two working days.

parameters.trigger: operator markings no longer visible
parameters.action: contact regional center to request re-mark

rules.applies_to: Excavators
rules.quote: During the course of the job, if the operator’s markings become no longer visible, the excavator must contact the regional center and request that the operator re-mark the lines within two working days.
rules.notes: The wording is ambiguous: 'within two working days' most naturally reads as the operator's re-mark window, not a deadline for the excavator's request.

rules.title: Pothole with hand tools or vacuum before using power equipment
rules.plain_english: Using the operator's marks, find the exact location of underground facilities with hand tools or a vacuum device before using any power equipment.
rules.applies_to: Excavators
rules.quote: Using the operator’s markings, an excavator must determine the exact location of underground facilities with hand tools or a vacuum device before any power equipment may be used.
rules.notes: The tolerance zone width is not stated in this source.

rules.title: New subsurface installations after Jan 1, 2023 must be GIS-mapped
rules.plain_english: All new underground installations after January 1, 2023 must be mapped in a geographic information system and kept as permanent records by the operator.
rules.applies_to: Operators of subsurface installations (and contractors installing for them)
rules.quote: After January 1, 2023, all new subsurface installations must be mapped using a geographic information system and maintained as permanent records of the operator.
rules.notes: This obligation falls on the operator. Contractors installing utilities may be asked to supply as-built GIS data.

rules.title: Report damage to the notification center within 48 hours
rules.plain_english: If you discover or cause damage to an underground facility, notify the regional notification center within 48 hours.

parameters.trigger: discovering or causing damage to subsurface installation

rules.applies_to: Excavators
rules.quote: An excavator must notify the regional notification center within 48 hours of discovering or causing damage.
rules.notes: Separate immediate-notification duties (operator, 911 for gas or hazardous liquid releases) may also apply but are not stated here.
rules.correction: Quote matches PDF p.86. Gov. Code 4216-4216.9 (B&P 7110(f), PDF p.351, only names the article) is not reproduced in the law book (the 2026 edition removed non-B&P code sections, PDF p.10); primary text not visible.

rules.title: Information to give when calling 811
rules.plain_english: When requesting a ticket, give the start date and time, your name and company details, the nature of the work, who it is for, the foreman, the permit name and number, whether the area is white-lined, and a detailed site location.

ticket_fields: whether excavation outlined in white paint
site description: address, side of street, intersection corner, footage and total distances or tie-in measurements, nearest intersecting street, city, county

rules.applies_to: Excavators requesting USA tickets
rules.quote: Give your name, company’s name, company’s mailing address, email address, telephone number where you can be contacted, nature of work (grading, drilling, etc.), whom the work is being done for, name of the foreman, permit name and number, if excavation has been outlined in white paint, and a description of the excavation site.
rules.notes: Good template for a pre-filled 811 request form.

rules.title: USA negligent violation: fine up to $10,000
rules.plain_english: An operator or excavator who negligently violates the 811 law can be fined up to $10,000.
rules.applies_to: Excavators and operators
rules.quote: Any operator or excavator who negligently violates any portion of Government Code sections 4216–4216.9 is subject to a fine not to exceed $10,000.
rules.notes: The penalty provision is believed to be Gov. Code 4216.6 (extractor's note).
rules.correction: Quote matches PDF p.86. Gov. Code 4216-4216.9 (B&P 7110(f), PDF p.351, only names the article) is not reproduced in the law book (the 2026 edition removed non-B&P code sections, PDF p.10); primary text not visible. The $10,000 cap cannot be checked against primary text.

rules.title: USA knowing and willful violation: fine up to $50,000
rules.plain_english: An operator or excavator who knowingly and willfully violates the 811 law can be fined up to $50,000.
rules.applies_to: Excavators and operators
rules.quote: Any operator or excavator who knowingly and willfully violates any portion of Government Code sections 4216–4216.9 is subject to a fine not to exceed $50,000.
rules.correction: Quote matches PDF p.86. Gov. Code 4216-4216.9 (B&P 7110(f), PDF p.351, only names the article) is not reproduced in the law book (the 2026 edition removed non-B&P code sections, PDF p.10); primary text not visible. The $50,000 cap cannot be checked against primary text.

rules.title: Willful violation damaging gas/hazardous liquid pipeline with release: up to $100,000
rules.plain_english: If a knowing and willful violation damages a gas or hazardous liquid pipeline and flammable, toxic or corrosive gas or liquid escapes, the civil penalty can reach $100,000.

conditions: damage to gas or hazardous liquid pipeline subsurface installation
escape of flammable, toxic, or corrosive gas or liquid

rules.applies_to: Excavators and operators
rules.quote: Any operator or excavator who knowingly and willfully violates any of the provisions of this article in a way that results in damage to a gas or hazardous liquid pipeline subsurface installation and that results in the escape of any flammable, toxic, or corrosive gas or liquid is subject to a civil penalty in an amount not to exceed $100,000.
rules.correction: Quote matches PDF p.87. Gov. Code 4216-4216.9 (B&P 7110(f), PDF p.351, only names the article) is not reproduced in the law book (the 2026 edition removed non-B&P code sections, PDF p.10); primary text not visible. The $100,000 cap cannot be checked against primary text.

rules.title: USA violations: third-party damage claims and CSLB discipline
rules.plain_english: Beyond fines, excavators can face third-party damage claims. A willful or deliberate violation of the 811 law is grounds for CSLB discipline, which can include license revocation (B&P 7110(f)).

parameters.civil_exposure: third party claims for damages from excavation work (CSLB narrative; no statute in book)
parameters.license_discipline_mental_state: willful or deliberate disregard and violation of Gov. Code 4216 et seq.

rules.applies_to: Licensed contractors who excavate
rules.source: 2026 CSLB Law Book, PDF page 87 (summary); PDF page 351 (B&P 7110)
rules.quote: An excavator also may be subject to third party claims for damages that arise from the excavation work. ... Violation of Government Code sections 4216–4216.9 could result in disciplinary action and possible revocation of your contractor license by CSLB. | B&P 7110: "Willful or deliberate disregard and violation of ... (f) Any provision of Article 2 (commencing with Section 4216) of Chapter 3.1 of Division 5 of Title 1 of the Government Code ... constitutes a cause for disciplinary action against a licensee."
rules.correction: The license-discipline part checks out against B&P 7110(f), with one gap. The statute makes only a "willful or deliberate disregard and violation" of the Gov. Code 4216 article a cause for disciplinary action. The book's unqualified "Violation ... could result in disciplinary action" leaves out that mental-state condition. Added the condition and the 7110(f) citation. The third-party damage-claim statement is CSLB narrative with no statute in the book, so that part is unverifiable.

rules.title: Which 811 center serves each California county
rules.plain_english: Both centers are reached by dialing 811. USA North (usanorth811.org) serves 49 Northern and Central California counties plus Nevada. DigAlert (digalert.org) serves 9 Southern California counties.
rules.applies_to: Excavators in California
rules.quote: Underground Service Alert of Southern California: 811 www.digalert.org Serves the following counties in Southern California: Imperial, Inyo, Los Angeles, Orange, Riverside, San Bernardino, San Diego, Santa Barbara, and Ventura
rules.notes: 49 + 9 = 58 counties, all of California.

rules.title: Human remains found: stop all work nearby and call the county coroner
rules.plain_english: If human remains or burial artifacts are found anywhere other than a dedicated cemetery, immediately stop all excavation at the site and any nearby area that may contain remains, and contact the county coroner.

parameters.trigger: discovery or recognition of human remains or burial artifacts outside a dedicated cemetery
parameters.timing: immediately
actions: stop all work at site and nearby area reasonably suspected to contain remains

rules.applies_to: Contractors, excavators and property owners on any site
rules.citation: Health & Safety Code 7050.5; Pub. Resources Code 5097.9-5097.991
rules.quote: In the event of discovery or recognition of any human remains in any location other than a dedicated cemetery, there shall be no further excavation or disturbance of the site or nearby area. ... Stop all work immediately at that site and any nearby area reasonably suspected to have remains and contact the county coroner.

rules.title: Coroner: 2 working days to examine; 24 hours to notify NAHC if Native American
rules.plain_english: The coroner has two working days after notification to examine the remains. If they are Native American, the coroner has 24 hours to notify the Native American Heritage Commission. Work stays stopped meanwhile.

parameters.clock_start: coroner notified by person responsible for excavation

rules.applies_to: Projects with discovered human remains (owners and contractors track the work stoppage)
rules.quote: The coroner has two working days to examine the remains after being notified by the person responsible for the excavation. If the remains are Native American, the coroner has 24 hours to notify the Native American Heritage Commission.
rules.notes: These are agency deadlines, useful for estimating the minimum work-stoppage duration.
rules.correction: Quote matches PDF p.88. Health & Safety Code 7050.5 is not reproduced in the law book (the 2026 edition removed non-B&P code sections, PDF p.10); primary text not visible.

rules.title: NAHC notifies most likely descendant; MLD has 24 hours to recommend treatment
rules.plain_english: The NAHC immediately notifies the most likely descendant (MLD), who then has 24 hours to recommend to the owner how to treat and dispose of the remains and grave goods with dignity.
rules.applies_to: Property owners and contractors on sites with Native American remains
rules.quote: The Native American Heritage Commission will immediately notify the person it believes to be the most likely descendant of the deceased Native American. 4. The most likely descendant has 24 hours to make recommendations to the owner or representative for the treatment and disposition, with proper dignity, of the remains and grave goods.
rules.notes: The book says 24 hours. The extractor believes current PRC 5097.98(a) gives descendants 48 hours after being granted site access; verify before hard-coding. The citation section is inferred, since the book cites the range 5097.9-5097.991.
rules.correction: Quote matches PDF p.88. PRC 5097.98 is not reproduced in the law book (the 2026 edition removed non-B&P code sections, PDF p.10); primary text not visible. Caution (not verifiable here; the extractor flagged it too): current PRC 5097.98(a) is believed to give the most likely descendant 48 hours after being granted access to the site, not 24 hours. The book's 24-hour figure may be out of date. Do not hard-code 24 hours.

rules.title: Owner may request NAHC mediation; if it fails, reinter on-site
rules.plain_english: If the owner does not accept the descendant's recommendations, either side may ask the NAHC to mediate. If mediation fails, the landowner must reinter the remains and associated items with dignity, in a spot on the property that will not be disturbed again.

parameters.step_1: owner rejects MLD recommendations -> owner or MLD may request NAHC mediation
parameters.step_2: mediation fails -> landowner reinters remains and burial items with dignity on property
parameters.reinterment_location_requirement: not subject to further subsurface disturbance

rules.applies_to: Property owners (and their contractors)
rules.quote: If the owner doesn’t accept the descendant’s recommendations, the owner or the descendant may request mediation by the Native American Heritage Commission. ... the landowner or their authorized representative shall reinter the human remains and items associated with Native American burials, with appropriate dignity, and in a location on the property not subject to further subsurface disturbance.
rules.notes: This affects site planning: the reinterment area becomes a permanent no-dig zone. Section number inferred from the book's range citation.

rules.title: Removing or possessing Native American remains or grave goods is a felony
rules.plain_english: Knowingly or willfully removing, taking or keeping Native American remains or burial artifacts without legal authority is a felony punishable by state prison.

prohibited_acts: remove
obtain
possess

rules.applies_to: Anyone, including contractors and workers on excavation sites
rules.quote: Any person who knowingly or willfully removes, obtains, or possesses any Native American remains or associated burial artifacts, without authority of law, is guilty of a felony, punishable by imprisonment in state prison.
rules.notes: NAHC contact: (916) 373-3710, nahc@nahc.ca.gov, www.nahc.ca.gov.
rules.correction: Quote matches PDF p.89. PRC 5097.94, 5097.98 and 5097.99 is not reproduced in the law book (the 2026 edition removed non-B&P code sections, PDF p.10); primary text not visible.

rules.title: C-57 Water Well license required to drill, deepen, reperforate, abandon or destroy wells
rules.plain_english: Only a person holding a C-57 Water Well Contractor license may dig, bore, drill, deepen, reperforate, abandon or destroy a water well, cathodic protection well, groundwater monitoring well or geothermal heat exchange well.
rules.applies_to: Anyone performing well construction, alteration, abandonment or destruction
rules.quote: No person shall undertake to dig, bore, or drill a water well, cathodic protection well, groundwater monitoring well, or geothermal heat exchange well, to deepen or reperforate such a well, or to abandon or destroy such a well, unless the person responsible for that construction, alteration, destruction, or abandonment possesses a C-57 Water Well Contractor’s License.
rules.notes: Useful as a license-class check: job type 'well' requires C-57.

rules.title: File Well Completion Report (DWR 188) within 60 days
rules.plain_english: Anyone who builds, alters (drills, deepens, reperforates, abandons) or destroys a water, cathodic protection, monitoring or geothermal heat exchange well must file a Well Completion Report (DWR 188) with DWR within 60 days after finishing. This also applies when converting an oil or gas well to one of those uses.

parameters.form: Well Completion Report, DWR 188 (formerly Water Well Driller's Report; a.k.a. well log/driller's log)
activities: convert oil or gas well to water/cathodic/monitoring well
parameters.filing_system: Online System of Well Completion Reports (OSWCR)

rules.applies_to: C-57 contractors and others constructing, altering, destroying or converting wells
rules.quote: people who construct, alter (including, but not limited to, drilling, deepening, reperforation, or abandonment), or destroy a water well, cathodic protection well, monitoring well, or geothermal heat exchange well, to file a report of completion, called the “Well Completion Report, DWR 188,” with the California Department of Water Resources (DWR) within 60 days after completion of the work.
rules.notes: The quoted sentence begins 'California Water Code sections 13751 through 13754 require...'. File through OSWCR with an account tied to the C-57 license (page 91).
rules.correction: Quote matches PDF p.90 (OSWCR filing details match p.91). Water Code 13751-13754 is not reproduced in the law book (the 2026 edition removed non-B&P code sections, PDF p.10); primary text not visible. The 60-day deadline cannot be checked against primary text.

rules.title: Failure to file Well Completion Report: misdemeanor and license discipline
rules.plain_english: Not filing the Well Completion Report is a misdemeanor (Water Code 13754, per the book). A willful or deliberate violation of the water-well provisions is also grounds for CSLB discipline against your license (B&P 7110(e)).

parameters.violation: failure to file Well Completion Report
parameters.offense_level: misdemeanor (Water Code 13754 per book summary; primary text not in book)
parameters.license_consequence: cause for disciplinary action when the violation is a willful or deliberate disregard and violation of H&S Code or Water Code provisions relating to digging, boring or drilling water wells (B&P 7110(e))

rules.applies_to: Well contractors
rules.citation: Water Code 13754 (misdemeanor, per book); B&P 7110(e) (license discipline)
rules.source: 2026 CSLB Law Book, PDF page 90 (summary); PDF page 351 (B&P 7110)
rules.quote: NOTE: Failure to file the Well Completion Report is a misdemeanor (Water Code §13754) and constitutes cause for disciplinary action against your contractor license (Business and Professions Code section 7110). | B&P 7110: "Willful or deliberate disregard and violation of ... (e) Any provision of the Health and Safety Code or Water Code, relating to the digging, boring, or drilling of water wells ... constitutes a cause for disciplinary action against a licensee."
rules.correction: License-discipline part: B&P 7110(e) makes a "willful or deliberate disregard and violation" of Health & Safety Code or Water Code provisions on digging, boring or drilling water wells a cause for discipline. The book's note that failure to file "constitutes cause for disciplinary action" leaves out that condition. Added the condition and the subdivision cite. 7110(e) names water wells only; whether it reaches cathodic protection, monitoring or geothermal wells is not stated. The misdemeanor classification (Water Code 13754) is not in the book and remains unverifiable.

rules.title: File well reports online via OSWCR with a C-57-based account
rules.plain_english: Drillers file Well Completion Reports through DWR's Online System of Well Completion Reports (OSWCR), using an account tied to their C-57 license that DWR validates.

parameters.system: Online System of Well Completion Reports (OSWCR)

rules.applies_to: C-57 well drillers
rules.quote: Drillers submit their well completion reports to DWR with the Online System of Well Completion Reports (OSWCR). OSWCR users create an account based on their C-57 license that DWR will validate. Upon approval, users will be able to submit Well Completion Reports.
rules.notes: Set up the OSWCR account before the first job so DWR validation does not eat into the 60-day filing window.

rules.title: Follow DWR Bulletin 74 well standards and local well ordinances and permits
rules.plain_english: Well construction, modification, rehabilitation and destruction must follow DWR Bulletin 74 (California Well Standards, Bulletins 74-81 and 74-90) plus any stricter local ordinances. Contact the local enforcing agency (usually county environmental health) before any well work; many require a permit and fee.

state_standards: DWR Bulletin 74-90 California Well Standards (draft supplement)

rules.applies_to: Well contractors (C-57) and owners planning well work
rules.citation: None cited (DWR Bulletin 74; local well ordinances)
rules.quote: The designated local enforcing agency, which is usually the county environmental health department, should be contacted whenever work on a well is being planned to ensure compliance with local ordinances. Many of these local agencies require permits for any work on a well and charge a fee for that permit.
rules.notes: Permit fees vary by county and are not stated.

rules.title: DCA general laws apply to CSLB licensees
rules.plain_english: CSLB is one of the boards inside the Department of Consumer Affairs, so the general DCA rules in B&P Division 1 (address changes, license misuse, citations, cost recovery, lawsuits for pay, settlement terms) apply to contractors on top of the Contractors License Law.
rules.applies_to: All CSLB licensees and registrants
rules.quote: The department is comprised of the following: ... (j) The Contractors State License Board.
rules.notes: Several sections here say they yield where a board's own licensing act has a specific provision (e.g., B&P 125.3(j), 114.3(g), 115.6(j)); check the CSLB-specific rule in Chapter 9 before applying a DCA default.

rules.title: What counts as a conviction for licensing
rules.plain_english: For licensing, a conviction means a guilty plea or verdict, a no-contest plea, or a finding of guilt. The board can act on it once the appeal time has run, it is upheld on appeal, or probation is granted, but it cannot deny a license to an applicant who is otherwise qualified under B&P 480(b) or (c).

board_may_act_when_any_of: order granting probation suspending imposition of sentence

rules.applies_to: License applicants and licensees with criminal convictions
rules.quote: A conviction within the meaning of this code means a judgment following a plea or verdict of guilty or a plea of nolo contendere or finding of guilt. Any action which a board is permitted to take following the establishment of a conviction may be taken when the time for appeal has elapsed, or the judgment of conviction has been affirmed on appeal
rules.notes: The actual denial standards and look-back rules are in B&P 480 (not in this chunk). Do not build a criminal-history eligibility calculator from this section alone.

rules.title: Citations can be issued for regulation violations too
rules.plain_english: Where the code lets the board cite you for breaking a statute, it can also cite you for breaking any regulation adopted under that statute.

citable: violation of regulation adopted under code provision

rules.applies_to: All CSLB licensees
rules.quote: Whenever in any provision of this code authority is granted to issue a citation for a violation of any provision of this code, that authority also includes the authority to issue a citation for the violation of any regulation adopted pursuant to any provision of this code.
rules.notes: CSLB's regulations (California Code of Regulations, Title 16) are therefore citable. A compliance checker should include regulation-level rules, not only statutes.

rules.title: Spouse includes registered domestic partner
rules.plain_english: Wherever the B&P Code says spouse, it also means a registered domestic partner. This matters for the military-spouse licensing rules.
rules.applies_to: Any B&P Code provision using the term spouse
rules.quote: “Spouse” includes “registered domestic partner,” as required by Section 297.5 of the Family Code.

rules.title: Definitions of license and licensee
rules.plain_english: A license is any license, certificate, registration, or other authorization to do a regulated business. A licensee is anyone holding one, so the DCA rules reach CSLB registrations (such as home improvement salesperson registrations) as well as contractor licenses.

license_includes: other means to engage in a regulated business or profession

rules.applies_to: All CSLB licensees and registrants
rules.quote: Unless otherwise expressly provided, “license” means license, certificate, registration, or other means to engage in a business or profession regulated by this code or referred to in Section 1000 or 3600. ... “Licensee” means any person authorized by a license, certificate, registration, or other means to engage in a business or profession regulated by this code
rules.notes: Several sections (119, 121, 125.6, 152.6) also define license broadly to include permit, authority and registration.

rules.title: Prison rehabilitation training cannot bar licensure
rules.plain_english: Someone trained in a trade through an approved prison rehabilitation program cannot be refused the exam or the license just because of the imprisonment, the conviction behind it, or the fact that the training happened in prison, as long as the board finds them fit.

conditions: training in a rehabilitation program approved by the licensing agency and provided by the prison or institution
licensing agency finds the person fit, upon recommendation of the Adult Authority or Department of the Youth Authority

rules.applies_to: Applicants released from state prison or correctional institutions
rules.quote: shall not be denied such license, certificate, or other evidence of proficiency, because of that individual’s imprisonment or the conviction from which the imprisonment resulted, or because the individual obtained the individual’s training in prison ... if the licensing agency ... finds that the individual is a fit person to be licensed.
rules.notes: Relevant for workforce and hiring programs. The fitness finding remains discretionary.

rules.title: License status and enforcement history are public online
rules.plain_english: CSLB must post the status of every license online, including suspensions, revocations, accusations and other enforcement actions, plus information the Labor Commissioner sends it under Labor Code 98.9. Home phone, date of birth and SSN are not posted.

public_online: related enforcement actions including accusations filed under the APA
information provided by the Labor Commissioner under Labor Code 98.9

rules.applies_to: All CSLB licensees and registrants; owners and prime contractors verifying a contractor
rules.quote: The Contractors State License Board shall disclose information on its licensees and registrants in accordance with Chapter 9 (commencing with Section 7000) of Division 3. In addition to information related to licenses as specified in subdivision (a), the board shall also disclose information provided to the board by the Labor Commissioner pursuant to Section 98.9 of the Labor Code.
rules.notes: A tool can pull CSLB's online license lookup before contract signing, before each payment, and before hiring subcontractors, and flag suspensions, revocations, accusations or Labor Commissioner items. Labor Code 98.9 is not in this chunk, so what it covers is not described here.

rules.title: You may use a P.O. box as your public address of record
rules.plain_english: Your address of record is published, but you may give CSLB a P.O. box or another alternate address instead of your home address. CSLB may still require a physical business or home address for internal use only.

parameters.board_may_require_physical_address: for internal administrative use only, not disclosed

rules.applies_to: All CSLB licensees, especially sole owners working from home
rules.quote: Each entity shall disclose a licensee’s address of record. However, each entity shall allow a licensee to provide a post office box number or other alternate address, instead of the licensee’s home address, as the address of record.
rules.notes: Board notices can be served by regular mail to the last known address (B&P 124), so whatever address you use must be one you actually monitor.

rules.title: Updating legal name or gender on a license
rules.plain_english: If you legally change your name or gender and give the board the required government documents, the board must update your license and its online lookup on request (your former name is not published) and reissue the license for no more than its normal reissue fee. Records of the request are confidential.

name_change_documents_any_of: certified court order under CCP 1277(b) plus copy of Secretary of State Safe at Home certificate
certified court order under CCP 1277.5 or Health and Safety Code 103425 et seq.
gender_change_documents_any_of: state-issued driver’s license or ID card
court order indicating gender change (California, another state, DC, US territory, or foreign court)
parameters.reissue_fee_cap: not higher than the fee regularly charged for reissuing with other updated information

rules.applies_to: Individual licensees and registrants
rules.quote: the board, upon request by the licensee or registrant, shall update the individual’s license or registration by replacing references to the former name or gender on the license or registration, as applicable, with references to the current name or gender.
rules.notes: Prior enforcement records under a former name are replaced online by a statement telling the public to contact the board (27.5(a)(2)(B)). After a name change, remember to update the name on contracts, ads and insurance.

rules.title: Child support compliance for issuance and renewal
rules.plain_english: License applicants and renewing licensees must comply with Family Code 17520. If you are not complying with a support judgment or order, your license issuance or renewal is subject to that law.

parameters.trigger: applicant or licensee not in compliance with a judgment or order for support

rules.applies_to: All CSLB applicants and renewing licensees
rules.quote: applicants for licensure and licensees renewing their licenses shall also comply with Section 17520 of the Family Code. ... Each applicant for the issuance or renewal of a license, certificate, registration, or other means to engage in a business or profession regulated by a board who is not in compliance with a judgment or order for support shall be subject to Section 17520 of the Family Code.
rules.notes: The consequences under Family Code 17520 (such as license withholding or suspension) are in the Law Book Appendix, not in this chunk.

rules.title: FEIN, SSN or ITIN required to process a license application
rules.plain_english: When applying, a partnership must give its federal employer identification number, an individual must give an SSN or ITIN, and other applicants an SSN. CSLB will not process an initial application without the number where the application asks for it. These numbers are not public records.

parameters.individual: social security number or individual taxpayer identification number

rules.applies_to: All CSLB license applicants
rules.quote: (c) In addition to the penalty specified in subdivision (b), a licensing board shall not process an application for an initial license unless the applicant provides its federal employer identification number, or individual taxpayer identification number or social security number where requested on the application.
rules.notes: An application checklist generator should require the right ID type for each business form. The board shares this data with FTB and EDD on request (30(d)).

rules.title: Failing to provide a tax ID is reported to the FTB
rules.plain_english: A licensee who does not provide the required FEIN, ITIN or SSN is reported to the Franchise Tax Board. If the number still is not provided after the FTB's notice, the licensee faces the penalty in Revenue and Taxation Code 19528(b)(2).

parameters.trigger: failure to provide FEIN/ITIN/SSN, continuing after notification under R&TC 19528(b)(1)

rules.applies_to: All CSLB licensees
rules.quote: A licensee failing to provide the federal employer identification number, or the individual taxpayer identification number or social security number shall be reported by the licensing board to the Franchise Tax Board. If the licensee fails to provide that information after notification ... the licensee shall be subject to the penalty
rules.notes: The penalty amount is set in R&TC 19528 and is not stated in this source. Do not assume a figure.

rules.title: Entity licensees must give the SSN or ITIN of every listed person and qualifier
rules.plain_english: When an entity's license is issued, the entity must provide the SSN or ITIN of every individual listed on the license and of anyone who qualifies the license.

ids_required_for: each individual listed on the license
any person who qualifies for the license
parameters.when: at time of issuance of the license

rules.applies_to: Corporations, LLCs, partnerships and other entity contractor licenses
rules.quote: a board, as defined in Section 22, the State Bar of California, and the Department of Real Estate shall at the time of issuance of the license require that each licensee provide the individual taxpayer identification number or social security number of each individual listed on the license and any person who qualifies for the license.
rules.notes: In CSLB practice, listed individuals typically include officers, members, partners and the qualifying individual (RMO/RME). That mapping is an interpretation and is not stated in this section.

rules.title: No license denial based on citizenship or immigration status
rules.plain_english: CSLB cannot require you to disclose your citizenship or immigration status and cannot deny a license because of it. An individual may give an ITIN instead of an SSN.

parameters.exception_reference: B&P 7583.23(e) (private security services law, not the Contractors License Law)

rules.applies_to: All CSLB license applicants
rules.quote: (B) In implementing the requirements of subparagraph (A), a licensing board shall not require an individual to disclose either citizenship status or immigration status for purposes of licensure. (C) A licensing board shall not deny licensure to an otherwise qualified and eligible individual based solely on the individual’s citizenship status or immigration status.
rules.notes: An application tool should not make citizenship or immigration status a required field.

rules.title: Top-500 state tax delinquents face license suspension
rules.plain_english: If you are on the state's list of the 500 largest tax delinquencies, your license is subject to suspension under B&P 494.5. License applications must state that CDTFA and the FTB can share taxpayer information with the board and that a license may be suspended for unpaid state tax.

parameters.trigger: name appears on list of 500 largest tax delinquencies under R&TC 7063 or 19195
info_sharing_agencies: California Department of Tax and Fee Administration

rules.applies_to: All CSLB licensees and applicants
rules.quote: (d) Each licensee or applicant whose name appears on a list of the 500 largest tax delinquencies pursuant to Section 7063 or 19195 of the Revenue and Taxation Code shall be subject to Section 494.5. ... the licensee’s license may be suspended if the state tax obligation is not paid.
rules.notes: R&TC Part 1 covers sales and use tax, Part 10 personal income tax and Part 11 corporation tax. Those labels are general knowledge and are not stated in the source. The B&P 494.5 procedure is not in this chunk.

rules.title: Military training and experience can count toward licensure
rules.plain_english: Board rules must provide a way to evaluate education, training and experience from the U.S. armed services and say how it can count toward license requirements. Every license application must ask whether the applicant is serving or has served in the military.

creditable: experience obtained in the armed services
parameters.application_question_required: is applicant serving in, or has previously served in, the military

rules.applies_to: Contractor license applicants with military service
rules.quote: rules and regulations of boards provided for in this code shall provide for methods of evaluating education, training, and experience obtained in the armed services, if applicable to the requirements of the business, occupation, or profession regulated.
rules.notes: CSLB's own rules for crediting experience toward the 4-year experience requirement are in Chapter 9 and its regulations, not in this chunk.

rules.title: Witness fee at board hearings: $12 per day plus expenses
rules.plain_english: A witness who appears at the board's request in a board investigation, proceeding or hearing may be paid $12 per day of attendance plus actual, necessary and reasonable expenses. Witnesses appearing for another party are not paid from the board's fund.
rules.applies_to: Homeowners, contractors or others testifying in CSLB proceedings
rules.quote: any witness appearing at the investigation, proceeding, or hearing whether upon a subpoena or voluntarily, may be paid the sum of twelve dollars ($12) per day for every day in actual attendance at the investigation, proceeding, or hearing and for the witness’s actual, necessary, and reasonable expenses
rules.notes: The statute says may be paid, so payment is discretionary.

rules.title: Reinstating a license that expired during active military duty
rules.plain_english: If your license expired while you were on active duty in the U.S. Armed Forces or California National Guard, you can reinstate it without an exam or penalty. The license must have been valid when you entered service, you must apply while serving or within 1 year of discharge, and you must file an affidavit of your service dates and pay the current renewal fee.

parameters.window: while serving, or not later than 1 year from discharge from active service or return to inactive military status
parameters.window_trigger: date of discharge from active service or return to inactive status
required_documents: affidavit showing date of entrance into service, whether still serving, or date of discharge
renewal fee for the current renewal period
exam_may_be_required_if: filed more than 1 year after discharge or return to inactive status
board finds applicant did not actively practice the profession while on active duty
parameters.excluded_from_1_year_period: time in treatment or hospitalization in a veterans’ facility that prevented practice

rules.applies_to: Licensees whose licenses expired during active military service
rules.quote: may, upon application, reinstate their license or registration without examination or penalty, provided that ... (2) The application for reinstatement is made while serving in the California National Guard or the United States Armed Forces, or not later than one year from the date of discharge from active service or return to inactive military status.
rules.notes: A deadline calculator should compute discharge date + 1 year, extended by any documented veterans' facility treatment time.

rules.title: Keep your license current if you work in California while in the military
rules.plain_english: If you do licensed work in California, part time or full time, while in military service, you must keep your license in good standing.

parameters.trigger: practicing the licensed vocation in California part time or full time while in military service

rules.applies_to: Licensees in military service who continue contracting in California
rules.quote: any licensee or registrant who, either part time or full time, practices in this state the profession or vocation for which the licensee or registrant is licensed or registered shall be required to maintain their license in good standing even though the licensee or registrant is in military service.
rules.notes: Applies unless the code specifically provides otherwise.

rules.title: Renewal fee and requirement waiver while on active duty
rules.plain_english: If you are called to active duty, the board waives renewal fees, continuing education and other renewal requirements for the active-duty period. Your license must have been current when you were called up, and you must give written proof of service. While the waiver is in effect you may not do licensed work, except under a military active status with no private practice.

conditions: current and valid license when called to active duty
written documentation substantiating active duty service
waived: other renewal requirements as determined by the board
parameters.exception: license converted to military active status if providing services while on active duty; no private practice of any type
parameters.active_duty_definition: 10 USC 101 plus California National Guard active duty under Mil. & Vet. Code 143 or 146

rules.applies_to: Licensees called to active duty in the U.S. Armed Forces or California National Guard
rules.quote: every board ... within the department shall waive the renewal fees, continuing education requirements, and other renewal requirements as determined by the board, if any are applicable, for a licensee or registrant called to active duty ... the licensee or registrant shall not engage in any activities requiring a license during the period that the waivers provided by this section are in effect.
rules.notes: Under 114.3(g) this section does not apply to a board that has its own statutory renewal waiver process. Verify whether CSLB has one in Chapter 9.

rules.title: After discharge: notify within 60 days, renew within 6 months
rules.plain_english: After you get notice of your discharge date, tell the board within 60 days. Before doing licensed work again, meet all renewal requirements within 6 months of your discharge date.

parameters.notify_trigger: receipt of notice of discharge date
parameters.renewal_trigger: date of discharge from active duty service

rules.applies_to: Licensees who used the B&P 114.3 active-duty waiver
rules.quote: shall meet all necessary renewal requirements as determined by the board within six months from the licensee’s or registrant’s date of discharge from active duty service. ... shall notify the board of their discharge from active duty within 60 days of receiving their notice of discharge.
rules.notes: Two calculable deadlines: notice receipt + 60 days, and discharge date + 6 months. B&P 114.3(g): the section does not apply to a board with a similar statutory renewal-waiver process. CSLB B&P 7071.3 (designating a responsible managing person while in the armed forces, renewal fee still paid) is not such a waiver.

rules.title: Expedited initial licensure for veterans and SkillBridge members
rules.plain_english: CSLB must expedite initial licensing for applicants who show they were honorably discharged after active duty in the U.S. Armed Forces, and since July 1, 2024 for active-duty members enrolled in the DoD SkillBridge program. This applies only to individual licenses, not business or entity licenses.

eligible_groups.group: honorably discharged former active duty members of the U.S. Armed Forces
active duty members of a regular component enrolled in DoD SkillBridge (10 USC 1143(e))

parameters.required_evidence: satisfactory evidence of service and honorable discharge, or SkillBridge enrollment
parameters.license_scope: individual license only; not business or entity licenses

rules.applies_to: Veteran and SkillBridge applicants for an individual license
rules.quote: on and after July 1, 2016, a board within the department shall expedite, and may assist, the initial licensure process for an applicant who supplies satisfactory evidence to the board that the applicant has served as an active duty member of the Armed Forces of the United States and was honorably discharged.
rules.effective: July 1, 2016; SkillBridge from July 1, 2024 (amended effective September 22, 2024)
rules.notes: The section states no fee waiver. How 'individual license' maps to CSLB sole-owner versus entity licenses is not stated, so verify with CSLB.

rules.title: Military spouses: expedited license with application and initial fees waived
rules.plain_english: CSLB must expedite licensing and waive both the application fee and the initial license fee for an applicant who is married to (or a domestic partner of) an active-duty service member stationed in California under orders, and who holds a current license for the same trade in another state or U.S. territory.

parameters.waived_fee_usd: full amount of the listed fees
conditions: married to, domestic partner of, or in another legal union with an active duty U.S. Armed Forces member assigned to a California duty station under official orders
holds a current license in another U.S. state, district, or territory in the same profession or vocation
parameters.license_scope: individual license only; not business or entity licenses

rules.applies_to: Military-spouse applicants for an individual contractor license
rules.quote: A board within the department shall expedite the licensure process and waive the licensure application fee and the initial or original license fee charged by the board for an applicant who meets both of the following requirements:
rules.effective: Operative July 1, 2021 version as amended effective September 22, 2024
rules.notes: A fee calculator should set the application and initial license fees to $0 for qualifying applicants. Renewal fees are not waived by this section.

rules.title: Temporary license for military spouses: issued in 30 days, valid 12 months, no fee
rules.plain_english: A spouse or domestic partner of an active-duty member stationed in California who holds an active, unrestricted out-of-state license with the same scope can get a free, nonrenewable temporary license. The board must issue it within 30 days of complete documents if the background check is clean, and it expires after 12 months or when a regular license is issued or denied, whichever comes first.

parameters.issue_trigger: receipt of documentation meeting 115.6(c) and (d), with criminal background check showing no grounds for denial
expires_at_earliest_of: issuance or denial of standard license
issuance or denial of license by endorsement
issuance or denial of expedited license under 115.5
required_documents: evidence of marriage, domestic partnership or legal union with an active duty member assigned to a California duty station under official orders
current, active, unrestricted out-of-state license within the same scope
application with signed affidavit of eligibility and accuracy
written verification of good standing from original licensing jurisdiction
full set of fingerprints on request
disqualifiers: act in any jurisdiction that would be grounds for denial, suspension or revocation
discipline by a licensing entity in another jurisdiction
unresolved complaint, review procedure or disciplinary proceeding in another jurisdiction
parameters.exam_required: California law and ethics exam only if otherwise required by the board
parameters.termination: may be terminated immediately for failing requirements or inaccurate information; holder must cease practice immediately on receipt of notice
parameters.license_scope: individual license only; not business or entity licenses

rules.applies_to: Military-spouse applicants holding an out-of-state contractor license
rules.quote: a board shall issue a temporary license pursuant to this section within 30 days of receiving documentation that the applicant has met the requirements ... A temporary license issued pursuant to this section is nonrenewable and shall expire 12 months after issuance
rules.notes: Under 115.6(j) this section does not apply to a board that already has an expedited temporary authorization (at least 1 year) or endorsement process. Verify CSLB's status.

rules.title: Registration for servicemembers and spouses relocated on military orders
rules.plain_english: A servicemember or spouse who moved to California on military orders and holds a good-standing out-of-state license for similar work can register with the board for free, if they performed at least one licensed activity in the 2 years before relocating. The board must register them within 30 days of complete documents, and the registration ends when the orders expire.

parameters.register_trigger: receipt of all applicable documentation under 115.10(b)
required_documents: copy of military orders for service in California
written verification or online printout of good standing from original licensing jurisdiction
good-standing verification for each jurisdiction if licensed in more than one
evidence of marriage, domestic partnership or legal union (spouse applicants)
publicly_posted: state name and license number of each original license
parameters.license_scope: individual professional license only; not business or entity licenses

rules.applies_to: Servicemembers and spouses relocated to California under military orders
rules.quote: (3) The applicant performed at least one activity within the scope and under the authority of their professional license during the two years immediately preceding the relocation to this state. ...
