CSLB must file its action within 10 years after the act or within 18 months after the complaint, whichever is later. Latent means not apparent by reasonable inspection.

parameters.action_deadline_rule: later of (act + 10 years) or (complaint filing date + 18 months)
parameters.defect_type: latent structural defect, as defined by regulation
parameters.latent_definition: act or omission not apparent by reasonable inspection

rules.applies_to: Owners/complainants and licensed contractors
rules.quote: A complaint against a licensee alleging commission of any latent acts or omissions that may be grounds for legal action pursuant to subdivision (a) of Section 7109 regarding structural defects, as defined by regulation, shall be filed in writing with the registrar within 10 years after the act or omission alleged as the ground for the disciplinary action.
rules.notes: Structural defect definition is in CSLB regulations (not on these pages).

rules.title: License fraud and criminal conviction actions: 2 years from discovery
rules.plain_english: CSLB must file discipline for application misrepresentation (B&P 7112) within 2 years after CSLB discovers the facts, and for a criminal conviction (B&P 7123) within 2 years after CSLB discovers the conviction.

parameters.start_event: discovery by the registrar or board

rules.applies_to: Licensed contractors
rules.quote: A disciplinary action alleging a violation of Section 7112 shall be filed within two years after the discovery by the registrar or by the board of the alleged facts constituting the fraud or misrepresentation prohibited by the section.

rules.title: Breach of written warranty: CSLB action up to 18 months after warranty expires
rules.plain_english: CSLB can discipline a contractor for breaching an express written warranty the contractor issued, as long as the action is filed no later than 18 months after the warranty expires.

parameters.start_event: expiration of the express written warranty
parameters.warranty_type: express, written, issued by the contractor

rules.applies_to: Licensed contractors who issue written warranties; owners holding them
rules.quote: A disciplinary action regarding an alleged breach of an express, written warranty issued by the contractor shall be filed not later than 18 months from the expiration of the warranty.
rules.notes: A warranty tracker can compute CSLB exposure end date = warranty expiration + 18 months.

rules.title: What a CSLB disciplinary decision can order
rules.plain_english: A CSLB decision can immediately suspend all contracting operations for a set period, allow the contractor to finish specific uncompleted contracts, impose specific conditions (and refuse license restoration until met), or stay the decision during probation.

options: immediate complete suspension of all operations for fixed period
permit completion of uncompleted contracts shown at hearing
specific terms and conditions; no restoration application accepted until met
stay of execution pending probation terms

rules.applies_to: Licensed contractors subject to accusation/discipline
rules.quote: Provide for the immediate complete suspension by the licensee of all operations as a contractor during the period fixed by the decision. (2) Permit the licensee to complete any or all contracts shown by competent evidence taken at the hearing to be then uncompleted.
rules.notes: Owners with active projects should verify whether a suspended contractor was permitted to complete their contract.

rules.title: Probation violation can end a stayed suspension/revocation without notice
rules.plain_english: If a disciplinary decision is stayed on probation, failing to fully meet the probation terms may automatically terminate the stay without further notice, and the decision then counts as a disciplinary action.

parameters.trigger: failure to fully comply with probation terms
parameters.result: automatic termination of stay of execution

rules.applies_to: Licensed contractors on CSLB probation
rules.quote: Failure to fully comply with the terms and conditions of probation set pursuant to subparagraph (A) may result in automatic termination of the stay of execution without further notice.

rules.title: Discipline conditions: restitution, enforcement costs, coursework, exams
rules.plain_english: Conditions in a CSLB disciplinary decision or probation can include paying restitution to injured people, paying CSLB's investigation and enforcement costs (B&P 125.3), completing administrative or trade coursework, passing the law and business or trade exam, and other terms in CSLB disciplinary guidelines (16 CCR 871).

possible_conditions: law and business examination or trade examination

rules.applies_to: Licensed contractors subject to discipline/probation
rules.quote: Payment of restitution to persons injured as a result of the violation. (2) Payment of the costs of investigation and enforcement pursuant to Section 125.3. (3) Enrollment in, and completion of, specified administrative or trade-specific coursework.
rules.notes: Amended by SB 630 (Stats 2023 ch 153).

rules.title: Licensee includes the entity and its qualifying individuals
rules.plain_english: For CSLB discipline, a licensee is not just the business (individual, partnership, corporation, LLC, joint venture) but also its named RMO, RMM, responsible managing member, or other personnel whose qualifications got the license issued.
rules.applies_to: All licensed contracting businesses and their qualifiers
rules.quote: shall also include any named responsible managing officer, responsible managing manager, responsible managing member, or personnel of that licentiate whose appearance has qualified the licentiate under the provisions of Section 7068.

rules.title: One license suspended: other licenses can be suspended without notice
rules.plain_english: When a license is suspended by CSLB decision, for a judgment/bond issue under B&P 7071.17(b), for ignoring an arbitration award (7085.6), or for ignoring a citation (7090.1), any other license in the licensee's name or that the person qualified can be suspended without further notice.

affected_licenses: licenses for which licensee furnished qualifying experience/appearance under B&P 7068

rules.applies_to: Licensees and qualifiers holding or qualifying multiple licenses
rules.quote: any additional license issued under this chapter in the name of the licensee or for which the licensee furnished qualifying experience and appearance under the provisions of Section 7068, may be suspended by the registrar without further notice.
rules.notes: A subcontractor-vetting tool should check related licenses that share a qualifier.

rules.title: One license revoked: other licenses can be revoked without notice
rules.plain_english: When any license is revoked, any other license in the licensee's name or that the licensee qualified can be revoked without further notice.

affected_licenses: licenses qualified by licensee under B&P 7068

rules.applies_to: Licensees and qualifiers holding or qualifying multiple licenses
rules.quote: when any license has been revoked under the provisions of this chapter, any additional license issued under this chapter in the name of the licensee or for which the licensee furnished qualifying experience and appearance under the provisions of Section 7068, may be revoked by the registrar without further notice.

rules.title: What a CSLB citation contains
rules.plain_english: Instead of formal discipline, CSLB can issue a written citation that describes the violation and the law violated. It may include an order to correct within a reasonable time, an order (licensees only) to pay a specified sum to the injured party instead of correcting, and a civil penalty.

parameters.form: in writing, describing violation with particularity and citing provisions violated
possible_orders: order of correction with reasonable time to correct
order to pay specified sum to injured party in lieu of correction (licensee only)

rules.applies_to: Licensed contractors and license applicants
rules.quote: In addition, each citation may contain an order of correction fixing a reasonable time for correction of the violation or an order, against the licensee only, for payment of a specified sum to an injured party in lieu of correction, and may contain an assessment of a civil penalty.

rules.title: Citation civil penalty caps before July 1, 2026
rules.plain_english: For citations under the version in effect until July 1, 2026, the civil penalty could not exceed $8,000, except up to $30,000 for violating B&P 7110 (willful violation of building/labor/safety laws), 7114 (aiding unlicensed persons) or 7118 (contracting with an unlicensed contractor). No minimum was set.
rules.applies_to: Licensees/applicants cited for violations under the pre-July 2026 version
rules.quote: a civil penalty shall not be assessed in an amount greater than eight thousand dollars ($8,000). Notwithstanding Section 125.9, a civil penalty not to exceed thirty thousand dollars ($30,000) may be assessed for a violation of Section 7110, 7114, or 7118.
rules.notes: Superseded by the July 1, 2026 version with minimums. Stats 2025 ch 455 (SB 291) prevails over ch 233.

rules.title: Citation civil penalty ranges from July 1, 2026: $500-$8,000; $1,500-$30,000
rules.plain_english: Starting July 1, 2026, a CSLB citation civil penalty must be at least $500 and no more than $8,000. For violations of B&P 7110, 7114 or 7118 (willful violation of building/labor/safety laws, aiding unlicensed persons, contracting with unlicensed contractors), it must be at least $1,500 and no more than $30,000.
rules.applies_to: Licensees and applicants cited by CSLB
rules.quote: a civil penalty shall be assessed in an amount not less than five hundred dollars ($500) nor greater than eight thousand dollars ($8,000). Notwithstanding Section 125.9, a civil penalty shall be assessed in an amount not less than one thousand five hundred dollars ($1,500) nor greater than thirty thousand dollars ($30,000) for a violation of Section 7110, 7114, or 7118.
rules.effective: Effective January 1, 2026; operative July 1, 2026 (Stats 2025 ch 455 § 2.2, SB 291, which prevails over Stats 2025 ch 233 § 4, SB 779)
rules.notes: Unlicensed-contractor citations are governed separately (B&P 7028.7 et seq., earlier pages). Some sections (e.g., 7125.4 workers' comp) set their own minimums. Penalties cannot be paid from the contractor's license bond (7099.7).
rules.correction: Amounts ($500-$8,000 general; $1,500-$30,000 for 7110/7114/7118), factors and quote confirmed. "effective" said "July 1, 2026"; the book says effective January 1, 2026, operative July 1, 2026 (Stats 2025 ch 455 § 2.2 prevails). Fixed.

rules.title: Minimum civil penalties may be CPI-adjusted every 5 years
rules.plain_english: CSLB may raise the minimum citation penalties for inflation every 5 years based on the California CPI increase since the subdivision took effect. Increases are rounded to multiples of $100 for penalties over $100 up to $1,000, and to multiples of $1,000 for penalties over $1,000.

parameters.index: Consumer Price Index per Revenue and Taxation Code 2212
parameters.base_period: CPI "at the time this subdivision goes into effect" (statutory wording). The section is effective January 1, 2026 but operative July 1, 2026; the statute does not say which date is the base. July 1, 2026 is an interpretation.

rules.applies_to: Licensees and applicants cited by CSLB
rules.quote: The board may adjust all minimum civil penalties imposed by this section for inflation every five years. The adjustment shall be equivalent to the percentage, if any, that the Consumer Price Index, as determined pursuant to Section 2212 of the Revenue and Taxation Code, exceeds the Consumer Price Index at the time this subdivision goes into effect.
rules.effective: Effective January 1, 2026; operative July 1, 2026 (Stats 2025 ch 455 § 2.2, SB 291, which prevails)
rules.notes: Earliest possible adjustment would be about 2031; check CSLB for current minimums before calculating. Base date for the CPI comparison is ambiguous (effective Jan 1, 2026 vs operative July 1, 2026); confirm with CSLB before computing adjusted minimums.
rules.correction: 5-year interval, CPI index (R&T 2212), minimums-only scope, discretionary "may", and rounding tiers ($100 multiples for >$100 to <=$1,000; $1,000 multiples for >$1,000) confirmed. "effective" said "July 1, 2026"; the book says effective January 1, 2026, operative July 1, 2026. base_period stated July 1, 2026 as fact; the text only says "at the time this subdivision goes into effect", which is ambiguous here. Flagged as an interpretation.

rules.title: Contest a CSLB citation within 15 days of service (B&P 7099.8(a); 7099.3 says 15 working days)
rules.plain_english: B&P 7099.3 lets a cited licensee or applicant appeal to the Registrar within 15 working days from service of the citation, challenging the alleged violations, correction periods, penalty amounts, or reasonableness of the required correction, and 7099.5 requires an APA hearing if the citation is contested. But B&P 7099.8(a), which applies "notwithstanding any other law" to citations under 7099, requires a written request for an administrative hearing within 15 days after service, and it does not say working days. Treat 15 calendar days from service as the deadline.

parameters.day_type: calendar days (safe reading; B&P 7099.8(a) says "within 15 days" and applies "notwithstanding any other law")
parameters.start_event: service of the citation
appealable_items: reasonableness of change required to correct
parameters.hearing: APA hearing (Gov Code 11500 et seq.) under B&P 7099.5; decision affirms, modifies, or vacates

overriding_rule_b_p_7099_8.text_controls: B&P 7099.8(a) applies "notwithstanding any other law" to citations under 7099
overriding_rule_b_p_7099_8.informal_conference_alternative: written request to chief of enforcement division within 15 days after service (7099.8(b))

parameters.safe_deadline: 15 calendar days after service of the citation

rules.applies_to: Licensed contractors and applicants served with a citation
rules.quote: Any licensee or applicant for licensure served with a citation pursuant to Section 7099, may appeal to the registrar within 15 working days from service of the citation with respect to violations alleged by the registrar, correction periods, amount of penalties, and the reasonableness of the change required by the registrar to correct the condition.
rules.notes: Do not compute this deadline in working days. 7099.8 (added 2019, amended 2020) is later and says "notwithstanding any other law"; 15 calendar days after service is the safe date.
rules.correction: The 7099.3 quote ("15 working days") is accurate, but the title and parameters treated 15 working days as the deadline. B&P 7099.8(a) (PDF page 342): "Notwithstanding any other law, if a person cited pursuant to Section 7028.7 or 7099 wishes to contest the citation, that person shall, within 15 days after service of the citation, file in writing a request for an administrative hearing". It does not say working days. Set day_type to calendar (safe reading), kept the 7099.3 working-day figure as b_p_7099_3_text_working_days, added the 7099.8 override, retitled the rule and rewrote the plain_english and notes. Same correction as the prior verified chunk made for 7028.10.

rules.title: Uncontested citation becomes final and unreviewable
rules.plain_english: Under B&P 7099.4, if the cited person does not notify CSLB within 15 working days of service that they intend to contest, the citation becomes a final order of the Registrar and cannot be reviewed by any court or agency; the Registrar may extend the 15-day period for cause. But B&P 7099.8(a) ("notwithstanding any other law") requires the written hearing request within 15 days after service, so do not rely on the working-day count: file within 15 calendar days.

parameters.start_event: service of the citation
parameters.result_if_missed: final order of registrar; not subject to review by any court or agency
parameters.safe_deadline: 15 calendar days after service of the citation (B&P 7099.8(a))

rules.applies_to: Licensed contractors and applicants served with a citation
rules.quote: If within 15 working days from service of the citation issued by the registrar, the licensee or applicant for licensure fails to notify the registrar that he or she intends to contest the citation, the citation shall be deemed a final order of the registrar and not be subject to review by any court or agency.
rules.notes: Once final, non-compliance triggers automatic suspension (7090.1) and is grounds for suspension/revocation (7099.6). B&P 7099.8(a) (PDF page 342) sets a 15-day (not working-day) deadline for a written hearing request "notwithstanding any other law"; the safe contest date is 15 calendar days after service.
rules.correction: 7099.4 quote, 15 working days, extension for cause and finality effect confirmed. The rule omitted B&P 7099.8(a), which applies "notwithstanding any other law" and requires a written hearing request within 15 days (not working days) after service. Relying on 15 working days could miss that deadline. Added the 7099.8(a) safe deadline to parameters, plain_english and notes.

rules.title: Ignoring a final citation: grounds for suspension, revocation, or denial
rules.plain_english: A licensee who fails to comply with a final citation can have the license suspended or revoked; an applicant who fails to comply can be denied a license.

parameters.condition: citation is final

rules.applies_to: Licensed contractors and applicants
rules.quote: The failure of a licensee to comply with a citation after it is final is a ground for suspension or revocation of license.

rules.title: Civil penalties cannot be charged against the contractor's bond
rules.plain_english: CSLB cannot order a civil penalty to be paid from the contractor's license bond (B&P 7071.5-7071.8); the contractor pays it directly.
rules.applies_to: Licensed contractors and their sureties
rules.quote: No order for payment of a civil penalty shall be made against any bond required pursuant to Sections 7071.5 to 7071.8.

rules.title: File written request for administrative hearing within 15 days of citation
rules.plain_english: Anyone cited by CSLB, licensed (B&P 7099) or unlicensed (B&P 7028.7), who wants to contest must file a written request for an administrative hearing within 15 days after service of the citation.

parameters.start_event: service of the citation

rules.applies_to: Licensed contractors, applicants and unlicensed persons cited by CSLB
rules.quote: if a person cited pursuant to Section 7028.7 or 7099 wishes to contest the citation, that person shall, within 15 days after service of the citation, file in writing a request for an administrative hearing as provided pursuant to Section 7028.12 or 7099.5.
rules.notes: Overlaps the 15 working-day periods in 7099.3/7099.4; calendar the shorter (15 calendar days) to be safe.

rules.title: Informal citation conference: request within 15 days; held within 60
rules.plain_english: Instead of or in addition to a hearing request, a cited person may ask in writing for an informal citation conference with the CSLB enforcement chief within 15 days after service. CSLB must hold it within 60 days of the request; the person may bring an attorney or representative. If held, the hearing request is deemed withdrawn, and any affirmed or modified citation (with reasons) is mailed within 10 days after the conference.

parameters.request_to: chief of the enforcement division or designee
parameters.representation: attorney or other authorized representative allowed

rules.applies_to: Licensed contractors, applicants and unlicensed persons cited by CSLB
rules.quote: Upon receipt of a written request for an informal citation conference, the chief of the enforcement division or a designee shall, within 60 days of the request, hold an informal citation conference with the person requesting the conference. The cited person may be accompanied and represented by an attorney or other authorized representative.

rules.title: Contest an affirmed/modified citation within 30 days
rules.plain_english: After an informal conference, if you still want to contest the affirmed or modified citation, you must submit a written request for an administrative hearing to the enforcement chief within 30 days after service of that citation. No second informal conference is allowed.

parameters.start_event: service of the modified or affirmed citation

rules.applies_to: Persons whose citation was affirmed or modified after an informal conference
rules.quote: If a cited person wishes to contest a citation affirmed or modified pursuant to paragraph (3), the person shall, within 30 days after service of the modified or affirmed citation, contest the affirmed or modified citation by submitting a written request for an administrative hearing to the chief of the enforcement division or a designee.

rules.title: Letter of admonishment: respond within 30 days
rules.plain_english: CSLB may issue a letter of admonishment instead of a citation. Within 30 days of service you may either request an office conference in writing to contest it, or comply (and submit a written corrective action plan if required). Complying without requesting a conference is not an admission of the violation.

parameters.start_event: service of the letter of admonishment
options: written request for office conference to contest
comply and, if required, submit written corrective action plan

rules.applies_to: Licensees, HIS registrants and applicants receiving a letter of admonishment
rules.quote: The letter of admonishment shall inform the licensee, registrant, or applicant that within 30 days of service of the letter of admonishment the licensee, registrant, or applicant may do either of the following:
rules.notes: Service by certified mail is effective on deposit in the mail (7099.9(c)), so the 30 days run from mailing.

rules.title: LOA office conference: decision in 14 days; writ within 30 days
rules.plain_english: At the office conference only your attorney or authorized representative may accompany you, and you may submit declarations and documents. CSLB may affirm, modify or withdraw the letter and must serve its written decision within 14 calendar days; that is the final administrative decision. Court review is by writ of mandate (CCP 1094.5) filed within 30 days after the decision is served or mailed.

parameters.who_may_accompany: legal counsel or authorized representative only
parameters.documents: declarations and documents may be submitted prior to or at conference
parameters.decision_service: personal service or certified mail to address of record
parameters.writ_start_event: date decision personally served or sent by certified mail
parameters.writ_procedure: petition for writ of mandate, CCP 1094.5

rules.applies_to: Licensees, HIS registrants and applicants contesting a letter of admonishment
rules.quote: Within 14 calendar days from the date of the office conference, the registrar, or their designee, shall personally serve or send the written decision by certified mail to the licensee’s, registrant’s, or applicant’s address of record. This decision shall be deemed the final administrative decision concerning the letter of admonishment.

rules.title: LOA served by certified mail is effective when mailed
rules.plain_english: A letter of admonishment is served personally or by certified mail to your CSLB address of record, and certified-mail service is effective the day it is deposited in the U.S. mail, not when you receive it.

service_methods: certified mail to address of record
parameters.certified_mail_effective: upon deposit in United States mail

rules.applies_to: Licensees, HIS registrants and applicants
rules.quote: The letter of admonishment shall be served upon the licensee, registrant, or applicant personally or by certified mail at their address of record with the board. If the licensee, registrant, or applicant is served by certified mail, service shall be effective upon deposit in the United States mail.
rules.notes: Keep the CSLB address of record current; deadlines run from mailing.

rules.title: Keep the letter of admonishment and corrective plan for 1 year
rules.plain_english: You must keep a copy of the letter of admonishment and any corrective action plan readily available for at least 1 year from the date the letter was issued.

parameters.start_event: date of issuance of the letter

rules.applies_to: Licensees, HIS registrants and applicants issued a letter of admonishment
rules.quote: The licensee, registrant, or applicant shall maintain and have readily available a copy of the letter of admonishment and corrective action plan, if any, for at least one year from the date of issuance of the letter of admonishment.

rules.title: A letter of admonishment is not discipline
rules.plain_english: A letter of admonishment is not treated as a disciplinary action for licensing or discipline-reporting purposes, though it is publicly disclosed for 1 or 2 years (B&P 7124.6). CSLB keeps the power to cite or discipline instead.
rules.applies_to: Licensees, HIS registrants and applicants
rules.quote: The issuance of a letter of admonishment shall not be construed as a disciplinary action or discipline for purposes of licensure or the reporting of discipline for licensure.

rules.title: When CSLB cannot use a letter of admonishment
rules.plain_english: CSLB may not resolve a case with a letter of admonishment if the person was unlicensed at the time, has a history of the same or similar violations, caused financial harm to someone, harmed an elder or dependent adult, or the violation involved repairing natural-disaster damage.

disqualifying_factors: history of same or similar violations
violation resulted in financial harm to another
victim is elder or dependent adult (Penal Code 368)
violation related to repair of natural disaster damage

rules.applies_to: Licensees, HIS registrants and applicants
rules.quote: The board shall not issue a letter of admonishment when any one of the following factors is present: (1) The licensee, registrant, or applicant was unlicensed at the time of the violation. (2) The licensee, registrant, or applicant has a history of the same or similar violations. (3) The violation resulted in financial harm to another.
rules.notes: Disaster-repair and elder/dependent-adult jobs therefore carry at least citation-level exposure.

rules.title: Unlicensed directory ads: order to stop and disconnect phone numbers
rules.plain_english: If someone advertises construction work in an alphabetical or classified directory without being properly licensed (B&P 7027.1), CSLB can issue a citation ordering them to stop and to have the phone company disconnect every number in the ad, with no referral to a new number. A contested citation gets a hearing within 90 days; if the order is ignored after it is final, the PUC orders the phone service cut off.

parameters.trigger: advertising in alphabetical or classified directory without proper license (B&P 7027.1)
order_of_correction: notify telephone company to disconnect numbers in ad
no referral of calls to new number
parameters.noncompliance_after_final: registrar informs Public Utilities Commission, which requires disconnection

rules.applies_to: Licensed contractors advertising outside their classification and unlicensed persons
rules.quote: the registrar may issue a citation under Section 7099 containing an order of correction which requires the violator to cease the unlawful advertising and to notify the telephone company furnishing services to the violator to disconnect the telephone service furnished to any telephone number contained in the unlawful advertising
rules.notes: Advertising rules themselves (B&P 7027.1, 7030.5 license number in ads) are on earlier pages.

rules.title: Asbestos removal ads must show certification and registration numbers
rules.plain_english: You may not advertise asbestos removal unless you hold CSLB asbestos certification (B&P 7058.5) and Cal/OSHA registration (Labor Code 6501.5). Every ad must show both numbers and use the same name under which you are certified and registered. Missing numbers get a notice to comply; ignoring it, or advertising without valid certification/registration, gets a citation.

parameters.name_requirement: same name under which certified and registered
citation_triggers: advertising without valid certification and registration

rules.applies_to: Contractors advertising asbestos removal
rules.quote: No person shall advertise, as that term is defined in Section 7027.1, to promote his or her services for the removal of asbestos unless he or she is certified to engage in asbestos-related work pursuant to Section 7058.5, and registered for that purpose pursuant to Section 6501.5 of the Labor Code. Each advertisement shall include that person’s certification and registration numbers
rules.notes: Category chosen because this dictates required advertisement text (not a contract).

rules.title: Bond of at least $1,000 to keep operating during court review
rules.plain_english: While a court reviews a CSLB decision, the court may let the contractor keep doing business only if the contractor posts a bond in an amount the court sets, at least the greater of $1,000 or what the court finds sufficient to protect the public. Without such a bond, there is no stay of CSLB's decision pending appeal.

parameters.bond_rule: greater of $1,000 or amount court finds sufficient to protect the public

rules.applies_to: Licensed contractors seeking court review of CSLB discipline
rules.quote: upon the filing of a proper bond by the licensee in an amount to be fixed by the court, but not less than one thousand dollars ($1,000) or an amount the court finds is sufficient to protect the public, whichever is greater

rules.title: Reinstatement after suspension requires proof of compliance
rules.plain_english: After a suspension, CSLB may reinstate the license once the contractor proves compliance with the decision's reinstatement terms; if the decision has none, reinstatement is at the Registrar's discretion.

parameters.requirement: proof of compliance with all reinstatement provisions of the decision

rules.applies_to: Suspended licensees
rules.quote: After suspension of a license upon any of the grounds set forth in this chapter, the registrar may reinstate the license upon proof of compliance by the contractor with all provisions of the decision as to reinstatement

rules.title: After revocation: 1-5 year wait and all losses paid
rules.plain_english: A revoked license cannot be reinstated or reissued, and no license can go to personnel of the revoked licensee who knew of or took part in the violations, for at least 1 and up to 5 years after the final revocation decision. Even then, all losses caused must be fully satisfied and all conditions met. The wait can be extended based on gravity, prior violations and criminal convictions.

parameters.start_event: final decision of revocation
parameters.applies_to_personnel: members of personnel who had knowledge of or participated in the acts
preconditions: all loss caused by the act/omission fully satisfied
all conditions of revocation decision complied with

rules.applies_to: Revoked licensees and their officers/personnel; companies considering hiring them as qualifiers
rules.quote: the license shall not be reinstated or reissued and a license shall not be issued to any member of the personnel of the revoked licensee found to have had knowledge of or participated in the acts or omissions constituting grounds for revocation, within a minimum period of one year and a maximum period of five years after the final decision of revocation

rules.title: Debts discharged in bankruptcy need not be paid to relicense
rules.plain_english: To be relicensed after revocation, a monetary debt from the violation does not have to be paid to the extent it was discharged in bankruptcy. Non-monetary conditions not discharged in bankruptcy must still be met first.
rules.applies_to: Revoked licensees seeking reissuance
rules.quote: the satisfaction of the monetary obligation or debt as a prerequisite for the issuance, reissuance, or reinstatement of a license shall not be required to the extent the monetary obligation or debt was discharged in a bankruptcy proceeding.

rules.title: Discipline in another state is grounds for California discipline
rules.plain_english: If another state revokes, suspends or otherwise disciplines a person's contractor license, that is grounds for discipline of a California licensee or applicant; a certified copy of the other state's action is conclusive evidence.

parameters.trigger: revocation, suspension, or other disciplinary action by another state

rules.applies_to: California licensees and applicants licensed in other states
rules.quote: The revocation, suspension, or other disciplinary action of a license to act as a contractor by another state shall constitute grounds for disciplinary action in this state if the individual is a licensee, or applies for a license, in this state.

rules.title: CSLB must tell the complainant (and contractor) how a complaint was resolved
rules.plain_english: When CSLB resolves a complaint it must notify the complainant in writing of its action and reasons, and send the same notice to the licensed contractor unless it would jeopardize an action or investigation.

notice_to: licensed contractor (unless it would jeopardize an action/investigation)

rules.applies_to: Owners/complainants and licensed contractors
rules.quote: When the board resolves a complaint, the board shall notify the complainant in writing of its action and the reasons for taking that action. The board shall provide the same notice in writing to the contractor provided that the contractor is licensed and the notification would not jeopardize an action or investigation that involves the contractor.

rules.title: Letting a license lapse or surrendering it does not stop discipline
rules.plain_english: Expiration, cancellation, forfeiture, suspension, revocation or voluntary surrender of a license does not stop CSLB from investigating, prosecuting, or issuing a suspension or revocation decision. A court case about the contractor's performance can also include license suspension or revocation (B&P 7106).
rules.applies_to: Licensed contractors
rules.quote: The expiration, cancellation, forfeiture, revocation, or suspension of a license by operation of law or by order or decision of the registrar or a court of law, or the voluntary surrender of a license by a licensee, shall not deprive the registrar of jurisdiction to proceed with any investigation of or action or disciplinary proceeding against the license

rules.title: Abandoning a project without legal excuse
rules.plain_english: Walking off a construction project without a legal excuse is grounds for CSLB discipline.

parameters.prohibited_act: abandonment of construction project or operation

rules.applies_to: Licensed contractors
rules.quote: Abandonment without legal excuse of any construction project or operation engaged in or undertaken by the licensee as a contractor constitutes a cause for disciplinary action.
rules.notes: Document any legal excuse (e.g., owner non-payment, stop-work notice) in writing before leaving a job.

rules.title: Diverting project funds or failing to account for them
rules.plain_english: Using money or property received for a specific project (or for a specific purpose on a project) for something else, or failing to substantially account for how those funds were used on that project, is grounds for discipline.

prohibited_acts: diversion of funds/property received for a specific project
diversion of funds received for a specified purpose on a project
failure to substantially account for application of such funds

rules.applies_to: Licensed contractors receiving owner deposits or progress payments
rules.quote: Diversion of funds or property received for prosecution or completion of a specific construction project or operation, or for a specified purpose in the prosecution or completion of any construction project or operation, or failure substantially to account for the application or use of such funds or property on the construction project or operation
rules.notes: Job-cost accounting by project supports compliance.

rules.title: Pay subcontractors within 7 days of receiving a progress payment
rules.plain_english: A prime contractor or subcontractor must pay each subcontractor its share of a progress payment within 7 days after receiving that progress payment, unless otherwise agreed in writing. This applies on all private works and on public works except where Public Contract Code 10262 applies.

parameters.start_event: receipt of each progress payment
parameters.amount: amounts allowed the contractor on account of the sub's work, to extent of sub's interest
parameters.scope: all private works and all public works, except where Public Contract Code 10262 applies

rules.applies_to: Prime contractors and subcontractors with lower-tier subs, private and public works
rules.quote: A prime contractor or subcontractor shall pay to any subcontractor, not later than seven days after receipt of each progress payment, unless otherwise agreed to in writing, the respective amounts allowed the contractor on account of the work performed by the subcontractors, to the extent of each subcontractor’s interest therein.
rules.notes: Public Contract Code 10262 (state contracts) is reproduced in the Appendix, not here. Civil Code prompt-payment statutes may also apply; not covered on these pages.

rules.title: Good-faith dispute: withhold no more than 150% of disputed amount
rules.plain_english: If there is a good-faith dispute over all or part of a progress payment owed to a subcontractor, the paying contractor may withhold no more than 150% of the disputed amount and must pay the rest on time.

parameters.formula: max_withhold = 1.5 * disputed_amount; must pay = amount_due - min(amount_due, max_withhold)
parameters.condition: good faith dispute over all or any portion of progress payment

rules.applies_to: Prime contractors and subcontractors paying subs
rules.quote: In the event that there is a good faith dispute over all or any portion of the amount due on a progress payment from the prime contractor or subcontractor to a subcontractor, the prime contractor or subcontractor may withhold no more than 150 percent of the disputed amount.
rules.notes: Formula is derived from the text.

rules.title: Late sub payment: 2% per month penalty plus attorney's fees
rules.plain_english: Violating the 7-day subcontractor payment rule is grounds for CSLB discipline and makes the contractor pay the sub a penalty of 2% of the amount due per month for every month it is unpaid. The winner of a lawsuit to collect wrongfully withheld funds gets attorney's fees and costs. These sanctions are in addition to all other remedies.

parameters.penalty_period: every month payment is not made

rules.applies_to: Prime contractors and subcontractors paying subs, private and public works
rules.quote: Any violation of this section shall constitute a cause for disciplinary action and shall subject the licensee to a penalty, payable to the subcontractor, of 2 percent of the amount due per month for every month that payment is not made. (c) In any action for the collection of funds wrongfully withheld, the prevailing party shall be entitled to his or her attorney’s fees and costs.
rules.notes: Statute does not say whether partial months are prorated.

rules.title: Pay dump truck carriers by the 20th of the following month
rules.plain_english: A licensed contractor must pay a licensed dump truck carrier's transportation charges by the 20th day after the end of the month in which hauling was done, if the carrier submits its charges with all documentation by the 5th day after month-end, unless otherwise agreed in writing. Applies on all private and public works.

parameters.carrier_submission_deadline: 5th day following last day of calendar month in which transportation performed
parameters.payment_deadline: 20th day following last day of calendar month in which transportation performed
parameters.condition: charges and all necessary documentation submitted by the 5th day
parameters.waivable_by: written agreement between contractor and carrier
parameters.scope: all private and public works of improvement

rules.applies_to: Licensed contractors using dump truck haulers (duly authorized motor carriers of property)
rules.quote: A licensed contractor is required to pay all transportation charges submitted by a duly authorized motor carrier of property in dump truck equipment by the 20th day following the last day of the calendar month in which the transportation was performed, if the charges, including all necessary documentation, are submitted by the fifth day following the last day of the calendar month
rules.notes: Example: hauling in March, invoice by April 5, pay by April 20.

rules.title: Dump truck charges: 150% dispute withholding cap; 2% monthly penalty
rules.plain_english: In a good-faith dispute over part of a dump truck carrier's charges, the contractor may withhold up to 150% of the disputed amount (or another agreed amount). Late payment is grounds for discipline under B&P 7120 and carries a penalty to the carrier of 2% of the amount due per month outstanding; the winner of a collection suit gets attorney's fees and costs.

parameters.alt_withhold: amount otherwise agreed by the parties

rules.applies_to: Licensed contractors using dump truck carriers
rules.quote: In the event that there is a good faith dispute over a portion of the charges claimed, the contractor may withhold payment of up to 150 percent of the disputed amount or an amount otherwise agreed to by the parties.

rules.title: Willful departure from good and workmanlike trade standards
rules.plain_english: Willfully departing in any material way from accepted trade standards for good and workmanlike construction is grounds for discipline, unless the work followed plans and specs prepared by or under an architect.

parameters.standard: accepted trade standards for good and workmanlike construction
parameters.defense: departure was per plans and specifications prepared by or under direct supervision of an architect

rules.applies_to: Licensed contractors
rules.quote: A willful departure in any material respect from accepted trade standards for good and workmanlike construction constitutes a cause for disciplinary action, unless the departure was in accordance with plans and specifications prepared by or under the direct supervision of an architect.
rules.notes: Latent structural defects under 7109(a) have a 10-year complaint window (7091(b)).

rules.title: Deviating from plans/specs without owner consent
rules.plain_english: Willfully departing from or disregarding plans or specifications in a material way that harms someone, without the consent of the owner (or authorized representative) and of the person entitled to have the project built to those plans, is grounds for discipline. Get written change orders.

consent_needed_from: person entitled to have project completed per plans/specs

rules.applies_to: Licensed contractors
rules.quote: A willful departure from or disregard of plans or specifications in any material respect, which is prejudicial to another, without the consent of the owner or his or her duly authorized representative and without the consent of the person entitled to have the particular construction project or operation completed in accordance with such plans or specifications
rules.notes: A change-order tool can require owner sign-off before deviations from plans/specs.

rules.title: Safety violations as grounds for discipline
rules.plain_english: Violating the Title 8 safety orders in Article 12 (starting at 8 CCR 3420) is grounds for discipline whether or not anyone was hurt. Violating any Labor Code Division 5 (Cal/OSHA, Section 6300+) safety provision is grounds for discipline if it results in an employee's death or serious injury.

parameters.title8_article12_3420: discipline regardless of death or serious injury
parameters.labor_code_division5_6300: discipline if death or serious injury to an employee resulted

rules.applies_to: Licensed contractors with employees
rules.quote: Violation of any safety provision in, or authorized by, Division 5 (commencing with Section 6300) of the Labor Code resulting in death or serious injury to an employee constitutes a cause for disciplinary action.
rules.notes: The text does not name the subject of 8 CCR Article 12 (Section 3420 et seq.); it is understood to be the tree work safety orders (AB 2210), not verified on these pages. DOSH citations under that article trigger CSLB action within 18 months (7110.5).

rules.title: Willful violation of building, labor, safety and other listed laws
rules.plain_english: Willfully or deliberately disregarding state or local building laws, or the other listed laws, is grounds for discipline. The list covers pest control rules (B&P 8550/8556), Civil Code 1689.5-1689.15, safety, labor, workers' comp and unemployment insurance laws, the Subletting and Subcontracting Fair Practices Act, water well laws, Gov Code 4216 et seq., Penal Code 374.3, and building permit laws. Citations for 7110 violations carry the higher penalty range.

listed_laws: building laws of the state or any political subdivision
safety laws, labor laws, compensation insurance laws, Unemployment Insurance Code
Subletting and Subcontracting Fair Practices Act (Public Contract Code 4100 et seq.)
Health and Safety Code or Water Code provisions on digging, boring, drilling water wells
Government Code 4216 et seq. (Article 2, Chapter 3.1, Division 5, Title 1)
Penal Code 374.3 or substantially similar local law
any state or local law relating to issuance of building permits

rules.applies_to: Licensed contractors
rules.quote: Willful or deliberate disregard and violation of the building laws of the state, or of any political subdivision thereof, or of any of the following references to or provisions of law, constitutes a cause for disciplinary action against a licensee:
rules.notes: Topic labels not printed in the text: Civil Code 1689.5-1689.15 are the home solicitation contract cancellation rules; Gov Code 4216 et seq. is the underground utility excavation (811/DigAlert) law; Penal Code 374.3 is illegal dumping; B&P 8550/8556 are structural pest control provisions. Verify before display.

rules.title: Cannot require workers to release wage claims
rules.plain_english: Requiring or causing a worker to sign a release of a wage claim in violation of Labor Code 206.5 is grounds for CSLB discipline.

parameters.prohibited_act: requiring or causing execution of release of claim in violation of Labor Code 206.5

rules.applies_to: Licensed contractors with employees
rules.quote: The requiring of an execution of release of any claim or the causing of the execution of any such release in violation of Section 206.5 of the Labor Code is a cause for disciplinary action.
rules.notes: Labor Code 206.5 is in the Appendix.

rules.title: Labor Commissioner willful-violation finding or DOSH citation triggers CSLB action
rules.plain_english: When CSLB receives a certified Labor Commissioner finding of a willful or deliberate Labor Code violation (Labor Code 98.9), or DOSH citations under 8 CCR Article 12 (Section 3420 et seq.), the Registrar must start disciplinary action within 18 months of receipt.

triggers: certified copy of Labor Commissioner finding of willful/deliberate Labor Code violation (Labor Code 98.9)
DOSH citations or actions under 8 CCR Article 12 (Section 3420 et seq.)
parameters.start_event: registrar's receipt of the violation

rules.applies_to: Licensed contractors with employees
rules.quote: the registrar shall initiate disciplinary action against the licensee within 18 months from the date of the registrar’s receipt of the violation.
rules.notes: Labor violations carry license consequences, not just Labor Commissioner penalties.

rules.title: Keep all contract and financial records for 5 years after completion
rules.plain_english: A contractor must make and keep records of all contracts, documents, receipts and disbursements for its contracting work, and keep them available for CSLB inspection for at least 5 years after each project is completed. Refusing a written CSLB request to inspect them is grounds for discipline.

parameters.start_event: completion of the construction project or operation to which the records refer
violation_triggers: failure to have records available for inspection
refusal to comply with registrar's written request

rules.applies_to: All licensed contractors
rules.quote: Failure to make and keep records showing all contracts, documents, records, receipts, and disbursements by a licensee of all of his or her transactions as a contractor, and failure to have those records available for inspection by the registrar or his or her duly authorized representative for a period of not less than five years after completion of any construction project
rules.notes: Calculation: retain_until = project_completion_date + 5 years (per project).

rules.title: Respond to CSLB written requests for records and cooperation
rules.plain_english: Delaying, obstructing or refusing, without lawful excuse, a written CSLB request for information or records, or failing to respond to a written request to cooperate in a complaint investigation, is grounds for discipline.

parameters.trigger: written request of registrar or designee
prohibited: delay
obstruct
refuse to provide information or records
fail to respond to request to cooperate in complaint investigation

rules.applies_to: Licensed contractors, applicants and HIS registrants
rules.quote: The failure of, or refusal by, a licensee to respond to a written request of the registrar to cooperate in the investigation of a complaint against that licensee constitutes a cause for disciplinary action.
rules.notes: No specific response deadline is stated in the statute; follow the date in CSLB's letter.

rules.title: False or omitted facts on license applications
rules.plain_english: Omitting or misrepresenting a material fact when obtaining or renewing a license, or when adding a classification, is grounds for discipline. Any classification added through misrepresentation is expunged from the license record on a final order.
rules.applies_to: Licensed contractors and applicants
rules.quote: Omission or misrepresentation of a material fact by an applicant or a licensee in obtaining, or renewing a license, or in adding a classification to an existing license constitutes a cause for disciplinary action.

rules.title: Failing to complete for the contract price
rules.plain_english: Failing in a material way to complete a project for the price stated in the contract or any modification of it is grounds for discipline. Price changes need written change orders.

parameters.price_basis: price stated in contract or any modification of contract

rules.applies_to: Licensed contractors
rules.quote: Failure in a material respect on the part of a licensee to complete any construction project or operation for the price stated in the contract for such construction project or operation or in any modification of such contract constitutes a cause for disciplinary action.
rules.notes: A budget tool can flag projected cost to owner exceeding contract price plus approved change orders.

rules.title: Settling contractor debts for less than full (non-bankruptcy)
rules.plain_english: Avoiding or settling lawful contracting debts for less than the full amount through a creditor composition or reorganization under state law or agreement, receivership, assignment for the benefit of creditors, trusteeship or dissolution is grounds for discipline. Individual settlements with one creditor are not covered, and federal bankruptcy discharge is not grounds as long as non-discharged debts are paid.

covered_methods: composition, arrangement, or reorganization with creditors under state law
composition, arrangement, or reorganization by agreement
excluded: individual settlement with one creditor not part of a multi-creditor settlement
federal bankruptcy discharge, if non-discharged obligations are satisfied

rules.applies_to: Licensed contractors in financial distress
rules.quote: The avoidance or settlement by a licensee for less than the full amount of the lawful obligations of the licensee incurred as a contractor, whether by (a) composition, arrangement, or reorganization with creditors under state law, (b) composition, arrangement, or reorganization with creditors under any agreement or understanding,

rules.title: Aiding unlicensed contractors or letting them use your license
rules.plain_english: Helping an unlicensed person evade the License Law, conspiring with them, letting them use your license, or acting as their agent, partner or associate to evade the law is grounds for discipline. CSLB can order the licensee to pay injured parties, including for harm caused by the unlicensed person. Citations carry the higher penalty range.

prohibited_acts: aiding or abetting unlicensed person to evade chapter
combining or conspiring with unlicensed person
allowing license to be used by unlicensed person
acting as agent, partner, associate of unlicensed person with intent to evade
parameters.remedy: order to pay specified sum to injured party, including injury from unlicensed person's acts

rules.applies_to: Licensed contractors
rules.quote: Aiding or abetting an unlicensed person to evade the provisions of this chapter or combining or conspiring with an unlicensed person, or allowing one’s license to be used by an unlicensed person, or acting as agent or partner or associate, or otherwise, of an unlicensed person with the intent to evade the provisions of this chapter constitutes a cause for disciplinary action.

rules.title: Signing a false experience certificate for an applicant
rules.plain_english: A licensee who signs a falsified certificate of an applicant's experience, or otherwise certifies false or misleading experience claims for a license application, is subject to discipline.

parameters.prohibited_act: signing falsified experience certificate or certifying false/misleading experience claims

rules.applies_to: Licensed contractors who verify employees' or others' experience
rules.quote: Any licensee whose signature appears on a falsified certificate in support of an examinee’s experience qualifications, or otherwise certifying to false or misleading experience claims by an applicant, which have been submitted to obtain a contractor’s license shall be subject to disciplinary action.

rules.title: Misuse of a license (B&P 119) subject to CSLB remedies
rules.plain_english: Anyone, licensed or not, who commits an act prohibited by B&P 119 (misuse of licenses) is subject to CSLB administrative remedies, in addition to any civil or criminal remedies.
rules.applies_to: Licensed and unlicensed persons
rules.quote: Any licensed or unlicensed person who commits any act prohibited by Section 119 is subject to the administrative remedies authorized by this chapter.
rules.notes: The acts prohibited by B&P 119 are not listed on these pages.

rules.title: Material failure to comply with License Law, CSLB rules, or PCC 7106
rules.plain_english: Failing in any material respect to comply with the Contractors State License Law, any CSLB rule or regulation, or Public Contract Code 7106 is grounds for discipline.

covered: Contractors State License Law (B&P 7000 et seq.)

rules.applies_to: Licensed contractors (PCC 7106 relevant to public works bidders)
rules.quote: Failure in any material respect to comply with the provisions of this chapter, or any rule or regulation adopted pursuant to this chapter, or to comply with the provisions of Section 7106 of the Public Contract Code, constitutes a cause for disciplinary action.
rules.notes: PCC 7106 content (understood to be the public works bid noncollusion declaration) is not printed here; verify.

rules.title: Willful or fraudulent act that substantially injures another
rules.plain_english: Any willful or fraudulent act by a contractor that substantially injures another person is grounds for discipline, and fixing the problem later does not by itself avoid discipline (B&P 7090.5).
rules.applies_to: Licensed contractors
rules.quote: The doing of any wilful or fraudulent act by the licensee as a contractor in consequence of which another is substantially injured constitutes a cause for disciplinary action.

rules.title: Obstructing investigations, threatening witnesses, retaliatory firing
rules.plain_english: It is grounds for discipline to subvert or try to subvert a CSLB investigation, to threaten or harass anyone for providing evidence in a disciplinary action, arbitration or other legal action, or to fire an employee mainly because the employee tried to comply with or help enforce the License Law.

prohibited_acts: conduct that subverts or attempts to subvert a board investigation
threaten or harass any person for providing evidence in disciplinary action, arbitration, or other legal action
discharge employee primarily because of employee's attempt to comply with or aid compliance with the chapter

rules.applies_to: Licensed contractors
rules.quote: Threaten or harass any person or licensee for providing evidence in any possible or actual disciplinary action, arbitration, or other legal action. (c) Discharge an employee primarily because of the employee’s attempt to comply with or aid in compliance with the provisions of this chapter.

rules.title: Contract only in the exact licensed name and with listed personnel
rules.plain_english: A contractor must act only under the name shown on the license and with the personnel listed with CSLB (as updated through proper filings). Contracting under another name or with unreported personnel changes is grounds for discipline.

parameters.name_must_match: name of licensee as set forth upon the license
parameters.personnel_must_match: personnel as set forth in application or as later changed per chapter

rules.applies_to: All licensed contractors; contracts, bids, invoices and ads
rules.quote: Acting in the capacity of a contractor under any license issued hereunder except: (a) in the name of the licensee as set forth upon the license, or (b) in accordance with the personnel of the licensee as set forth in the application for such license, or as later changed as provided in this chapter, constitutes a cause for disciplinary action.
rules.notes: A contract generator should print the business name exactly as on the CSLB license record. Business name change fee: see fees-misc.

rules.title: No contracting on an inactive, suspended or expired license
rules.plain_english: Acting as a contractor while your license is inactive, suspended for any reason, or expired (if still renewable under B&P 7141) is grounds for discipline, in addition to any civil or criminal remedies.

prohibited_license_statuses: expired and subject to renewal under B&P 7141

rules.applies_to: All licensed contractors; owners/GCs checking a sub's license status
rules.quote: Acting in the capacity of a contractor under any license that has been suspended for any reason constitutes a cause for disciplinary action. (c) Acting in the capacity of a contractor under any license that has expired constitutes a cause for disciplinary action if the license is subject to renewal pursuant to Section 7141.
rules.notes: Workers' comp lapse causes automatic suspension (7125.2), which then bars contracting.

rules.title: Work only in the classifications you hold
rules.plain_english: Contracting in a classification you do not currently hold is grounds for discipline. Check the license classifications against the scope of each contract.

parameters.rule: contract scope must fall within classification(s) currently held by licensee

rules.applies_to: All licensed contractors; GCs/owners vetting subs
rules.quote: Acting in the capacity of a contractor in a classification other than that currently held by the licensee constitutes a cause for disciplinary action.
rules.notes: Classification scopes are defined in B&P 7055-7059 and 16 CCR 832 (other chunks).

rules.title: Do not contract with an unlicensed contractor
rules.plain_english: A licensee who enters into a contract with a contractor who is not licensed can be disciplined, and the citation penalty range is the higher one ($1,500-$30,000 from July 1, 2026). Verify every subcontractor's license before signing.

parameters.prohibited_act: entering into contract with contractor not licensed
parameters.check_timing: at contract execution (and while contract in force)

rules.applies_to: Licensed contractors hiring subcontractors
rules.quote: Entering into a contract with a contractor while such contractor is not licensed as provided in this chapter constitutes a cause for disciplinary action.
rules.notes: Strong candidate for an automated CSLB license lookup at sub onboarding.

rules.title: Asbestos inspectors must disclose ties to the abatement company
rules.plain_english: If a contractor inspects for asbestos knowing the report is required by a lender or by a public agency for a permit, it must disclose orally and in writing any ownership, common ownership, or financial relationship (including commissions or referral fees) with a company that does the corrective work. Violation is grounds for discipline and a misdemeanor fined $3,000-$5,000 and/or up to 1 year in county jail.

parameters.trigger: asbestos inspection report required by lender as loan condition or by public entity as permit condition
disclose: any financial relationship incl. commissions or referral fees with corrective-work entity
parameters.exception: contractor doing corrective work after another company's report may inspect before and after its own work

rules.applies_to: Contractors performing asbestos inspections
rules.quote: the contractor shall disclose orally and in writing if it is owned or has any common ownership, or any financial relationship whatsoever, including, but not limited to, commissions or referral fees, with an entity in the business of performing the corrective work.
rules.notes: Asbestos is defined by Labor Code 6501.7.

rules.title: Hiring an uncertified asbestos contractor: $1,000-$3,000, then $3,000-$5,000
rules.plain_english: A contractor who knowingly, negligently, or by failing to ask contracts with someone who must be asbestos-certified (B&P 7058.5) but is not faces: first offense, an infraction with a $1,000-$3,000 fine and possible license suspension or revocation; later offenses, a misdemeanor with mandatory suspension or revocation and a $3,000-$5,000 fine and/or up to 1 year in jail.

parameters.required_certification: B&P 7058.5 asbestos certification (asbestos-related work per Labor Code 6501.8)

rules.applies_to: Contractors, applicants and persons required to be licensed who hire asbestos subcontractors
rules.quote: Any contractor, applicant for licensure, or person required to be licensed, who, either knowingly or negligently, or by reason of a failure to inquire, enters into a contract with another person who is required to be, and is not, certified pursuant to Section 7058.5 to engage in asbestos-related work, as defined in Section 6501.8 of the Labor Code, is subject to the following penalties:
rules.notes: Failure to inquire is enough: verify certification before contracting.

rules.title: Hiring an uncertified hazardous substance removal contractor
rules.plain_english: A contractor who knowingly, negligently, or by failing to ask contracts with someone who must hold hazardous substance removal/remedial action certification (B&P 7058.7) but does not faces the same penalties: first offense $1,000-$3,000 infraction; subsequent offenses a misdemeanor with mandatory license suspension or revocation and $3,000-$5,000 fine and/or up to 1 year in jail.

parameters.required_certification: B&P 7058.7 hazardous substance removal or remedial action certification

rules.applies_to: Contractors hiring hazardous substance removal subcontractors
rules.quote: Any contractor who, either knowingly or negligently, or by reason of a failure to inquire, enters into a contract with another person who is required to be, and is not certified pursuant to Section 7058.7 to engage in a removal or remedial action, as defined in Section 7058.7, is subject to the following penalties:

rules.title: Failing to work on the project with reasonable diligence
rules.plain_english: Willfully failing or refusing, without legal excuse, to carry out a project with reasonable diligence, causing material injury to someone, is grounds for discipline.
rules.applies_to: Licensed contractors
rules.quote: Wilful failure or refusal without legal excuse on the part of a licensee as a contractor to prosecute a construction project or operation with reasonable diligence causing material injury to another constitutes a cause for disciplinary action.
rules.notes: Schedule tracking with documented delay causes supports a legal-excuse defense.

rules.title: Not paying suppliers/vendors when able or when paid for that work
rules.plain_english: Willfully failing to pay for materials or services when due, if the contractor can pay or has received enough money for that job, is grounds for discipline, as is falsely denying a debt to get a discount or to hinder, delay or defraud the creditor.

triggers: has received sufficient funds for the particular project
parameters.also_prohibited: false denial of amount due or validity of claim, to obtain discount or to hinder, delay, or defraud

rules.applies_to: Licensed contractors and their officers/agents
rules.quote: Wilful or deliberate failure by any licensee or agent or officer thereof to pay any moneys, when due for any materials or services rendered in connection with his operations as a contractor, when he has the capacity to pay or when he has received sufficient funds therefor as payment for the particular construction work, project, or operation
rules.notes: A pay-when-paid tracker can flag supplier invoices unpaid after owner payment for that job is received.

rules.title: People tied to denied, revoked or suspended licenses cannot be personnel of record
rules.plain_english: A person denied a license (other than for lacking experience for a supplemental class), whose license was revoked or is suspended, or who was a partner, officer, director, manager or associate of such a company and knew of or took part in the violations, cannot be an officer, director, associate, partner, manager, qualifier or personnel of record of a licensee. Employing them in any role other than a non-supervising bona fide employee is grounds for discipline.

barred_persons: denied a license (not merely for insufficient experience for a supplemental classification)
failed to renew while under suspension
partner/officer/director/manager/associate of such an entity who knew of or participated in the prohibited acts

rules.applies_to: Contracting companies hiring or appointing officers, managers or qualifiers
rules.quote: shall be prohibited from serving as an officer, director, associate, partner, manager, qualifying individual, or member of the personnel of record of a licensee, and the employment, election, or association of this type of person by a licensee in any capacity other than as a nonsupervising bona fide employee shall constitute grounds for disciplinary action.
rules.notes: Screen proposed officers/qualifiers against CSLB records before appointment.

rules.title: Leaving the company does not relieve officers or qualifiers of a citation
rules.plain_english: A partner, officer, director, manager or associate who knew of or participated in the cited acts stays responsible for complying with the citation after leaving the company, and the 7121 bar applies if it is not complied with. A qualifying individual who leaves after the act stays responsible regardless of knowledge, and the 7122.5 rule applies.

parameters.officers_partners: responsible if they had knowledge of or participated in the cited acts (B&P 7121.1)
parameters.qualifying_individual: responsible regardless of knowledge if disassociated after the act (B&P 7122.1)

rules.applies_to: Officers, partners, managers and qualifiers of cited licensees
rules.quote: the disassociation of a partner, officer, director, manager, or associate from the license of a partnership, corporation, limited liability company, firm, or association whose license has been cited pursuant to Section 7099 shall not relieve the partner, officer, director, manager, or associate from responsibility for complying with the citation

rules.title: Qualifier of a revoked or suspended license is barred regardless of knowledge
rules.plain_english: Anyone who was the qualifying individual on a license that was revoked, is suspended, or was not renewed while suspended cannot be an officer, director, associate, partner, manager or qualifier of a licensee, even without knowledge of the violations. Employing or associating with them in those roles is grounds for discipline.

parameters.barred_person: qualifying individual on revoked, suspended, or not-renewed-while-suspended license

rules.applies_to: Contracting companies appointing qualifiers (RMO/RME) or officers
rules.quote: A person who was the qualifying individual on a revoked license, or of a license under suspension, or of a license that was not renewed while it was under suspension, shall be prohibited from serving as an officer, director, associate, partner, manager, or qualifying individual of a licensee, whether or not the individual had knowledge of or participated in the prohibited acts or omissions

rules.title: Revoked-license principals may only work as non-supervising employees
rules.plain_english: An officer, owner, manager, partner or associate of a revoked license who knew of or took part in the violations, or the qualifier of a revoked license (regardless of knowledge), who is not yet eligible for reinstatement under B&P 7102, may not do any licensed contracting act for a licensee except as a bona fide non-supervising employee. Violation is a misdemeanor: fine of at least $4,500 and/or 90 days to 1 year in county jail; charges may be filed within 4 years.

restricted_persons: listed officer/director/owner/manager/partner/associate of revoked license who knew of or participated in the acts
qualifier of revoked license during the acts, regardless of knowledge
parameters.condition: not eligible for reinstatement under B&P 7102

rules.applies_to: Individuals tied to revoked licenses
rules.quote: A violation of this section is a misdemeanor punishable by a fine of not less than four thousand five hundred dollars ($4,500), by imprisonment in a county jail for not less than 90 days nor more than one year, or by both the fine and imprisonment.

rules.title: Revoked-license individuals must tell prospective employers in writing
rules.plain_english: Before taking any job with a licensed contracting business, a person described in B&P 7121.6(a) or (b) must give the prospective employer written notice of the license revocation.

parameters.timing: prior to becoming employed in any capacity

rules.applies_to: Individuals tied to revoked licenses; contractors hiring them
rules.quote: Prior to becoming employed in any capacity by an entity that is subject to licensure under this chapter, an individual who is described in subdivision (a) or (b) of Section 7121.6 shall provide the prospective employer with written notice of the license revocation.
rules.notes: Onboarding checklists can ask for and file this notice.

rules.title: Knowingly employing a revoked-license individual in a supervising role
rules.plain_english: A qualifier, officer, partner or other person named on a license may not knowingly employ a person described in B&P 7121.6(a) or (b) except as a bona fide non-supervising employee. Violation is a misdemeanor: fine of at least $4,500 and/or 30 days to 1 year in county jail; charges may be filed within 4 years.
rules.applies_to: Contracting companies and their named personnel
rules.quote: A qualifying individual, officer, partner, or other person named on a license shall not knowingly employ an individual who is described in subdivision (a) or (b) of Section 7121.6, except as a bona fide nonsupervising employee.

rules.title: Definition: bona fide nonsupervising employee
rules.plain_english: A bona fide non-supervising employee is someone exempt from licensing as an employee under B&P 7053 who does not meet the independent-contractor test of Labor Code 2750.5.
rules.applies_to: Contracting companies employing barred individuals
rules.quote: “bona fide nonsupervising employee” means a person who is exempt from the provisions of this chapter under Section 7053, and who does not otherwise meet the test of an independent contractor, as set forth under Section 2750.5 of the Labor Code.

rules.title: Officers and partners can be disciplined for the company's violations they knew of
rules.plain_english: A violation by a business is also grounds for discipline against any of its partners, officers, directors, managers or associates who hold their own license, if they were in that role at the time and knew of or participated in the violation.

parameters.timing: in that role when act occurred

rules.applies_to: Officers and partners of contracting businesses who hold licenses
rules.quote: a licensee other than the individual qualifying on behalf of the individual or entity, if the licensee was a partner, officer, director, manager, or associate of that individual, partnership, corporation, limited liability company, firm, or association at the time the act or omission occurred, and had knowledge of or participated in the prohibited act or omission.

rules.title: Qualifiers are liable for the company's violations even without knowledge
rules.plain_english: A violation by a business is grounds for discipline against whoever was its qualifying individual at the time, whether or not the qualifier knew of or participated in it. A qualifier who leaves also stays responsible for arbitration awards arising from their time as qualifier.

parameters.who: qualifying individual at the time of the act

rules.applies_to: RMOs, RMEs and other qualifying individuals
rules.quote: likewise constitutes a cause for disciplinary action against a licensee who at the time that the act or omission occurred was the qualifying individual of that individual, partnership, corporation, limited liability company, firm, or association, whether or not he or she had knowledge of or participated in the prohibited act or omission.
rules.notes: Qualifiers should monitor citations, arbitrations and complaints against every license they qualify.

rules.title: Departing qualifier still responsible for arbitration awards
rules.plain_english: A qualifying individual who disassociates from a license referred to CSLB arbitration remains responsible for complying with any award arising from acts or omissions while they were qualifier, and B&P 7122.5 applies if the licensee does not comply.

parameters.responsible_for: arbitration award for acts/omissions committed while acting as qualifier

rules.applies_to: RMOs, RMEs and other qualifying individuals
rules.quote: the disassociation of a qualifying individual from a license that has been referred to arbitration pursuant to Section 7085 shall not relieve the qualifying individual from the responsibility of complying with an arbitration award rendered as a result of acts or omissions committed while acting as the qualifying individual for the license

rules.title: Substantially related criminal conviction
rules.plain_english: A conviction for a crime substantially related to a contractor's qualifications, functions and duties is grounds for discipline; the conviction record is conclusive evidence. A guilty plea, guilty verdict, or no-contest plea followed by conviction counts, and CSLB may act once the appeal time passes, the conviction is affirmed, or probation is granted, even if the plea is later withdrawn under Penal Code 1203.4.

conviction_includes: conviction following plea of nolo contendere
board_may_act_when: order granting probation suspending imposition of sentence

rules.applies_to: Licensed contractors and applicants
rules.quote: A conviction of a crime substantially related to the qualifications, functions and duties of a contractor constitutes a cause for disciplinary action. The record of the conviction shall be conclusive evidence thereof.

rules.title: Post-disaster price gouging conviction: at least 6-month suspension
rules.plain_english: If a contractor is convicted of price gouging after a declared emergency (Penal Code 396 or similar local law) in selling repair or reconstruction services, CSLB must discipline, including at least a 6-month suspension or permanent revocation.

parameters.trigger: conviction under Penal Code 396 or substantially similar local ordinance re repair or reconstruction services

rules.applies_to: Contractors doing post-disaster repair or reconstruction
rules.quote: the Contractors State License Board shall take disciplinary action against the contractor, which shall include a suspension of at least six months or the permanent revocation of the contractor’s license.
rules.notes: Penal Code 396 price limits are in the Appendix, not on these pages.

rules.title: Which complaints CSLB discloses to the public
rules.plain_english: CSLB publicly discloses the date, nature and status of complaints that have been referred for accusation, or referred for investigation after staff found a probable violation (supervisor-reviewed) serious enough for suspension, revocation or criminal prosecution. Each disclosure carries a disclaimer that it is only an allegation. Complaints resolved in the contractor's favor are not disclosed.

disclosed_complaints: referred for investigation after probable-violation determination, supervisor-reviewed, alleging risk of harm warranting suspension/revocation or criminal prosecution

rules.applies_to: Licensed contractors; owners researching contractors
rules.quote: The registrar shall make available to members of the public the date, nature, and status of all complaints on file against a licensee that do either of the following: (1) Have been referred for accusation.
rules.notes: Last amended Stats 2022 ch 293 (AB 2916); effective date not printed.

rules.title: Letters of admonishment are public for 1 or 2 years
rules.plain_english: A letter of admonishment is not treated as resolved in the contractor's favor and is publicly disclosed for 1 or 2 years from the date of service, based on the gravity, good faith and prior-violation factors.

parameters.start_event: date of service of letter of admonishment (B&P 7099.9(c))

rules.applies_to: Licensees issued letters of admonishment; owners researching contractors
rules.quote: A letter of admonishment issued to a licensee shall be disclosed for a period of either one year or two years from the date of service described in subdivision (c) of Section 7099.9.

rules.title: Citations are public until 5 years after compliance
