parameters.aggregation: aggregate contract price specified in one or more improvement contracts, including all labor, services and materials furnished by the contractor

rules.applies_to: Residential home improvement contracts
rules.quote: if the aggregate contract price specified in one or more improvement contracts, including all labor, services, and materials to be furnished by the contractor, exceeds five hundred dollars ($500).
rules.notes: Splitting a job into multiple contracts does not avoid the threshold because the price is aggregated. Service and repair contracts of $750 or less that meet 7159.10 use the separate service-and-repair form.
rules.correction: Note said service and repair contracts are "under $750". B&P 7159.10(a)(1)(A) and 7159.14(a)(1) say "$750 or less", so a $750 contract still qualifies. Note fixed. The $500 "exceeds" threshold itself is correct.

rules.title: HIC must be legible; at least 10-point text and 10-point bold headings
rules.plain_english: Every home improvement contract must be legible. Printed forms must use at least 10-point type for text and at least 10-point bold type for headings, unless a larger size is required for a specific notice.
rules.applies_to: All home improvement contracts over $500
rules.quote: Unless a larger typeface is specified in this article, text in any printed form shall be in at least 10-point typeface and the headings shall be in at least 10-point boldface type.
rules.notes: Several notices require 12-point bold (entitled-to-copy statement, downpayment and progress payment statements, right-to-cancel notices, CSLB information notice at 12-point).

rules.title: Give buyer a signed and dated copy before any work starts
rules.plain_english: Before starting any work, the contractor must give the buyer a copy of the contract signed and dated by both the contractor and the buyer. The buyer's cancellation rights begin when they receive this copy.

parameters.timing: before any work is started

rules.applies_to: Home improvement contractors
rules.quote: Before any work is started, the contractor shall give the buyer a copy of the contract that is signed and dated by both the contractor and the buyer. The buyer’s receipt of the copy of the contract initiates the buyer’s rights to cancel the contract pursuant to Sections 1689.5 to 1689.14, inclusive, of the Civil Code.
rules.notes: Software should record the date the buyer received the signed copy, because the 3/5/7 business-day cancellation period runs from it.

rules.title: First page must show buyer's signing date and contractor contact for cancellation
rules.plain_english: Page one of the contract, in type at least as large as the body text, must show the date the buyer signed, and the contractor's name, address and email address for sending the Notice of Cancellation, introduced by a statement that the notice may be sent there. It must also show a phone number for help locating and filling out the Notice of Cancellation.

required_items: date the buyer signed the contract
contractor name, address and email address for Notice of Cancellation
statement immediately preceding it advising that the Notice of Cancellation may be sent to the contractor at that address or email address
telephone number of contractor or contractor's representative to assist with the Notice of Cancellation

rules.applies_to: Home improvement contracts over $500
rules.quote: The name, address, and email address of the contractor to whom the applicable “Notice of Cancellation” is to be sent, immediately preceded by a statement advising the buyer that the “Notice of Cancellation” may be sent to the contractor at the address or email address noted on the contract.
rules.effective: Section amended effective January 1, 2026 (Stats 2025 ch 348 AB 1327 and ch 585 SB 517)
rules.notes: The text says 'both of the following' but lists three items (i)-(iii); include all three. The email address and email cancellation language appear in the 2026 text; the book does not say exactly which words the 2026 amendments added.

rules.title: Contract must promise unconditional lien release after each payment
rules.plain_english: The contract must state that after satisfactory payment for any portion of the work, and before any further payment, the contractor will give the owner a full and unconditional release from any lien claim or mechanics lien (Civil Code 8400 and 8404) for that paid portion.

parameters.trigger: satisfactory payment for any portion of work
parameters.timing: before any further payment is made

rules.applies_to: Home improvement and swimming pool contracts
rules.quote: The contract shall include a statement that, upon satisfactory payment being made for any portion of the work performed, the contractor, prior to any further payment being made, shall furnish to the person contracting for the home improvement or swimming pool work a full and unconditional release from any potential lien claimant claim or mechanics lien
rules.notes: For pool contracts, substantial noncompliance with this paragraph voids the contract (B&P 7167).

rules.title: Change-order form must be part of the contract
rules.plain_english: A change-order form for changes or extra work must be incorporated into the contract. A change order becomes part of the contract only if it is written and signed by both parties before the changed work begins.

valid_only_if: signed before commencement of work covered by the change order

rules.applies_to: Home improvement and swimming pool contracts
rules.quote: A change-order form for changes or extra work shall be incorporated into the contract and shall become part of the contract only if it is in writing and signed by the parties prior to the commencement of any work covered by a change order.
rules.notes: Pool contracts that do not substantially comply are void (B&P 7167), but the contractor may still recover in quantum meruit for this paragraph.

rules.title: Notice of owner's right to require performance and payment bond
rules.plain_english: Near the owner's and contractor's signatures, the contract must state that the owner or tenant has the right to require the contractor to have a performance and payment bond.

parameters.placement: in close proximity to the signatures of owner and contractor
parameters.content: owner or tenant has right to require contractor to have a performance and payment bond

rules.applies_to: Home improvement contracts over $500
rules.quote: The contract shall contain, in close proximity to the signatures of the owner and contractor, a notice stating that the owner or tenant has the right to require the contractor to have a performance and payment bond.
rules.notes: No exact wording is prescribed.

rules.title: Subcontractor Yes/No checkbox and disclaimer, repeated on each change order
rules.plain_english: The contract must state whether subcontractors will be used, with Yes/No checkboxes. If Yes, it must include a disclaimer that a list of subcontractors (names, contact info, license numbers and classifications) will be provided on request, and the same disclaimer must appear on every change order.

parameters.if_yes_required_text: One or more subcontractors will be used on this project, and the contractor is aware that a list of subcontractors is required to be provided, upon request, along with the names, contact information, license number, and classification of those subcontractors.

rules.applies_to: Home improvement contracts over $500 and their change orders
rules.quote: “One or more subcontractors will be used on this project, and the contractor is aware that a list of subcontractors is required to be provided, upon request, along with the names, contact information, license number, and classification of those subcontractors.”
rules.notes: Software should keep a subcontractor roster per job (name, contact, license number, classification) ready to produce on request.

rules.title: Contractor may have no interest in the joint control it furnishes
rules.plain_english: If the contract provides for the contractor to furnish joint control (a funds-control arrangement), the contractor must not have any financial or other interest in that joint control.

parameters.applies_when: contract provides for contractor to furnish joint control

rules.applies_to: Home improvement contractors using joint control
rules.source: 2026 CSLB Law Book, PDF pages 399 and 411
rules.quote: If the contract provides for a contractor to furnish joint control, the contractor shall not have any financial or other interest in the joint control.

rules.title: Contract and all changes must be written and signed before work
rules.plain_english: A home improvement contract and every change to it must be in writing and signed by the parties before work on the contract or change order begins, and must include the items listed in 7159(d).

parameters.timing: prior to commencement of work covered by the contract or applicable change order

rules.applies_to: Home improvement contracts over $500
rules.quote: A home improvement contract and any changes to the contract shall be in writing and signed by the parties to the contract prior to the commencement of work covered by the contract or an applicable change order

rules.title: Contract must show contractor name, address, license no., and salesperson registration
rules.plain_english: The contract must list the contractor's name, business address and license number, and, if a home improvement salesperson solicited or negotiated the deal, the salesperson's name and registration number.
rules.applies_to: Home improvement contracts over $500
rules.quote: (1) The name, business address, and license number of the contractor. (2) If applicable, the name and registration number of the home improvement salesperson that solicited or negotiated the contract.

rules.title: Contract heading 'Home Improvement' in 10-point bold
rules.plain_english: The contract form must carry the heading 'Home Improvement' in at least 10-point bold type to identify the contract type.
rules.applies_to: Home improvement contracts over $500
rules.quote: The following heading on the contract form that identifies the type of contract in at least 10-point boldface type: “Home Improvement.”

rules.title: 12-point bold 'entitled to a completely filled in copy' statement
rules.plain_english: The contract must include, in at least 12-point bold type, the statement that the buyer is entitled to a completely filled-in copy signed by both parties before any work starts.

parameters.required_text: You are entitled to a completely filled in copy of this agreement, signed by both you and the contractor, before any work may be started.

rules.applies_to: Home improvement contracts over $500
rules.quote: The following statement in at least 12-point boldface type: “You are entitled to a completely filled in copy of this agreement, signed by both you and the contractor, before any work may be started.”

rules.title: 'Contract Price' heading with full price in dollars and cents
rules.plain_english: The contract must have the heading 'Contract Price' followed by the amount in dollars and cents. The contract amount must include the entire cost (profit, labor and materials) but exclude finance charges.
rules.applies_to: Home improvement contracts over $500
rules.source: 2026 CSLB Law Book, PDF pages 399 and 410
rules.quote: The contract shall be in writing and shall include the agreed contract amount in dollars and cents. The contract amount shall include the entire cost of the contract, including profit, labor, and materials, but excluding finance charges.
rules.notes: Violating 7159.5(a)(1) is also a misdemeanor (7159.5(b)(1)).

rules.title: 'Finance Charge' heading, stated separately from contract price
rules.plain_english: If a finance charge will be charged, the contract must show the heading 'Finance Charge' followed by the amount in dollars and cents, separate from the contract amount.

parameters.condition: a finance charge will be charged

rules.applies_to: Home improvement contracts with contractor financing
rules.source: 2026 CSLB Law Book, PDF pages 400 and 410
rules.quote: If a finance charge will be charged, the heading: “Finance Charge,” followed by the amount in dollars and cents. The finance charge is to be set out separately from the contract amount.

rules.title: Project description and significant materials/equipment; pool plan and scale drawing
rules.plain_english: The contract must have the heading 'Description of the Project and Description of the Significant Materials to be Used and Equipment to be Installed' followed by those descriptions. Swimming pool contracts must also include a plan and scale drawing showing shape, size, dimensions and construction and equipment specs.

parameters.required_heading: Description of the Project and Description of the Significant Materials to be Used and Equipment to be Installed

rules.applies_to: Home improvement and swimming pool contracts
rules.quote: For swimming pools, the project description required under this paragraph also shall include a plan and scale drawing showing the shape, size, dimensions, and the construction and equipment specifications.
rules.notes: Pool contracts not substantially complying with this paragraph are void and unenforceable by the contractor (B&P 7167).

rules.title: 'Downpayment' heading and 12-point bold downpayment limit statement
rules.plain_english: If a downpayment is charged, the contract must show the heading 'Downpayment', a space with the actual downpayment amount, and the 12-point bold statement that the downpayment may not exceed $1,000 or 10% of the contract price, whichever is less.

parameters.amount_field: space where the actual downpayment appears
parameters.required_text: THE DOWNPAYMENT MAY NOT EXCEED $1,000 OR 10 PERCENT OF THE CONTRACT PRICE, WHICHEVER IS LESS.

rules.applies_to: Home improvement and pool contracts that charge a downpayment
rules.quote: “THE DOWNPAYMENT MAY NOT EXCEED $1,000 OR 10 PERCENT OF THE CONTRACT PRICE, WHICHEVER IS LESS.”
rules.notes: Bonded contractors under B&P 7159.5(a)(8) need not include the (C) statement. Pool contracts not substantially complying are void (B&P 7167).

rules.title: Downpayment cap: lesser of $1,000 or 10% of contract amount
rules.plain_english: On a home improvement contract, any downpayment may not be more than $1,000 or 10% of the contract amount, whichever is less. Taking more is a misdemeanor and grounds for discipline, unless the contractor has a registrar-approved bond or joint control covering full performance and payment.

parameters.contract_amount_basis: entire contract amount incl. profit, labor, materials; excluding finance charges
parameters.exempt_if: contractor furnishes registrar-approved performance and payment bond, lien and completion bond, bond equivalent or joint control covering full performance and payment (B&P 7159.5(a)(8))
parameters.violation_penalty: misdemeanor: fine $100-$5,000 and/or up to 1 year county jail (B&P 7159.5(b)(1)); max fine in declared disaster area

rules.applies_to: Home improvement contracts (owner or tenant) by licensed or should-be-licensed contractors
rules.quote: If a downpayment will be charged, the downpayment shall not exceed one thousand dollars ($1,000) or 10 percent of the contract amount, whichever amount is less.
rules.notes: Examples: $8,000 job -> max $800; $25,000 job -> max $1,000. Service and repair contracts (<= $750) may not take any payment before completion (B&P 7159.14(a)(7)).

rules.title: 'Schedule of Progress Payments' with dollar amounts tied to work, plus 12-point bold statement
rules.plain_english: If payments other than the downpayment are due before completion, the contract must include a 'Schedule of Progress Payments' with each payment in dollars and cents tied to specific work, services, materials and equipment, plus a required 12-point bold statement that collecting payment for work not yet done or materials not yet delivered is against the law.

each_payment: references amount of work or services to be performed
references materials and equipment to be supplied
parameters.required_text: The schedule of progress payments must specifically describe each phase of work, including the type and amount of work or services scheduled to be supplied in each phase, along with the amount of each proposed progress payment. IT IS AGAINST THE LAW FOR A CONTRACTOR TO COLLECT PAYMENT FOR WORK NOT YET COMPLETED, OR FOR MATERIALS NOT YET DELIVERED. HOWEVER, A CONTRACTOR MAY REQUIRE A DOWNPAYMENT.

rules.applies_to: Home improvement and pool contracts with progress payments
rules.source: 2026 CSLB Law Book, PDF pages 400 and 410
rules.quote: IT IS AGAINST THE LAW FOR A CONTRACTOR TO COLLECT PAYMENT FOR WORK NOT YET COMPLETED, OR FOR MATERIALS NOT YET DELIVERED. HOWEVER, A CONTRACTOR MAY REQUIRE A DOWNPAYMENT.
rules.notes: Pool contracts not substantially complying with 7159(d)(9) are void (B&P 7167). Bonded contractors under 7159.5(a)(8) are exempt.

rules.title: No payment beyond value of work performed or materials delivered
rules.plain_english: Apart from the allowed downpayment, a home improvement contractor may not request or accept payment that exceeds the value of work performed or materials delivered. This includes advance payments from a lender or financier. Violation is a misdemeanor.

parameters.exempt_if: registrar-approved bond or joint control under B&P 7159.5(a)(8)
parameters.violation_penalty: misdemeanor: fine $100-$5,000 and/or up to 1 year county jail; max fine in declared disaster area (B&P 7159.5(b)(1))

rules.applies_to: Home improvement contractors billing owners or tenants
rules.quote: Except for a downpayment, the contractor shall neither request nor accept payment that exceeds the value of the work performed or material delivered. The prohibition prescribed by this paragraph extends to advance payment in whole or in part from any lender or financier for the performance or sale of home improvement goods or services.
rules.notes: A billing tool can block invoices whose running total exceeds earned value plus the allowed downpayment.

rules.title: Define substantial commencement; 'Approximate Start Date'
rules.plain_english: The contract must describe what counts as substantial commencement of work and include the heading 'Approximate Start Date' with the approximate date work will begin.

required_items: statement describing what constitutes substantial commencement of work
heading: Approximate Start Date
approximate start date

rules.applies_to: Home improvement contracts over $500
rules.quote: (A) A statement that describes what constitutes substantial commencement of work under the contract. (B) The heading: “Approximate Start Date.” (C) The approximate date on which work will be commenced.

rules.title: 'Approximate Completion Date' heading
rules.plain_english: The contract must include the heading 'Approximate Completion Date' followed by the approximate completion date.
rules.applies_to: Home improvement contracts over $500
rules.quote: The estimated completion date of the work shall be referenced in the contract in substantially the following form: (A) The heading: “Approximate Completion Date.” (B) The approximate date of completion.

rules.title: 'List of Documents to be Incorporated into the Contract'
rules.plain_english: If other documents (plans, specs, etc.) are part of the contract, list them under the heading 'List of Documents to be Incorporated into the Contract'.

parameters.required_heading: List of Documents to be Incorporated into the Contract
parameters.condition: if applicable

rules.applies_to: Home improvement contracts over $500
rules.quote: If applicable, the heading: “List of Documents to be Incorporated into the Contract,” followed by the list of documents incorporated into the contract.

rules.title: 'Note About Extra Work and Change Orders' statement
rules.plain_english: The contract must include the heading 'Note About Extra Work and Change Orders' followed by a set statement that change orders are binding only once written and signed before the work starts, and must describe scope, cost change and effect on progress payments.

parameters.required_heading: Note About Extra Work and Change Orders
parameters.required_text: Extra Work and Change Orders become part of the contract once the order is prepared in writing and signed by the parties prior to the commencement of work covered by the new change order. The order must describe the scope of the extra work or change, the cost to be added or subtracted from the contract, and the effect the order will have on the schedule of progress payments.

rules.applies_to: Home improvement contracts over $500
rules.quote: “Extra Work and Change Orders become part of the contract once the order is prepared in writing and signed by the parties prior to the commencement of work covered by the new change order. The order must describe the scope of the extra work or change, the cost to be added or subtracted from the contract, and the effect the order will have on the schedule of progress payments.”

rules.title: Commercial General Liability Insurance (CGL) notice
rules.plain_english: The contract must include a notice headed 'Commercial General Liability Insurance (CGL)' with whichever prescribed statement is true: no CGL, CGL with a named insurer and phone number, self-insured, or LLC with insurance or other security. It may be an attachment if the contract says one is attached.

options.A_no_cgl: (The name on the license or ‘This contractor’) does not carry commercial general liability insurance.
options.B_carries_cgl: (The name on the license or ‘This contractor’) carries commercial general liability insurance written by (the insurance company). You may call (the insurance company) at __________ to check the contractor’s insurance coverage.
options.C_self_insured: (The name on the license or ‘This contractor’) is self-insured.
options.D_llc: (The name on the license or ‘This contractor’) is a limited liability company that carries liability insurance or maintains other security as required by law. You may call (the insurance company or trust company or bank) at ____ to check on the contractor’s insurance coverage or security.

parameters.attachment_allowed_if_contract_states: A notice concerning commercial general liability insurance is attached to this contract.
parameters.selection_rule: whichever statement is both relevant and correct

rules.applies_to: Home improvement contracts over $500
rules.quote: The notice shall include the heading “Commercial General Liability Insurance (CGL),” followed by whichever of the following statements is both relevant and correct:
rules.notes: Generator should pull insurer name and phone from the company's insurance records.

rules.title: Workers' Compensation Insurance notice
rules.plain_english: The contract must include a notice headed 'Workers' Compensation Insurance' stating either that the contractor has no employees and is exempt, or that it carries workers' comp for all employees. It may be an attachment if the contract says so.

options.A_no_employees: (The name on the license or ‘This contractor’) has no employees and is exempt from workers’ compensation requirements.
options.B_carries_wc: (The name on the license or ‘This contractor’) carries workers’ compensation insurance for all employees.

parameters.attachment_allowed_if_contract_states: A notice concerning workers’ compensation insurance is attached to this contract.

rules.applies_to: Home improvement contracts over $500
rules.quote: The notice shall include the heading “Workers’ Compensation Insurance” followed by whichever of the following statements is correct: (A) “(The name on the license or ‘This contractor’) has no employees and is exempt from workers’ compensation requirements.” (B) “(The name on the license or ‘This contractor’) carries workers’ compensation insurance for all employees.”

rules.title: Notice to buyer about extra/change-order work
rules.plain_english: The contract must tell the buyer that (A) they cannot require extra or change-order work without written authorization before it starts, (B) a change order is not enforceable unless it states scope, price change, and effect on progress payments or completion date in writing before the work starts, and (C) the contractor's noncompliance does not bar recovery for work done under unjust-enrichment remedies.

required_statements: buyer may not require extra or change-order work without written authorization prior to commencement of that work
change order not enforceable against buyer unless it identifies in writing, before the work: scope of work; amount added or subtracted; effect on progress payments or completion date
contractor's failure to comply does not preclude recovery for work performed under legal or equitable remedies preventing unjust enrichment

rules.applies_to: Home improvement contracts over $500
rules.quote: A statement informing the buyer that extra work or a change order is not enforceable against a buyer unless the change order also identifies all of the following in writing prior to the commencement of work covered by the new change order: (i) The scope of work encompassed by the order. (ii) The amount to be added or subtracted from the contract.
rules.notes: No exact wording prescribed; content must cover these three statements.

rules.title: Mechanics Lien Warning (home improvement contract version)
rules.plain_english: Every home improvement contract must include the statutory 'Mechanics Lien Warning' explaining liens, 20-day preliminary notices, how to protect against liens with a subcontractor/supplier list and joint checks, and CSLB contact information.

parameters.required_text:
MECHANICS LIEN WARNING:
Anyone who helps improve your property, but who is not paid, may record what is called a mechanics lien on your property. A mechanics lien is a claim, like a mortgage or home equity loan, made against your property and recorded with the county recorder.
Even if you pay your contractor in full, unpaid subcontractors, suppliers, and laborers who helped to improve your property may record mechanics liens and sue you in court to foreclose the lien. If a court finds the lien is valid, you could be forced to pay twice or have a court officer sell your home to pay the lien. Liens can also affect your credit.
To preserve their right to record a lien, each subcontractor and material supplier must provide you with a document called a ‘Preliminary Notice.’ This notice is not a lien. The purpose of the notice is to let you know that the person who sends you the notice has the right to record a lien on your property if they are not paid.
BE CAREFUL. The Preliminary Notice can be sent up to 20 days after the subcontractor starts work or the supplier provides material. This can be a big problem if you pay your contractor before you have received the Preliminary Notices.
You will not get Preliminary Notices from your prime contractor or from laborers who work on your project. The law assumes that you already know they are improving your property.
PROTECT YOURSELF FROM LIENS. You can protect yourself from liens by getting a list from your contractor of all the subcontractors and material suppliers that work on your project. Find out from your contractor when these subcontractors started work and when these suppliers delivered goods or materials. Then wait 20 days, paying attention to the Preliminary Notices you receive.
PAY WITH JOINT CHECKS. One way to protect yourself is to pay with a joint check. When your contractor tells you it is time to pay for the work of a subcontractor or supplier who has provided you with a Preliminary Notice, write a joint check payable to both the contractor and the subcontractor or material supplier.
For other ways to prevent liens, visit CSLB’s internet website at www.cslb.ca.gov or call CSLB at 800-321-CSLB (2752).
REMEMBER, IF YOU DO NOTHING, YOU RISK HAVING A LIEN PLACED ON YOUR HOME. This can mean that you may have to pay twice, or face the forced sale of your home to pay what you owe.

rules.applies_to: Home improvement contracts over $500 (except bonded contractors under 7159.5(a)(8))
rules.quote: BE CAREFUL. The Preliminary Notice can be sent up to 20 days after the subcontractor starts work or the supplier provides material. This can be a big problem if you pay your contractor before you have received the Preliminary Notices.
rules.notes: In the book the phone number line is printed as '800-321-CSLB (2752) .REMEMBER' (typesetting); the period placement here is normalized. The B&P 7164 single-family-dwelling version has slightly different wording.

rules.title: 'Information about the Contractors State License Board (CSLB)' notice in 12-point
rules.plain_english: Every home improvement contract must include the prescribed CSLB information notice in at least 12-point type, telling the buyer to use licensed contractors, that complaints are usually due within four years, and how to contact CSLB.

parameters.required_text:
Information about the Contractors State License Board (CSLB): CSLB is the state consumer protection agency that licenses and regulates construction contractors.
Contact CSLB for information about the licensed contractor you are considering, including information about disclosable complaints, disciplinary actions, and civil judgments that are reported to CSLB.
Use only licensed contractors. If you file a complaint against a licensed contractor within the legal deadline (usually four years), CSLB has authority to investigate the complaint. If you use an unlicensed contractor, CSLB may not be able to help you resolve your complaint. Your only remedy may be in civil court, and you may be liable for damages arising out of any injuries to the unlicensed contractor or the unlicensed contractor’s employees.
For more information:
Visit CSLB’s internet website at www.cslb.ca.gov
Call CSLB at 800-321-CSLB (2752)
Write CSLB at P.O. Box 26000, Sacramento, CA 95826.

rules.applies_to: Home improvement contracts over $500
rules.quote: Use only licensed contractors. If you file a complaint against a licensed contractor within the legal deadline (usually four years), CSLB has authority to investigate the complaint.
rules.notes: Bold is not required for this notice; 12-point is.

rules.title: 'Three-Day Right to Cancel' notice (five-day for seniors)
rules.plain_english: Unless the contract was negotiated at the contractor's place of business, is a disaster-repair contract (7-day notice), or is by an alarm company licensee following Civil Code 1689.5-1689.7, the buyer must get the prescribed 'Three-Day Right to Cancel' notice; for a buyer 65 or older it becomes the 'Five-Day Right to Cancel'. The buyer can cancel by email, mail, fax or delivery by midnight of the 3rd (or 5th) business day after receiving the signed contract.

parameters.deadline_rule: midnight of the Nth business day after buyer received a signed and dated copy of the contract including this notice
cancel_methods: delivery to contractor's place of business
exceptions: negotiated at the contractor's place of business
subject to the Seven-Day Right to Cancel (disaster repair)
Alarm Company Act licensee complying with Civil Code 1689.5, 1689.6 and 1689.7
parameters.required_text:
Three-Day Right to Cancel
You, the buyer, have the right to cancel this contract within three business days. You may cancel by emailing, mailing, faxing, or delivering a written notice to the contractor at the contractor’s place of business by midnight of the third business day after you received a signed and dated copy of the contract that includes this notice. Include your name, your address, and the date you received the signed copy of the contract and this notice.
If you cancel, the contractor must return to you anything you paid within 10 days of receiving the notice of cancellation. For your part, you must make available to the contractor at your residence, in substantially as good condition as you received them, goods delivered to you under this contract or sale. Or, you may, if you wish, comply with the contractor’s instructions on how to return the goods at the contractor’s expense and risk. If you do make the goods available to the contractor and the contractor does not pick them up within 20 days of the date of your notice of cancellation, you may keep them without any further obligation. If you fail to make the goods available to the contractor, or if you agree to return the goods to the contractor and fail to do so, then you remain liable for performance of all obligations under the contract.
parameters.senior_substitution: replace “three” with “five” and “third” with “fifth” (title becomes Five-Day Right to Cancel)

rules.applies_to: Home improvement contracts over $500 not excepted
rules.quote: You, the buyer, have the right to cancel this contract within three business days. You may cancel by emailing, mailing, faxing, or delivering a written notice to the contractor at the contractor’s place of business by midnight of the third business day after you received a signed and dated copy of the contract that includes this notice.
rules.effective: Section amended effective January 1, 2026; five-day senior right applies to contracts entered into on or after January 1, 2021
rules.notes: Business day definition is in Civil Code 9 / 1689.5 (not in this excerpt). A deadline calculator must skip non-business days.

rules.title: Right-to-cancel notice format: 12-pt bold, by signature, signed, same language; attachment checkbox
rules.plain_english: The 3/5/7-day cancellation notices must be in at least 12-point bold type, placed right next to the owner's signature space, signed and dated by the owner, and written in the same language as the oral sales presentation (for example Spanish). The notice may be attached instead if the contract has a 12-point bold checkbox statement the buyer initials.

parameters.placement: immediate proximity to space reserved for owner's signature
parameters.language: same as principally used in any oral sales presentation

attachment_checkbox_text.senior: The law requires that the contractor give you a notice explaining your right to cancel. Initial the checkbox if the contractor has given you a ‛Notice of the Five-Day Right to Cancel.’
attachment_checkbox_text.standard: The law requires that the contractor give you a notice explaining your right to cancel. Initial the checkbox if the contractor has given you a ‛Notice of the Three-Day Right to Cancel.’
attachment_checkbox_text.disaster_seven_day: The law requires that the contractor give you a notice explaining your right to cancel. Initial the checkbox if the contractor has given you a ‘Notice of the Seven-Day Right to Cancel.’

rules.applies_to: Home improvement contracts requiring a right-to-cancel notice
rules.quote: (i) The text of the notice is at least 12-point boldface type. (ii) The notice is in immediate proximity to a space reserved for the owner’s signature. (iii) The owner acknowledges receipt of the notice by signing and dating the notice form in the signature space. (iv) The notice is written in the same language, e.g., Spanish, as that principally used in any oral sales presentation.

rules.title: Completed 'Notice of Cancellation' form in duplicate, easily detachable
rules.plain_english: The right-to-cancel notice must be accompanied by a completed 'Notice of Cancellation' form in duplicate, attached to the contract and easily detachable, in the same language as the contract, with the transaction date, seller name, seller's business address and cancellation deadline filled in.

parameters.language: same as used in the contract
fill_in_fields: address of seller's place of business
parameters.required_text:
Notice of Cancellation
[enter date of transaction] (Date)
You may cancel this transaction, without any penalty or obligation, within three business days from the above date.
If you cancel, any property traded in, any payments made by you under the contract or sale, and any negotiable instrument executed by you will be returned within 10 days following receipt by the seller of your cancellation notice, and any security interest arising out of the transaction will be canceled.
If you cancel, you must make available to the seller at your residence, in substantially as good condition as when received, any goods delivered to you under this contract or sale, or you may, if you wish, comply with the instructions of the seller regarding the return shipment of the goods at the seller’s expense and risk.
If you do make the goods available to the seller and the seller does not pick them up within 20 days of the date of your notice of cancellation, you may retain or dispose of the goods without any further obligation. If you fail to make the goods available to the seller, or if you agree to return the goods to the seller and fail to do so, then you remain liable for performance of all obligations under the contract.
To cancel this transaction, mail or deliver a signed and dated copy of this cancellation notice, or any other written notice, or send a telegram to [name of seller], at [address of seller’s place of business] not later than midnight of [Date].
I hereby cancel this transaction. [Date]
[Buyer’s signature]

rules.applies_to: Home improvement contracts requiring a right-to-cancel notice
rules.quote: The notice shall be accompanied by a completed form in duplicate, captioned “Notice of Cancellation,” which also shall be attached to the agreement or offer to purchase and be easily detachable, and which shall contain the following statement written in the same language, e.g., Spanish, as used in the contract:
rules.notes: Bracketed placeholders replace the blank lines and captions printed in the book (/enter date of transaction/, /name of seller/, /address of seller’s place of business/).

rules.title: Five business days to cancel for buyers 65+ (contracts on/after Jan 1, 2021)
rules.plain_english: For a buyer who is a senior citizen (65 or older), the home improvement cancellation period is five business days instead of three, and the notice and Notice of Cancellation form must say 'five'/'fifth'. This applies to contracts entered into on or after January 1, 2021.
rules.applies_to: Home improvement contracts with a senior citizen buyer
rules.source: 2026 CSLB Law Book, PDF pages 404, 406 and 408
rules.quote: References to “three” and “third” in the notice set forth in clause (i) shall be changed to “five” and “fifth,” respectively, for a buyer who is a senior citizen.
rules.effective: Contracts entered into on or after January 1, 2021
rules.notes: The text does not say how to handle multiple buyers where only one is a senior; using the five-day notice is the conservative choice (interpretation, not stated in text).

rules.title: 'Seven-Day Right to Cancel' for declared-emergency disaster repairs
rules.plain_english: For contracts to repair or restore homes damaged by a sudden or catastrophic event with a state of emergency declared by the President or Governor, or a local emergency declared by a city or county, the buyer must get the 'Seven-Day Right to Cancel' notice and may cancel by midnight of the 7th business day after receiving the signed contract.

parameters.trigger: repair or restoration of residential premises damaged by sudden or catastrophic event
declaration_sources: executive officer or governing body of a city, county or city and county (local emergency)
cancel_methods: delivery to contractor's place of business
parameters.format: same as 3-day notice: 12-pt bold, by owner's signature, signed and dated, same language as oral presentation
parameters.required_text:
Seven-Day Right to Cancel
You, the buyer, have the right to cancel this contract within seven business days. You may cancel by emailing, mailing, faxing, or delivering a written notice to the contractor at the contractor’s place of business by midnight of the seventh business day after you received a signed and dated copy of the contract that includes this notice. Include your name, your address, and the date you received the signed copy of the contract and this notice.
If you cancel, the contractor must return to you anything you paid within 10 days of receiving the notice of cancellation. For your part, you must make available to the contractor at your residence, in substantially as good condition as you received them, goods delivered to you under this contract or sale. Or, you may, if you wish, comply with the contractor’s instructions on how to return the goods at the contractor’s expense and risk. If you do make the goods available to the contractor and the contractor does not pick them up within 20 days of the date of your notice of cancellation, you may keep them without any further obligation. If you fail to make the goods available to the contractor, or if you agree to return the goods to the contractor and fail to do so, then you remain liable for performance of all obligations under the contract.

rules.applies_to: Disaster-repair home improvement contracts
rules.quote: The following notice entitled “Seven-Day Right to Cancel” shall be provided to the buyer for any contract that is written for the repair or restoration of residential premises damaged by any sudden or catastrophic event for which a state of emergency has been declared by the President of the United States or the Governor, or for which a local emergency has been declared
rules.notes: Unlike the 3-day notice, the 7-day notice has no place-of-business exception in the text. Note also the place-of-business exception applies only to the 3/5-day notice.

rules.title: After cancellation: refund within 10 days; goods kept if not picked up in 20 days
rules.plain_english: When a buyer cancels within the right-to-cancel period, the contractor must return everything the buyer paid (and any trade-ins and negotiable instruments, and cancel security interests) within 10 days of receiving the cancellation notice. If the buyer makes delivered goods available and the contractor does not pick them up within 20 days of the cancellation notice, the buyer may keep them.

parameters.refund_measured_from: contractor's receipt of the notice of cancellation
parameters.goods_measured_from: date of buyer's notice of cancellation
parameters.consequence_if_not_picked_up: buyer may keep or dispose of goods without further obligation

rules.applies_to: Home improvement contractors receiving a cancellation
rules.quote: If you cancel, the contractor must return to you anything you paid within 10 days of receiving the notice of cancellation.
rules.notes: Rule text is drawn from the mandatory notice language; underlying rights are in Civil Code 1689.5-1689.14 (Appendix, not in this excerpt).

rules.title: Door-to-door sale secured by lien on home: 18-point bold warning on separate page
rules.plain_english: If a door-to-door home improvement goods or services contract includes or is secured by a lien on real property, it must come with a separate, signed and dated 18-point bold 'WARNING TO BUYER' page stating the home is being put up as security. The buyer gets a copy at signing. Without it, the security interest is void.

parameters.trigger: door-to-door sale of home improvement goods or services that contains or is secured by a lien on real property
parameters.required_text: WARNING TO BUYER: IF YOU SIGN THE CONTRACT WHICH ACCOMPANIES THIS NOTICE, YOU WILL BE PUTTING UP YOUR HOME AS SECURITY. THIS MEANS THAT YOUR HOME COULD BE SOLD WITHOUT YOUR PERMISSION AND WITHOUT ANY COURT ACTION IF YOU MISS ANY PAYMENT REQUIRED BY THIS CONTRACT.
exclusions: contracts subject to Civil Code 1801 et seq. (Unruh Act)
mechanics liens under Civil Code 8400 et seq.

rules.applies_to: Contractors and salespersons selling door-to-door with real-property security
rules.quote: “WARNING TO BUYER: IF YOU SIGN THE CONTRACT WHICH ACCOMPANIES THIS NOTICE, YOU WILL BE PUTTING UP YOUR HOME AS SECURITY. THIS MEANS THAT YOUR HOME COULD BE SOLD WITHOUT YOUR PERMISSION AND WITHOUT ANY COURT ACTION IF YOU MISS ANY PAYMENT REQUIRED BY THIS CONTRACT.”
rules.notes: The 'Unruh Act' label for Civil Code 1801 et seq. is a common name, not stated in the text.

rules.title: No security interest in real property on contracts of $5,000 or less
rules.plain_english: A home improvement goods or services contract worth $5,000 or less may not include a security interest in real property, other than a mechanics lien or interest arising by law. Any such lien is void.

allowed: other interest arising by operation of law

rules.applies_to: Home improvement goods or services contracts
rules.quote: No home improvement goods or services contract of a value of five thousand dollars ($5,000) or less shall provide for a security interest in real property, except for a mechanic’s lien or other interest in property that arises by operation of law. Any lien in violation of this subdivision is void and unenforceable.

rules.title: Mortgage-funded jobs over $5,000: lender pays by borrower/joint check or escrow
rules.plain_english: When proceeds of a loan secured by a mortgage on real property fund a home improvement contract over $5,000, the lender may pay the contractor only by an instrument payable to the borrower or jointly to the borrower and contractor, or, if the borrower chooses, through a third-party escrow under a written agreement signed by borrower, lender and contractor before disbursement.

allowed_payment_methods: instrument payable jointly to borrower and contractor
third-party escrow at borrower's election, per written agreement signed by borrower, lender and contractor prior to disbursement

rules.applies_to: Lenders, contractors and owners on mortgage-financed home improvement jobs
rules.quote: the person or entity making the loan shall only pay a contractor under the home improvement goods or services contract from the proceeds of the loan by either of the following methods: (1) By an instrument payable to the borrower or jointly to the borrower and the contractor.

rules.title: 7159.2 violations: actual damages, treble contract price, $5,000 senior/disabled award, attorney fees
rules.plain_english: Violating 7159.2 makes the violator liable for the borrower's actual damages. Intentional or pattern violations add liability of three times the contract price. Seniors or disabled persons may also be awarded up to $5,000, and a prevailing plaintiff gets court costs and attorney's fees.

parameters.defendant_attorney_fees: only if plaintiff's action was not in good faith

rules.applies_to: Contractors and lenders on home improvement contracts with real-property security
rules.quote: Any person or entity who intentionally or as a pattern or practice violates any provision of this section shall be additionally liable for three times the contract price for the home improvement.

rules.title: Furnish unconditional lien releases on request; owner may withhold payment until received
rules.plain_english: After each payment by the owner and before any further payment, the contractor must, if asked, obtain and give the owner full and unconditional lien releases for the paid portion of the work. The owner may withhold all further payments until those releases are provided.

parameters.trigger: any payment by the person contracting for home improvement
parameters.timing: prior to any further payment
parameters.release_type: full and unconditional release from any potential lien claimant claim or mechanics lien (Civil Code 8400, 8404)

rules.applies_to: Home improvement contractors and owners
rules.quote: Upon any payment by the person contracting for home improvement, and prior to any further payment being made, the contractor shall, if requested, obtain and furnish to the person a full and unconditional release from any potential lien claimant claim or mechanics lien ... The person contracting for home improvement may withhold all further payments until these releases are furnished.
rules.notes: Releases must cover subs and suppliers ('any potential lien claimant'), not just the prime.

rules.title: Salesperson commission paid pro rata with contractor's payment schedule
rules.plain_english: If the contract provides for paying a salesperson's commission out of the contract price, the commission must be paid pro rata, in proportion to the payments made to the contractor under the payment schedule.

parameters.rule: commission paid in proportion to schedule of payments made to contractor by disbursing party

rules.applies_to: Home improvement contracts paying salesperson commissions from the contract price
rules.quote: If the contract provides for a payment of a salesperson’s commission out of the contract price, that payment shall be made on a pro rata basis in proportion to the schedule of payments made to the contractor by the disbursing party in accordance with paragraph (4).
rules.notes: The formula is an interpretation of 'pro rata'; the statute gives no formula.

rules.title: Bonded/joint-control contractors exempt from downpayment and progress-payment limits
rules.plain_english: A contractor that furnishes a registrar-approved performance and payment bond, lien and completion bond, bond equivalent or joint control covering full performance and payment is exempt from the downpayment cap, progress-payment schedule and no-payment-ahead rules, may accept payment before completion, and need not include the downpayment statement, progress-payment details or Mechanics Lien Warning. A licensee must be actively licensed for at least two years before applying for a blanket performance and payment bond approval.

exempt_from: B&P 7159.5(a)(5) no payment ahead of work
parameters.blanket_bond_regulation: 16 CCR 858.2 as it read on January 1, 2016

rules.applies_to: Home improvement contractors using blanket bonds or joint control
rules.quote: Notwithstanding any other law, a licensee shall be licensed in this state in an active status for not less than two years prior to submitting an Application for Approval of Blanket Performance and Payment Bond as provided in Section 858.2 of Title 16 of the California Code of Regulations as it read on January 1, 2016.
rules.notes: Bond amounts are not stated in this excerpt.

rules.title: Unwritten contract, excess downpayment or payment ahead of work: misdemeanor $100-$5,000
rules.plain_english: Violating the written-contract/price rule, the downpayment cap, or the no-payment-ahead-of-work rule is a misdemeanor punishable by a $100 to $5,000 fine and/or up to one year in county jail. In a declared natural-disaster area, the court must impose the maximum fine.

parameters.disaster_area_rule: court shall impose the maximum fine ($5,000)
disaster_triggers: Presidential emergency or major disaster declaration

rules.applies_to: Licensees, persons required to be licensed, agents and salespersons
rules.quote: A violation of paragraph (1), (3), or (5) of subdivision (a) by a licensee or a person subject to be licensed under this chapter, or by their agent or salesperson, is a misdemeanor punishable by a fine of not less than one hundred dollars ($100) nor more than five thousand dollars ($5,000), or by imprisonment in a county jail not exceeding one year, or by both that fine and imprisonment.
rules.effective: Operative July 1, 2021; amended effective January 1, 2022 and 2023

rules.title: Criminal filing deadline for HIC violations: 4 years (unlicensed) / 2 years (licensed)
rules.plain_english: Criminal charges for 7159.5 violations must be filed within four years for an unlicensed person who should be licensed, or within two years for a licensee, counted from the contract date, or from the buyer's first payment if the contract was not written. These limits do not apply to CSLB administrative actions.

parameters.measured_from: date of the contract; if not in writing, date buyer makes first payment

rules.applies_to: Contractors facing prosecution for home improvement contract violations
rules.quote: An indictment or information against a person who is licensed under this chapter shall be brought, or a criminal complaint filed, for a violation of this section ... within two years from the date of the contract or, if the contract is not reduced to writing, from the date the buyer makes the first payment to the contractor.

rules.title: Disaster-repair fraud under 7159.5: full restitution plus fine $500-$25,000
rules.plain_english: A person who violates 7159.5 in a scheme to defraud an owner or tenant over natural-disaster repairs must pay full restitution (based on ability to pay) and may be fined $500 to $25,000 on top of jail.

parameters.restitution: full, based on ability to pay

rules.applies_to: Contractors doing natural-disaster repairs
rules.quote: In addition to full restitution, and imprisonment authorized by this section, the court may impose a fine of not less than five hundred dollars ($500) nor more than twenty-five thousand dollars ($25,000), based upon the defendant’s ability to pay.

rules.title: Change order enforceable only if it states scope, price change and schedule/payment effect
rules.plain_english: An extra-work or change order cannot be enforced against the buyer unless it states the scope of work, the amount added or subtracted, and the effect on progress payments or the completion date. The buyer cannot require extra work without written authorization. The contractor can still seek payment for work done under unjust-enrichment remedies.

required_change_order_fields: scope of work encompassed by the order
amount to be added or subtracted from the contract
effect on progress payments or completion date

rules.applies_to: Home improvement contractors and buyers
rules.quote: An extra work or change order is not enforceable against a buyer unless the change order sets forth all of the following: (1) The scope of work encompassed by the order. (2) The amount to be added or subtracted from the contract. (3) The effect the order will make in the progress payments or the completion date.
rules.notes: Combine with 7159(c)(5)/(d): change orders must also be signed before the changed work begins, and if subs are used, carry the subcontractor disclaimer (7159(c)(7)(C)).

rules.title: Fire alarm (<= $500) exemption: certification statement, address, contractor data, copies
rules.plain_english: To use the 7159 exemption for a fire alarm sold with an alarm system, the licensee must follow the alarm contract rules (B&P 7599.54) and Civil Code 1689.5-1689.7, sign a certification that all costs to make the fire alarm operable are $500 or less, include the residence address and the contractor's name, business address and license number, and give the customer exact copies.

parameters.required_certification_text: All costs attributable to making the fire alarm system operable for the residence identified by this document, including sale and installation costs, do not exceed five hundred dollars ($500).
parameters.separate_document_certification_text: I certify that all statements and representations made by me in this document are true and accurate.
required_fields: contractor name, business address and license number as in CSLB records
parameters.copies: exact copy of all documents to the party contracting for installation

rules.applies_to: Licensees selling/installing fire alarms with alarm systems
rules.quote: “All costs attributable to making the fire alarm system operable for the residence identified by this document, including sale and installation costs, do not exceed five hundred dollars ($500).”

rules.title: Keep fire alarm exemption documents 5 years; produce within 30 days
rules.plain_english: All fire alarm exemption documents must be kept for five years and given to CSLB within 30 days of a written request. Failing to produce them is cause for discipline and creates a presumption that 7159 was violated.

failure_consequences: presumption of violation of B&P 7159 unless rebutted within board's timeframe

rules.applies_to: Licensees using the fire alarm exemption
rules.quote: All documents required pursuant to this section shall be retained by the licensee for a period of five years in accordance with the provisions of Section 7111, and shall be made available to the board within 30 days of a written request.

rules.title: Service and repair contract: <= $750, buyer-initiated, no upsell, no payment until done
rules.plain_english: A service and repair contract is a home improvement agreement of $750 or less where the buyer called the contractor, the contractor sells only what is reasonably needed to fix that problem, and no payment is due or accepted until the work is completed (the problem fully corrected and, if applicable, approved by the building department).

conditions: buyer initiated contact to request the work
no goods/services beyond those reasonably necessary for the particular problem
no payment due or accepted until work completed
parameters.work_completed_definition: all conditions that caused the call fully corrected and, if applicable, building department accepted and approved the corrective work

rules.applies_to: Residential service and repair work
rules.quote: (A) The contract amount is seven hundred fifty dollars ($750) or less. (B) The prospective buyer initiated contact with the contractor to request the work. ... (D) No payment is due, or accepted by the contractor, until the work is completed.
rules.notes: Contract selector logic: if all four conditions are true -> service and repair form; otherwise -> the full 7159(c), (d) and (e) requirements and Civil Code 1689.6/1689.7 rescission rights apply regardless of the aggregate contract price, for any contract written under 7159.10(a) or presented as a service and repair contract (7159.10(b)). A contract never presented as service and repair falls under 7159 only if over $500 (7159(b)).
rules.correction: Note said a non-conforming contract goes to the full 7159 contract "(if over $500) per 7159.10(b)". 7159.10(b) says the 7159(c)-(e) requirements apply "regardless of the aggregate contract price" to any contract written or presented as a service and repair contract. Note fixed. The four conditions and $750 cap are correct.

rules.title: Non-conforming 'service and repair' contract must meet full HIC rules regardless of price
rules.plain_english: If a contract is presented as a service and repair contract but does not meet all four conditions, the full home improvement contract requirements of 7159(c), (d) and (e), including cancellation rights, apply regardless of the contract price. parameters.required_text:
YOUR RIGHTS TO CANCEL BEFORE WORK BEGINS
(A) You, the buyer, have the right to cancel this contract until:
1. You receive a copy of this contract signed and dated by you and the contractor; and
2. The contractor starts work.
(B) However, even if the work has begun you, the buyer, may still cancel the contract for any of the reasons specified in items 1 through 4 of this paragraph. If any of these reasons occur, you may cancel the contract within three business days of signing the contract for normal service and repairs, or within seven business days of signing a contract to repair or correct conditions resulting from any sudden or catastrophic event for which a state of emergency has been declared by the President of the United States or the Governor, or for which a local emergency has been declared by the executive officer or governing body of any city, county, or city and county:
1. You may cancel the contract if the price, including all labor and materials, is more than seven hundred fifty dollars ($750).
2. You may cancel the contract if you did not initiate the contact with the contractor to request the work.
3. You may cancel the contract if the contractor sold you goods or services beyond those reasonably necessary to take care of the particular problem that caused you to contact the contractor.
4. You may cancel the contract if the payment was due or the contractor accepted any money before the work was complete.
(C) If any of these reasons for canceling occurred, you may cancel the contract as specified under paragraph (B) above by e-mailing, mailing, faxing, or delivering a written notice to the contractor at the contractor’s place of business within three business days or, if applicable, seven business days of the date you received a signed and dated copy of this contract. Include your name, your address, and the date you received a signed copy of the contract and this notice.
If you cancel, the contractor must return to you anything you paid within 10 days of receiving the notice of cancellation. For your part, you must make available to the contractor at your residence, in substantially as good condition as you received it, any goods delivered to you under this contract. Or, you may, if you wish, comply with the contractor’s instructions on how to return the goods at the contractor’s expense and risk. If you make the goods available to the contractor and the contractor does not pick them up within 20 days of the date of your notice of cancellation, you may keep them without any further obligation. If you fail to make the goods available to the contractor, or if you agree to return the goods to the contractor and fail to do so, then you remain liable for performance of all obligations under the contract.

parameters.required_text:
MECHANICS LIEN WARNING:
Anyone who helps improve your property, but who is not paid, may record what is called a mechanics lien on your property. A mechanics lien is a claim, like a mortgage or home equity loan, made against your property and recorded with the county recorder.
Even if you pay your contractor in full, unpaid subcontractors, suppliers, and laborers who helped to improve your property may record mechanics liens and sue you in court to foreclose the lien. If a court finds the lien is valid, you could be forced to pay twice or have a court officer sell your home to pay the lien. Liens can also affect your credit.
To preserve their right to record a lien, each subcontractor and material supplier must provide you with a document called a ‘Preliminary Notice.’ This notice is not a lien. The purpose of the notice is to let you know that the person who sends you the notice has the right to record a lien on your property if he or she is not paid.
BE CAREFUL. The Preliminary Notice can be sent up to 20 days after the subcontractor starts work or the supplier provides material. This can be a big problem if you pay your contractor before you have received the Preliminary Notices.
You will not get Preliminary Notices from your prime contractor or other persons you contract with directly or from laborers who work on your project. The law assumes that you already know they are improving your property.
PROTECT YOURSELF FROM LIENS. You can protect yourself from liens by getting a list from your contractor of all the subcontractors and material suppliers that work on your project. Find out from your contractor when these subcontractors started work and when these suppliers delivered goods or materials. Then wait 20 days, paying attention to the Preliminary Notices you receive.
PAY WITH JOINT CHECKS. One way to protect yourself is to pay with a joint check. When your contractor tells you it is time to pay for the work of a subcontractor or supplier who has provided you with a Preliminary Notice, write a joint check payable to both the contractor and the subcontractor or material supplier.
For other ways to prevent liens, visit CSLB’s Web site at www.cslb.ca.gov or call CSLB at 800-321-CSLB (2752).
REMEMBER, IF YOU DO NOTHING, YOU RISK HAVING A LIEN PLACED ON YOUR HOME. This can mean that you may have to pay twice, or face the forced sale of your home to pay what you owe.

rules.applies_to: Single-family dwelling construction contracts (owner retains 1+ year)
rules.quote: You will not get Preliminary Notices from your prime contractor or other persons you contract with directly or from laborers who work on your project. The law assumes that you already know they are improving your property.
rules.notes: Differences from the 7159(e)(4) version: 'if he or she is not paid', 'or other persons you contract with directly', and 'CSLB’s Web site'. Use the correct version per contract type.

rules.title: Single-family dwelling contract: legible, describe incorporated documents, signed copy before work
rules.plain_english: The single-family home contract must be legible and clearly describe any other documents incorporated into it, and before any work starts the owner must receive a copy of the written agreement signed by the contractor. Other agreed terms may be added.
rules.applies_to: Single-family dwelling construction contracts
rules.quote: The writing shall be legible and shall clearly describe any other document which is to be incorporated into the contract. Prior to commencement of any work, the owner shall be furnished a copy of the written agreement, signed by the contractor.

rules.title: Single-family dwelling contract: bond notice in 10-point bold or all caps near signatures
rules.plain_english: Near the owner's and contractor's signatures, the single-family home contract must state, in at least 10-point bold or all capital letters, that the owner can require the contractor to have a performance and payment bond and that the owner may pay for the bond.

parameters.placement: in close proximity to signatures of owner and contractor
parameters.format: at least 10-point boldface type OR all capital letters
content: owner has right to require contractor to have a performance and payment bond
expense of the bond may be borne by the owner

rules.applies_to: Single-family dwelling construction contracts
rules.quote: Every contract subject to the provisions of this section shall contain, in close proximity to the signatures of the owner and contractor, a notice in at least 10-point boldface type or in all capital letters, stating that the owner has the right to require the contractor to have a performance and payment bond and that the expense of the bond may be borne by the owner.

rules.title: Lender-financed pool: conditions to start before loan rescission period ends
rules.plain_english: For a pool financed by a third-party lender, work may start before the loan rescission period ends only if the lender has agreed in writing to finance the maximum estimated cost, provided written TILA loan terms, agreed to hold the offer at least 15 days after excavation is complete (and to lend a lesser amount on same or better terms if cost is lower), and the buyer, at least three business days after receiving these writings, signs a separate request to start.

lender_written_commitments: if cost after excavation is lower, offer lesser amount on same security at APR and monthly payment not exceeding disclosed
parameters.wait_measured_from: buyer's receipt of all lender writings

rules.applies_to: Swimming pool contractors with third-party lender financing
rules.quote: The lender’s written agreement shall state the duration of the offer, which shall not be less than 15 days following the completion of the excavation of the swimming pool.
rules.notes: Business day has the meaning in Civil Code 9 (7165(h)).

rules.title: Pool early-start NOTICE and REQUEST form (separate document, 10/12-point)
rules.plain_english: The buyer's request to start pool construction early must be on a separate document from the pool contract containing the statutory NOTICE in at least 10-point type (one paragraph in 12-point), with the contractor inserting the first date the buyer may sign (the third business day after receiving the lender writings), and a signed REQUEST. The contractor must give the buyer a copy of the signed request at signing; it applies to each buyer who signs the contract or loan documents.

parameters.twelve_point_paragraph: If you sign this request, the contractor will be permitted to immediately begin performance of the contract... lien against your property for the value of the labor and materials provided.
parameters.contractor_inserts: third business day after buyer receives writings described in 7165(a), (b) and (c)
parameters.applies_to_each_buyer: each buyer who signs the pool contract or the note/security instrument
parameters.required_text:
NOTICE
Under the law, this contract is not enforceable until:
(1) A third party agrees to make a loan to finance the construction cost of the swimming pool;
(2) You agree to accept the loan; and
(3) You do not cancel the loan within the period prescribed for cancellation under the federal Truth in Lending Act or Regulation Z (usually three business days after the loan is consummated).
Until the cancellation period is over, the contractor cannot deliver any materials or perform any services except preliminary services for which no mechanic’s lien can be claimed.
However, as an alternative to the above, you can ask the contractor to start work and deliver materials before the cancellation period on the loan is over if all of the following have occurred:
(1) The lender has agreed, in writing, to provide you with financing for up to the maximum estimated construction cost of the swimming pool.
(2) The lender has provided you with a written copy of the terms and conditions of a loan for the maximum estimated cost, including the annual percentage rate, the finance charge, the amount financed, the total of payments, the payment schedule, and a description of the security interest to be taken by the lender.
(3) The lender has agreed in writing to offer these terms and conditions for a period not less than 15 days following completion of the excavation of the swimming pool.
(4) Three business days have passed since you received the writing mentioned in paragraphs (1), (2), and (3), and you then sign a copy of this form to request that the contractor begin construction of the swimming pool before the cancellation period on your loan is over.
The first day you can sign the request for the contractor to begin construction of the swimming pool is [contractor to insert third business day after buyer receives writings described in subdivisions (a), (b), and (c)]
If you sign this request, the contractor will be permitted to immediately begin performance of the contract, and if the contractor is not paid in accordance with the terms of the contract, he or she may file a lien against your property for the value of the labor and materials provided. [This paragraph shall be printed in 12-point type.]
REQUEST
I/we request that the contractor immediately start construction of the swimming pool.
[Date]
Buyer(s)

rules.applies_to: Swimming pool contractors with third-party lender financing
rules.quote: The request of a buyer, described in subdivision (d), shall be set forth on a document separate and apart from the swimming pool contract and shall contain the following notice in at least 10-point type unless otherwise stated:
rules.notes: Date calculator: earliest_request_date = add_business_days(receipt_of_lender_writings, 3) using Civil Code 9 business days.

rules.title: Article 10 does not apply to non-single-family pools or pools built with a new home
rules.plain_english: The home improvement article does not apply to pools built for use by more than a single-family unit (or not on/next to premises occupied only by a single-family unit), or to pools built as part of the original building plan by the same contractor who builds the single-family home.

excluded: pool for use and enjoyment of other than a single-family unit upon or contiguous to premises occupied only by a single-family unit
pool built as part of original building plan by same contractor building the single-family dwelling

rules.applies_to: Swimming pool contractors
rules.quote: The provisions of Article 10 shall not apply to contracts for the construction of swimming pools to be built for the use and enjoyment of other than a single-family unit ... nor shall they apply to the construction of swimming pools built as part of an original building plan by the same contractor who builds a single-family dwelling unit on the premises.

rules.title: Pool contract void if key 7159 items missing
rules.plain_english: A contract mainly for building a swimming pool is void and unenforceable by the contractor if it does not substantially comply with the lien release statement, change-order form, project description/plan and scale drawing, downpayment disclosure, or progress-payment schedule requirements. For a missing change-order form, the contractor can still recover for work done under quantum meruit or similar remedies.

required_provisions: 7159(d)(7) project description incl. plan and scale drawing
parameters.consequence: void and unenforceable by the contractor

rules.applies_to: Swimming pool contractors
rules.quote: Any contract, the primary purpose of which is the construction of a swimming pool, that does not substantially comply with paragraph (4) or (5) of subdivision (c) or paragraph (7), (8), or (9) of subdivision (d) of Section 7159, shall be void and unenforceable by the contractor as contrary to public policy.
rules.notes: Pool contract validator should hard-fail if any of these five items are missing.

rules.title: Prevailing party gets attorney's fees in pool contract disputes
rules.plain_english: In any lawsuit between a pool buyer and a pool contractor arising from a pool construction contract, the court must award reasonable attorney's fees to the prevailing party.

parameters.dispute_type: action arising out of swimming pool construction contract

rules.applies_to: Swimming pool contractors and buyers
rules.quote: In any action between a person contracting for construction of a swimming pool and a swimming pool contractor arising out of a contract for swimming pool construction, the court shall award reasonable attorney’s fees to the prevailing party.

rules.title: Solar Energy System Disclosure Document on the front page, bold 16-point
rules.plain_english: A solar energy system company must give the consumer CSLB's 'solar energy system disclosure document' before completing a sale, financing or lease. It must be printed on the front or cover page of every solar contract in bold 16-point type and show total cost and payments (including financing), how to complain, and the cancellation rights under 7159. The contract and disclosure must be in the same language as the sales presentation or marketing material.

parameters.timing: prior to completion of a sale, financing or lease of a solar energy system
parameters.placement: front page or cover page of every solar energy contract
primary_information: total cost and payments for the system, including financing costs
how and to whom customers may provide complaints
consumer's right to applicable cancellation period under B&P 7159
parameters.language: same as principally used in oral sales presentation or print/digital marketing material
parameters.source_of_form: CSLB website (developed with CPUC by July 1, 2018)
parameters.pace_rule: PACE Financing Estimate and Disclosure form (Sts & Hwy Code 5898.17(b)) satisfies this section for the financing contract only, not the installation contract
parameters.exclusion: does not apply to a solar energy system installed as a standard feature on new construction (B&P 7169(h))

rules.applies_to: Residential solar energy system companies and contractors
rules.quote: The “solar energy system disclosure document” shall be printed on the front page or cover page of every solar energy contract. The “solar energy system disclosure document” shall be printed in boldface 16-point type and include the following types of primary information:
rules.effective: Section added effective January 1, 2018; last amended effective January 1, 2022. Disclosure document to be available on or before July 1, 2018
rules.notes: Optional supporting info CSLB may include after the front page: financing amounts and sources, panel-count and energy-production calculations, extra utility/monitoring fees, guaranteed rebate terms, final price without rebates, contractor license number, code-noncompliance impacts, malfunction types, lease vs purchase differences, home-sale impacts (balloon payments, relocation), performance calculator (7169(c)(1)-(12)).
rules.correction: Rule left out the 7169(h) exclusion (page 432, just past this chunk): the section does not apply to a solar energy system installed as a standard feature on new construction. Added it to parameters and citation. "effective" now gives the section history (added eff. 1/1/2018, amended eff. 1/1/2020 and 1/1/2022) and keeps the July 1, 2018 availability date. Disclosure requirements (a)-(f) themselves are correct.

rules.title: Prevailing party gets attorney's fees in pool contract disputes
rules.plain_english: In any lawsuit between an owner who contracted for swimming pool construction and the pool contractor over that contract, the court must award reasonable attorney's fees to whichever side wins.

parameters.trigger: action arising out of a contract for swimming pool construction
parties: person contracting for construction of a swimming pool

rules.applies_to: Swimming pool contractors (C-53 or B) and owners who contract for pool construction
rules.quote: In any action between a person contracting for construction of a swimming pool and a swimming pool contractor arising out of a contract for swimming pool construction, the court shall award reasonable attorney’s fees to the prevailing party.
rules.effective: Added Stats 1979 ch 747 as 7169; renumbered Stats 1991 ch 1160 (no effective date printed)
rules.notes: Fee shifting is two-way (owner or contractor). Useful for a dispute-risk warning on pool contracts. Page 430 overlaps the previous chunk.

rules.title: Give CSLB solar disclosure document before sale, financing or lease
rules.plain_english: A solar energy system company must give the consumer CSLB's Solar Energy System Disclosure Document before completing a sale, financing, or lease of a residential solar energy system. CSLB (with the CPUC) publishes the form on its website.

parameters.document: Solar Energy System Disclosure Document (CSLB + CPUC, posted on CSLB website)
parameters.timing: prior to completion of a sale, financing, or lease of a solar energy system

rules.applies_to: Solar energy system companies/contractors selling, financing or leasing residential solar energy systems (1 kW to 5 MW AC)
rules.quote: that a solar energy system company shall provide to a consumer prior to completion of a sale, financing, or lease of a solar energy system.
rules.notes: Does not apply to systems installed as a standard feature on new construction (7169(h)). See solar-energy-system-definition-threshold for scope.

rules.title: Solar disclosure on contract front page in 16-point bold
rules.plain_english: The solar disclosure document must be printed on the front page or cover page of every solar energy contract, in boldface 16-point type.

parameters.placement: front page or cover page of every solar energy contract

rules.applies_to: Every residential solar energy contract (sale, financing, lease)
rules.quote: The “solar energy system disclosure document” shall be printed on the front page or cover page of every solar energy contract. The “solar energy system disclosure document” shall be printed in boldface 16-point type
rules.notes: Statute says 16-point (not 'at least'); a document generator should use exactly 16-pt bold or larger only if CSLB form permits.

rules.title: Solar disclosure must show total cost, complaint info, cancellation right
