rules.plain_english: The front-page solar disclosure must include: (1) total cost and payments for the system including financing costs, (2) how and to whom the customer can complain, and (3) the consumer's cancellation right under B&P 7159.

required_primary_items: total cost and payments for the system, including financing costs
information on how and to whom customers may provide complaints
consumer's right to the applicable cancellation period pursuant to B&P 7159

rules.applies_to: Residential solar energy contracts
rules.quote: (1) The total cost and payments for the system, including financing costs. (2) Information on how and to whom customers may provide complaints. (3) The consumer’s right to the applicable cancellation period pursuant to Section 7159 of the Business and Professions Code.
rules.notes: The cancellation period length is set in B&P 7159 (not in this chunk).

rules.title: Optional supporting pages of the solar disclosure
rules.plain_english: After the front page, CSLB's solar disclosure may include supporting information such as financing amounts and sources, panel-count and energy-production calculations, extra utility/monitoring fees, guaranteed rebate terms, final price without rebates, the company's contractor license number, lease vs. purchase differences, effects on home sale, and a performance calculator. A sales system should be able to supply these figures.

parameters.included_at: board's discretion, following the front/cover page
possible_items: amounts and sources of financing obtained
calculations used by the home improvement salesperson to determine number of panels needed
calculations used to determine how much energy the panels will generate
additional monthly electric company fees, turn-on charges, and internet monitoring fees for panels or inverters
terms and conditions of any guaranteed rebate
final contract price, without the inclusion of possible rebates
solar energy system company's contractor's license number
impacts of installations not performed to code
types of solar energy system malfunctions
difference between a solar lease and a solar purchase
impacts of financing/lease/contract terms on sale of the home, including balloon payments or system relocation if contract not assigned to new owner
calculator of projected system output, which may include an expected performance-based buy-down calculator

rules.applies_to: Residential solar energy contracts
rules.quote: (6) The final contract price, without the inclusion of possible rebates. (7) The solar energy system company’s contractor’s license number.
rules.notes: Whether these items are required depends on the current CSLB-published disclosure form; the statute makes them discretionary for the board.

rules.title: Solar contract and disclosure in the language of the sales pitch
rules.plain_english: The solar contract (sale, financing, or lease) and the disclosure document must be written in the same language that was principally used in the oral sales presentation or in the printed/digital marketing given to the consumer.

parameters.language_rule: same language principally used in oral sales presentation or print/digital marketing material given to consumer

rules.applies_to: Residential solar energy contracts
rules.quote: A contract for sale, financing, or lease of a solar energy system and the solar energy system disclosure document shall be written in the same language as was principally used in the oral sales presentation made to the consumer or the print or digital marketing material given to the consumer.
rules.notes: A CRM can capture the sales language and select the contract template accordingly.

rules.title: PACE form covers financing contract only, not installation contract
rules.plain_english: If the solar system uses PACE financing, the PACE Financing Estimate and Disclosure form (Streets & Highways Code 5898.17(b)) satisfies the disclosure requirement for the financing contract only; the installation contract still needs the CSLB solar disclosure.

parameters.trigger: Property Assessed Clean Energy (PACE) financing used
parameters.does_not_satisfy_for: underlying contract for installation of the solar energy system
parameters.form: Financing Estimate and Disclosure form, Streets & Highways Code 5898.17(b)

rules.applies_to: Residential solar projects financed through PACE
rules.quote: the Financing Estimate and Disclosure form required by subdivision (b) of Section 5898.17 of the Streets and Highways Code shall satisfy the requirements of this section with respect to the financing contract only, but not, however, with respect to the underlying contract for installation of the solar energy system.
rules.notes: CSLB posts the PACE form on its website (7169(f)).

rules.title: Solar disclosure scope: residential, 1 kW to 5 MW AC
rules.plain_english: For the solar disclosure law, a 'solar energy system' is a device installed on a residential building, mainly to generate electricity, producing at least 1 kW and no more than 5 MW AC rated peak, and meeting Public Resources Code 25782 eligibility criteria.

parameters.primary_purpose: collection and distribution of solar energy for generation of electricity
parameters.eligibility: meets or exceeds criteria under Public Resources Code 25782

rules.applies_to: Determining whether B&P 7169 disclosure rules apply to a solar project
rules.quote: “solar energy system” means a solar energy device to be installed on a residential building that has the primary purpose of providing for the collection and distribution of solar energy for the generation of electricity, that produces at least one kW, and not more than five MW, alternating current rated peak electricity
rules.notes: Systems under 1 kW AC, over 5 MW AC, or on non-residential buildings fall outside this definition.

rules.title: Solar disclosure not required for standard-feature new construction
rules.plain_english: The solar disclosure rules do not apply when the solar system is installed as a standard feature on new construction.

parameters.exempt_if: solar energy system installed as a standard feature on new construction

rules.applies_to: Builders/developers including solar as a standard feature of new homes
rules.quote: This section does not apply to a solar energy system that is installed as a standard feature on new construction.
rules.notes: An optional upgrade sold to a new-home buyer may not be a 'standard feature'; not addressed in text.

rules.title: CSLB publishes annual solar complaint report
rules.plain_english: CSLB takes consumer complaints and questions about solar companies and solar contractors (including complaints from other state agencies) and, starting July 1, 2019, publishes an annual report on its and the CPUC's websites listing complaint numbers and types, the ZIP code where each originated, and the disposition of every complaint against a solar contractor.

report_contents: ZIP Code where consumer complaint originated
disposition of all complaints received against a solar contractor

rules.applies_to: Solar energy system companies and solar contractors (reputation/complaint exposure)
rules.quote: Beginning on July 1, 2019, the board annually shall compile a report documenting consumer complaints relating to solar contractors. The report shall be made available publicly on the board’s and the Public Utilities Commission’s internet websites.
rules.notes: Board-administration duty, included because complaint dispositions against solar contractors become public.

rules.title: Asbestos consultants and site surveillance technicians need DOSH certification
rules.plain_english: Since July 1, 1992, nobody may work as an asbestos consultant or site surveillance technician unless certified by Cal/OSHA's Division of Occupational Safety and Health (DOSH).

parameters.certifying_agency: Division of Occupational Safety and Health (DOSH)

rules.applies_to: Persons providing asbestos consulting/monitoring services on projects with 100+ sq ft of asbestos-containing material
rules.quote: No person shall, on or after July 1, 1992, engage in the practice of an asbestos consultant as defined in Section 7181, or as a site surveillance technician as defined in Section 7182, unless he or she is certified by the Division of Occupational Safety and Health
rules.notes: Article 11 applies only to asbestos abatement projects involving 100 sq ft or more of ACM surface area (7189.5).

rules.title: Contractor may take up to 12 asbestos bulk samples without consultant certification
rules.plain_english: A licensed contractor or registered asbestos abatement contractor does not need asbestos consultant certification to take no more than 12 bulk samples of suspected asbestos material that will be removed, repaired or disturbed on a residential construction project, but only for bid preparation, checking its own employees' exposure, or confirming an abatement contract was completed. The person sampling must be an AHERA-certified building inspector.

parameters.setting: construction project in a residential dwelling
parameters.material: suspected asbestos-containing material required to be removed, repaired, or disturbed
permitted_purposes: evaluating exposure to its own employees during construction or asbestos abatement
determining for its own purposes or for communicating whether an asbestos abatement contract has been satisfactorily completed
parameters.sampler_qualification: certified building inspector under AHERA, 40 CFR 763, appendix C to subpart E

rules.applies_to: Licensed contractors and registered asbestos abatement contractors on residential projects
rules.quote: Certification as an asbestos consultant or site surveillance technician shall not be required when a licensed contractor or registered asbestos abatement contractor takes no more than 12 bulk samples of suspected asbestos-containing material that is required to be removed, repaired, or disturbed as part of a construction project in a residential dwelling
rules.effective: Added Stats 1990 ch 1255; amended Stats 1996 ch 526 (no effective date printed)
rules.notes: Text does not state the consequence beyond 12 samples; by implication the exemption is lost and consultant certification rules apply. The same 12-sample exemption also applies to the 7187 conflict-of-interest rule.
rules.correction: No error. 12-sample limit, residential-dwelling setting, three permitted purposes and AHERA building-inspector requirement confirmed; the same exemption is restated in 7187. The quote spans the page 432/433 break ("re-/moved"), which is the only reason it does not machine-match.

rules.title: Contractors may not do asbestos risk assessment or clearance air monitoring
rules.plain_english: A licensed contractor or asbestos abatement contractor may not provide professional asbestos health and safety services, perform asbestos risk assessments, or (unless another law allows) perform clearance air monitoring after abatement. Those are consultant functions.

prohibited_activities: clearance air monitoring following asbestos abatement, unless otherwise permitted by law

rules.applies_to: All licensed contractors and asbestos abatement contractors
rules.source: 2026 CSLB Law Book, PDF pages 433 and 437
rules.quote: No licensed contractor or asbestos abatement contractor may provide professional health and safety services or perform any asbestos risk assessment. ... nor does it permit a licensed contractor or asbestos abatement contractor to perform clearance air monitoring following asbestos abatement, unless otherwise permitted by law.
rules.effective: Added Stats 1990 ch 1255; amended Stats 1996 ch 526 (no effective date printed)
rules.notes: Clearance air monitoring must be done by an independent certified asbestos consultant/technician.

rules.title: Asbestos bid may report sampling results; contractor may charge for bid prep
rules.plain_english: An asbestos abatement bid may state the results and locations of asbestos sampling and how the asbestos will be abated, and the contractor may charge for bid preparation, including lab analysis costs.

bid_may_include: how the asbestos will be abated
parameters.may_charge_for: bid preparation, including cost of laboratory analysis of asbestos-containing material

rules.applies_to: Licensed contractors and asbestos abatement contractors bidding abatement work
rules.source: 2026 CSLB Law Book, PDF pages 433 and 437
rules.quote: A bid for asbestos abatement may communicate the results and location of sampling for the presence of asbestos and how the asbestos will be abated. ... A licensed contractor or asbestos abatement contractor may seek compensation for bid preparation, including the cost of laboratory analysis of asbestos-containing material.
rules.effective: Added Stats 1990 ch 1255; amended Stats 1996 ch 526 (no effective date printed)
rules.notes: Bid template field: sampling results, sample locations, abatement method; optional bid-prep/lab fee line item.

rules.title: Building owner must hire DOSH-certified asbestos consultant
rules.plain_english: When a building owner or operator hires someone for asbestos consulting or site surveillance technician work, the owner must contract with a DOSH-certified person.

parameters.trigger: engaging asbestos consulting or site surveillance technician services (B&P 7181/7182) after 1992-07-01
parameters.must_hire: person certified by DOSH under Labor Code 9021.5(b) regulations

rules.applies_to: Building owners/operators (project owners) on asbestos projects
rules.quote: When a building owner or operator engages the services of a person to perform asbestos consulting or site surveillance technician activities as defined in Sections 7181 and 7182 after July 1, 1992, the building owner or operator shall contract with a person who is certified by the Division of Occupational Safety and Health
rules.notes: Owner-side compliance check: verify consultant's DOSH certification card before contracting.

rules.title: Definition: asbestos consultant
rules.plain_english: An asbestos consultant is anyone who contracts to provide professional health and safety services for asbestos-containing material, including building inspections, abatement design, contract administration, supervising site surveillance technicians, sampling, asbestos management plans and clearance air monitoring.
rules.applies_to: Classifying asbestos-related service roles on a project
rules.quote: An “asbestos consultant,” as used in this chapter, means any person who contracts to provide professional health and safety services relating to asbestos-containing material ... including building inspections, abatement project design, contract administration, supervision of site surveillance technicians
rules.effective: Added Stats 1990 ch 1255 (no effective date printed)

rules.title: Definition: site surveillance technician
rules.plain_english: A site surveillance technician is an independent on-site representative of an asbestos consultant who monitors others' abatement work, does area and personnel air monitoring, and performs building surveys and contract administration at the consultant's direction.

parameters.role: independent onsite representative of an asbestos consultant
duties: monitors asbestos abatement activities of others
asbestos air monitoring for area and personnel samples
building surveys and contract administration at direction of an asbestos consultant

rules.applies_to: Classifying asbestos-related service roles on a project
rules.quote: A “site surveillance technician” means any person who acts as an independent onsite representative of an asbestos consultant who monitors the asbestos abatement activities of others, provides asbestos air monitoring services for area and personnel samples, and performs building surveys and contract administration at the direction of an asbestos consultant.
rules.effective: Added Stats 1990 ch 1255 (no effective date printed)

rules.title: DOSH asbestos certification: 15-day completeness notice, 45-day issuance
rules.plain_english: DOSH must tell an asbestos consultant/technician applicant within 15 days of receipt whether the application is complete or deficient, and must issue the certification card within 45 days after a complete application is filed. If it misses these deadlines, it must issue a provisional card.

parameters.issue_card_from: date of filing of completed application
parameters.if_deadline_missed: provisional certification card issued until procedures completed

rules.applies_to: Applicants for DOSH asbestos consultant / site surveillance technician certification
rules.quote: Within 15 days of receipt of an application for certification pursuant to this article, the division shall inform the applicant in writing either (1) that the application is complete and accepted, or (2) that it is deficient ... Within 45 days of the date of filing of a completed application, the division shall issue
rules.effective: Added Stats 1990 ch 1255 (no effective date printed)
rules.notes: Agency deadline; useful for scheduling when a company's staff must get certified before a project.

rules.title: DOSH must revoke asbestos certification for fraud or gross/repeated negligence
rules.plain_english: DOSH must revoke an asbestos consultant's or technician's certification if it was obtained under false pretenses, or if the holder acted with gross negligence or fraud, or committed repeated negligent acts (after an Administrative Procedure Act hearing).

parameters.procedure: Government Code 11500 et seq. (Administrative Procedure Act)

rules.applies_to: DOSH-certified asbestos consultants and site surveillance technicians
rules.quote: In the event the division determines that a certified asbestos consultant or site surveillance technician obtained certification under false pretenses, or that a certified asbestos consultant or site surveillance technician acted in a grossly negligent or fraudulent manner, or engaged in repeated acts of negligence, the division shall revoke that person’s certification.
rules.effective: Added Stats 1990 ch 1255 (no effective date printed)

rules.title: Asbestos consultant qualification: experience/education ladder + AHERA + exam
rules.plain_english: To be a certified asbestos consultant you need one of: 1 year asbestos experience + BS in engineering/architecture/industrial hygiene/construction management/related science; 2 years + any bachelor's; 3 years + related AA; or 4 years + high school diploma. You also need a valid federal AHERA certificate for the work type and must pass a DOSH exam.

experience_education_options.education: bachelor of science in engineering, architecture, industrial hygiene, construction management, or related biological or physical science
associate of arts in engineering, architecture, industrial hygiene, construction management, or related biological or physical science

also_required: valid federal AHERA certificate (15 USC 2641 et seq.) for the type of work, or DOSH-determined equivalent
passing score on DOSH-approved or DOSH-administered examination
exam_subjects: OSHA, DOSH, EPA, air district and DHS regulatory requirements
state-of-the-art abatement and control work procedures
AHERA training for inspectors, management planners, supervisors
industrial hygiene sampling methodology and recordkeeping

rules.applies_to: Individuals seeking asbestos consultant certification
rules.quote: (1) One year of asbestos-related experience, and a bachelor of science degree in engineering, architecture, industrial hygiene, construction management, or a related biological or physical science. (2) Two years of asbestos-related experience, and a bachelor’s degree.
rules.effective: Added Stats 1990 ch 1255 (no effective date printed)

rules.title: Site surveillance technician qualification: 6 months + HS + AHERA + exam
rules.plain_english: A certified site surveillance technician needs 6 months of asbestos experience under an asbestos consultant's supervision, a high school diploma or equivalent, a valid AHERA certificate, and a passing DOSH exam score.

parameters.experience_condition: under the supervision of an asbestos consultant
parameters.federal_certificate: valid AHERA certificate for type of work, or equivalent
parameters.exam: passing score on DOSH-approved/administered exam (5 subject areas)

rules.applies_to: Individuals seeking site surveillance technician certification
rules.quote: (a) Having six months of asbestos-related experience under the supervision of an asbestos consultant. (b) Possession of a high school diploma or equivalent.
rules.effective: Added Stats 1990 ch 1255 (no effective date printed)

rules.title: Owner's asbestos consultant cannot have an interest in the abatement contractor
rules.plain_english: When a building owner hires an asbestos consultant or site surveillance technician, that consultant may not have any financial or ownership interest in the asbestos abatement contractor hired for the same project. A contractor may still hire its own consultant for its workers' health and safety.

parameters.trigger: building owner or operator contracts with asbestos consultant or site surveillance technician
parameters.prohibited: consultant/technician has any financial or proprietary interest in an asbestos abatement contractor hired for the same project
parameters.exception_contractor_hire: contractor may hire a consultant to provide health and safety services for the contractor's personnel
parameters.exception_bulk_samples: does not apply to contractor taking <= 12 bulk samples in residential dwelling for the listed purposes

rules.applies_to: Building owners, asbestos consultants/technicians, and asbestos abatement contractors on the same project
rules.quote: that asbestos consultant or site surveillance technician shall not have any financial or proprietary interest in an asbestos abatement contractor hired for the same project. However, this section shall not preclude the hiring of a consultant by a contractor for the purpose of providing health and safety services for the personnel of the contractor.
rules.effective: Added Stats 1990 ch 1255; amended Stats 1996 ch 526 (no effective date printed)
rules.notes: Legislative intent: consultant work (clearance air monitoring, design, contract administration) must reflect independent professional judgment.

rules.title: Penalties: uncertified asbestos consulting or conflict of interest
rules.plain_english: Practicing as an asbestos consultant or site surveillance technician without certification, or violating the conflict-of-interest rule, is an infraction on a first conviction ($1,000-$3,000 fine). A later conviction is a misdemeanor: certification must be revoked or suspended, and the fine is $3,000-$5,000 and/or up to one year in county jail.

violations: practicing as asbestos consultant or site surveillance technician without DOSH certification

rules.applies_to: Uncertified asbestos consultants/technicians and consultants with conflicts of interest
rules.quote: (a) Conviction of a first offense is an infraction punishable by a fine of not less than one thousand dollars ($1,000) or more than three thousand dollars ($3,000).
rules.effective: Added Stats 1990 ch 1255 (no effective date printed)
rules.notes: Subsection (b) text in the book reads 'a fine not not less than three thousand dollars ($3,000) or more than five thousand dollars ($5,000), or imprisonment in the county jail not exceeding one year, or both' (typo 'not not' is in the source).
rules.correction: No error. $1,000-$3,000 infraction (first offense) and $3,000-$5,000 and/or up to 1 year county jail misdemeanor with mandatory revocation or suspension (subsequent offense) confirmed; the "not not" typo is in the book.

rules.title: Asbestos consultant rules apply at 100+ sq ft of ACM
rules.plain_english: The asbestos consultant certification article applies to asbestos abatement projects involving 100 square feet or more of asbestos-containing material surface area.
rules.applies_to: Asbestos abatement projects (owners, consultants, contractors)
rules.quote: This article shall apply to asbestos abatement projects within the meaning of asbestos-related work as defined in Section 6501.8 of the Labor Code, and which involves 100 square feet or more of surface area of asbestos containing material.
rules.effective: Added Stats 1990 ch 1255 (no effective date printed)
rules.notes: Below 100 sq ft, Article 11 (B&P 7180-7189.7) does not apply; other Cal/OSHA asbestos rules may still apply.

rules.title: State agencies may use their own DOSH-certified staff as asbestos consultants
rules.plain_english: State agencies need not hire outside asbestos consultants if their own assigned employees are DOSH-certified; where feasible, the state should use associate or senior industrial hygienists. Attorneys giving asbestos legal advice to owners need not be certified.

parameters.condition: state employees performing B&P 7181/7182 activities must be DOSH-certified
parameters.attorney_exemption: attorneys providing asbestos legal advice to building owners/operators need not be certified (7189.7(b))

rules.applies_to: State agencies as owners of state-owned or leased buildings
rules.quote: Nothing in this article shall be construed to require agencies of the state to contract with asbestos consultants or site surveillance technicians who are not employees of the state as long as employees of the state who are assigned to perform the activities described in Sections 7181 and 7182 have been certified by the division
rules.effective: Added Stats 1990 ch 1255 (no effective date printed)

rules.title: No public official's name in ads without written authorization
rules.plain_english: A licensed contractor may not use the name or position of a public official (local or state agency member, officer, employee, or consultant) in advertising or promotional material without that official's written authorization.

parameters.requires: written authorization of the public official
parameters.public_official_definition: member, officer, employee, or consultant of a local government agency (Gov Code 82041) or state agency (Gov Code 82049)

rules.applies_to: All CSLB licensees' advertising
rules.quote: The name or position of a public official may not be used in an advertisement or any promotional material by a person licensed under this chapter, without the written authorization of the public official.
rules.effective: Added Stats 1994 ch 1135 (no effective date printed)
rules.notes: Book cross-references Civil Code 1770 (Unfair Practices) in the Appendix.

rules.title: Required disclaimer when an authorized public official appears in ads
rules.plain_english: If a printed ad uses a public official's name or position with written authorization, it must include a disclaimer in at least 10-point roman boldface, in a contrasting color, set apart from other text, stating the official does not endorse the product/service in an official capacity. Broadcast ads must read the statement aloud clearly.

parameters.trigger: printed advertisement/promotional material uses public official's name or position with written authorization
parameters.color: contrasts with background so as to be easily legible
parameters.placement: set apart from any other printed matter
parameters.disclaimer_template: The name of {public_official_name} does not imply that {public_official_name} endorses this product or service in {his_or_her} official capacity and does not imply an endorsement by any governmental entity.
parameters.broadcast_requirement: statement read in a clearly audible tone of voice

rules.applies_to: All CSLB licensees' advertising that names a public official
rules.quote: The disclaimer shall consist of a statement that reads “The name of (specify name of public official) does not imply that (specify name of public official) endorses this product or service in (his or her) official capacity and does not imply an endorsement by any governmental entity.”
rules.effective: Added Stats 1994 ch 1135 (no effective date printed)
rules.notes: Ad-copy generator can fill the template automatically.
rules.correction: No error. At-least-10-point roman boldface, contrasting color, set apart, and the disclaimer wording (template matches the statute once the placeholders are filled) confirmed.

rules.title: Residential (1-4 unit) arbitration clause must be titled ARBITRATION OF DISPUTES
rules.plain_english: If a contract for work on residential property with four or fewer units has an arbitration clause, it must be clearly titled 'ARBITRATION OF DISPUTES'. In a printed contract it must be in at least 10-point roman boldface, or contrasting red print in at least 8-point roman boldface; in a typed contract, in capital letters.

parameters.trigger: contract for work on residential property contains an arbitration provision between the principals
printed_contract_format_options: contrasting red print in at least 8-point roman boldface type

rules.applies_to: Contractors whose contracts for work on 1-4 unit residential property include arbitration
rules.quote: If a contract for work on residential property with four or fewer units contains a provision for arbitration of a dispute between the principals in the transaction, the provision shall be clearly titled “ARBITRATION OF DISPUTES.”
rules.effective: Added Stats 1994 ch 1135 (no effective date printed)
rules.notes: Applies to any contract for work on such property (not only home improvement contracts).

rules.title: Mandatory arbitration NOTICE text and initial line
rules.plain_english: Right after the arbitration clause and immediately before the space where the parties initial agreement or refusal, the contract must print the statutory NOTICE (giving up court/jury trial, discovery and appeal rights) and the statement 'WE HAVE READ AND UNDERSTAND...'. Same formatting rules: 10-pt roman bold or red 8-pt roman bold if printed; capitals if typed.

parameters.placement: immediately following the arbitration provision and immediately before the line or space for parties to indicate assent or nonassent
parameters.notice_text: NOTICE: BY INITIALING IN THE SPACE BELOW YOU ARE AGREEING TO HAVE ANY DISPUTE ARISING OUT OF THE MATTERS INCLUDED IN THE ‘ARBITRATION OF DISPUTES’ PROVISION DECIDED BY NEUTRAL ARBITRATION AS PROVIDED BY CALIFORNIA LAW AND YOU ARE GIVING UP ANY RIGHTS YOU MIGHT POSSESS TO HAVE THE DISPUTE LITIGATED IN A COURT OR JURY TRIAL. BY INITIALING IN THE SPACE BELOW YOU ARE GIVING UP YOUR JUDICIAL RIGHTS TO DISCOVERY AND APPEAL, UNLESS THOSE RIGHTS ARE SPECIFICALLY INCLUDED IN THE ‘ARBITRATION OF DISPUTES’ PROVISION. IF YOU REFUSE TO SUBMIT TO ARBITRATION AFTER AGREEING TO THIS PROVISION, YOU MAY BE COMPELLED TO ARBITRATE UNDER THE AUTHORITY OF THE BUSINESS AND PROFESSIONS CODE OR OTHER APPLICABLE LAWS. YOUR AGREEMENT TO THIS ARBITRATION PROVISION IS VOLUNTARY.
parameters.acknowledgment_text: WE HAVE READ AND UNDERSTAND THE FOREGOING AND AGREE TO SUBMIT DISPUTES ARISING OUT OF THE MATTERS INCLUDED IN THE ‘ARBITRATION OF DISPUTES’ PROVISION TO NEUTRAL ARBITRATION.
printed_contract_format_options: contrasting red print in at least 8-point roman boldface type

rules.applies_to: Contracts for work on residential property with 4 or fewer units that include arbitration
rules.quote: NOTICE: BY INITIALING IN THE SPACE BELOW YOU ARE AGREEING TO HAVE ANY DISPUTE ARISING OUT OF THE MATTERS INCLUDED IN THE ‘ARBITRATION OF DISPUTES’ PROVISION DECIDED BY NEUTRAL ARBITRATION AS PROVIDED BY CALIFORNIA LAW AND YOU ARE GIVING UP ANY RIGHTS YOU MIGHT POSSESS TO HAVE THE DISPUTE LITIGATED IN A COURT OR JURY TRIAL.
rules.effective: Added Stats 1994 ch 1135 (no effective date printed)
rules.notes: Full notice text is in parameters.notice_text (dehyphenated from the printed line breaks). Generator should reproduce it word-for-word.
rules.correction: No error. notice_text and acknowledgment_text were matched word for word against the book (after removing line-end hyphens); placement and 10-pt bold / 8-pt red bold / capitals format confirmed.

rules.title: Noncompliant residential arbitration clause binds only the contractor
rules.plain_english: An arbitration clause in a contract for work on 1-4 unit residential property that doesn't meet the title, notice and formatting rules may not be enforceable against anyone except the licensee (the contractor can still be held to it). CSLB can still investigate and discipline.

parameters.trigger: arbitration provision fails B&P 7191 requirements
parameters.consequence: may not be enforceable against any person other than the licensee

rules.applies_to: Contractors using arbitration clauses on 1-4 unit residential work
rules.quote: A provision for arbitration of a dispute between a principal in a contract for work on a residential property with four or fewer units that does not comply with this section may not be enforceable against any person other than the licensee.
rules.effective: Added Stats 1994 ch 1135 (no effective date printed)
rules.notes: Contract checker should flag missing title, missing notice, wrong font size/color, or missing initial line. Statute wording is "may not be enforceable against any person other than the licensee"; enforceability against the licensee is implied, not stated.
rules.correction: No error. The statute says the clause "may not be enforceable against any person other than the licensee"; still_enforceable_against = licensee is the implied reading, not express text.

rules.title: Definition: home inspection and home inspector
rules.plain_english: A home inspection is a noninvasive, physical, paid examination of the mechanical, electrical, plumbing, structural and essential components of a 1-4 unit residence done in connection with a property transfer, to find material defects. Any consultation called a home inspection (or similar) counts. A home inspector is anyone who performs one.

parameters.trigger: in connection with a transfer of real property (see 7195(e))
parameters.includes: any consultation represented to be a home inspection or any confusingly similar term
parameters.home_inspector: any individual who performs a home inspection

rules.applies_to: Contractors or firms offering pre-sale/transfer inspections of 1-4 unit homes
rules.quote: “Home inspection” is a noninvasive, physical examination, performed for a fee in connection with a transfer, as defined in subdivision (e), of real property, of the mechanical, electrical, or plumbing systems or the structural and essential components of a residential dwelling of one to four units designed to identify material defects in those systems, structures, and components.
rules.notes: Chapter 9.3 does not create a CSLB license for home inspectors; it sets duties and unfair practices.

rules.title: Definition: transfer (triggers home inspection rules)
rules.plain_english: A 'transfer' means a sale, exchange, installment land sales contract, lease with option to purchase, any other option to purchase, or ground lease coupled with improvements, of real property or a residential stock cooperative with 1 to 4 dwelling units.

transfer_types: lease with an option to purchase
parameters.property: real property or residential stock cooperative

rules.applies_to: Determining whether an inspection is a regulated home inspection
rules.quote: “Transfer” is a transfer by sale, exchange, installment land sales contract, as defined in Section 2985 of the Civil Code, lease with an option to purchase, any other option to purchase, or ground lease coupled with improvements, of real property or residential stock cooperative, improved with or consisting of not less than one nor more than four dwelling units.

rules.title: Home inspection of pool/spa must report drowning prevention features
rules.plain_english: When a property with a pool or spa is transferred, the home inspection must check which of the seven drowning prevention safety features listed in Health & Safety Code 115922(a) are present, and the report must identify them and specifically state if the pool or spa has fewer than two.

parameters.trigger: transfer of real property with a swimming pool or spa
parameters.report_must_identify: which, if any, of the seven features the pool or spa is equipped with
parameters.flag_statement: report shall specifically state if the pool or spa has fewer than two listed features

rules.applies_to: Home inspectors (including contractors performing home inspections) on 1-4 unit homes with pools/spas
rules.quote: In a dwelling with a pool or spa, the “home inspection report” shall identify which, if any, of the seven drowning prevention safety features listed in subdivision (a) of Section 115922 of the Health and Safety Code the pool or spa is equipped with and shall specifically state if the pool or spa has fewer than two of the listed drowning prevention safety features.
rules.notes: The seven features themselves are listed in H&S 115922(a), not in this chunk.

rules.title: Optional energy-efficiency items in a home inspection
rules.plain_english: If the client asks, a home inspection may include an energy-efficiency inspection covering items such as insulation R-values, window panes and frames, HVAC and water heating, appliance age and fuel type, fans, thermostats, air leakage areas, and window solar control.

parameters.trigger: requested by the client
optional_items: noninvasive inspection of insulation R-values in attics, roofs, walls, floors, ducts
number of window glass panes and frame types
heating and cooling equipment and water heating systems
age and fuel type of major appliances
type of thermostat and other systems
general integrity and potential leakage areas of walls, window areas, doors, duct systems
solar control efficiency of existing windows

rules.applies_to: Home inspectors
rules.quote: “Home inspection,” if requested by the client, may include an inspection of energy efficiency.
rules.notes: Checklist generator input.

rules.title: Definition: material defect
rules.plain_english: A material defect is a condition that significantly affects the value, desirability, habitability or safety of the dwelling. Style or aesthetics do not make something defective.
rules.applies_to: Home inspection reports
rules.quote: A “material defect” is a condition that significantly affects the value, desirability, habitability, or safety of the dwelling. Style or aesthetics shall not be considered in determining whether a system, structure, or component is defective.

rules.title: Home inspection report contents
rules.plain_english: A home inspection report is a written, paid report issued after the inspection that clearly describes the inspected systems, structures and components, any material defects found, and recommendations (including referrals for evaluation by appropriate persons).

must_include: description and identification of the inspected systems, structures, or components
recommendations regarding conditions observed or recommendations for evaluation by appropriate persons
pool/spa: drowning prevention features identified; statement if fewer than two

rules.applies_to: Home inspectors
rules.quote: A “home inspection report” is a written report prepared for a fee and issued after a home inspection. The report clearly describes and identifies the inspected systems, structures, or components of the dwelling, any material defects identified, and any recommendations regarding the conditions observed or recommendations for evaluation by appropriate persons.
rules.notes: Report template generator input.

rules.title: Optional landscape irrigation inspection report contents
rules.plain_english: A home inspection report on a parcel with an owner-controlled in-ground irrigation system may include an irrigation inspection report (by the home inspector or a certified landscape irrigation auditor) covering the controller, activation of each turf zone noting valve/piping/head malfunctions, overspray onto hardscape, runoff and ponding during a stated number of minutes, and any limits due to snow, ice or site conditions. No watering-restriction penalty may be imposed for running the system for the inspection.

parameters.trigger: parcel with in-ground landscape irrigation system under exclusive control of owner or occupant
report_contents_if_provided: examination of irrigation controller, noting observable defects in installation or operation
activation of each zone/circuit to turf grass, noting malfunctions of irrigation valve, visible supply piping, sprinkler heads and stems
observation during operation (minutes specified in report) of spray to hardscape, surface runoff, ponding
notation whether inspection limited by snow, ice, or other site conditions
parameters.watering_restriction_sanction_shield: no state/local agency or water purveyor sanction for operating system for the inspection (7195.5(b))

rules.applies_to: Home inspectors and landscape irrigation auditors; owners/occupants
rules.quote: a home inspection report on a dwelling unit prepared pursuant to this chapter on a parcel containing an in-ground landscape irrigation system, the operation of which is under the exclusive control of the owner or occupant of the dwelling, may include an irrigation system inspection report, prepared by either a home inspector or certified landscape irrigation auditor
rules.notes: Home inspectors are also encouraged (not required) to provide information on water-efficient irrigation (7195.5(c)).

rules.title: Home inspector may not give a property valuation opinion
rules.plain_english: A home inspector may not give an opinion of the property's value.

parameters.prohibited: opinion of valuation on a property

rules.applies_to: Home inspectors
rules.quote: A home inspector shall not give an opinion of valuation on a property.

rules.title: Home inspector standard of care: reasonably prudent home inspector
rules.plain_english: A home inspector who is not a licensed general contractor, structural pest control operator, architect, or registered professional engineer must perform inspections with the care a reasonably prudent home inspector would use. This duty cannot be waived by contract.

parameters.standard: degree of care a reasonably prudent home inspector would exercise

rules.applies_to: Home inspectors who are not GC/SPCO/architect/PE
rules.quote: It is the duty of a home inspector who is not licensed as a general contractor, structural pest control operator, or architect, or registered as a professional engineer to conduct a home inspection with the degree of care that a reasonably prudent home inspector would exercise.
rules.effective: Added Stats 1996 ch 338 (no effective date printed)
rules.notes: Licensed general contractors doing home inspections are presumably held to their own professional standard; the text does not state it.

rules.title: Home inspectors not exempt from contractor/engineer/architect licensing
rules.plain_english: A home inspector who is not a registered engineer may not perform analysis that amounts to civil, electrical or mechanical engineering, and being a home inspector does not exempt anyone from the Contractors License Law, architect, engineer, structural pest control or appraiser licensing laws.

not_exempt_from: Contractors State License Law (B&P 7000 et seq.)
Structural Pest Control Act (B&P 8500 et seq.)
Real Estate Appraisers law (B&P 11300 et seq.)

rules.applies_to: Home inspectors; contractors who also inspect
rules.quote: Nothing in this chapter shall be construed to allow home inspectors who are not registered engineers to perform any analysis of the systems, components, or structural integrity of a dwelling that would constitute the practice of civil, electrical, or mechanical engineering, or to exempt a home inspector from Chapter 3
rules.notes: Any repair work a home inspector performs still requires a CSLB license (subject to 7197 limits).

rules.title: Who the home inspector chapter does not cover; appraisers barred from inspecting
rules.plain_english: The home inspector chapter does not apply to registered engineers, licensed land surveyors, or licensed architects acting under their licenses, and does not change real estate licensees' or sellers' disclosure duties. A licensed real estate appraiser doing an appraisal may not also act as a home inspector, except as required by law or regulation standards.

parameters.condition: acting pursuant to their professional registration or license
parameters.appraiser_bar: licensed real estate appraiser performing an appraisal shall not engage in home inspection activity, except as required to comply with standards in law or regulation

rules.applies_to: Engineers, surveyors, architects, appraisers, real estate licensees
rules.quote: This chapter does not apply to a registered engineer, licensed land surveyor, or licensed architect acting pursuant to their professional registration or license

rules.title: Yellow CSST gas tubing: required notice in home inspection report
rules.plain_english: If a home inspector sees any shade of yellow corrugated stainless steel tubing (CSST gas line), the report must note it and include a statutory notice that proper bonding and grounding can only be determined by a licensed electrical contractor.

parameters.trigger: home inspector observes any shade of yellow corrugated stainless steel tubing
parameters.notice_text: Manufacturers of yellow corrugated stainless steel tubing believe that yellow corrugated stainless steel tubing is safer if properly bonded and grounded as required by the manufacturer’s installation instructions. Proper bonding and grounding of this product can only be determined by a licensed electrical contractor.
parameters.csst_definition: flexible stainless steel pipe used to supply natural gas and propane in residential, commercial, and industrial structures

rules.applies_to: Home inspectors; refers owners to C-10 electrical contractors
rules.quote: Manufacturers of yellow corrugated stainless steel tubing believe that yellow corrugated stainless steel tubing is safer if properly bonded and grounded as required by the manufacturer’s installation instructions. Proper bonding and grounding of this product can only be determined by a licensed electrical contractor.
rules.notes: Lead source for electrical (C-10) bonding/grounding work.
rules.correction: No error. Notice text matched word for word; effective January 1, 2019 (Stats 2018 ch 225) confirmed.

rules.title: Home inspector/company may not do paid repairs within 12 months of its report
rules.plain_english: It is an unfair business practice for a home inspector, the inspector's employer, or an affiliated company to perform or offer to perform, for an extra fee, repairs on a structure for which it prepared a home inspection report in the past 12 months. Exceptions exist for home warranty repairs, structural pest control repairs, C-39 roof certifications and C-36 sewer laterals (with conditions).

parameters.measured_from: date home inspection report was prepared
covered_parties: company controlled by a company that also has a financial interest in a company employing a home inspector
parameters.prohibited: perform or offer to perform, for an additional fee, any repairs to a structure on which the inspector or inspector's company prepared a home inspection report
exceptions: home protection company affiliated with/retaining inspector, repairs under home protection contract claims (7197(b))
structural pest control operator repairs under B&P 8505 after a structural pest inspection (7197(c))
C-39 roofing contractor roof-certification repairs meeting 7197(d) conditions
C-36 plumbing contractor sewer lateral repairs with 7197(e) disclosure

rules.applies_to: Contractors and companies that also perform home inspections
rules.quote: (1) To perform or offer to perform, for an additional fee, any repairs to a structure on which the inspector, or the inspector’s company, has prepared a home inspection report in the past 12 months.
rules.effective: Added Stats 1996 ch 338; amended effective January 1, 2018 and January 1, 2022
rules.notes: A CRM can block repair quotes on addresses where the company issued a home inspection report < 12 months earlier.

rules.title: Home inspector may not inspect property it has an interest in
rules.plain_english: A home inspector or the inspector's company may not inspect for a fee any property in which it has a financial interest or any interest in the transfer.

parameters.prohibited: inspect for a fee any property in which inspector/company has any financial interest or interest in the transfer

rules.applies_to: Home inspectors and their companies/affiliates
rules.quote: (2) Inspect for a fee any property in which the inspector, or the inspector’s company, has any financial interest or any interest in the transfer of the property.
rules.effective: Added Stats 1996 ch 338; amended effective January 1, 2018 and January 1, 2022

rules.title: No referral payments to owners, brokers or agents
rules.plain_english: A home inspector or inspection company may not offer or give any compensation, inducement or reward to the property owner, broker or agent for referring business.

parameters.prohibited: any compensation, inducement, or reward for referral of business

rules.applies_to: Home inspectors and their companies/affiliates
rules.quote: (3) To offer or deliver any compensation, inducement, or reward to the owner of the inspected property, the broker, or agent, for the referral of any business to the inspector or the inspection company.
rules.effective: Added Stats 1996 ch 338; amended effective January 1, 2018 and January 1, 2022

rules.title: No contingent-fee home inspections
rules.plain_english: A home inspector may not accept an engagement where the job or the fee depends on the report's conclusions, pre-set findings, or the close of escrow.
rules.applies_to: Home inspectors and their companies/affiliates
rules.quote: (4) Accept an engagement to make an inspection or to prepare a report in which the employment itself or the fee payable for the inspection is contingent upon the conclusions in the report, preestablished findings, or the close of escrow.
rules.effective: Added Stats 1996 ch 338; amended effective January 1, 2018 and January 1, 2022

rules.title: C-39 roofer may repair after roof certification inspection if conditions met
rules.plain_english: A C-39 roofing contractor whose company also does the home inspection may still repair the roof for a roof certification if: different employees do the home and roof inspections; the roof inspection is ordered before or with the home inspection (or finished before it starts); and before the consumer authorizes the home inspection, the consumer gets a consumer disclosure with three specific statements.

conditions_all_required: different employees perform the home inspection and the roof inspection
roof inspection ordered prior to or at the same time as the home inspection, or completed before commencement of the home inspection
consumer disclosure provided before consumer authorizes the home inspection
disclosure_statements: The same company that performs the roof inspection and roof repairs will perform the home inspection on the same property.

Any repairs that are authorized by the consumer are for the repairs identified in the roofing contractor’s roof inspection report and no repairs identified in the home inspection are authorized or allowed as specified in the roof inspection.
The consumer has the right to seek a second opinion.
parameters.disclosure_timing: before the consumer authorizes the home inspection
parameters.roof_certification_definition: written statement by licensed C-39 who inspected the roof, made any necessary repairs, and warrants the roof is free of leaks at time of certification and should perform as designed for the specified term

rules.applies_to: C-39 roofing contractors whose company also performs home inspections
rules.quote: (1) Different employees perform the home inspection and the roof inspection. (2) The roof inspection is ordered prior to, or at the same time as, the home inspection, or the roof inspection is completed before the commencement of the home inspection.
rules.effective: Amended effective January 1, 2018 (Stats 2017 ch 508) and January 1, 2022
rules.notes: Disclosure statements copied from 7197(d)(3)(A)-(C); a generator can produce the disclosure form and a workflow can check timing and employee separation. The statute does not say the disclosure must be in writing; giving it in writing is prudent for proof.
rules.correction: plain_english said the consumer must get a "written disclosure"; 7197(d)(3) only says "a consumer disclosure" (no writing requirement stated). Removed "written". Conditions and the three disclosure statements match word for word (the printed (d)(3)(B) reads "authorized or allowed as specified", without the "except" used in 7197(e)(2)).

rules.title: C-36 plumber may repair sewer lateral after inspection with disclosure
rules.plain_english: A C-36 plumbing contractor whose company also does the home inspection may repair a sewer lateral it inspected if, before the consumer authorizes the home inspection, the consumer gets a disclosure with three specific notifications.

parameters.work: repairs pursuant to inspection of sewer lateral pipe connecting a residence or business to a sewer system
parameters.disclosure_timing: before the consumer authorizes the home inspection
disclosure_statements: The same company that performs the sewer lateral inspection and the sewer lateral repairs will perform the home inspection on the same property.

Any repairs that are authorized by the consumer are for the repairs identified in the sewer lateral inspection report and no repairs identified in the home inspection report are authorized or allowed except as specified in the sewer lateral inspection report.
The consumer has the right to seek a second opinion on the sewer lateral inspection.

rules.applies_to: C-36 plumbing contractors whose company also performs home inspections
rules.quote: (1) The same company that performs the sewer lateral inspection and the sewer lateral repairs will perform the home inspection on the same property.
rules.notes: Unlike the C-39 exception, no separate-employee or timing-of-order condition is stated.
rules.correction: No error. All three disclosure statements matched word for word.

rules.title: Home inspection contracts cannot waive duty or cap liability at the fee
rules.plain_english: Contract terms that waive the home inspector's duty of care or limit the inspector's liability to the cost of the inspection report are void as against public policy.

invalid_clauses: waiver of the B&P 7196 duty of care
limitation of home inspector liability to the cost of the home inspection report
parameters.effect: contrary to public policy and invalid

rules.applies_to: Home inspection agreements
rules.quote: Contractual provisions that purport to waive the duty owed pursuant to Section 7196, or limit the liability of the home inspector to the cost of the home inspection report, are contrary to public policy and invalid.
rules.effective: Added Stats 1996 ch 338 (no effective date printed)
rules.notes: Contract checker can flag these clauses.

rules.title: 4-year limit to sue over a home inspection report
rules.plain_english: A lawsuit for breach of duty arising from a home inspection report must be started within four years from the date of the inspection.

parameters.claim: breach of duty arising from a home inspection report

rules.applies_to: Home inspectors and their clients (buyers, owners)
rules.quote: The time for commencement of a legal action for breach of duty arising from a home inspection report shall not exceed four years from the date of the inspection.
rules.effective: Added Stats 1996 ch 338 (no effective date printed)
rules.notes: Record-retention tool: keep inspection records at least 4 years from inspection date.

rules.title: HERS California home energy audit with home inspection, on request
rules.plain_english: If the client asks, a home inspection may come with a HERS California home energy audit. The HERS report must meet California Energy Commission standards (20 CCR 1670 et seq.), and the audit may be done by a home inspector who meets those requirements.

parameters.trigger: client requests
parameters.audit: Home Energy Rating System (HERS) California home energy audit
parameters.standards: Energy Commission HERS regs, Title 20 CCR Division 2, Chapter 4, Article 8 (section 1670 et seq.)
parameters.performer: home inspector meeting 20 CCR 1670 et seq. requirements

rules.applies_to: Home inspectors offering HERS audits
rules.quote: If the client requests a HERS California home energy audit, the HERS California home inspection report accompanying any home inspection report defined in subdivision (c) of Section 7195 shall comply with the standards and requirements established by the Energy Commission for HERS California home energy audits

rules.title: Statutes control over regulations not yet updated
rules.plain_english: CSLB regulations interpret the statutes; if a law changed and the regulation was not yet updated, the law still controls.

parameters.applies_when: rules and regulations not yet corrected to reflect changes in law

rules.applies_to: Any compliance tool using 16 CCR rules
rules.citation: CSLB Law Book Chapter 9 introduction (16 CCR Division 8)
rules.quote: Laws take precedence and are in effect, even if the affected rules and regulations have not been corrected to reflect any changes in the law.
rules.notes: Editorial statement in the book, not a regulation itself.

rules.title: Definition: battery energy storage system (stayed)
rules.plain_english: A battery energy storage system is one or more devices assembled together that store energy to supply electricity later. This definition's effective date was temporarily stayed when the book was printed.

parameters.definition: one or more devices, assembled together, capable of storing energy in order to supply electrical energy at a future time
parameters.status: effective date temporarily stayed at time of printing

rules.applies_to: C-10, C-46 and other contractors installing batteries
rules.quote: For purposes of this division, “battery energy storage system” means one or more devices, assembled together, capable of storing energy in order to supply electrical energy at a future time.
rules.effective: Effective date temporarily stayed at time of printing
rules.notes: Check current status with CSLB before relying on it; tied to C-10 and C-46 BESS rules.

rules.title: CSLB application fees
rules.plain_english: CSLB application fees: original license (one classification) $450; each extra classification with the original application $150; additional classification later (B&P 7059) $230; replacing the qualifier (RMO/RME etc.) $230; adding non-qualifying personnel $125; asbestos certification exam $125; hazardous substance removal certification exam $125.
rules.applies_to: License applicants and licensees
rules.quote: (1) An application for an original license in a single classification is $450. (2) An application for each additional classification applied for in connection with an original license is $150. (3) An application for each additional classification pursuant to Business and Professions Code Section 7059 is $230.
rules.notes: Qualifier replacement covers RMO, RMM, responsible managing member, or RME (B&P 7068.2).
rules.correction: No error. All seven amounts match 811(a) and the base amounts in B&P 7137(a)(1)(A)-(G).

rules.title: CSLB exam rescheduling fee $100
rules.plain_english: Rescheduling a CSLB exam (original license, added class, qualifier change, asbestos or hazardous substance certification) costs $100. Scheduling or rescheduling an exam required as a probation condition also costs $100.
rules.applies_to: Exam applicants and licensees on probation
rules.quote: (2) Scheduling or rescheduling an examination for a licensee who is required to take the examination as a condition of probation is $100.

rules.title: CSLB initial license and HIS registration fees
rules.plain_english: Initial license fee: $200 for an individual owner (active or inactive); $350 for a partnership, corporation, LLC or joint venture. Home improvement salesperson registration: $200.

parameters.veteran_fee_reduction_condition: applicant is a veteran of the U.S. Armed Forces (incl. National Guard or Reserve) and was not dishonorably discharged; proof by driver license/ID marked "Veteran" or DD214 long form (B&P 7137(a)(3)(D), PDF page 375)

rules.applies_to: New licensees and HIS registrants
rules.quote: (1) The initial license fee for an active or inactive license for an individual owner is $200. (2) The initial license fee for an active or inactive license for a partnership, corporation, limited liability company, or joint venture is $350. (3) The registration fee for a home improvement salesperson is $200.
rules.notes: Initial license fee is in addition to the application fee in 811(a). B&P 7137(a)(3)(D) halves these initial fees for qualifying veterans.
rules.correction: No error in the amounts. Added: B&P 7137(a)(3)(D) requires a 50% reduction of these initial license/registration fees for an applicant who is a U.S. Armed Forces veteran (incl. National Guard/Reserve) not dishonorably discharged; 811(c) does not repeat this.

rules.title: CSLB license and HIS renewal fees
rules.plain_english: Renewal fees: individual owner active $450, inactive $300; partnership/corporation/LLC/joint venture active $700, inactive $500; home improvement salesperson registration renewal $200.
rules.applies_to: Licensees and HIS registrants renewing
rules.quote: (1) The renewal fee for an active license for an individual owner is $450. (2) The renewal fee for an inactive license for an individual owner is $300. (3) The renewal fee for an active license for a partnership, corporation, limited liability company, or joint venture is $700.
rules.notes: Delinquency fee = 50% of the renewal fee if renewed after expiration (B&P 7137(a)(5)); C-10 holders pay an extra $20 with an active renewal (B&P 7137(a)(6)(A)). Renewal period length is set in B&P 7140 (not in this chunk).
rules.correction: No error in the amounts. Added from B&P 7137: delinquency fee = 50% of the renewal fee when renewed after expiration (7137(a)(5)); C-10 licensees pay an extra $20 with an active renewal (7137(a)(6)(A)).

rules.title: Business name change fee $100
rules.plain_english: Changing the business name recorded on a CSLB license costs $100.
rules.applies_to: Licensees changing their recorded business name
rules.quote: (1) The fee to change the business name of a license as it is recorded under Chapter 9 of Division 3 of the Business and Professions Code is $100.
rules.notes: Regulation 812 (dishonored check service charge) is repealed, but B&P 7137(a)(6)(F) still sets a $25 charge per dishonored check (PDF page 377). Statute allows the name-change fee to rise to $125 (7137(a)(6)(E)).
rules.correction: No error. $100 confirmed (statute allows up to $125). Note refined: regulation 812 is repealed, but B&P 7137(a)(6)(F) still sets a $25 dishonored-check charge.

rules.title: Rejected application abandoned if not returned within 90 days
rules.plain_english: A non-renewal application that CSLB rejected as insufficient or incomplete is considered abandoned if the applicant does not return it within 90 days from the original rejection notice (the Registrar may extend for good cause). An abandoned application cannot be reinstated; you must file a new one with a new fee.

parameters.measured_from: date of original notice of rejection
parameters.applies_to: all applications other than renewal applications
parameters.extension: Registrar may extend for good cause
parameters.consequence: application deemed abandoned; cannot be reinstated; must file new application with required fee

rules.applies_to: License, classification, qualifier and HIS applicants
rules.quote: An application, other than a renewal application, shall be deemed abandoned whenever an applicant fails to return an application rejected for insufficiency or incompleteness within 90 days from date of original notice of rejection. This 90-day period may be extended by the Registrar for good cause.
rules.notes: Deadline calculator: rejection_notice_date + 90 days.

rules.title: License application: experience record, prior license history, signed under perjury
rules.plain_english: The CSLB license application asks each member of the applicant's personnel for the qualifier's construction experience and whether anyone involved ever had a license refused or revoked, and must be signed under penalty of perjury by each member of the personnel.

information_required: record of previous construction experience of the personnel member who will qualify
whether applicant, any personnel, or known associates in contracting ever had a professional or vocational license refused or revoked
parameters.signature: each member of the personnel of the applicant, under penalty of perjury
parameters.experience_record_exemption: Registrar may exempt applicants eligible for exam waiver (B&P 7065.1) or not required to test (B&P 7065)

rules.applies_to: Original license applicants
rules.quote: (b) The application shall be signed, under penalty of perjury, by each member of the personnel of the applicant.
rules.notes: Registrar may require any other information needed to determine qualifications.

rules.title: Corporations must certify Secretary of State filings
rules.plain_english: A domestic or foreign corporation applying for a license must complete a Registrar-prescribed certification showing it has met California Secretary of State filing requirements (Corporations Code 200 and 2105).

parameters.required: certification prescribed by Registrar showing Secretary of State filing requirements fulfilled

rules.applies_to: Corporate license applicants
rules.quote: A foreign or domestic corporation, applying for a license, shall complete a certification as prescribed by the Registrar, showing that it has fulfilled the filing requirements of the California Secretary of State as set out in Sections 200 and 2105 of the Corporations Code.
rules.notes: Corp Code 2105 is the foreign-corporation qualification statement.

rules.title: Claimed experience must be documented; at least 3% field-investigated
rules.plain_english: All experience claimed on a license application must be supportable by documentation satisfactory to CSLB, and CSLB conducts a comprehensive field investigation of at least 3% of applications.

parameters.documentation_standard: all claimed experience supportable by documentation satisfactory to the Board

rules.applies_to: License applicants and their qualifiers
rules.quote: the Registrar shall conduct a comprehensive field investigation of a minimum of 3% of all such applications. ... All claimed experience shall be supportable by documentation satisfactory to the Board.
rules.notes: Employee experience-tracking tools should retain proof (pay records, project lists, employer letters).

rules.title: License experience: 4 years within the last 10 years in the class
rules.plain_english: Every license applicant needs at least four years of experience as a journeyman, foreman, supervising employee or contractor in the specific classification, within the 10 years immediately before filing. A journeyman is a fully qualified worker who can work without supervision, or who completed an apprenticeship.

parameters.journeyman_definition: experienced worker fully qualified (not a trainee) able to perform the trade without supervision, or one who has completed an apprenticeship program

rules.applies_to: Qualifying individuals for all contractor license applications
rules.quote: Every applicant for a contractor’s license must have had, within the last 10 years immediately preceding the filing of the application, not less than four years experience as a journeyman, foreman, supervising employee or contractor in the particular class within which the applicant intends to engage as a contractor.
rules.notes: See 825(b)-(e) for former-qualifier, military, training credit and qualifier rules; 826 allows equivalent experience.

rules.title: Former qualifier in same class: no 10-year lookback
rules.plain_english: Someone who was previously the qualifier on a license in the same classification can count experience without the 10-year time limit.

parameters.condition: applicant formerly a qualifier on a license in the same classification

rules.applies_to: Former qualifiers re-applying in same classification
rules.quote: An applicant who was formerly a qualifier on a license in the same classification applied for may compute experience without regard to the ten-year limitation.

rules.title: Military service during National Emergency extends 10-year window
rules.plain_english: Time served in the U.S. armed forces during a National Emergency can be added to the 10-year experience window.

parameters.extension: length of U.S. armed forces service during a National Emergency added to the 10 years

rules.applies_to: License applicants with military service
rules.quote: An applicant shall not be jeopardized in computing time for service in the armed forces of the United States during a National Emergency and the length of service may be added to the 10 years mentioned above.
rules.notes: Calculator: lookback_years = 10 + years_of_qualifying_service.

rules.title: School training/apprenticeship counts for at most 3 years
rules.plain_english: Accredited school training or a completed approved apprenticeship in the trade counts as experience, but never for more than 3 of the 4 required years.

creditable: acceptable training in an accredited school
completion of approved apprenticeship program (Labor Code 3070 et seq.) or Registrar-approved equivalent
parameters.must_be_in: the construction trade for which application is made

rules.applies_to: License applicants
rules.quote: In no case, however, will such training or completion of an approved apprenticeship program count for more than 3 years of the experience.
rules.notes: Therefore at least 1 year must be practical experience.

rules.title: Experience must be held by the qualifier, who takes the exam
rules.plain_english: The required experience must belong to one member of the applicant entity or its responsible managing employee, and that person must take the exam.

parameters.experience_holder: one member of the applicant entity or a responsible managing employee
parameters.exam_taker: the same member or responsible managing employee

rules.applies_to: All license applicants (individuals and entities)
rules.quote: The required experience shall be possessed by one member of the applicant entity or by a responsible managing employee therefore, and the member or responsible managing employee shall be required to take the examination.

rules.title: C-47 applicants must submit HUD installer training certificate
rules.plain_english: Since September 30, 2021, a C-47 General Manufactured Housing applicant must complete HUD-compliant initial installer training (24 CFR 3286.308(a)) from a HUD-confirmed trainer and submit the Certificate of Completion of Training with the application; without it the application is incomplete.

parameters.proof_document: Certificate of Completion of Training (24 CFR 3286.303(c))
parameters.trainer: qualified trainer confirmed by HUD under 24 CFR 3286.301 et seq.

rules.applies_to: C-47 license applicants
rules.quote: An application submitted without the certificate prescribed by this subdivision is not complete within the meaning of section 7072 of the Business and Professions Code.
rules.notes: In addition to the 825 experience requirement.

rules.title: Registrar may accept equivalent knowledge/training
rules.plain_english: CSLB's Registrar may decide that an applicant lacking the exact experience in 16 CCR 825 has comparable knowledge, training or experience that is equivalent.
rules.applies_to: License applicants short of the 825 experience
rules.quote: The Registrar may determine that an applicant who does not have the specific experience required in Section 825 has some comparable knowledge, training, and/or experience which is equivalent to the required experience.

rules.title: CSLB processing deadlines: applications requiring exam
rules.plain_english: For applications that require an exam (original license, added class, replacement qualifier), CSLB must: say within 60 days of receipt if it is complete (and referred to exam) or deficient; decide within 5 days on a resubmitted application; decide licensure within 115 days after referral to exam (once exam passed and bonds/fees/documents filed); decide within 45 days after a later exam is passed; and may add 60 days if the application must be investigated.
rules.applies_to: Applicants for original license, additional classification, or qualifier replacement with exam
rules.quote: (1) The Board shall inform an applicant in writing within 60 days of receipt whether the application is complete and has been referred for examination or is deficient and what specific information is required.
rules.notes: Board-side deadlines; useful for estimating when a company can start contracting in a new classification.

rules.title: Historical CSLB processing times (with exam)
rules.plain_english: CSLB's printed past-two-year processing times for applications with exam: original license 11 / 253 / 726 days (min/median/max); additional classification 20 / 96 / 617 days; qualifier replacement 20 / 78 / 428 days. These include time the applicant was responsible for.

parameters.basis: Board's past two years performance (as printed in regulation)

rules.applies_to: Planning for license/classification timelines
rules.quote: These periods include not only the Board’s processing time, but also the time for which the applicant is responsible: e.g., the return of a rejected application, failure of and/or failure to appear at examinations, filing of the required bond(s) and fee.
rules.notes: Figures are historical statistics embedded in the regulation, not legal deadlines; the reference period is not dated in the text and may be outdated.
rules.correction: No error. All nine min/median/max figures match.

rules.title: CSLB processing deadlines: applications not requiring exam
rules.plain_english: For applications without exam (B&P 7065 or 7065.1 waivers): CSLB must say within 50 days of receipt whether complete and what is required; decide within 5 days on a resubmitted application; and decide licensure within 15 days after acceptable bonds and documents are filed. The 50-day period can be extended 60 days for investigation.

applies_to_types: replacement of qualifying person without exam

rules.applies_to: Applicants under B&P 7065 or 7065.1 (no exam)
rules.quote: (3) Once the applicant has filed acceptable bond(s) and other documents required by Division 3 of the Business and Professions Code, the Board shall decide within 15 days whether the applicant meets the requirements for licensure.

rules.title: Historical CSLB processing times (without exam)
rules.plain_english: CSLB's printed past-two-year processing times without exam: original license 1 / 48 / 349 days (min/median/max); additional classification 24 / 58.5 / 358 days; qualifier replacement 1 / 29 / 253 days. These include applicant-caused time.

parameters.basis: Board's past two years performance (as printed in regulation)

rules.applies_to: Planning for license/classification timelines
rules.quote: These periods include not only the Board’s processing time, but also the time for which the applicant is responsible: e.g., return of a rejected application and filing of the required bond(s) and fee.
rules.notes: Historical statistics, not legal deadlines; reference period not dated.
rules.correction: No error. All nine min/median/max figures match (incl. 58.5-day median).

rules.title: Home improvement salesperson registration processing
rules.plain_english: CSLB must tell an HIS applicant within 30 days of receipt whether the application is deficient or the registration is issued, and decide within 5 days after a corrected application is returned. These periods can be extended 5 weeks if paid by personal or company check, or 60 days if investigation is needed. Historical times: 1 / 8 / 53 days (min/median/max).

parameters.completed_application_definition: acceptable form plus all required information, documentation and fee

rules.applies_to: Home improvement salesperson (HIS) applicants and the contractors who employ them
rules.quote: (c) The time periods outlined in (a) and (b) may be extended by 5 weeks if the fee is in the form of a personal or company check, or by 60 days if an application requires investigation to determine if a statement of issues must be filed.
rules.notes: Onboarding tool: budget up to ~30 days (plus extensions) before a new salesperson can sell home improvement contracts.

rules.title: Licensees may not contract outside their classifications
rules.plain_english: Every license is classified as Class A (general engineering), Class B (general building), or a specialty (C) class. A contractor licensed in one classification may not contract in another classification's field unless also licensed in it or the work is incidental and supplemental (16 CCR 831).

parameters.rule: no contracting in field of another classification unless also licensed in it or permitted by 16 CCR 831

rules.applies_to: All licensed contractors
rules.quote: (b) Contractors licensed in one classification shall be prohibited from contracting in the field of any other classification unless they are also licensed in that classification or are permitted to do so by Section 831.
rules.notes: Core check for bid/contract scope vs. license classes held.

rules.title: Incidental and supplemental work: essential to licensed work
rules.plain_english: Work in another classification is 'incidental and supplemental' to a specialty contractor's licensed work if it is essential to accomplish the licensed work. The specialty contractor may do it with its own employees or subcontract it.

parameters.test: work in other classification is essential to accomplish the work in which the contractor is classified

rules.applies_to: Specialty (C) contractors
rules.quote: For purposes of Section 7059, work in other classifications is “incidental and supplemental” to the work for which a specialty contractor is licensed if that work is essential to accomplish the work in which the contractor is classified. A specialty contractor may use subcontractors to complete the incidental and supplemental work, or they may use their own employees to do so.
rules.notes: Subcontracting incidental work still requires the sub to hold the proper class (general CSLB rules).

rules.title: List of CSLB specialty (C) classifications
