rules.plain_english: CSLB specialty classes are: C-2 Insulation/Acoustical, C-4 Boiler/Hot Water/Steam, C-5 Framing/Rough Carpentry, C-6 Cabinet/Millwork/Finish Carpentry, C-7 Low Voltage, C-8 Concrete, C-9 Drywall, C-10 Electrical, C-11 Elevator, C-12 Earthwork/Paving, C-13 Fencing, C-15 Flooring, C-16 Fire Protection, C-17 Glazing, C-20 HVAC, C-21 Building Moving/Demolition, C-22 Asbestos Abatement, C-23 Ornamental Metal, C-27 Landscaping, C-28 Lock/Security, C-29 Masonry, C-31 Traffic Control, C-32 Parking/Highway Improvement, C-33 Painting, C-34 Pipeline, C-35 Lathing/Plastering, C-36 Plumbing, C-38 Refrigeration, C-39 Roofing, C-42 Sanitation, C-43 Sheet Metal, C-45 Sign, C-46 Solar, C-47 Manufactured Housing, C-49 Tree/Palm, C-50 Reinforcing Steel, C-51 Structural Steel, C-53 Swimming Pool, C-54 Tile, C-55 Water Conditioning, C-57 Well Drilling, C-60 Welding, C-61 Limited Specialty. Specialty contractors must work to the standards of their trade.

classes.C-4: Boiler, Hot Water Heating and Steam Fitting
classes.C-6: Cabinet, Mill Work and Finish Carpentry
classes.C-20: Warm-Air Heating, Ventilating and Air Conditioning

parameters.performance_standard: art, experience, science and skill necessary to satisfactorily organize, administer, construct and complete projects, in accordance with the standards of their trade

rules.applies_to: All specialty contractors; scope-to-license matching
rules.quote: Specialty contractors shall perform their trade using the art, experience, science and skill necessary to satisfactorily organize, administer, construct and complete projects under their classification, in accordance with the standards of their trade.
rules.notes: Class A and Class B are defined in B&P 7056/7057 (not in this chunk). C-61 has many CSLB-designated subcategories (D-codes) not listed here.

rules.title: C-2 Insulation and Acoustical scope
rules.plain_english: C-2 contractors install any insulating media and preformed architectural acoustical materials for temperature and/or sound control.
rules.applies_to: Insulation and acoustical work
rules.quote: An insulation and acoustical contractor installs any insulating media and preformed architectural acoustical materials for the purpose of temperature and/or sound control.

rules.title: C-4 Boiler, Hot-Water Heating and Steam Fitting scope
rules.plain_english: C-4 contractors install, service and repair power boilers, hot-water heating systems and steam fitting, including fire-tube and water-tube boilers, low-pressure hot-water boilers, piping, valves, gauges, pumps, radiators, convectors, fuel oil tanks/lines, chimneys, flues, heat insulation and associated equipment including solar heating equipment.

scope_includes: fire-tube and water-tube steel power boilers
solar heating equipment associated with these systems

rules.applies_to: Boiler and hydronic/steam heating work
rules.quote: A boiler, hot-water heating and steam fitting contractor installs, services and repairs power boiler installations, hot-water heating systems and steam fitting ... and all other equipment, including solar heating equipment, associated with these systems.

rules.title: C-5 Framing and Rough Carpentry scope
rules.plain_english: C-5 contractors do form work, framing and rough carpentry for framed structures, including sub-flooring, siding, exterior staircases and railings, overhead doors, roof decking, truss members and sheathing.
rules.applies_to: Framing and rough carpentry work
rules.quote: A framing and rough carpentry contractor performs any form work, framing or rough carpentry necessary to construct framed structures; installs or repairs individual components of framing systems and performs any rough carpentry or associated work

rules.title: C-6 Cabinet, Millwork and Finish Carpentry scope
rules.plain_english: C-6 contractors make cabinets, cases, sashes, doors, trims, nonbearing partitions and other finish carpentry from wood or other products, and place, erect and finish them in structures.

scope_includes: placing, erecting and finishing cabinets and millwork in structures

rules.applies_to: Cabinet and finish carpentry work
rules.quote: A cabinet, millwork and finish carpentry contractor makes cabinets, cases, sashes, doors, trims, nonbearing partitions and other items of ... This contractor also places, erects, and finishes such cabinets and millwork in structures.

rules.title: C-7 Low Voltage Systems: energy-limited, max 91 volts, no fire alarms
rules.plain_english: C-7 contractors install, service and maintain energy-limited communication and low voltage systems not exceeding 91 volts (phone, sound, cable TV, CCTV, satellite dishes, instrumentation and temperature controls, low voltage landscape lighting). Low voltage fire alarm systems are excluded.
rules.applies_to: Low voltage and communications work
rules.quote: A communication and low voltage contractor installs, services and maintains all types of communication and low voltage systems which are energy limited and do not exceed 91 volts. ... Low voltage fire alarm systems are specifically not included in this section.
rules.notes: Scope check: system voltage > 91 V or fire alarm requires another class (e.g., C-10).

rules.title: C-8 Concrete scope
rules.plain_english: C-8 contractors form, pour, place, finish and install mass, pavement, flat and other concrete work and set screeds. The class does not cover contractors whose only business is plaster coatings or placing reinforcing steel.

scope_includes: forming, pouring, placing, finishing, installing mass, pavement, flat and other concrete work
placing and setting screeds for pavements or flatwork
scope_excludes: contractors whose sole business is application of plaster coatings
contractors whose sole business is placing/erecting reinforcing steel or bars

rules.applies_to: Concrete work
rules.quote: A concrete contractor forms, pours, places, finishes and installs specified mass, pavement, flat and other concrete work; and places and sets screeds for pavements or flatwork.

rules.title: C-9 Drywall scope
rules.plain_english: C-9 contractors lay out and install gypsum wallboard and assemblies, including nonstructural metal framing, and do taping and texturing.
rules.applies_to: Drywall work
rules.quote: A drywall contractor lays out and installs gypsum wall board and gypsum wallboard assemblies including nonstructural metal framing members, and performs the taping and texturing operations including the applications of compounds that adhere to wall board to produce a continuous smooth or textured surface.

rules.title: C-10 Electrical scope (includes batteries and PV; stayed amendment)
rules.plain_english: C-10 contractors place, install, erect or connect any electrical wires, fixtures, appliances, apparatus, raceways, conduits, battery energy storage systems, photovoltaic solar systems or parts thereof that generate, transmit, transform or use electricity.

parameters.status: effective date temporarily stayed at time of printing (amended text)

rules.applies_to: Electrical, PV and battery storage work
rules.quote: An electrical contractor places, installs, erects or connects any electrical wires, fixtures, appliances, apparatus, raceways, conduits, battery energy storage systems, photovoltaic solar energy systems or any part thereof, which generate, transmit, transform or utilize electrical energy in any form or for any purpose.
rules.effective: Effective date temporarily stayed at time of printing
rules.notes: The explicit battery/PV language is part of a stayed amendment; verify current status with CSLB.

rules.title: C-11 Elevator scope
rules.plain_english: C-11 contractors fabricate, erect, install and repair elevators, including sheave beams, motors, cables, guides, cabs, counterweights, doors (including sidewalk elevator doors), controls and signal systems for electric, hydraulic and manual elevators.
rules.applies_to: Elevator work
rules.quote: An elevator contractor fabricates, erects, installs and repairs elevators, including sheave beams, motors, sheaves, cable and wire rope, guides, cab, counterweights, doors (including sidewalk elevator doors), automatic and manual controls, signal systems

rules.title: C-12 Earthwork and Paving scope
rules.plain_english: C-12 contractors dig, move and place earth materials for cuts, fills, excavations, grades, trenches, backfill and incidental tunnels (including use of explosives), and mix, fabricate and place paving and other surfacing.

scope_includes: use of explosives for these purposes
mixing, fabricating and placing paving and surfacing materials

rules.applies_to: Earthwork, grading and paving
rules.quote: An earthwork and paving contractor digs, moves, and places material forming the surface of the earth, other than water, in such a manner that a cut, fill, excavation, grade, trench, backfill, or tunnel (if incidental thereto) can be executed, including the use of explosives for these purposes.

rules.title: C-13 Fencing scope (excludes masonry walls)
rules.plain_english: C-13 contractors build and repair all types of fences, corrals, runs, railings, cribs, game court enclosures, guard rails and barriers, playground equipment, backstops, posts, flagpoles and gates, but not masonry walls.
rules.applies_to: Fencing work
rules.quote: A fencing contractor constructs, erects, alters, or repairs all types of fences, corrals, runs, railings, cribs, game court enclosures, guard rails and barriers, playground game equipment, backstops, posts, flagpoles, and gates, excluding masonry walls.
rules.notes: Masonry walls require C-29 (or B).

rules.title: C-15 Flooring and Floor Covering scope (excludes ceramic tile)
rules.plain_english: C-15 contractors prepare surfaces and install carpet, resilient sheet and tile, wood floors (including finishing and repair) and other flooring materials, except ceramic tile.

scope_includes: wood floors and flooring including finishing and repairing

rules.applies_to: Flooring work
rules.quote: A flooring and floor covering contractor prepares any surface for the installation of flooring and floor coverings, and installs carpet, resilient sheet goods, resilient tile, wood floors and flooring (including the finishing and repairing thereof), and any other materials established as flooring and floor covering material, except ceramic tile.
rules.notes: Ceramic tile requires C-54.

rules.title: C-16 Fire Protection scope (excludes electrical alarms)
rules.plain_english: C-16 contractors lay out, fabricate and install all types of fire protection systems and associated equipment, excluding electrical alarm systems.

scope_includes: all types of fire protection systems

rules.applies_to: Fire sprinkler / fire protection work
rules.quote: A fire protection contractor lays out, fabricates and installs all types of fire protection systems; including all the equipment associated with these systems, excluding electrical alarm systems.

rules.title: C-17 Glazing scope
rules.plain_english: C-17 contractors select, cut, assemble and install all glass, mirrored glass and glass substitutes, and fabricate and glaze frames, panels, sashes and doors.

scope_includes: fabrication and glazing of frames, panels, sashes and doors

rules.applies_to: Glazing work
rules.quote: A glazing contractor selects, cuts, assembles and/or installs all makes and kinds of glass, glass work, mirrored glass, and glass substitute materials for glazing; executes the fabrication and glazing of frames, panels, sashes and doors; and/or installs these items in any structure.

rules.title: C-20 Warm-Air Heating, Ventilating and Air-Conditioning scope
rules.plain_english: C-20 contractors fabricate, install, maintain, service and repair warm-air heating systems, water heating heat pumps, ventilating and air-conditioning systems with their ducts, registers, flues, controls and filters, including solar-powered HVAC.

scope_includes: ventilating systems with blowers and plenum chambers

rules.applies_to: HVAC work
rules.quote: A warm-air heating, ventilating and air-conditioning contractor fabricates, installs, maintains, services and repairs warm-air heating systems and water heating heat pumps, complete with warm-air appliances
rules.notes: Refrigeration below 50 F is C-38.

rules.title: C-21 Building Moving/Demolition scope
rules.plain_english: C-21 contractors raise, lower, crib, underpin, demolish, and move or remove structures and their foundations, but not alterations, additions, repairs or rehabilitation of the parts of a structure that stay.

scope_includes: moving or removing structures including foundations
scope_excludes: alterations, additions, repairs or rehabilitation of permanently retained portions

rules.applies_to: Demolition and building moving
rules.quote: A building moving/demolition contractor raises, lowers, cribs, underpins, demolishes and moves or removes structures, including their foundations. This classification does not include the alterations, additions, repairs or rehabilitation of the permanently retained portions of such structures.

rules.title: C-22 Asbestos Abatement scope; DOSH rules govern work and documents
rules.plain_english: C-22 contractors perform asbestos abatement (containment, encapsulation, removal and disposal of asbestos-containing construction materials) in and on buildings. All work and documentation must follow DOSH (Cal/OSHA) regulations. C-22 does not include rebuilding retained portions or hazardous substance removal.

scope_includes: disposal of asbestos containing construction materials (Labor Code 6501.8)
scope_excludes: addition to or alteration, repair, or rehabilitation of permanently retained portions of buildings/structures

rules.applies_to: Asbestos abatement work
rules.quote: An asbestos abatement contractor performs abatement, including containment, encapsulation, or removal, and disposal of asbestos containing construction materials, as defined in Section 6501.8 of the Labor Code, in and on buildings and structures.
rules.notes: Hazardous substance removal requires separate HAZ certification (B&P 7058.7).

rules.title: C-22: DOSH registration; proof within 90 days or automatic suspension
rules.plain_english: CSLB will not issue a C-22 unless the applicant is registered with DOSH (Labor Code 6501.5) or has a registration application pending, and all C-22 holders must complete DOSH registration training (8 CCR 1529). Within 90 days after the license issues, the contractor must give CSLB proof of DOSH registration; no asbestos work or documentation may be done until then. Missing the 90 days automatically suspends the license or removes the C-22 class.

parameters.pre_issuance_requirement: registered with DOSH under Labor Code 6501.5 or active DOSH registration application in process
parameters.proof_deadline_from: issuance of asbestos abatement contractor license
parameters.consequence_if_missed: automatic suspension of license or removal of C-22 classification at end of 90 days

rules.applies_to: C-22 applicants and licensees
rules.citation: 16 CCR 832.22(b)-(c); B&P 7180(b) (Labor Code 6501.5 registration still required)
rules.quote: Failure of a licensee to provide proof of current registration with DOSH within 90 days after issuance shall result in the automatic suspension of the license or removal of the C-22—asbestos abatement contractor classification at the end of the 90 days.
rules.notes: Deadline calculator: license_issue_date + 90 days; block scheduling asbestos jobs until proof is submitted.

rules.title: C-22 experience: 4 years in last 10 performing asbestos abatement
rules.plain_english: A C-22 applicant needs at least 4 years in the 10 years before applying performing asbestos abatement as a journeyman, foreman, supervisor or contractor for: a licensed C-22 (or asbestos-certified) DOSH-registered contractor, an out-of-state/federal licensed abatement contractor, a regulated utility, a state or federal government division, or the U.S. armed forces.

qualifying_employers: licensed contractor with C-22 or asbestos certification (B&P 7058.5) and DOSH registration
asbestos abatement contractor licensed in another state or federal jurisdiction
utility company operating under state or federal regulatory agency
division of a state or the federal government

rules.applies_to: C-22 applicants
rules.quote: Every applicant for the C-22—asbestos abatement contractor classification must have had, within the last 10 years immediately preceding the filing of the application, not less than four years of experience performing asbestos abatement duties as a journeyman,

rules.title: C-22 renewal requires current DOSH registration on file
rules.plain_english: A C-22 license can only be renewed if the licensee has proof of current DOSH registration on file with CSLB.

parameters.renewal_precondition: proof of current DOSH registration (Labor Code 6501.5) on file

rules.applies_to: C-22 licensees renewing
rules.quote: The Board shall require as a condition precedent to the renewal of an asbestos abatement contractor license that the licensee have on file proof of current registration with DOSH pursuant to Section 6501.5 of the Labor Code.
rules.notes: Track DOSH registration expiration alongside CSLB renewal date.

rules.title: C-23 Ornamental Metal scope
rules.plain_english: C-23 contractors fabricate and install sheet, rolled and cast metals (brass, bronze, copper, iron, stainless, steel, etc.) for architectural treatment and ornamental decoration, but not sheet metal contractor work.

scope_includes: assembling, casting, cutting, shaping, stamping, forging, welding, fabricating and installing metals for architectural treatment and ornamental decoration
scope_excludes: work of a sheet metal contractor

rules.applies_to: Ornamental metal work
rules.quote: This classification does not include the work of a sheet metal contractor.

rules.title: C-27 Landscaping scope
rules.plain_english: C-27 contractors construct, maintain, repair, install, or subcontract landscape systems and facilities for gardens and grounds, and prepare and grade land for architectural, horticultural and decorative treatment.

scope_includes: construct, maintain, repair, install, or subcontract landscape systems and facilities
public and private gardens and grounds
preparing and grading plots for architectural, horticultural and decorative treatment

rules.applies_to: Landscaping work
rules.quote: A landscape contractor constructs, maintains, repairs, installs, or subcontracts the development of landscape systems and facilities for public and private gardens and other areas which are designed to aesthetically, architecturally, horticulturally, or functionally improve the grounds within or surrounding a structure or a tract or plot of land.

rules.title: C-28 Lock and Security Equipment scope (excludes fire alarms)
rules.plain_english: C-28 contractors install and repair doors and door assemblies, gates, locks, panic and fire-rated exit devices, door/gate operators, jail locking devices, built-in safes and vaults, master key systems, window guards, security doors, card/electronic access control, detectors and related control computers. Fire alarm systems are excluded.

scope_includes: panic and fire rated exit devices
manual and automatic gate and door closures and releases
card activated and electronic access control systems

rules.applies_to: Locks, access control and security equipment work
rules.quote: A lock and security equipment contractor evaluates, sets up, installs, maintains and repairs all doors and door assemblies, gates, locks and locking devices, panic and fire rated exit devices ... Fire alarm systems are specifically not included in this section.

rules.title: C-29 Masonry scope
rules.plain_english: C-29 contractors install concrete units, clay products, block, stone, terra cotta and refractory brick, including load-bearing and non-load-bearing masonry walls and fences, ceramic veneer and thin brick, masonry paving, and incidental waterproofing, cleaning and caulking.

scope_includes: concrete units and baked clay products
structural load bearing and non-load bearing masonry walls and fences
ceramic veneer (not tile) and thin brick
clear waterproofing, cleaning and caulking incidental to masonry

rules.applies_to: Masonry work
rules.quote: A masonry contractor installs concrete units and baked clay products; concrete, glass and clay block; natural and manufactured stone; terra cotta; and fire brick or other material for refractory work.

rules.title: C-31 Construction Zone Traffic Control scope
rules.plain_english: C-31 contractors set up or remove lane closures, flagging or traffic diversions on roadways using portable devices like cones, delineators, barricades, sign stands, flashing beacons, arrow trailers and changeable message signs.
rules.applies_to: Construction zone traffic control
rules.quote: A construction zone traffic control contractor prepares or removes lane closures, flagging or traffic diversions, utilizing portable devices, such as cones, delineators, barricades, sign stands, flashing beacons, flashing arrow trailers, and changeable message signs, on roadways

rules.title: C-32 Parking and Highway Improvement scope (no re-paving)
rules.plain_english: C-32 contractors apply protective coatings and install vehicle stops, guard rails, striping, buttons, markers, signs and arrows on game courts, parking lots, airports and roads, including surface prep for coatings, but not re-paving.

scope_includes: signs and arrows on horizontal surfaces
surfaces: highway or roadway (concrete, asphalt or similar)

rules.applies_to: Striping, sealcoat and parking improvements
rules.quote: This classification includes the surface preparatory work necessary for the application of protective coatings but does not include the re-paving of these surfaces.
rules.notes: Re-paving requires C-12 or A.

rules.title: C-33 Painting and Decorating scope
rules.plain_english: C-33 contractors prepare surfaces (scraping, sandblasting, etc.) and apply paints, papers, textures, fabrics, stains, varnishes, sealers, waxes, adhesives and similar materials to structures for decorating, protecting, fireproofing and waterproofing.

scope_includes: surface preparation by scraping, sandblasting or other means

rules.applies_to: Painting and wallcovering
rules.quote: A painting and decorating contractor prepares by scraping, sandblasting or other means and applies any of the following: paints, papers, textures, fabrics, pigments, oils, turpentines, japans, driers, thinners, varnishes, shellacs, stains, fillers, waxes, adhesives

rules.title: C-34 Pipeline scope
rules.plain_english: C-34 contractors fabricate and install pipelines for water, gas, petroleum or other materials, including protective coatings and the trenching, boring, shoring, backfilling, compacting, paving and surfacing needed to complete them.

scope_includes: pipelines for conveyance of fluids (water, gas, petroleum)
pipelines for containment or protection of other material
trenching, boring, shoring, backfilling, compacting, paving and surfacing necessary to complete installation

rules.applies_to: Pipeline work
rules.quote: A pipeline contractor fabricates and installs pipelines for the conveyance of fluids, such as water, gas, or petroleum, or for the containment or protection of any other material, including the application of protective coatings or systems and the trenching, boring, shoring, backfilling, compacting, paving and surfacing necessary to complete the installation of such pipelines.

rules.title: C-35 Lathing and Plastering scope
rules.plain_english: C-35 contractors apply plaster and cement coatings (troweled or sprayed, including soundproofing and fireproofing) and install lath, metal studs, channel work and other plaster bases.

scope_includes: plaster/cement/lime surface coatings applied by trowel or spray
wood and metal lath and other plaster bases
channel work and metal studs for lathing and solid plaster partitions

rules.applies_to: Lath and plaster/stucco work
rules.quote: This classification includes the channel work and metal studs for the support of metal or any other lathing material and for solid plaster partitions.

rules.title: C-36 Plumbing scope
rules.plain_english: C-36 contractors provide safe water supply and fluid waste disposal, including on-site waste systems, gas/liquid/medical gas piping and tanks, gas appliances and flues (not forced warm air units), water and gas piping from the owner's side of the meter, water heaters including solar, and maintenance of safety devices like gas earthquake valves and backflow preventers.

scope_includes: complete removal of waste; construction and connection of on-site waste disposal systems
piping, storage tanks and venting for gases and liquids incl. vacuum, compressed air, medical/dental/commercial/industrial gases
gas appliances, flues and gas connections incl. suspended space heating units
water and gas piping from property owner's side of utility meter to structure
equipment to heat water or fluids, incl. solar equipment
maintenance and replacement of above and of gas earthquake valves, gas control valves, backflow preventers, water conditioning equipment, regulating valves

rules.applies_to: Plumbing work
rules.quote: (d) Water and gas piping from the property owner’s side of the utility meter to the structure or fixed works;

rules.title: C-38 Refrigeration: temperatures below 50 F (10 C)
rules.plain_english: C-38 contractors build, install, maintain and repair refrigerators, refrigerated rooms and spaces, insulation, AC units, ducts, blowers and controls for controlling air, liquid or gas temperatures below 50 degrees F (10 degrees C).
rules.applies_to: Refrigeration work
rules.quote: units, ducts, blowers, registers, humidity and thermostatic controls for the control of air, liquid, and/or gas temperatures below fifty degrees Fahrenheit (50°), or ten degrees Celsius (10°).
rules.notes: Scope check: design temperature < 50 F -> C-38; comfort cooling -> C-20.

rules.title: C-39 Roofing scope
rules.plain_english: C-39 contractors install and repair surfaces that seal, waterproof and weatherproof structures, using asphalt, pitch, tar, felt, glass fabric, urethane foam, metal roofing, shakes, shingles, tile, slate and other roofing or membrane materials.

materials: other roofing, waterproofing, weatherproofing or membrane materials

rules.applies_to: Roofing and waterproofing
rules.quote: A roofing contractor installs products and repairs surfaces that seal, waterproof and weatherproof structures.

rules.title: C-42 Sanitation System scope
rules.plain_english: C-42 contractors fabricate and install cesspools, septic tanks, storm drains and other sewage disposal and drain structures, including laying the associated pipe.

scope_includes: other sewage disposal and drain structures
cast-iron, steel, concrete, vitreous and non-vitreous pipe and related hardware

rules.applies_to: Septic, sewer and storm drain work
rules.quote: A sanitation system contractor fabricates and installs cesspools, septic tanks, storm drains, and other sewage disposal and drain structures.

rules.title: C-43 Sheet Metal scope
rules.plain_english: C-43 contractors fabricate and install sheet metal such as cornices, flashings, gutters, leaders, pans, kitchen equipment, ductwork (including insulation), patented chimneys, metal flues and metal roofing.
rules.applies_to: Sheet metal work
rules.quote: A sheet metal contractor selects, cuts, shapes, fabricates and installs sheet metal such as cornices, flashings, gutters, leaders, pans, kitchen equipment, duct work (including insulation, patented chimneys, metal flues, metal roofing systems and any other installations requiring sheet metal).

rules.title: C-45 Sign scope (includes sign wiring)
rules.plain_english: C-45 contractors fabricate, install and erect electrical signs (including their wiring) and non-electrical signs such as pole signs, building-mounted signs, painted wall signs and sign modifications.

scope_includes: electrical signs including wiring of such signs

rules.applies_to: Sign work
rules.quote: A sign contractor fabricates, installs, and erects electrical signs, including the wiring of such electrical signs, and non-electrical signs

rules.title: C-46 Solar: batteries only as incidental to PV and up to 80 kWh (stayed)
rules.plain_english: C-46 contractors install, modify, maintain and repair thermal and PV solar systems and may not do other building trades except as required for the solar install. A battery energy storage system is not part of a PV system; a C-46 may install a battery only as incidental and supplemental to a PV installation and only if the battery is rated 80 kWh or less.

parameters.other_trades_allowed: only when required to install a thermal or PV system
parameters.bess_allowed_if: installed as incidental and supplemental to installation of a PV system
parameters.status: effective date temporarily stayed at time of printing

rules.applies_to: Solar contractors installing PV and battery storage
rules.quote: a licensee classified in this section may install a battery energy storage system as “incidental and supplemental” to the installation of a photovoltaic solar energy system if the battery energy storage system does not exceed a rating of 80 kilowatt-hours (kWh).
rules.effective: Effective date temporarily stayed at time of printing
rules.notes: Verify current status with CSLB; standalone battery retrofits or batteries > 80 kWh would need C-10 (or other appropriate class) under this text.
rules.correction: No error. 80 kWh limit and the "effective date temporarily stayed at time of printing" flag confirmed.

rules.title: C-47 General Manufactured Housing scope
rules.plain_english: C-47 contractors install, alter, repair or prepare for moving manufactured homes, mobilehomes and multifamily manufactured homes, including accessory structures and foundations, and may connect gas, water, sewer and electric utilities on a single-family individual site placement. RVs, commercial coaches and factory-built housing are excluded.

parameters.utility_services_allowed: connection of gas, water, sewer, and electrical utilities on a single-family individual site placement

rules.applies_to: Manufactured housing installers
rules.quote: A general manufactured housing contractor may provide utility services on a single-family individual site placement. Utility services mean the connection of gas, water, sewer, and electrical utilities to the home.
rules.notes: See 825.5 for HUD installer training requirement.

rules.title: C-49 Tree and Palm scope (operative Jan 1, 2024)
rules.plain_english: Since January 1, 2024, C-49 contractors plant, maintain and remove trees and palms, including pruning, stump grinding and guying. No license is needed for incidental pruning or guying of planted trees by a nurseryperson, or incidental pruning by a gardener (B&P 7026.1).

license_not_required_for: incidental pruning of trees or guying of planted trees and limbs by a nurseryperson
incidental pruning of trees by a gardener (B&P 7026.1)

rules.applies_to: Tree service work
rules.quote: (a) A tree and palm contractor plants, maintains, and removes trees and palms. The duties include pruning, stump grinding, and tree, palm, or limb guying. (b) Effective January 1, 2024, this regulation shall become operative.

rules.title: C-50 Reinforcing Steel scope
rules.plain_english: C-50 contractors fabricate, place and tie steel mesh or reinforcing bars of any profile used to reinforce concrete.

scope_includes: fabricate, place and tie steel mesh
steel reinforcing bars (rods) of any profile, perimeter, or cross-section for reinforcing concrete

rules.applies_to: Rebar work
rules.quote: A reinforcing steel contractor fabricates, places and ties steel mesh or steel reinforcing bars (rods), of any profile, perimeter, or cross-section, that are or may be used to reinforce concrete structures.

rules.title: C-51 Structural Steel scope
rules.plain_english: C-51 contractors fabricate and erect structural steel shapes and plates used as structural members, including riveting, welding, rigging and metal roofing systems needed for that work.

scope_includes: fabricate and erect structural steel shapes and plates
metal roofing systems necessary to perform this work

rules.applies_to: Structural steel work
rules.quote: A structural steel contractor fabricates and erects structural steel shapes and plates, of any profile, perimeter or cross-section, that are or may be used as structural members for buildings and structures, including the riveting, welding, rigging, and metal roofing systems necessary to perform this work.

rules.title: C-53 Swimming Pool scope
rules.plain_english: C-53 contractors build swimming pools, spas and hot tubs, including solar heating equipment, using the trades necessary for that construction.

scope_includes: trades or skills necessary for such construction

rules.applies_to: Pool and spa construction
rules.quote: A swimming pool contractor constructs swimming pools, spas or hot tubs, including installation of solar heating equipment using those trades or skills necessary for such construction.

rules.title: C-54 Tile (Ceramic and Mosaic) scope
rules.plain_english: C-54 contractors prepare surfaces and install glazed wall, ceramic, mosaic, quarry, paver, faience, glass mosaic and stone tile, thin brick-look tile, and natural or simulated stone slabs for tubs, showers and interior horizontal surfaces, excluding hollow or structural partition tile.

scope_includes: glazed wall, ceramic, mosaic, quarry, paver, faience, glass mosaic and stone tiles
thin tile that resembles full brick
natural or simulated stone slabs for bathtubs, showers and horizontal surfaces inside buildings

rules.applies_to: Tile and stone slab work
rules.quote: A ceramic and mosaic tile contractor prepares surfaces as necessary and installs glazed wall, ceramic, mosaic, quarry, paver, faience, glass mosaic and stone tiles

rules.title: C-55 Water Conditioning scope
rules.plain_english: C-55 contractors install water conditioning equipment using only the pipe and fittings needed to connect it to the water supply and bypass parts of the system that should not get conditioned water.

parameters.piping_limit: only pipe and fittings necessary to connect equipment to water supply and bypass parts excluded from conditioned water

rules.applies_to: Water softener/conditioning installs
rules.quote: A water conditioning contractor installs water conditioning equipment with the use of only such pipe and fittings as are necessary to connect the water conditioning equipment to the water supply system

rules.title: C-57 Well Drilling scope
rules.plain_english: C-57 contractors install and repair water wells and pumps by boring, drilling, excavating, casing, cementing and cleaning to provide uncontaminated water.
rules.applies_to: Water well work
rules.quote: A well drilling contractor installs and repairs water wells and pumps by boring, drilling, excavating, casing, cementing and cleaning to provide a supply of uncontaminated water.

rules.title: C-60 Welding scope
rules.plain_english: C-60 contractors permanently join and fabricate metals using gases and electrical energy that create enough heat to do the work.

scope_includes: permanently attaching, joining and fabricating metals using gases and electrical energy

rules.applies_to: Welding work
rules.quote: A welding contractor causes metals to become permanently attached, joined and fabricated by the use of gases and electrical energy, which creates temperatures of sufficient heat to perform this work.

rules.title: C-61 Limited Specialty: confined to endorsed scope
rules.plain_english: C-61 is for specialty work not covered by any other C class. A C-61 licensee may work only in the field and scope stated in its application, accepted by the Registrar and endorsed on the license, plus incidental and supplemental work. Other specialty contractors may do C-61-type work if it is consistent with industry usage and related to their own class.

parameters.eligibility: field and scope of specialty contracting not covered by any other listed specialty classification
parameters.scope_limit: field(s) and scope set forth in application and accepted by Registrar, or permitted by 16 CCR 831
parameters.license_endorsement: Registrar endorses field and scope on face of license certificate
other_specialty_may_perform_c61_work_if: consistent with established usage and procedure in construction industry
related to the specialty contractor's classification

rules.applies_to: C-61 licensees and other specialty contractors
rules.quote: (b) An applicant classified and licensed in the classification Limited Specialty shall confine activities as a contractor to that field or fields and scope of operations set forth in the application and accepted by the Registrar or to that permitted by Section 831.
rules.notes: D-subcategory list not in this chunk.

rules.title: Active solar systems within Class A and Class B; C-61 pool maintenance may repair pool solar
rules.plain_english: An active solar energy system counts as a fixed work requiring specialized engineering knowledge (so within Class A), and counts as using more than two unrelated building trades (relevant to Class B under B&P 7057). C-61 swimming pool maintenance contractors may repair active solar heating systems for swimming pools.

parameters.class_a: active solar energy system is within 'fixed works requiring specialized engineering knowledge and skill' (B&P 7056)
parameters.class_b: active solar energy system constitutes use of more than two unrelated building trades or crafts (B&P 7057)
parameters.c61_swimming_pool_maintenance: authorized to repair active solar heating systems for swimming pools (after SC-44 sunset one year after C-46 implementation)

rules.applies_to: Class A, Class B, and C-61 (Swimming Pool Maintenance) contractors doing solar work
rules.quote: (b) An active solar energy system constitutes use of more than two unrelated building trades or crafts within the meaning of Section 7057 of the Business and Professions Code.
rules.notes: The two-unrelated-trades test for Class B prime contracts is in B&P 7057 (not in this chunk). Regulation does not mention batteries.

rules.title: General building contractor needs C-22/asbestos cert or must subcontract asbestos work
rules.plain_english: C-22 is a stand-alone class for asbestos abatement no matter what other classes a contractor holds. A Class B general building contractor may not contract for a project that includes asbestos abatement unless it holds C-22, or the asbestos certification plus DOSH registration, or subcontracts the asbestos work to an appropriately licensed contractor.

parameters.trigger: project includes asbestos abatement work
allowed_if_any: holds asbestos certification (B&P 7058.5) AND DOSH registration
subcontracts with an appropriately licensed contractor

rules.applies_to: General building contractors bidding projects with asbestos abatement
rules.quote: (b) No general building contractor, as defined in Section 7057 of the Code, shall contract for any project that includes asbestos abatement work unless the general building contractor holds the C-22—asbestos abatement contractor classification or the asbestos certification, as defined in Section 7058.5 of the Code, and DOSH registration or unless the general building contractor subcontracts
rules.notes: Bid checker: if scope includes asbestos abatement and GC lacks C-22/cert+DOSH, require a C-22 subcontractor line.

rules.title: Asbestos certification works only within the contractor's licensed trades
rules.plain_english: The asbestos certification (B&P 7058.5) works together with the contractor's other classes; a certified contractor may not contract for asbestos abatement in a trade it is not licensed for unless it also holds C-22.

parameters.prohibited: contracting for project with asbestos abatement in a trade the contractor is not licensed in

rules.applies_to: Contractors holding the asbestos certification
rules.quote: No licensed contractor who holds the asbestos certification shall contract for any project that includes asbestos abatement work in a trade for which the contractor is not licensed, unless the licensee also holds the C-22—asbestos abatement contractor classification.

rules.title: C-22 trade exam waiver for long-time asbestos certification holders
rules.plain_english: The Registrar may waive the C-22 trade exam for a licensee holding the asbestos certification who shows at least 4 years of journey-level C-22 experience within the last 10 years, having passed the written asbestos certification exam and held the certification active and in good standing for the whole 4-year period.

parameters.certification_status_required: active and good standing throughout the four-year experience period

rules.applies_to: Licensees with asbestos certification seeking C-22
rules.quote: possesses not less than four years journey-level experience in the C-22—asbestos abatement contractor classification within the last 10 years immediately preceding the filing of the application.
rules.notes: Waiver is "pursuant to Section 7065.3" (PDF page 283); check the statute's own conditions too (qualifier listed on an active license 5 of the last 7 years; closely related classification).
rules.correction: No error. Added note: the waiver is granted "pursuant to Section 7065.3", so the statute's own conditions (e.g. qualifier listed on an active license 5 of the last 7 years, closely related classification) may also apply.

rules.title: Class A, B and specialty operating limits
rules.plain_english: A Class A general engineering contractor may operate only in the areas defined in B&P 7056; a Class B general building contractor may take prime contracts or subcontracts only as allowed by B&P 7057; a specialty contractor may not act as a contractor in any other classification except for work incidental or supplemental to a contract in a classification any contractor is licensed in.

parameters.class_a_limit: only within areas defined in B&P 7056
parameters.class_b_limit: prime contract or subcontract only as authorized by B&P 7057
parameters.specialty_limit: only in own classification(s), except work incidental or supplemental to performance of a contract in a classification in which any contractor is licensed

rules.applies_to: All licensed contractors
rules.quote: (c) A licensee classified as a specialty contractor, as defined in Section 7058 of the Code, shall not act in the capacity of a contractor in any classification other than one in which he/she is classified except on work incidental or supplemental to the performance of a contract in a classification in which any contractor is licensed by the Board.

rules.title: Written exam required for license and added classes; no oral exams
rules.plain_english: Unless the exam is waived under B&P 7065.1, every applicant, including for added classifications, must pass CSLB's written exam. No oral exams are given (reading instructions or translation by authorized staff or sworn translators is not an oral exam).

parameters.exception: exam waiver under B&P 7065.1
not_oral_exam: reading of instructions or questions by authorized Board personnel

rules.applies_to: License and classification applicants
rules.quote: Except as provided in Section 7065.1 of the Code, an applicant, including an applicant for an additional classification or classifications, must pass the written examination prescribed by the Registrar. No oral examination shall be given to any applicant.

rules.title: Renewal must be postmarked or delivered by the expiration date
rules.plain_english: CSLB mails a renewal form before expiration. The renewal application and fee must be postmarked or hand-delivered to CSLB headquarters on or before the license expiration date, or the renewal is delinquent. If CSLB returns an incomplete renewal, the corrected one must also be postmarked/delivered by the expiration date or the license expires. An expired license cannot be renewed until any delinquency fee is paid.

parameters.deadline: on or before license expiration date
parameters.incomplete_renewal: returned with reasons; resubmission must also be postmarked/delivered by expiration date
parameters.delinquency_fee: 50% of the renewal fee (B&P 7137(a)(5), PDF page 376)

rules.applies_to: All licensees
rules.quote: (b) A renewal application and fee must be postmarked or hand delivered to the Board's headquarters office on or before the expiration date of the license. Failure to comply with the requirements of this subsection shall result in the renewal application being deemed delinquent.
rules.notes: Reminder tool: send internal reminders well before expiration so an incomplete renewal can be fixed before the date. Delinquency fee is 50% of the renewal fee (B&P 7137(a)(5)).
rules.correction: No error. Added: the delinquency fee is 50% of the renewal fee (B&P 7137(a)(5)).

rules.title: Certificate of deposit in lieu of contractor bond: requirements
rules.plain_english: A certificate of deposit used instead of a contractor's bond (or qualifier's bond) must show the exact license name style (and the responsible managing individual for a qualifier bond), be payable to the Contractors State License Board without the word 'trustee', be issued for at least one year, auto-renew at each maturity, and pay interest to the depositor.

parameters.name_style_applicant: as on page one of the application
parameters.name_style_licensee: as currently recorded in CSLB official files
parameters.qualifier_bond_extra: name of the responsible managing individual

rules.applies_to: Applicants/licensees posting a cash-equivalent instead of a surety bond
rules.quote: (3) Be made payable to the Contractors State License Board. The word “trustee” shall not be included. (4) Be issued for a period of not less than one year. (5) Be automatically renewable at each maturity date. (6) Provide that any interest earned shall be paid to the depositor.
rules.notes: Bond amounts themselves are in B&P 7071.6/7071.9 (not in this chunk).

rules.title: Savings/credit union account assignment in lieu of bond: form contents
rules.plain_english: Assigning a savings and loan or credit union certificate/share account to CSLB instead of a bond requires a Registrar-approved form showing the assignment to the Board, the license name style, the applicant's/licensee's current address, the institution's name and address, a signed and titled officer declaration that the institution received written notice, and a Board receipt directing earnings to the assignor; plus the passbook/certificate showing the depositor, licensee/applicant, qualifier and required amount.

form_fields: assignment of the account to the board
current address of applicant or licensee
name and address of savings and loan association or credit union
declaration signed by institution officer (with title) acknowledging written notice of assignment
Board receipt directing earnings be paid to assignor
attachments: passbook or investment certificate / credit union certificate or share account passbook showing depositor, licensee/applicant, responsible managing individual (if applicable), and required amount

rules.applies_to: Applicants/licensees using account assignment in lieu of bond
rules.quote: (E) A declaration signed by an officer of the savings and loan association or the credit union that it received written notice of the assignment. This declaration shall include the title of the officer signing it.

rules.title: Bearer bonds in lieu of bond: 125% value; no personal checks for cash deposits
rules.plain_english: Eligible bearer bonds used instead of a surety bond go to a Sacramento bank acting as agent, with coupons attached, and their bid price on the first day of the month of deposit must be at least 25% more than the required bond or cash deposit amount. For cash deposits, personal checks are not accepted as cash.

parameters.valuation_basis: bid price on Pacific Coast Stock Exchange or other authoritative source on first day of month of submission
parameters.custodian: bank in Sacramento, California, acting as agent; delivers to State Treasurer only on Registrar order
parameters.coupons: remain attached until bonds permanently withdrawn

rules.applies_to: Applicants/licensees using bearer bonds or cash deposits in lieu of a surety bond
rules.quote: shall be at least 25% in excess of the amount of the surety bond or cash deposit required to be submitted.

rules.title: Blanket performance and payment bond: purpose and definition
rules.plain_english: A contractor can get Registrar approval for a blanket performance and payment bond to use the B&P 7159.5(a)(8) exemption (relating to home improvement down payment/progress payment limits). The blanket bond is a single instrument from an admitted surety guaranteeing full payment of all claims arising from the licensee's obligations under all its home improvement contracts.

parameters.instrument: single surety instrument executed by an admitted surety
parameters.covers: payment in full of all claims arising from obligations under any contract subject to B&P 7159 (home improvement contract)
parameters.obligation_definition: Civil Code 1427: a legal duty by which a person is bound to do or not to do a certain thing

rules.applies_to: Home improvement contractors seeking blanket bond approval
rules.quote: the term “blanket bond” means a single surety instrument, executed by an admitted surety that is conditioned for the payment in full of all claims that arise from the obligations created by a licensee under any contract that is subject to the provisions of Section 7159 of the Code

rules.title: Blanket bond must cover 100% of open home improvement contracts

rules.plain_english: On written request, the Registrar may approve a capped blanket bond if the licensee or its parent files Form 10-K with the SEC, submits its latest 10-K with the request and each later 10-K within 10 days of SEC filing, and keeps net worth of at least 10 times the bond amount, initially and annually.

rules.title: Capped blanket bond amounts: $10M / $5M / $1M by SEC filer status
rules.plain_english: A capped blanket bond amount depends on the licensee's (or parent's) SEC filer status: large accelerated filer $10 million; accelerated filer $5 million; non-accelerated filer $1 million.

(2) If a licensee, or the parent company of a licensee, is classified as an “accelerated filer” by the U.S. SEC, the amount of the blanket bond shall be $5 million.
rules.notes: Combined with 10x net worth test: large accelerated filer needs net worth >= $100M, accelerated >= $50M, non-accelerated >= $10M.

rules.title: Current ratio and quick ratio formulas for blanket bond
rules.plain_english: For blanket bond financial reporting, current ratio = current assets / current liabilities, and quick ratio = (current assets - inventory) / current liabilities.

rules.quote: (A) Current ratio calculation: current assets; divided by current liabilities. (B) Quick ratio calculation: current assets minus inventory; divided by current liabilities.

The Registrar may also deny or rescind approval if the financial information shows the licensee cannot meet current liabilities.

rules.plain_english: Every probation order requires the contractor to obey all laws governing contractors, have personnel of record appear for interviews with the Regional Deputy on request, and submit documents about its construction operations on demand. parameters.template_text: Information About Commercial General Liability Insurance Home Improvement Pursuant to California Business & Professions Code § 7159.3 (SB 2029), home improvement contractors must provide this notice and disclose whether or not they carry commercial general liability insurance. Did your contractor tell you whether he or she carries Commercial General Liability Insurance? Home improvement contractors are required by law to tell you whether or not they carry Commercial General Liability Insurance. This written statement must accompany the bid, if there is one, and the contract. What does this insurance cover? Commercial General Liability Insurance can protect against third-party bodily injury and accidental property damage. It is not intended to cover the work the contractor performs. Is this insurance required? No. But the Contractors State License Board strongly recommends that all contractors carry it. The Board cautions you to evaluate the risk to your family and property when you hire a contractor who is not insured. Ask yourself, if something went wrong, would this contractor be able to cover losses ordinarily covered by insurance? How can you make sure the contractor is insured? If he or she is insured, your contractor is required to provide you with the name and telephone number of the insurance company. Check with the insurance company to verify that the contractor’s insurance coverage will cover your project. What about a contractor who is self-insured? A self-insured contractor has made a business decision to be personally responsible for losses that would ordinarily be covered by insurance. Before contracting with a self-insured contractor, ask yourself, if something went wrong, would this contractor be able to cover losses ordinarily covered by insurance? ■ _______________ does not carry Commercial General Liability (CONTRACTOR’S NAME) Insurance. ■ _______________ carries Commercial General Liability (CONTRACTOR’S NAME) Insurance. The insurance company is ____________________________ (COMPANY NAME) You may call the insurance company at ___________________ (TELEPHONE NUMBER) to verify coverage. For more information about Commercial General Liability Insurance, contact the Contractors State License Board at www.cslb.ca.gov or call 800-321-CSLB (2752). (This form meets the requirements of Rule 872 and Sections 7159.3 and 7164, Business and Professions Code.)

rules.title: Per-citation total cap when all violations are on the same project
rules.plain_english: If one citation lists several violations that all relate to the same construction project, the total penalty on that citation cannot exceed $8,000. The cap rises to $15,000 for B&P 7028.7 (unlicensed) violations and to $30,000 for violations of B&P 7110, 7114, 7118 or 7125.4.

parameters.trigger: citation lists more than one violation AND each violation relates to the same construction project

rules.applies_to: Any person receiving a multi-violation CSLB citation tied to a single construction project
rules.quote: (c) Where a citation lists more than one violation and each of the violations relates to the same construction project, the total penalty assessment in each citation shall not exceed $ 8,000, except as provided for violations of Section 7028.7, in which case ... shall not exceed $ 15,000, and for violations of Sections 7110, 7114, 7118, or 7125.4, in which case ... shall not exceed $ 30,000.
rules.effective: Subsection (c) amended by change without regulatory effect filed 8-17-2023 (PDF page 558)
rules.notes: The text does not say how the cap works when a single citation mixes a $30,000-cap section with ordinary sections; a reasonable reading is that the higher cap applies to the citation, but treat as an interpretation. Cap does not apply when violations relate to different projects. Since 7-1-2026 each penalty also has a statutory minimum (B&P 7099.2(b)(1): $500, or $1,500 for 7110/7114/7118; B&P 7028.7(c): $1,500).

rules.title: Factors the Registrar weighs when setting the penalty amount
rules.plain_english: Within the allowed range, CSLB must consider whether the citation has multiple violations, whether the person has a history of similar violations, bad faith, whether the violation is serious or harmful, whether the victims are seniors or disabled people, and whether the work repairs natural disaster damage. The regulation lists these as factors to consider. It does not say how much any one factor raises the penalty.

factors: history of violations of the same or similar sections
violation is serious or harmful (Registrar's judgment)
violation perpetrated against a senior citizen or disabled person
violation involves a project repairing damage from a natural disaster as described in B&P 7158

rules.title: Multi-violation citations must state the penalty per section

rules.title: Contest a CSLB citation within 15 days after service (statute), not 15 working days from receipt (regulation)
rules.plain_english: To contest a CSLB citation issued under B&P 7099, file a written request with the Registrar within 15 days after the citation is served. The regulation (16 CCR 885) says 15 working days from receipt, and B&P 7099.3/7099.4 say 15 working days from service. But B&P 7099.8(a) applies 'notwithstanding any other law' and requires the written hearing request within 15 days after service. Use the 15-calendar-day period counted from the service date to be safe. Instead of (or as well as) a hearing, you can request an informal citation conference within the same 15 days. If you miss the deadline, the citation becomes a final order that no court or agency can review (B&P 7099.4).

parameters.trigger: service of the citation (not receipt)
parameters.file_with: Registrar (written request for administrative hearing per B&P 7099.5); alternatively a written request for an informal citation conference to the chief of the enforcement division or designee (B&P 7099.8(b)(1))

conflicting_periods_in_book.B&P 7099.4: 15 working days from service; extendable by registrar for cause (PDF p.341)
conflicting_periods_in_book.B&P 7099.8(a): within 15 days after service, notwithstanding any other law (PDF p.342)

parameters.extension: 16 CCR 885 and B&P 7099.4 allow the Registrar to extend for good cause/cause; B&P 7099.8 states no extension - do not rely on one
parameters.consequence_if_missed: citation deemed a final order of the registrar, not subject to review by any court or agency (B&P 7099.4)

rules.applies_to: Licensees (and others) served with a citation pursuant to B&P 7099

The 15 day period may be extended upon showing of good cause which determination is within the discretion of the Registrar.
rules.effective: New section effective 30th day after filing 4-7-81; renumbered 806 to 885 on 2-27-84 (PDF page 559)
rules.notes: 16 CCR 885 text is quoted correctly, but statute controls. Unlicensed-person citations (B&P 7028.7) follow the same rule: B&P 7028.10/7028.11 say 15 working days after service, and B&P 7099.8(a) also covers 7028.7 citations (15 days after service).
rules.correction: The 885 quote is accurate, but the deadline as stated is unsafe. B&P 7099.3/7099.4 run the period from service, not receipt. B&P 7099.8(a) ('Notwithstanding any other law') requires the written hearing request within 15 days after service, not 15 working days. Changed trigger to service and day_type to calendar days (formula service_date + 15 days). Added the informal-conference option (15/60/10/30 days) and the final-order consequence.

amount of the civil penalty (if assessed)

The amount of the civil penalty, if a civil penalty is assessed in the citation.

rules.title: How CSLB serves a citation

rules.title: Gravity factors for penalties on unlicensed contractors (B&P 7028.7)
rules.plain_english: Before setting a penalty against an unlicensed person cited under B&P 7028.7, CSLB considers how serious the conduct was, such as falsely claiming to be licensed, taking money without doing the work, using false documents or statements, misusing funds, doing hazardous or substandard work, breaking building/safety/labor/insurance laws, criminal convictions, and repeat violations.

criteria: falsely represented being licensed
failed to perform work for which money was received
executed or used false or misleading documents to induce contract or payment
made false or misleading statements to induce contract or payment
failed to apply funds received for services, labor, materials or equipment
performed work potentially hazardous to public health, safety or welfare
performed work violating building, safety, labor, compensation insurance or unemployment insurance laws
performed work not meeting acceptable trade standards
convicted of a crime in connection with the violation
committed any act that would be cause for discipline against a licensee
committed numerous or repeated violations

rules.applies_to: Contractors doing asbestos abatement
rules.quote: 833. ASBESTOS CLASSIFICATION AND CERTIFICATION LIMITATIONS AND EXAMINATION REQUIREMENT 1. New section filed 12-30-2014; operative 1-1-2015 pursuant to Government Code section 11343.4(b)(3)
rules.notes: Index (PDF p.568) describes C-22 as a 'Stand-alone specialty contractor classification, Ch 9 T 16 CCR 833'. An older 'C-22 Structural Pest Control' class (former 753) was repealed in 1955 - do not confuse.

rules.title: C-14 Metal Roofing classification repealed
rules.plain_english: The C-14 Metal Roofing classification was repealed in 2013 and is no longer a valid class; treat a C-14 entry as obsolete.
rules.applies_to: License classification validation
rules.quote: 832.14. CLASS C-14—METAL ROOFING CONTRACTOR 1. New section filed 10-22-86 ... 2. Repealer and new section filed 6-22-98 ... 3. Change without regulatory effect repealing section filed 8-7-2013 pursuant to section 100, title 1, California Code of Regulations (Register 2013, No. 32).
rules.notes: 832.14 also appears (without the repeal entry) in the current-rules history notes on PDF page 549; the repealed-rules entry controls. Metal roofing falls under C-39 Roofing (C-39 amended operative 7-1-98, same date as the 1998 C-14 rewrite) - confirm scope in 16 CCR 832.39.

rules.title: C-26 Lathing class repealed; C-35 is Lathing and Plastering
rules.plain_english: The separate C-26 Lathing classification was repealed effective January 1, 1998, and the C-35 class heading became 'Lathing and Plastering' the same date. Treat C-26 as obsolete.
rules.applies_to: License classification validation
rules.quote: 832.35. CLASS C-35—LATHING AND PLASTERING CONTRACTOR 1. Amendment of section heading, new subsection (a) designator and new subsections (b) and (c) filed 12-18-97; operative 1-1-98

rules.plain_english: Since January 1, 2003, C-5 is 'Framing and Rough Carpentry' and C-6 is 'Cabinet, Millwork and Finish Carpentry'. The old C-6 'Cabinet and Millwork' class was repealed effective January 1, 1998.

C-6.name: Cabinet, Millwork and Finish Carpentry Contractor

rules.applies_to: Carpentry and cabinet contractors; classification validation
rules.quote: 832.06. CLASS C-6—CABINET, MILLWORK AND FINISH CARPENTRY CONTRACTOR 1. New section filed 5-24-2002; operative 1-1-2003 (Register 2002, No. 21).
rules.notes: C-5 note: 'Amendment of section heading, section and Note filed 5-24-2002; operative 1-1-2003'. Scope text is in the prior chunk.

rules.title: C-10 Electrical, C-46 Solar and 16 CCR 810 definitions amended operative October 1, 2024
rules.plain_english: The C-10 Electrical and C-46 Solar classification rules and the definitions section (16 CCR 810, new subsection (a)) were all amended together, operative October 1, 2024. Check current scope text for work started on or after that date.

rules.title: Solar work within scope of Class A, Class B and C-61 (pool maintenance)
rules.plain_english: A separate rule (16 CCR 832.62) defines which solar system work General Engineering (A), General Building (B) and C-61 swimming pool maintenance licensees may perform.
rules.applies_to: Class A, Class B and C-61 swimming pool maintenance contractors doing solar work
rules.quote: 832.62. SOLAR SYSTEM WORK WITHIN SCOPE OF CLASS A, CLASS B, AND CLASS C-61 (SWIMMING POOL MAINTENANCE) 1. New section filed 4-28-82; effective thirtieth day thereafter
rules.notes: Only the heading appears in this chunk; scope limits are in the 832.62 text (prior chunk).

rules.title: C-47 General Manufactured Housing initial installer training requirement (operative 9-30-2021)
rules.plain_english: C-47 General Manufactured Housing contractor applicants must meet an initial installer training requirement in addition to experience; the rule took effect September 30, 2021.
rules.applies_to: C-47 applicants
rules.quote: 825.5. GENERAL MANUFACTURED HOUSING CONTRACTOR INITIAL INSTALLER TRAINING REQUIREMENT 1. New section filed 9-30-2021; operative 9-30-2021 pursuant to Government Code section 11343.4(b)(3)
rules.notes: Index (PDF p.567): 'General manufactured housing contractor initial installer training requirement in addition to experience requirement, Ch 9 T 16 CCR 825.5'. Training hours/content are in 825.5 text (prior chunk).

rules.title: Blanket performance and payment bond regulations (16 CCR 858-858.9), operative 12-22-2011
rules.plain_english: The blanket performance and payment bond program, which lets home improvement contractors with an approved blanket bond skip the downpayment and progress-payment limits, is governed by 16 CCR 858-858.9, operative December 22, 2011. Those rules cover the definition, requirements, application, denial standards, biennial certification and financial reporting, audits, bond increases, maintenance, rescission and posting to license records.

sections.858: Blanket performance and payment bond defined
sections.858.3: Minimum standards for approval; cause for denial
sections.858.4: Biennial certification and financial reporting requirements
sections.858.9: Posting of bond information to license records

rules.applies_to: Home improvement contractors using a blanket performance and payment bond under B&P 7159.5(a)(8)
rules.quote: 858.4. BLANKET PERFORMANCE AND PAYMENT BOND BIENNIAL CERTIFICATION AND FINANCIAL REPORTING REQUIREMENTS 1. New section filed 11-22-2011; operative 12-22-2011 (Register 2011, No. 47).
rules.notes: Only headings and dates are here; amounts and deadlines are in 858-858.9 text (prior chunk). The link to B&P 7159.5(a)(8) (which requires 2 years of active licensure before applying under 858.2) is from Law Book PDF page 411.

rules.title: Commercial general liability insurance disclosure rule (16 CCR 872) operative 2-26-2002
rules.plain_english: The required notice telling home improvement customers whether the contractor carries commercial general liability insurance (16 CCR 872) has been in effect since February 26, 2002.
rules.applies_to: Home improvement contractors (bids and contracts); single-family dwelling contracts under B&P 7164
rules.quote: 872. DISCLOSURE OF GENERAL LIABILITY INSURANCE 1. New section filed 11-28-2001; operative 2-26-2002 (Register 2001, No. 48).
rules.notes: Notice text and font sizes (14/12/11-point) are in 16 CCR 872 (Law Book PDF pages 535-538, prior chunk). A companion 872.1 'Checklist for Homeowners' (operative 2-26-2002, amended 11-22-2021) is listed under History Notes for REPEALED rules (PDF page 565) but no repeal entry is printed - treat its status as unclear.
rules.correction: Minor fix: the 872 notice text runs over PDF pages 535-538, not 535-537. The history note (filed 11-28-2001, operative 2-26-2002, Register 2001 No. 48), the 14/12/11-point type sizes, coverage of every bid and every home improvement contract (872(a)) and of B&P 7164 contracts (872(b)), and the 872.1 entry on the repealed list with no repeal line all match.

rules.title: Repealed CSLB regulations - do not cite or rely on
rules.plain_english: These CSLB regulations have been repealed and should not be cited in contracts, notices or compliance checks: 862 Notice to Owner, 852 Renewal of Licenses, 854 Renewal Fee and Reactivation Credit, 812 Dishonored Check Service Charge, 817 Operating Capital Defined, 818, 820, 821-822 Joint Venture License, 823 Bona Fide Employee/Direct Supervision definitions, 829 Credit for Experience, old 833 Additional Classifications, 842-844 exam rules, 866 Procedure to Inactivate License, and 869.5 Inquiry into Criminal Convictions.

rules.plain_english: Several CSLB regulations were amended or repealed between 2021 and 2025. A compliance tool should make sure its rule text reflects these versions: definitions (810), fees (811), classification and scope rules, renewal form (853), blanket bond application (858.1-858.2), criminal-history criteria (868-869.9), order-of-correction extension (883) and civil penalties (884).

rules.notes: Dates only; the substance of each change is not stated in the history notes. 'Change without regulatory effect' generally means a non-substantive/conforming change.

rules.title: Contractor's license bond: $25,000
rules.plain_english: Every active license must have a $25,000 contractor's bond (or cashier's check) on file with CSLB to be issued, reinstated, reactivated, renewed, or kept active. An inactive license does not need the bond.
rules.applies_to: All CSLB licensees with an active license (sole owner, partnership, corporation, LLC, joint venture)
rules.source: PDF page 295 of the 2026 CSLB Law Book (/home/user/Client/sources/lawbook.txt); https://www.cslb.ca.gov/Contractors/Maintain_License/Bond_Information/Bond_Requirements.aspx
rules.quote: The board shall require as a condition precedent to the issuance, reinstatement, reactivation, renewal, or continued maintenance of a license, that the applicant or licensee file or have on file a contractor's bond in the sum of twenty-five thousand dollars ($25,000).
rules.notes: Subdivision (c): bond not required while license is inactive. The $15,000 pre-2023 amount is from general knowledge of the repealed version (repealed 1/1/2023 per the law book history note) and is not needed for calculations. Bond must be from a surety admitted by the CA Department of Insurance, on an Attorney General-approved form (CSLB Bond Requirements page).
rules.correction: The $15,000 pre-2023 amount is not in the law book text; an official-domain search (leginfo SB 607 / CSLB notice) agrees it was $15,000 before 1/1/2023.

rules.title: Bond: $7,500 cap for claimants other than homeowners/employees
rules.plain_english: Of the $25,000 contractor's bond, the surety's total liability to everyone EXCEPT homeowners who contracted for home improvement on their own residence (B&P 7071.5(a)) is capped at $7,500. The remaining $17,500 is reserved exclusively for those home-improvement homeowners, who may recover up to the full bond. Single-family-home owners, fraud victims, unpaid employees and fringe-benefit trusts share the $7,500.

parameters.priority_beneficiaries: homeowners contracting for home improvement upon the homeowner's personal family residence (7071.5(a))
capped_nonpriority_beneficiaries: single-family dwelling owners not building for sale (7071.5(b))
persons damaged by willful and deliberate violation or fraud (7071.5(c))
fringe-benefit payees, e.g. union trust funds (7071.5(e))

rules.applies_to: Claims against any contractor's license bond
rules.source: PDF page 295 of the 2026 CSLB Law Book (/home/user/Client/sources/lawbook.txt)
rules.quote: Excluding the claims brought by the beneficiaries specified in subdivision (a) of Section 7071.5, the aggregate liability of a surety on claims brought against a bond required by this section shall not exceed the sum of seven thousand five hundred dollars ($7,500).
rules.notes: 7071.6(b) cross-references "subdivision (a) of Section 7071.5". In 7071.5, subdivision (a) is only home-improvement homeowners. (b)-(e) are separate subdivisions and are not priority. Reserved amount $17,500 derived (25,000 - 7,500).
rules.correction: 7071.6(b) reserves the excess over $7,500 only for beneficiaries in SUBDIVISION (a) of 7071.5, which is just homeowners contracting for home improvement on their own residence. 7071.5(b)-(e) are separate subdivisions (single-family-dwelling owners, willful-violation/fraud victims, unpaid employees, fringe-benefit payees), and they share the $7,500 cap. The extract read the reference as 7071.5(a)-(e) and listed all five groups as priority. Fixed priority_beneficiaries_section, plain_english and notes.

rules.title: Who the contractor's bond protects
rules.plain_english: The license bond pays: homeowners hurt by license-law violations on their own home, owners building a single-family home not for sale, anyone hurt by willful violations or fraud, unpaid employees, and fringe-benefit funds owed employer payments.
rules.applies_to: All contractor's bonds and qualifying individual's bonds
rules.source: PDF page 294 of the 2026 CSLB Law Book (/home/user/Client/sources/lawbook.txt); PDF page 300 of the 2026 CSLB Law Book (/home/user/Client/sources/lawbook.txt)
rules.quote: The contractor's bond shall be for the benefit of the following: (a) A homeowner contracting for home improvement upon the homeowner's personal family residence damaged as a result of a violation of this chapter by the licensee.
rules.notes: Bond must be executed by an admitted surety in favor of the State of California and filed with the registrar. Same beneficiary list applies to the qualifying individual's bond (7071.10).

rules.title: Double bond ($50,000) for applicants with unlicensed-contracting history
rules.plain_english: CSLB can make a new applicant post twice the normal bond until first renewal if they were convicted of unlicensed contracting or had a final unlicensed citation that caused substantial public injury.

triggers: citation under B&P 7028.7 reduced to final order

rules.applies_to: License applicants with a prior 7028 conviction or final 7028.7 citation
rules.source: PDF page 295 of the 2026 CSLB Law Book (/home/user/Client/sources/lawbook.txt)
rules.quote: the board may require an applicant to post a contractor's bond in twice the amount required pursuant to subdivision (a) until the time that the license is renewed
rules.notes: Discretionary ('may'). $50,000 derived as 2 x $25,000.

rules.title: LLC employee/worker bond: $100,000
rules.plain_english: An LLC license needs an extra $100,000 surety bond (on top of the $25,000 contractor bond) that protects workers against unpaid wages, interest on wages and fringe benefits. If the LLC is under a union agreement, the bond also covers welfare, pension and apprentice contributions.
rules.applies_to: Limited liability company licensees
rules.source: PDF page 296 of the 2026 CSLB Law Book (/home/user/Client/sources/lawbook.txt); https://www.cslb.ca.gov/About_Us/LLC.aspx
rules.quote: The board shall require, as a condition precedent to the issuance, reissuance, reinstatement, reactivation, renewal, or continued valid use of a limited liability company license, that the applicant or licensee file or have on file a surety bond in the sum of one hundred thousand dollars ($100,000).
rules.notes: Statute (e) says not applicable while license is inactive; CSLB LLC page sentence first says required for 'both active and inactive licenses' then '(not required for inactive LLC licenses)' - follow the statute (inactive exempt).

rules.title: LLC liability insurance: $1M + $100K per extra person, max $5M
rules.plain_english: An LLC licensee must carry liability insurance for its contracting work with an aggregate limit of at least $1,000,000 if 5 or fewer people are on its personnel of record, plus $100,000 more for each additional person, capped at $5,000,000 per policy period.
rules.applies_to: Limited liability company licensees (issuance, reinstatement, reactivation, continued valid use)
rules.source: PDF page 307 of the 2026 CSLB Law Book (/home/user/Client/sources/lawbook.txt); PDF page 43 of the 2026 CSLB Law Book (/home/user/Client/sources/lawbook.txt); https://www.cslb.ca.gov/About_Us/LLC.aspx
rules.quote: (1) For a limited liability company licensee with five or fewer persons listed on the members of the personnel of record, the aggregate limit shall not be less than one million dollars ($1,000,000).
rules.notes: Statute text says '$100,000 ... for each person listed on the personnel of record'; CSLB law book narrative (p.43) and CSLB LLC page read it as each ADDITIONAL person beyond five - formula follows CSLB. Required in addition to bonds. Cap is 'in any one designated period, less amounts paid in defending, settling, or discharging claims'.
rules.correction: Formula follows CSLB reading (each ADDITIONAL person beyond five), which the CSLB LLC page and law book p.43 both state; statute text says "for each person listed" - ambiguity already noted.

rules.title: LLC insurance: policy form, insurer and period rules
rules.plain_english: The LLC policy can be claims-made or occurrence, must cover a 'designated period' of no more than 12 months, and must come from a California-admitted insurer or an eligible surplus line insurer. Deductibles/self-insured retentions are allowed.

insurer_types_allowed: admitted (licensed by CA Dept. of Insurance)

rules.applies_to: LLC licensees
rules.source: PDF page 308 of the 2026 CSLB Law Book (/home/user/Client/sources/lawbook.txt); https://www.cslb.ca.gov/About_Us/LLC.aspx
rules.quote: For purposes of this section, "designated period" means a policy year or any other period designated in the policy that is not greater than 12 months.
rules.notes: Admitted/surplus line wording effective 1/1/2014 per CSLB LLC page (AB 1236).

rules.title: LLC insurance: restore full limit by next policy period or suspension
rules.plain_english: If claims use up the LLC's aggregate limit, it need not buy more for that period, but the full required limit must be back in place by the start of the next designated period or the license is suspended by law.

parameters.reinstate_by: commencement date of next designated period
parameters.consequence: license suspended by operation of law until compliant

rules.applies_to: LLC licensees whose aggregate limit is impaired or exhausted
rules.source: PDF page 308 of the 2026 CSLB Law Book (/home/user/Client/sources/lawbook.txt)
rules.quote: the aggregate limit of liability coverage (coverage limit) required by this section shall be reinstated by not later than the commencement date of the next designated period, and the license of any licensee that fails to comply with this provision shall be suspended by operation of law

rules.title: LLC dissolution: keep 3-year extended reporting (tail) coverage
rules.plain_english: When an LLC dissolves and winds up, it must keep or buy an extended reporting period endorsement at the full required aggregate limit for at least three years, if reasonably available.

parameters.trigger: dissolution and winding up of the LLC
parameters.limit: maximum total aggregate limit required by 7071.19
parameters.condition: if reasonably available from the insurer

rules.applies_to: Dissolving LLC licensees
rules.source: PDF page 308 of the 2026 CSLB Law Book (/home/user/Client/sources/lawbook.txt)
rules.quote: maintain or obtain an extended reporting period endorsement or equivalent provision in the maximum total aggregate limit of liability required to comply with this section for a minimum of three years if reasonably available from the insurer.

rules.title: LLC insurance: file Certificate of Liability Insurance with CSLB
rules.plain_english: Before an LLC license is issued, reinstated or reactivated, the LLC must prove its liability coverage; a Certificate of Liability Insurance signed by the insurer's authorized agent must be submitted to CSLB, and the insurer reports policy dates, claim payments and cancellations.

parameters.signed_by: authorized agent or employee of the insurer
insurer_reports: date and amount of claim payments

rules.applies_to: LLC applicants/licensees
rules.source: PDF page 308 of the 2026 CSLB Law Book (/home/user/Client/sources/lawbook.txt)-309
