rules.plain_english: No HIS registration is needed for: corporate officers of record; LLC managers/members/officers of record; general partners on the license; the license qualifier (all only while listed on that licensee's personnel of record); retail-store salespeople where the buyer initiated at a fixed store; appointment setters only; and the contractor's service repair employees handling only the requested repair.

exempt: officer of record of licensed corporation
manager, member, or officer of record of licensed LLC
general partner listed on partnership license
qualifying person (B&P 7025)
salesperson at general merchandise retail establishment with buyer-initiated negotiation at fixed location
person only scheduling appointments for a registered HIS
bona fide service repairperson employed by licensee limited to requested service/repair
parameters.personnel_exemption_condition: listed as personnel of record of the licensee at time of the sale

rules.applies_to: Home improvement contractors and their sales staff
rules.source: PDF page 389 of the 2026 CSLB Law Book (/home/user/Client/sources/lawbook.txt)-390
rules.quote: The exemption to registration provided under paragraphs (1), (2), and (3) of subdivision (d) shall apply only to those individuals who, at the time of the sales transaction, are listed as personnel of record for the licensee responsible for soliciting, negotiating, or contracting for a service or improvement

rules.title: Salesperson must identify the contractor's name and license number first
rules.plain_english: Before soliciting or selling, the salesperson must tell the owner or tenant the business name and license number of the contractor they represent for that transaction.

parameters.timing: prior to engaging in any sales activity

rules.applies_to: Home improvement salespersons
rules.source: PDF page 389 of the 2026 CSLB Law Book (/home/user/Client/sources/lawbook.txt)
rules.quote: prior to engaging in any activity described in subdivision (a) of this section, a home improvement salesperson shall identify to the owner or tenant the business name and license number of the contractor they are representing for the purposes of that transaction.

rules.title: Contractor must notify CSLB before an HIS starts and within 90 days after they leave
rules.plain_english: A home improvement contractor must file CSLB's form (name and registration number) before a registered salesperson begins work, and file again within 90 days after the salesperson stops working for it. Using an unregistered salesperson, or not reporting, is cause for discipline.
rules.applies_to: Home improvement contractors employing salespersons
rules.source: PDF page 393 of the 2026 CSLB Law Book (/home/user/Client/sources/lawbook.txt); PDF page 541 of the 2026 CSLB Law Book (/home/user/Client/sources/lawbook.txt)
rules.quote: The form shall be submitted prior to the home improvement salesperson beginning work for the contractor.
rules.notes: An HIS may not guide an owner to a contractor whose employment notification CSLB has not received (7156(c)). Electronic filing permitted (7156.6).

rules.title: HIS registration: 2-year term; late renewal +50%; 3-year limit
rules.plain_english: HIS registrations expire two years after issuance (end of month). Renew before expiration; late renewals within three years pay a 50% delinquency penalty ($200 renewal -> $300). After three years, apply anew. Incomplete renewal applications are abandoned if not corrected within 90 days.
rules.applies_to: Registered home improvement salespersons
rules.source: PDF page 391 of the 2026 CSLB Law Book (/home/user/Client/sources/lawbook.txt)-392; https://www.cslb.ca.gov/About_Us/Library/Fees.aspx
rules.quote: A registration may, however, still be renewed at any time within three years after its expiration upon the filing of an application for renewal on a form prescribed by the registrar and the payment of the renewal fee prescribed by this chapter and a delinquent renewal penalty equal to 50 percent of the renewal fee.

rules.title: Contract sold by unregistered salesperson: security interest unenforceable
rules.plain_english: Any security interest (e.g., lien, deed of trust) a contractor takes to secure payment on a home improvement contract is unenforceable if the salesperson who solicited it was neither registered nor exempt when the homeowner signed.
rules.applies_to: Home improvement contractors
rules.source: PDF page 391 of the 2026 CSLB Law Book (/home/user/Client/sources/lawbook.txt)
rules.quote: Any security interest taken by a contractor, to secure any payment for the performance of any act or conduct described in Section 7151 that occurs on or after January 1, 1995, is unenforceable if the person soliciting the act or contract was not a duly registered salesperson or was not exempt from registration

rules.title: Contractor is disciplined for its salesperson's violations
rules.plain_english: A salesperson's violations of the License Law are also grounds for discipline against the contractor employing them, even if the contractor did not know.
rules.applies_to: Home improvement contractors employing salespersons
rules.source: PDF page 394 of the 2026 CSLB Law Book (/home/user/Client/sources/lawbook.txt)
rules.quote: Violations of any provisions of this chapter by a home improvement salesperson likewise constitute cause for disciplinary action against the contractor, by whom he or she was employed at the time the violation occurred, whether or not the contractor had knowledge of or participated in the act or omission constituting violations of this chapter.

rules.title: Salespersons must remit payments; contract forms must name the contractor
rules.plain_english: It is a misdemeanor for a salesperson to fail to account for or remit customer payments to the employing contractor, and for anyone to use a contract form that does not disclose the name of the contractor principal.

prohibited: HIS failing to account for or remit payments to employing contractor
contract form not disclosing name of contractor principal
HIS guiding owner to contractor without CSLB employment notice on file

rules.applies_to: Home improvement salespersons and contractors
rules.source: PDF page 394 of the 2026 CSLB Law Book (/home/user/Client/sources/lawbook.txt)
rules.quote: (b) For any person to use a contract form in connection with any home improvement transaction or any other transaction involving a work of improvement if the form fails to disclose the name of the contractor principal by whom the person is employed.

rules.title: No referral rewards to owners; promotional gifts max $5
rules.plain_english: You may not offer an owner/tenant compensation for referring other home improvement business. Promotional gifts not conditioned on a contract are allowed only up to $5 in value and one per transaction. Salespersons may only be paid by the contractor they represent; contractors may not pay unlicensed persons for work requiring a license.
rules.applies_to: Contractors, agents and salespersons
rules.source: PDF page 395 of the 2026 CSLB Law Book (/home/user/Client/sources/lawbook.txt); PDF page 541 of the 2026 CSLB Law Book (/home/user/Client/sources/lawbook.txt)
rules.quote: A contractor or his or her agent or salesperson may give tangible items to prospective customers for advertising or sales promotion purposes where the gift is not conditioned upon obtaining a contract for home improvement work if the gift does not exceed a value of five dollars ($5) and only one such gift is given in connection with any one transaction.
rules.notes: Violation is a misdemeanor and cause for discipline.

rules.title: Keep all contracting records 5 years after project completion
rules.plain_english: Keep records of all contracts, documents, receipts and disbursements for every contracting transaction, available for CSLB inspection, for at least five years after the project is completed. Refusing a written CSLB request for records is cause for discipline.

parameters.board_request: must comply with registrar's written request to make records available

rules.applies_to: All licensees
rules.source: PDF page 352 of the 2026 CSLB Law Book (/home/user/Client/sources/lawbook.txt); PDF page 50 of the 2026 CSLB Law Book (/home/user/Client/sources/lawbook.txt)
rules.quote: failure to have those records available for inspection by the registrar or his or her duly authorized representative for a period of not less than five years after completion of any construction project or operation to which the records refer
rules.notes: B&P 7111.1: failing to respond to a written request to cooperate in a complaint investigation is also cause for discipline. B&P 7159.9 (fire alarm exemption, PDF pp.413-414) separately requires its documents be kept 5 years and produced within 30 days of a written request. Longest-of rule for a retention tool: CSLB 5 yrs after completion; IRS employment tax 4 yrs; EDD payroll 4 yrs (8 yrs if treating workers as non-employees); DIR payroll 3 yrs.

rules.title: Keep federal employment tax records at least 4 years
rules.plain_english: Keep payroll/employment tax records available for IRS inspection for at least four years after the tax due date for the period (or the date paid, if later).

parameters.measured_from: later of due date of the tax for the return period or date tax paid

rules.applies_to: All employers
rules.quote: every person required by the regulations in this part to keep records in respect of a tax (whether or not such person incurs liability for such tax) shall maintain such records for at least four years after the due date of such tax for the return period to which the records relate, or the date such tax is paid, whichever is the later.

rules.title: Keep California payroll records at least 4 years (8 if you claim no employees)
rules.plain_english: EDD requires payroll records for all workers (including former workers and independent contractors) to be kept at least four years; if you believe you are not a subject employer or workers are exempt, keep payment records at least eight years.
rules.applies_to: All California employers
rules.source: https://edd.ca.gov/siteassets/files/pdf_pub_ctr/de44.pdf (not fetched; host blocked - from search excerpt)
rules.quote: Employers must keep payroll records for at least four years.
rules.notes: edd.ca.gov could not be fetched from this environment; quote and 8-year figure come from web search excerpts of EDD DE 44 and DE 40. Verify before relying.

rules.title: Seller's permit for selling tangible property; possible security deposit
rules.plain_english: If the business sells tangible personal property, it needs a California seller's permit, and the tax agency may require a security deposit (the law book says up to six months of estimated sales tax). Collect sales tax from the customer unless tax on the materials was already paid at purchase.

parameters.security_deposit_estimate_basis: estimated sales tax for first six months (per law book)

rules.applies_to: Contractors that sell fixtures, materials over the counter, or otherwise act as retailers
rules.source: PDF page 41 of the 2026 CSLB Law Book (/home/user/Client/sources/lawbook.txt)
rules.quote: California requires a Seller's Permit for businesses that sell tangible personal property. The State Board of Equalization can require a deposit of the estimated sales tax for the first six months. The contractor must collect the required sales tax from the customer unless the tax on materials is already paid at the time of purchase.
rules.notes: Sales and use tax is now administered by CDTFA (not BOE). The law book's summary is simplified; Regulation 1521 controls (materials = consumer, fixtures = retailer). The $50,000 max (R&TC 6701) is from a CDTFA manual search excerpt, not read. CDTFA says permit issuance is not delayed pending deposit.

rules.title: Sales tax: contractor is the consumer of materials it installs
rules.plain_english: On ordinary (non-federal) construction contracts the contractor is the final consumer of 'materials' it furnishes and installs (lumber, drywall, concrete, windows, nails, etc.), so it pays sales tax to its supplier (or use tax) on its cost and does not charge sales tax to the customer on them. It may not buy materials for resale.

parameters.measure: sale price of materials to the contractor (purchase price)

rules.applies_to: Construction contractors (prime and sub) on non-U.S.-government contracts
rules.quote: Construction contractors are consumers of materials which they furnish and install in the performance of construction contracts.
rules.notes: cdtfa.ca.gov could not be fetched from this environment. Quote is from search excerpts of Regulation 1521 and CDTFA annotations. Examples come from CDTFA annotations. Exception: time-and-material contracts meeting title/separate-price test, or 'plus sales tax' billing (see reg1521-time-and-material-retailer).

rules.title: Sales tax: contractor is the retailer of fixtures it installs
rules.plain_english: The contractor is treated as the retailer of 'fixtures' it furnishes and installs (items that keep their identity as accessories, e.g., cabinets, lighting fixtures, plumbing fixtures, alarm systems, plants/trees). Tax applies to the fixture's stated sale price or, if none is stated (lump-sum contract), to the contractor's cost price. Fixtures may be bought for resale with a resale certificate.

parameters.measure_if_not_stated: cost price of fixture to contractor

rules.applies_to: Construction contractors installing fixtures
rules.quote: Construction contractors are retailers of fixtures which they furnish and install in the performance of construction contracts and tax applies to their sales of the fixtures.
rules.notes: From search excerpts only. 5% profit build-up for contractor-manufactured fixtures quoted in excerpt ('shall be deemed to be 5 percent of the sum of the preceding factors'). Regulation's full fixtures/materials definitions not read - verify classification of specific items.

rules.title: Time-and-material contracts: when the contractor becomes retailer of materials
rules.plain_english: On a time-and-material contract the contractor is normally still the consumer of materials. It becomes the retailer (and must collect sales tax on the materials' selling price) if the contract both transfers title to materials before installation and separately states the materials' sale price - or if it bills 'sales tax' on marked-up materials.

retailer_if_all: contract explicitly transfers title to materials before installation
contract separately states sale price of materials exclusive of installation
parameters.retailer_if_billing: bills customer sales tax computed on marked-up materials (time and material plus tax)

rules.applies_to: Contractors using time-and-material contracts
rules.quote: If the contract explicitly provides for the transfer of title to the materials prior to the time the materials are installed, and separately states the sale price of the materials, exclusive of the charge for installation, the contractor will be deemed to be the retailer of the materials.
rules.notes: Search excerpt. CDTFA annotations say both conditions must be met; a title clause alone is not enough.

rules.title: Lump-sum contract: separately stating items on the invoice does not change it
rules.plain_english: A lump-sum contract (one stated price to furnish and install) stays lump-sum even if the invoice separately lists materials, fixtures, labor or tax; the contractor remains consumer of materials and retailer of fixtures (measured by cost price if not stated).

parameters.definition: contract under which contractor for a stated lump sum agrees to furnish and install materials or fixtures, or both

rules.applies_to: Contractors using lump-sum contracts
rules.quote: A lump sum contract does not become a time and material contract when the amounts attributable to materials, fixtures, labor, or tax are separately stated in the invoice.
rules.notes: Subsection number (a)(8) as shown in search excerpt. CDTFA Pub 9 example: $15,000 lump sum with $2,000 materials (tax paid on purchase) and $5,000 fixture cost -> fixture tax measured on $5,000.

rules.title: Subcontractors cannot avoid tax by taking a resale certificate from the prime
rules.plain_english: A contractor (including a sub) cannot escape sales/use tax on materials or fixtures it furnishes and installs by accepting a resale certificate from the prime contractor, designers, decorators or others.
rules.applies_to: Subcontractors and prime contractors
rules.quote: A contractor cannot avoid liability for sales or use tax on materials or fixtures furnished and installed by him or her by taking a resale certificate from the prime contractor, interior decorators, designers, department stores, or others.
rules.notes: Search excerpt only.

rules.title: Federal (U.S. government) jobs: contractor is consumer of materials AND fixtures
rules.plain_english: On contracts with the United States Government, the contractor is the consumer of both materials and fixtures (pays tax on purchase; no sales tax to the government), but is the retailer of machinery and equipment it furnishes.
rules.applies_to: Contractors on U.S. government construction contracts
rules.quote: United States construction contractors are consumers of materials and fixtures which they furnish and install in the performance of contracts with the United States Government.
rules.notes: Search excerpt only.

rules.title: When a contractor needs a CDTFA seller's permit
rules.plain_english: A contractor needs a seller's permit if it sells fixtures, sells materials (e.g., T&M retailer, over-the-counter), machinery/equipment or other tangible property; contractors who only furnish and install materials on lump-sum jobs generally do not, but may need to register for use tax as a qualified purchaser.

permit_required_if: retailer of materials under T&M contract
furnishes and installs solar systems that include fixtures
parameters.generally_not_required: only furnishing and installing materials in lump-sum contracts
parameters.alternate_registration: qualified purchaser / consumer use tax account

rules.applies_to: Construction contractors
rules.quote: If a contractor is a seller or retailer because he or she makes sales of fixtures, materials, or machinery and equipment, or other tangible personal property either in connection with or as part of a construction contract, or otherwise, he or she is required to hold a seller's permit.
rules.notes: Search excerpts of Regulation 1521 and CDTFA Pub 9. Seller's permits are free (general knowledge; not verified here).

rules.title: Use tax on materials bought without CA tax (e.g., out of state)
rules.plain_english: If you buy materials or equipment from an out-of-state seller who does not charge California tax, you owe use tax at the rate where the item is used; if used in a higher-rate district than the rate paid, the difference is due.

parameters.rate_basis: rate in effect where property is used

rules.applies_to: Contractors buying taxable items without CA sales tax
rules.quote: if the property is used in a district with a higher tax rate than the rate paid at the time of purchase, the additional tax is due.
rules.notes: Search excerpt (paraphrase in search summary). Verify reporting method (sales and use tax return or CDTFA use tax account).

rules.title: California statewide base sales/use tax rate 7.25% plus district taxes
rules.plain_english: The statewide base sales and use tax rate is 7.25%; local district taxes of 0.10% to 2.00% each are added on top depending on location, so job-site/delivery location determines the total rate.
rules.applies_to: Retailers (fixtures/material sales) and consumers owing use tax
rules.citation: R&TC 6051 et seq.; CDTFA rate tables
rules.quote: the total rate for the district (statewide rate + district rate)
rules.notes: Search excerpt; look up current rate per address with CDTFA before filing. Base rate figure from search summary.
rules.correction: Not a correction, but district_tax_each_max_percent (2.0) is really the usual combined county cap, and some statutes authorize more.

rules.title: Withhold 7% on CA-source payments over $1,500/yr to nonresident subs
rules.plain_english: If you pay a nonresident (e.g., an out-of-state subcontractor) for services performed in California, you must withhold 7% of payments once the calendar-year total exceeds $1,500, unless the payee gives an exemption (Form 590) or FTB waiver. Report on Form 592 / 592-B.

parameters.applies_to: California-source nonwage payments to nonresidents (services performed in CA)

rules.applies_to: Contractors paying nonresident individuals/entities for CA services
rules.source: https://www.cslb.ca.gov/contractors/Tax_Info.aspx (read: obligation exists); https://www.ftb.ca.gov/pay/withholding/withholding-on-nonresidents.html (not fetched; search excerpt for 7%/$1,500)
rules.quote: If you pay California source income to nonresidents, then you may have withholding responsibilities including those under California Revenue and Taxation Code Section 18662.
rules.notes: CSLB Tax Info page (read) confirms the obligation and code section; the 7% rate and $1,500 threshold are from FTB search excerpts (ftb.ca.gov blocked). Payer can be liable for tax not withheld.

rules.title: LLC: $800 annual tax + gross-receipts fee at $250,000+
rules.plain_english: Every LLC doing business or organized/registered in California owes an $800 annual tax (Form FTB 3522, due by the 15th day of the 4th month of the tax year) and, if total California income is $250,000 or more, an additional LLC fee estimated by the 15th day of the 6th month (Form FTB 3536).

parameters.annual_tax_due: 15th day of 4th month of taxable year

rules.applies_to: LLCs (including contractor LLCs)
rules.quote: Every LLC that is doing business or organized in California must pay an annual tax of $800.
rules.notes: Search excerpt; fee tier amounts not verified (FTB LLC fee chart not retrieved). Corporations owe an $800 minimum franchise tax (general knowledge - not verified here).

rules.title: LLC Statement of Information: within 90 days, then every 2 years ($20)
rules.plain_english: An LLC must file its Statement of Information with the Secretary of State within 90 days of registering and then every two years during its filing period; fee $20. Updates between periods are free.
rules.applies_to: California and foreign LLCs registered with SOS
rules.citation: Corp. Code 17702.09 (citation from general knowledge; verify)
rules.quote: The filing fee for the initial and required biennial Statement of Information is $20
rules.notes: sos.ca.gov could not be fetched. Missing the filing can lead to SOS/FTB suspension, which triggers CSLB license suspension under B&P 7076.2.

rules.title: Stock corporation Statement of Information: every year ($25)
rules.plain_english: A California stock corporation (and foreign corporation) files a Statement of Information every year during its filing period; fee $25.
rules.applies_to: California stock corporations and foreign corporations
rules.citation: Corp. Code 1502 (citation from general knowledge; verify)
rules.quote: the fee to file the statement is $25 for California stock and foreign corporations
rules.notes: Initial filing within 90 days of incorporation is general knowledge, not confirmed here. Filing period is commonly the month of original registration and the preceding five months (general knowledge - verify).

rules.title: $250 penalty for missing Statement of Information
rules.plain_english: If a corporation or LLC fails to file its Statement of Information, it gets a delinquency notice with 60 more days to file; if still not filed, a $250 penalty is assessed (collected by FTB) and the entity can be suspended.
rules.applies_to: Corporations and LLCs
rules.citation: Corp. Code 2204; Corp. Code 17713.13 (citations from general knowledge; verify)
rules.quote: you may be assessed a $250 penalty for not filing your Statement of Information
rules.notes: Search excerpt. Ties to CSLB: SOS not-in-good-standing -> CSLB suspension 30 days after notice (B&P 7076.2).
rules.correction: Citation unresolved: the FTB penalty chart excerpt cites Corp. Code 2204 and 17653 (a former Beverly-Killea LLC Act section), not 17713.13. Keep the citation flagged "verify".

rules.title: Register with EDD once you pay employees over $100 in a quarter
rules.plain_english: A contractor that pays more than $100 in total wages in a calendar quarter must register with EDD, get a state employer account number, and pay state payroll and UI taxes on its employees' wages. The trigger is the employer's total quarterly wages, not each employee's earnings. Also get a federal EIN and pay federal withholding and Social Security taxes on schedule.

parameters.threshold_basis: total wages paid by the employer in a calendar quarter (not each employee's earnings)

rules.applies_to: Contractors with employees
rules.source: PDF page 41 of the 2026 CSLB Law Book (/home/user/Client/sources/lawbook.txt)
rules.quote: The contractor must register with the Employment Development Department, obtain a state EIN, and pay state payroll and unemployment insurance taxes for employees who earn over $100 in a calendar quarter.
rules.notes: The law book (p.41) says "for employees who earn over $100 in a calendar quarter". EDD guidance (search summaries) frames the $100 as the employer's total quarterly wages. See edd-registration-15-days for the deadline.
rules.correction: The law book text "employees who earn over $100 in a calendar quarter" was carried into plain_english as a per-employee test. The EDD trigger is employer-level: an employer that pays more than $100 in total wages in a calendar quarter must register and report, and once subject, all wages are covered (up to the applicable wage bases). Clarified plain_english and added threshold_basis. The $100 figure is unchanged.

rules.title: EDD employer registration due within 15 days of paying over $100
rules.plain_english: Register with EDD (online via e-Services for Business or Form DE 1) within 15 calendar days after you first pay more than $100 in wages in a calendar quarter. Wages include cash, checks, app payments and the value of meals/lodging.

parameters.trigger: paying more than $100 in wages in a calendar quarter
parameters.form: DE 1 (Commercial Employer Account Registration) or e-Services for Business

rules.applies_to: All employers (contractors) with California employees
rules.quote: Not available verbatim - page not fetched (host blocked). Search excerpt: a business that pays more than $100 in wages in a calendar quarter must register within 15 days.
rules.notes: edd.ca.gov blocked from this environment; the $100 trigger is confirmed by the CSLB law book (p.41, read), the 15-day deadline only by EDD search excerpts.

rules.title: California UI tax: new employer rate 3.4% on first $7,000 per employee
rules.plain_english: Employers pay state Unemployment Insurance tax on the first $7,000 of each employee's wages per year. New employers are assigned a 3.4% rate for two to three years (max $238 per employee per year at 3.4%); later rates come from the annual DE 2088 notice.
rules.applies_to: California employers
rules.quote: New employers are assigned a 3.4 percent UI rate for two to three years.
rules.notes: Search excerpt; $238 derived (7,000 x 3.4%). CUIC 930 citation for wage base from general knowledge - verify.

rules.title: Employment Training Tax (ETT): 0.1% on first $7,000
rules.plain_english: Most employers also pay ETT of 0.1% on the same first $7,000 of each employee's wages ($7 per employee per year). Employers with a negative UI reserve balance pay no ETT (shown as 0.0%).
rules.applies_to: California UI-rated employers
rules.quote: The ETT rate for 2026 is 0.1 percent.
rules.notes: Search excerpt; $7 derived.

rules.title: SDI employee withholding 2026: 1.3% of all wages (no cap)
rules.plain_english: Withhold State Disability Insurance (SDI) from employees' pay at 1.3% for 2026. There is no taxable wage limit or maximum withholding since 2024.
rules.applies_to: California employers withholding from employee wages
rules.citation: CUIC 984 (citation from general knowledge; verify); SB 951 (2022)
rules.quote: The 2026 SDI withholding rate is 1.3 percent (.013).
rules.notes: Search excerpt. 2025 rate 1.2% also from search excerpt.

rules.title: File DE 9 and DE 9C every quarter (even with no payroll)
rules.plain_english: Active employers file the Quarterly Contribution Return (DE 9) and Wage and Withholding report (DE 9C) every quarter, even if no wages were paid. 2026 quarters are due the 1st of the month after quarter end and delinquent if not filed by the last day of that month (Q3 2026 delinquent after Nov 2, 2026; Q4 delinquent after Feb 1, 2027).

forms: DE 9
DE 9C
parameters.weekend_holiday_rule: delinquent date moves to next business day

rules.applies_to: California employers
rules.citation: CUIC (quarterly returns); EDD Payroll Tax Calendar
rules.quote: Not available verbatim - page not fetched (host blocked). Search excerpt: DE 9 and DE 9C for Jan-Mar due April 1, delinquent after April 30.
rules.notes: Dates from search excerpt of EDD 2026 calendar. PIT/SDI deposits (DE 88) follow federal deposit schedule (not verified here).

rules.title: EDD e-file / e-pay mandate: paper filing penalties
rules.plain_english: All employers must file payroll tax returns/reports and pay deposits electronically. Penalties for noncompliance: $50 per paper DE 9, $20 per wage item on a paper DE 9C, and 15% of a non-electronic payment (credit-card DE 88 payments count as electronic).
rules.applies_to: California employers
rules.citation: CUIC e-file and e-pay mandate (AB 1245, Stats. 2015 - citation from general knowledge)
rules.quote: Not available verbatim - page not fetched (host blocked). Search excerpt: $50 per DE 9 return, $20 per wage item on the DE 9C, 15% of the amount due on DE 88 payments.
rules.notes: Search excerpt only.

rules.title: Report independent contractors (subs) to EDD on DE 542 within 20 days
rules.plain_english: If you must file a federal 1099 for a sole-proprietor independent contractor, report them to EDD on Form DE 542 within 20 calendar days of paying $600 or more in a calendar year or signing a contract for $600 or more, whichever is first. Materials included in the payment count toward $600.

parameters.trigger: earlier of paying >= $600 in calendar year or entering contract >= $600
parameters.report_frequency: once per year per service provider (check Ongoing box)

rules.applies_to: Businesses paying independent contractors (individuals/sole proprietors) for services
rules.quote: You must report independent contractor information to us within 20 calendar days if either of the following applies.
rules.notes: Search excerpt. EDD pages still show $600 even though the federal 1099-NEC threshold became $2,000 for 2026 payments - verify which threshold EDD now applies. $24 penalty from older EDD documents (unverified for 2026). See also labor-hr research file rule independent-contractor-report-de542.

rules.title: Get a federal EIN (Form SS-4) by 7 days after first wages
rules.plain_english: An employer paying wages subject to Social Security/Medicare or income tax withholding must apply for an Employer Identification Number on Form SS-4 no later than the seventh day after the first wage payment, and use it on returns, W-2s and deposits.
rules.applies_to: All employers
rules.quote: The application for an identification number shall be filed on or before the seventh day after the first payment of wages to which reference is made in paragraph (a)(1) of this section.
rules.notes: The CSLB law book (p.41) also says a federal EIN must be requested from the IRS. Partnership license applicants must give their EIN to CSLB (B&P 30).

rules.title: Form 941 due the last day of the month after each quarter
rules.plain_english: File Form 941 (quarterly federal payroll tax return) by the last day of the month after the quarter: April 30, July 31, October 31 and January 31. If all taxes were deposited on time and in full, you get until the 10th of the following month. Weekend/holiday dates roll to the next business day.

parameters.due: last day of first calendar month after quarter
parameters.extended_due_if_timely_deposits: 10th day of second month after quarter

rules.applies_to: All employers filing Form 941
rules.quote: shall be filed on or before the last day of the first calendar month following the period for which it is made. A return may be filed on or before the 10th day of the second calendar month following such period if timely deposits under section 6302(c) of the Code and the regulations have been made in full payment of such taxes due for the period.
rules.notes: 2026 adjusted dates computed: Oct 31, 2026 is a Saturday and Jan 31, 2027 is a Sunday, so they roll to Monday.

rules.title: Federal payroll tax deposits: monthly vs semiweekly ($50,000 lookback)
rules.plain_english: If total employment taxes in the lookback period (12 months ending the prior June 30) were $50,000 or less, deposit monthly by the 15th of the next month; above $50,000, deposit semiweekly (Wed-Fri paydays by next Wednesday; Sat-Tue paydays by next Friday). Deposits must be by electronic funds transfer.

parameters.safe_harbor_shortfall: greater of $100 or 2% of required deposit, made up by shortfall date

rules.applies_to: All employers
rules.quote: An employer is a monthly depositor for the entire calendar year if the aggregate amount of employment taxes reported for the lookback period is $50,000 or less.
rules.notes: New employers with no lookback history are monthly depositors (general rule; specific new-employer paragraph not extracted).
rules.correction: New employers are treated as having zero liability for any lookback period before they started the business (31.6302-1(b)(4)), so they start as monthly depositors.

rules.title: Federal deposit: $100,000 accumulated = deposit by next day
rules.plain_english: If you accumulate $100,000 or more of employment taxes on any day, deposit by the close of the next business day; a monthly depositor then becomes a semiweekly depositor for the rest of the year and the next year.

parameters.status_change: monthly depositor becomes semiweekly for remainder of year and following year

rules.applies_to: All employers
rules.quote: if on any day within a deposit period (monthly or semi-weekly) an employer has accumulated $100,000 or more of employment taxes, those taxes must be deposited by electronic funds transfer in time to satisfy the tax obligation by the close of the next day.

rules.title: Under $2,500 per quarter: may pay with the timely filed return
rules.plain_english: If total employment taxes for the quarter (or the prior quarter) are under $2,500, you may pay them with a timely filed Form 941 instead of making deposits.

parameters.period: return period (quarter) or immediately preceding quarter
parameters.condition: fully paid with timely filed return; one-day $100,000 rule not triggered

rules.applies_to: Small employers
rules.quote: The total amount of accumulated employment taxes is de minimis if it is less than $2,500 for the return period or if it is de minimis pursuant to paragraph (f)(4)(ii) of this section.

rules.title: Forms W-2: give employees and file with SSA by January 31
rules.plain_english: Furnish each employee's W-2 by January 31 of the following year and file W-2s (with W-3) with the government by January 31. For a terminated employee who asks, you may need to furnish it sooner.
rules.applies_to: All employers
rules.quote: Each statement required by this section for a calendar year and each corrected statement required for the year shall be furnished to the employee on or before January 31 of the year succeeding such calendar year.
rules.notes: Weekend roll-forward per 26 CFR 301.7503-1 (computed).

rules.title: Form 940 (FUTA) due January 31 (10 more days if fully deposited)
rules.plain_english: File the annual federal unemployment (FUTA) return, Form 940, by the last day of the month after the year ends (January 31); you get until February 10 if all FUTA tax was deposited on time.
rules.applies_to: Employers subject to FUTA
rules.quote: Each return of the tax imposed by the Federal Unemployment Tax Act required to be made under § 31.6011(a)-3 shall be filed on or before the last day of the first calendar month following the period for which it is made.
rules.notes: Annual return period from 26 CFR 31.6011(a)-3 (not separately fetched).

rules.title: FUTA: California credit reduction state (2025: 1.2%; 2026: 1.5%)
rules.plain_english: FUTA is 6.0% on the first $7,000 per employee less a normal 5.4% state credit. California employers lose part of the credit because of the state's federal UI loan: an extra 1.2% for 2025 ($84/employee) and 1.5% listed for 2026 ($105/employee), paid with Form 940 Schedule A.
rules.applies_to: California employers
rules.quote: California is 0.015 (1.5%).
rules.notes: From search excerpt of the 2026 Schedule A (Form 940) draft; EDD calls 1.5% a projection pending DOL final notice (after Nov 10, 2026). Effective rates and per-employee amounts derived (0.6% + reduction).

rules.title: Form 1099-NEC: $2,000 threshold for payments made in 2026
rules.plain_english: For nonemployee compensation paid after December 31, 2025, file Form 1099-NEC for each payee (e.g., unincorporated subcontractor) paid at least $2,000 in the year (was $600). The threshold is inflation-adjusted after 2026. Always file if you backup-withheld, regardless of amount.
rules.applies_to: Businesses paying non-corporate service providers (subcontractors)
rules.citation: IRC 6041(a) as amended by P.L. 119-21 (One Big Beautiful Bill Act); 26 CFR 1.6041-1
rules.source: https://www.irs.gov/instructions/i1099mec; https://www.irs.gov/publications/p15 (not fetched; search excerpt); https://www.ecfr.gov/current/title-26/chapter-I/subchapter-A/part-1/section-1.6041-1 (fetched; still says $600)
rules.quote: You made payments to the payee of at least $2,000 during the year
rules.notes: IRS sites blocked; $2,000 from IRS instructions search excerpt. The eCFR regulation 26 CFR 1.6041-1 (read) still reads 'payments of $600 or more' because Treasury has not updated it - the statute controls. California EDD DE 542 still references $600.

rules.title: Form 1099-NEC due to IRS and recipient by January 31
rules.plain_english: File Form 1099-NEC with the IRS and furnish the recipient copy by January 31 of the year after payment (paper filers include Form 1096). For 2026 payments, January 31, 2027 is a Sunday.
rules.applies_to: Businesses filing 1099-NEC
rules.quote: Section 6071(c) requires you to file Form 1099-NEC on or before January 31, using either paper or electronic filing procedures.
rules.notes: Search excerpt. Weekend roll to Feb 1, 2027 is computed (general IRS weekend rule), not confirmed by IRS text here.

rules.title: No 1099 needed for payments to corporations (except attorneys/medical)
rules.plain_english: Payments to corporations (C or S) generally do not require an information return; exceptions include attorneys' fees and medical/health care service corporations.

exceptions: attorneys' fees (after 1997)
corporations providing medical and health care services or billing for them
parameters.note_llc: LLCs taxed as corporations are corporations for this rule; single-member/partnership LLCs are not (general knowledge)

rules.applies_to: Businesses paying subcontractors and vendors
rules.quote: (p) Payments made to the following persons: (1) A corporation described in § 1.6049-4(c)(1)(ii)(A), except with respect to payments made to a corporation after December 31, 1997 for attorneys' fees, and except a corporation engaged in providing medical and health care services
rules.notes: Collect Form W-9 from every sub to determine entity type and TIN. LLC note is general knowledge.

rules.title: Backup withholding: 24% if a sub gives no TIN (W-9)
rules.plain_english: If a payee does not furnish a taxpayer identification number (e.g., no W-9), withhold 24% from reportable payments such as nonemployee compensation, deposit it, and report it; for 2026 the backup-withholding reporting threshold matches the $2,000 1099 threshold.

parameters.trigger: payee fails to furnish TIN (Form W-9) or IRS notice of incorrect TIN

rules.applies_to: Businesses paying subcontractors and service providers
rules.quote: the backup withholding rate is 24% for reportable payments
rules.notes: Search excerpt.

rules.title: Sole owners and partners must prepay income tax quarterly
rules.plain_english: If the business is a sole ownership or partnership, owners must prepay estimated federal and state income taxes (quarterly). Federal income tax and Social Security withheld from employees must be paid quarterly, monthly or semimonthly as required.
rules.applies_to: Sole proprietors and partners
rules.source: PDF page 41 of the 2026 CSLB Law Book (/home/user/Client/sources/lawbook.txt)
rules.quote: If the business is a sole ownership or partnership, estimated federal and state income taxes must be prepaid or paid quarterly.
rules.notes: Specific estimated-tax due dates and safe-harbor percentages not verified here.

rules.title: Written Injury and Illness Prevention Program (IIPP) required
rules.plain_english: Every employer must have a written IIPP that is actually implemented and kept up to date. Construction employers are required to have one by Construction Safety Order 1509, which points to the general IIPP rule in section 3203.
rules.applies_to: All California employers with employees on construction jobsites (every employer; no size exemption from having a program)
rules.quote: Effective July 1, 1991, every employer shall establish, implement and maintain an effective Injury and Illness Prevention Program (Program). The Program shall be in writing and, shall, at a minimum:
rules.notes: Element (a)(8) employee access was added effective 2020-07-01. 8 CCR 1509(a) separately requires construction employers to maintain an IIPP 'in accordance with section 3203'. A Workplace Violence Prevention Plan may be a separate section of the IIPP (Labor Code 6401.9).

rules.title: Construction employers: IIPP under CSO 1509
rules.plain_english: The Construction Safety Orders independently require every construction employer to establish, implement and maintain an effective IIPP following section 3203.
rules.applies_to: Construction employers
rules.quote: (a) Every employer shall establish, implement and maintain an effective Injury and Illness Prevention Program in accordance with section 3203 of the General Industry Safety Orders.

rules.title: IIPP hazard inspections: when they must happen
rules.plain_english: Your IIPP must include scheduled periodic inspections, and inspections are also required when the program is first set up, when new substances, processes, procedures or equipment bring new hazards, and whenever you learn of a new or previously unrecognized hazard.
rules.applies_to: All California employers with employees on construction jobsites
rules.quote: Include procedures for identifying and evaluating work place hazards including scheduled periodic inspections to identify unsafe conditions and work practices.
rules.notes: The regulation does not fix a numeric inspection interval; the frequency is set by the employer's program. Tool can schedule recurring jobsite inspections and log them (see iipp-inspection-records-1-year).

rules.title: IIPP: correct hazards in a timely manner; remove workers from imminent hazards
rules.plain_english: Unsafe conditions must be corrected in a timely manner based on severity. If an imminent hazard can't be fixed right away, everyone except the people needed to correct it must be removed from the area.
rules.applies_to: All California employers with employees on construction jobsites
rules.quote: When an imminent hazard exists which cannot be immediately abated without endangering employee(s) and/or property, remove all exposed personnel from the area except those necessary to correct the existing condition.

rules.title: IIPP training: when it must be given
rules.plain_english: Safety training must be given when the program starts, to every new employee, to employees given new assignments, when new substances/processes/equipment introduce new hazards, when new hazards are recognized, and to supervisors on the hazards their crews face.
rules.applies_to: All California employers with employees on construction jobsites
rules.quote: (B) To all new employees; (C) To all employees given new job assignments for which training has not previously been received;

rules.title: Employers with fewer than 10 employees may communicate safety orally
rules.plain_english: If you have fewer than 10 employees, you may meet the IIPP communication requirement by instructing employees orally on general safe work practices and job-specific hazards.
rules.applies_to: Employers with fewer than 10 employees
rules.quote: Exception: Employers having fewer than 10 employees shall be permitted to communicate to and instruct employees orally in general safe work practices with specific instructions with respect to hazards unique to the employees' job assignments as compliance with subsection (a)(3).
rules.notes: The program itself must still be in writing; this exception only relaxes the communication element.
rules.correction: None. Quote string-matched against the re-fetched official text and every parameter value checked against it.

rules.title: Give employees a copy of the IIPP within 5 business days
rules.plain_english: When an employee or their designated representative asks for the IIPP, you must provide access no later than 5 business days after the request. The first printed copy is free.

parameters.trigger: request from employee or designated representative
parameters.format_default: printed unless requester agrees to electronic
parameters.alternative: unobstructed electronic access via company server/website

rules.applies_to: All California employers with employees on construction jobsites
rules.quote: Provide access in a reasonable time, place, and manner, but in no event later than five (5) business days after the request for access is received from an employee or designated representative.
rules.notes: Additional copies within 1 year with no updates may carry reasonable reproduction cost. Records of implementation steps need not be included.
rules.correction: None. Quote string-matched against the re-fetched official text and every parameter value checked against it.

rules.title: Keep IIPP inspection records at least 1 year
rules.plain_english: Records of scheduled and periodic inspections (who inspected, what was found, what was done to fix it) must be kept at least one year.
rules.applies_to: All California employers with employees on construction jobsites
rules.quote: These records shall be maintained for at least one (1) year; and Exception: Employers with fewer than 10 employees may elect to maintain the inspection records only until the hazard is corrected.

rules.title: Keep safety training records at least 1 year
rules.plain_english: Document each employee's safety training (name or ID, dates, type of training, trainer) and keep it at least one year.

parameters.lt_10_employees_alternative: log of instructions given at hire/new duties
parameters.short_tenure_exception: employees with < 1 year may receive records at termination instead

rules.applies_to: All California employers with employees on construction jobsites
rules.quote: Documentation of safety and health training required by subsection (a)(7) for each employee, including employee name or other identifier, training dates, type(s) of training, and training providers. This documentation shall be maintained for at least one (1) year.
rules.notes: Note 2 to 3203: CSLB-licensed construction employers may use training records from a Division-approved OSH training program and need only keep records of program steps for hazards specific to the employee's job duties.

rules.title: Reduced IIPP documentation for some employers under 20 employees
rules.plain_english: Employers with fewer than 20 employees that are not on DIR's high-hazard list and have an experience modification rate (EMR) of 1.1 or less may limit written IIPP documentation to: the responsible person, periodic inspections, and training.

parameters.condition: industry not on DIR designated high-hazard list (or industry on DIR low-hazard list)

rules.applies_to: Small employers not in designated high-hazard industries
rules.quote: For Employers with fewer than 20 employees who are in industries that are not on a designated list of high-hazard industries established by the Department of Industrial Relations (Department) and who have a Workers' Compensation Experience Modification Rate of 1.1 or less
rules.notes: Many construction trades appear on DIR's high-hazard industry list, which would make this exception unavailable; the list itself was not reviewed here. Treat as 'check eligibility' rather than auto-apply.
rules.correction: None. Quote string-matched against the re-fetched official text and every parameter value checked against it. The low-hazard-list alternative in the condition is also in Exception No. 3.

rules.title: Labor/management safety committee option: meet at least quarterly
rules.plain_english: If you use a labor/management safety committee to satisfy IIPP communication, it must meet at least quarterly and keep written meeting records for at least one year.
rules.applies_to: Employers that elect a labor/management safety and health committee
rules.quote: (1) Meets regularly, but not less than quarterly;

rules.title: Written Code of Safe Practices required
rules.plain_english: Every construction employer must adopt a written Code of Safe Practices specific to its operations, using language equivalent to the relevant parts of Plate A-3 in the Construction Safety Orders appendix.
rules.applies_to: Construction employers
rules.quote: (b) Every employer shall adopt a written Code of Safe Practices which relates to the employer's operations. The Code shall contain language equivalent to the relevant parts of Plate A-3 of the Appendix.

rules.title: Post the Code of Safe Practices at each jobsite office
rules.plain_english: Post the Code of Safe Practices in a conspicuous place at each jobsite office, or give a copy to every supervisor to keep readily available.

parameters.posting_location: conspicuous location at each job site office
parameters.alternative: provided to each supervisory employee, readily available

rules.applies_to: Construction employers, each jobsite
rules.quote: (c) The Code of Safe Practices shall be posted at a conspicuous location at each job site office or be provided to each supervisory employee who shall have it readily available.
rules.correction: None. Quote string-matched against the re-fetched official text and every parameter value checked against it.

rules.title: Periodic management-led supervisor safety meetings
rules.plain_english: Management must hold periodic meetings of supervisors to discuss safety problems and accidents that have occurred.
rules.applies_to: Construction employers
rules.quote: (d) Periodic meetings of supervisory employees shall be held under the direction of management for the discussion of safety problems and accidents that have occurred.

rules.title: Toolbox/tailgate safety meetings at least every 10 working days
rules.plain_english: Supervisors must hold a toolbox or tailgate safety meeting (or equivalent) with their crews at least every 10 working days.
rules.applies_to: Construction employers, every crew
rules.quote: (e) Supervisory employees shall conduct "toolbox" or "tailgate" safety meetings, or equivalent, with their crews at least every 10 working days to emphasize safety.
rules.notes: 1509 itself does not set a sign-in sheet requirement; documenting attendance supports 3203(b)(2) training records. Interval counts working days, not calendar days.
rules.correction: None. Quote string-matched against the re-fetched official text and every parameter value checked against it.

rules.title: Instruct new workers and have them read the Code of Safe Practices
rules.plain_english: When workers are first employed they must be instructed on the hazards and precautions for their type of work and directed to read the Code of Safe Practices. Workers exposed to known site hazards (chemicals, confined spaces, etc.) must be trained on recognizing the hazard, protection, and first aid.

parameters.trigger: worker first employed

rules.applies_to: Construction employers
rules.quote: (a) When workers are first employed they shall be given instructions regarding the hazards and safety precautions applicable to the type of work in question and directed to read the Code of Safe Practices.

rules.title: Only qualified persons may operate equipment
rules.plain_english: Only qualified persons may be allowed to operate equipment and machinery.
rules.applies_to: Construction employers
rules.quote: (b) The employer shall permit only qualified persons to operate equipment and machinery.

rules.title: Survey the site for hazards before employees arrive
rules.plain_english: Before your employees are on site, survey site conditions to identify predictable hazards and the safeguards needed. No worker may be required to work in an unsafe place except to make it safe with precautions.

parameters.timing: prior to presence of employees on site
parameters.reference: CSO Appendix Plate A-2-a and b

rules.applies_to: Construction employers, each new jobsite
rules.quote: (b) Prior to the presence of its employees, the employer shall make a thorough survey of the conditions of the site to determine, so far as practicable, the predictable hazards to employees and the kind and extent of safeguards necessary to prosecute the work in a safe manner

rules.title: Definition: Competent Person (Construction Safety Orders)
rules.plain_english: A competent person can identify existing and predictable hazards and has authority to take prompt corrective action. Many rules (excavations, scaffolds, silica, asbestos, fall protection plans) require one to be designated.
rules.applies_to: Construction employers
rules.quote: Competent Person. One who is capable of identifying existing and predictable hazards in the surroundings or working conditions which are unsanitary, hazardous, or dangerous to employees, and who has authorization to take prompt corrective measures to eliminate them.

rules.title: Definition: Qualified Person (Construction Safety Orders)
rules.plain_english: A qualified person is someone the employer designates who, by training, experience or instruction, has shown they can safely perform the assigned duties and holds any required license.
rules.applies_to: Construction employers
rules.quote: Qualified Person, Attendant or Operator. A person designated by the employer who by reason of training, experience or instruction has demonstrated the ability to safely perform all assigned duties and, when required, is properly licensed in accordance with federal, state, or local laws and regulations.

rules.title: Outdoor heat standard applies to construction, including high-heat procedures
rules.plain_english: The outdoor heat illness standard covers all outdoor workplaces; construction is one of the listed industries that must also follow the high-heat (95F) procedures.

parameters.standard_name: Maria Isabel Vasquez Jimenez heat illness standard
industries_subject_to_high_heat_subsecti: transportation/delivery of agricultural products, construction materials or other heavy materials

rules.applies_to: Construction employers with employees working outdoors
rules.quote: (2) List of industries subject to all provisions of this standard, including subsection (e): (A) Agriculture (B) Construction

rules.title: Provide 1 quart of drinking water per employee per hour
rules.plain_english: Provide fresh, pure, suitably cool water free of charge, as close as practicable to the work. If water isn't plumbed, bring enough at the start of the shift for 1 quart per employee per hour for the whole shift (or have effective refill procedures).

parameters.location: as close as practicable to work areas
parameters.calc: quarts_at_shift_start = employees * shift_hours (unless effective replenishment procedures)

rules.applies_to: Construction employers with employees working outdoors
rules.quote: Where drinking water is not plumbed or otherwise continuously supplied, it shall be provided in sufficient quantity at the beginning of the work shift to provide one quart per employee per hour for drinking for the entire shift.
rules.notes: 4 cups/hour figure is from the training topic in 3395(h)(1)(C). Example: 8 workers x 10-hour shift = 80 quarts (20 gallons).
rules.correction: None. Quote string-matched against the re-fetched official text and every parameter value checked against it. The 4 cups/hour figure is from 3395(h)(1)(C).

rules.title: Shade must be up when temperature exceeds 80F
rules.plain_english: When the outdoor temperature in the work area exceeds 80F, keep shade set up at all times while employees are present, big enough for everyone on rest or recovery periods to sit fully in the shade without touching. At 80F or below, provide shade or timely access on request.

parameters.shade_capacity: all employees on recovery/rest periods seated in normal posture without contact
parameters.meal_period_capacity: employees on meal period who remain onsite
parameters.at_or_below_80f: provide shade or timely access on request
parameters.temperature_measurement: dry bulb, in full sun with sensor shielded

rules.applies_to: Construction employers with employees working outdoors
rules.quote: (1) Shade shall be present when the temperature exceeds 80 degrees Fahrenheit. When the outdoor temperature in the work area exceeds 80 degrees Fahrenheit, the employer shall have and maintain one or more areas with shade at all times while employees are present that are either open to the air or provided with ventilation or cooling.
rules.notes: Exceptions: alternative procedures if shade structure infeasible/unsafe; non-agriculture employers may use equally effective cooling measures (e.g., misters).
rules.correction: None. Quote string-matched against the re-fetched official text and every parameter value checked against it.

rules.title: Preventative cool-down rest: at least 5 minutes, monitored
rules.plain_english: Employees may take a cool-down rest in the shade whenever they need it. The employee must be monitored, asked about symptoms, encouraged to stay in shade, and not ordered back until symptoms are gone and at least 5 minutes have passed (plus time to reach the shade).

parameters.allowed: at all times on employee request

rules.applies_to: Construction employers with employees working outdoors
rules.quote: (C) shall not be ordered back to work until any signs or symptoms of heat illness have abated, but in no event less than 5 minutes in addition to the time needed to access the shade.
rules.correction: None. Quote string-matched against the re-fetched official text and every parameter value checked against it.

rules.title: High-heat procedures at 95F and above
rules.plain_english: When the temperature is 95F or higher, construction employers must: keep effective communication to a supervisor, observe employees (one supervisor/designee per 20 or fewer, a buddy system, or regular contact with solo workers), designate someone to call EMS, remind workers to drink water throughout the shift, and hold pre-shift meetings on high-heat procedures.
rules.applies_to: Construction employers with employees working outdoors (construction is a listed high-heat industry)
rules.quote: (e) High-heat procedures. The employer shall implement high-heat procedures when the temperature equals or exceeds 95 degrees Fahrenheit.
rules.notes: The mandatory 10-minute-every-2-hours cool-down at 95F in (e)(6) applies only to agriculture, not construction.
rules.correction: None. Quote string-matched against the re-fetched official text and every parameter value checked against it. Construction is listed in 3395(a)(2)(B), so (e) applies to it. The 10 min/2 hr rest in (e)(6) is limited to agriculture.

rules.title: Pre-shift heat meeting on 95F days
rules.plain_english: On high-heat days, hold a meeting before work starts to review high-heat procedures, encourage drinking water, and remind workers of their right to take cool-down rests.

parameters.timing: before commencement of work

rules.applies_to: Construction employers with employees working outdoors
rules.quote: (5) Pre-shift meetings before the commencement of work to review the high heat procedures, encourage employees to drink plenty of water, and remind employees of their right to take a cool-down rest when necessary.

rules.title: Indoor heat standard applies at 82F; full controls at 87F

rules.title: Report serious injury, illness or death to Cal/OSHA within 8 hours
rules.plain_english: Report any employee death or serious injury/illness to Cal/OSHA immediately: as soon as practically possible but no later than 8 hours after you knew or should have known. If the employer can demonstrate that exigent circumstances exist, the time frame for the report may be made no longer than 24 hours after the incident.

rules.title: Employer's Report of Occupational Injury (Form 5020) within 5 days
rules.plain_english: For every work injury or illness causing lost time beyond the day of injury or needing treatment beyond first aid, file the employer's report with your workers' comp insurer (or DIR/DLSR if uninsured/self-insured) within five days after you learn of it. The report must include the employee's SSN.

rules.quote: An employer-contractor MUST file a complete report of every employee occupational injury or occupational illness that results in lost time beyond the date of injury or illness, or which requires medical treatment beyond first aid, with the Department of Industrial Relations through its Division of Labor Statistics and Research or, if an insured employer, with the insurer (Labor Code §6409.1).
rules.notes: Five-day deadline text continues on PDF p.46: '...within five days after the employer obtains knowledge of the injury or illness. Each report ... must indicate the Social Security number of the injured employee'. Form number 5020 is from the DIR WVPP guidance page; the Law Book says 'the form required by the Division of Labor Statistics and Research'. Failure to report to insurer can lead to WCAB order within five days; noncompliance punishable as contempt (Labor Code 3760).
rules.correction: Not refuted. 8 CCR 14001 is the DLSR regulation that implements Labor Code 6409.1(a). It requires a report for lost time beyond the date of injury or treatment beyond first aid, filed on Form 5020 with the insurer, or directly with the Division if self-insured, within five days after the employer learns of it. That matches the parameters and the Law Book quote. Labor Code 6409.1 itself was not seen (leginfo is unreachable).

rules.title: Post the Cal/OSHA 'Safety and Health Protection on the Job' notice

The older '$1,000' figure in section 340's own text is outdated.

rules.correction: penalty_max_usd_per_violation was 1000. That figure comes from stale text in 8 CCR 340. 8 CCR 334(a) classifies "failure to post ... poster" as a Regulatory violation, and 8 CCR 336(a)(1) (2025 schedule, operative 1-1-2025) sets up to $16,285 per Regulatory violation, with a $500 minimum proposed penalty. 336's history says the (a)(1) amounts are adjusted under Labor Code 6431(b). rules.title: CSLB: C-22 or asbestos certification required for 100+ sq ft
rules.plain_english: A contractor may not do asbestos-related work involving 100 sq ft or more of asbestos-containing material unless it holds the C-22 Asbestos Abatement classification or its qualifier passed the CSLB asbestos certification exam. rules.title: C-22 licensees: submit DOSH registration proof within 90 days
rules.plain_english: A new C-22 Asbestos Abatement licensee must give CSLB proof of DOSH registration within 90 days of license issuance; no abatement work until proof is submitted. Missing the deadline automatically suspends the license or removes the C-22. Renewal also requires proof of current DOSH registration.

rules.plain_english: A competent person must inspect excavations, adjacent areas and protective systems daily before work starts, as needed during the shift, and after every rainstorm or other hazard-increasing event; remove employees if cave-in or hazardous conditions are found.

parameters.frequency: daily, prior to start of work, as needed through shift

rules.applies_to: Construction employers with employees in excavations
rules.quote: An inspection shall be conducted by the competent person prior to the start of work and as needed throughout the shift. Inspections shall also be made after every rain storm or other hazard increasing occurrence.

rules.title: Notify regional notification center (811) at least 2 working days before digging
rules.plain_english: Cal/OSHA's excavation order requires advising all regional notification centers (USA North/DigAlert via 811) and known non-member facility owners at least 2 working days before any digging, except emergency repairs.

parameters.exception: emergency repair work (Gov. Code 4216(d))

rules.applies_to: Excavators
rules.quote: (2) All Regional Notification Centers as defined by Government Code Section 4216(j) in the area involved and all known owners of subsurface facilities in the area who are not members of a Notification Center shall be advised of the proposed work at least 2 working days prior to the start of any digging or excavation work.
rules.notes: The 14-calendar-day maximum and 28-day ticket validity are from the CSLB Law Book (PDF pages 84-85) summary of Gov. Code 4216; Gov. Code fines up to $10,000 negligent / $50,000 knowing and willful (PDF p.86).

Code 4216.2 statute text was not seen (leginfo is unreachable), so treat those two values as unverified.

rules.title: Keep spoil and equipment at least 2 feet from excavation edge
rules.plain_english: Keep excavated material and equipment at least 2 feet back from the edge, or use retaining devices, to keep it from falling into the excavation.
rules.applies_to: Construction employers with excavations
rules.quote: Protection shall be provided by placing and keeping such materials or equipment at least 2 feet from the edge of excavations, or by the use of retaining devices that are sufficient to prevent materials or equipment from falling or rolling into excavations, or by a combination of both if necessary.

rules.title: Falsework/shoring: CA civil engineer design over 14 ft height or 16 ft span
rules.plain_english: Falsework or vertical shoring needs design calculations and working drawings signed by a California-registered civil engineer if it is more than 14 feet high (sills to soffit), has spans over 16 feet, or carries vehicle/rail traffic through it. Others may be approved by a CE, manufacturer's rep, or qualified contractor rep. Keep the plan on site; inspect and certify in writing before concrete placement.
rules.applies_to: Employers erecting falsework or vertical shoring
rules.quote: (A) The height, as measured from the top of the sills to the soffit of the superstructure exceeds 14 feet. (B) Individual horizontal span lengths exceed 16 feet.

rules.title: Scaffold erection/dismantling supervised by a qualified person; daily plank inspection
rules.plain_english: Scaffold erection and dismantling must be supervised and directed by a qualified person, and scaffold planks must be visually inspected for defects before use each day.

parameters.engineered_scaffold_designer: CA-registered civil engineer experienced in scaffold design

rules.applies_to: Employers erecting or using scaffolds
rules.quote: (1) The erection and dismantling of scaffolds or falsework shall be performed under the supervision and direction of a qualified person.

rules.title: Cranes over 3 tons: annual certification by licensed certifier
rules.plain_english: Cranes and derricks in lifting service over 3 tons rated capacity may not be used until you confirm they have current annual (and quadrennial) certificates from a Cal/OSHA-licensed certifying agency.
rules.applies_to: Employers using cranes/derricks
rules.quote: (1) Tests and examinations shall be conducted annually by a currently licensed certificating agency or designee listed in the certificating agency license, and a certificate shall be issued by the certificating agency;

rules.title: Construction crane operators: certification, renewed every 5 years
rules.plain_english: Crane operators in construction must be trained, certified (accredited certifying entity, valid up to 5 years) or government-licensed, and evaluated before operating; employers pay for certification. Re-certify every 5 years (1,000 documented hours waives the hands-on exam). Trainees work only under continuous monitoring with restrictions.
rules.applies_to: Employers operating cranes/derricks in construction
rules.quote: (1) Certification. Certificates shall be valid for a maximum of five (5) years.

rules.title: Appropriately trained first-aid persons available
rules.plain_english: Each employer must ensure enough appropriately trained persons are available to give first aid; employers on a multi-employer site may pool trained persons if the pool covers the combined workforce.
rules.applies_to: Construction employers
rules.quote: (b) Appropriately Trained Person. Each employer shall ensure the availability of a suitable number of appropriately trained persons to render first aid.
rules.notes: Rule states no fixed ratio or response-time threshold.

rules.title: First-aid kit in weatherproof container, contents by crew size
rules.plain_english: Every employer with personnel on a construction project must provide at least one first-aid kit in a weatherproof container, inspected regularly and restocked. Minimum contents are set by a licensed physician or by the table in 1512 based on crew size (1-5, 6-15, 16-200, over 200). No drugs or medicines without written physician approval.

items_16_plus: sterile surgical pads for pressure dressings

rules.applies_to: Construction employers
rules.quote: (1) Every employer working on or furnishing personnel on a construction project, on line crews and on other short duration or transient jobs shall provide at least one first-aid kit in a weatherproof container.

rules.title: Post emergency phone numbers at the job phone
rules.plain_english: Post the phone numbers of a physician (plus an alternate if available), hospitals, ambulance and fire services near the job telephone, or otherwise make them available. Inform all employees of what to do in case of injury or illness and provide transport or communication to get emergency care.

parameters.location: near job telephone or switchboard, or otherwise available

rules.quote: The telephone numbers of the following emergency services in the area shall be posted near the job telephone, telephone switchboard, or otherwise made available to the employees where no job site telephone exists:

rules.title: Written emergency medical services plan
rules.plain_english: Have a written plan describing how you meet the emergency medical service requirements; employers sharing a combined program may use one plan.

rules.quote: (i) Written Plan. The employer shall have a written plan to provide emergency medical services. The plan shall specify the means of implementing all applicable requirements in this section.

rules.title: Two-way emergency call system and basket litter at 5 floors / 48 ft
rules.plain_english: Buildings or structures five or more floors or 48 feet or more above or below ground need a two-way voice emergency communication system and at least one basket litter with straps and two blankets.
rules.applies_to: Construction employers on multi-story or deep projects
rules.quote: (g) Emergency Call Systems. A two-way voice emergency communication system shall be installed, for buildings and structures five or more floors or 48 feet or more above or below ground level, to notify persons designated in the emergency medical services plan.

rules.title: Jobsite toilets: 1 per 20 employees of each sex
rules.plain_english: Provide at least one separate toilet facility per 20 employees (or fraction) of each sex; with fewer than 5 employees one all-gender single-user toilet is enough. Mobile crews with ready transport to nearby toilets are exempt.

parameters.rounding: per 20 or fraction thereof, each sex

rules.quote: (a) A minimum of one separate toilet facility shall be provided for each 20 employees or fraction thereof of each sex.

rules.quote: A minimum of one washing station shall be provided for each twenty employees or fraction thereof.

rules.title: Written Hazard Communication program (incl. multi-employer sites)
rules.plain_english: Keep a written hazard communication program at the workplace covering labels, safety data sheets and training. On multi-employer sites it must explain how you will inform other employers of hazardous chemicals their workers may be exposed to.
rules.applies_to: Employers whose employees may be exposed to hazardous chemicals
rules.quote: (1) Employers shall develop, implement, and maintain at the workplace a written hazard communication program for their employees which at least describes how the criteria specified in sections 5194(f), (g), and (h) for labels and other forms of warning, safety data sheets, and employee information and training will be met,

rules.title: Written respiratory protection program; annual fit testing
rules.plain_english: Where respirators are necessary or required (e.g., silica, lead, asbestos), have a written worksite-specific respiratory protection program with a trained administrator, and fit-test tight-fitting respirators before first use, when changing models, and at least annually.
rules.applies_to: Employers whose employees use required respirators
rules.quote: (2) The employer shall ensure that an employee using a tight-fitting facepiece respirator is fit tested prior to initial use of the respirator, whenever a different respirator facepiece (size, style, model or make) is used, and at least annually thereafter.
