Approximate date when labor on the job stopped. 2. Confirmation that no further labor has been performed since the recording of the notice...'.

rules.title: Owner must send copy of recorded NOC/cessation within 10 days
rules.plain_english: An owner who records a notice of completion or cessation must, within 10 days of recording, send a copy to the direct contractor and to every claimant who served it a preliminary notice. If it doesn't, the notice does not shorten that person's lien deadline. Owner-occupants of 1-4 unit residences are excluded.

parameters.trigger: date notice of completion or cessation is recorded
recipients: each claimant that gave the owner preliminary notice
parameters.consequence_of_failure: notice ineffective to shorten that person's time to record under 8412/8414 (stays 90 days)
parameters.exempt: owner occupying the property as a personal residence with four or fewer units

rules.applies_to: Owners of private works recording notices of completion or cessation
rules.source: PDF page 76 of the 2026 CSLB Law Book
rules.quote: NOTE: An owner who files a Notice of Cessation or a Notice of Completion must notify any potential lien claimants within 10 days of recording the notices. This notification is designed to let you, the potential lien claimant, know that the time for filing a Claim of Lien has been reduced.
rules.notes: Leginfo (leginfo.legislature.ca.gov) is behind a Cloudflare challenge and could not be fetched from this environment; quote is a search-engine excerpt of the official leginfo page, not a fetched copy. Verify exact wording before generating documents. Leginfo excerpt of 8190(a): owner 'shall, within 10 days of the date the notice of completion or cessation is filed for record, give a copy of the notice to all of the following persons: (1) A direct contractor. (2) A claimant that has given the owner preliminary notice.' 8190 excerpt: failure makes the notice 'ineffective to shorten the time within which that person may record a claim of lien under Sections 8412 and 8414'. Law Book adds: 'This provision does not apply to a residential property of four or fewer units.'
rules.correction: Not refuted on the 10-day figure (matches Law Book p.76). FLAG on the exemption: the rule says the exemption covers an "owner occupying the property as a personal residence with four or fewer units". The only official text seen (Law Book p.76) says "does not apply to a residential property of four or fewer units", with no owner-occupancy condition. The two scopes differ and neither is the statute. Verify Civ. Code 8190 before applying the exemption either way.

rules.title: Direct contractor lien recording deadline (60/90 days)
rules.plain_english: A direct (prime) contractor records its lien after it completes its contract and no later than 60 days after the owner records a notice of completion or cessation, or 90 days after completion of the whole job if no valid notice is recorded - whichever is earlier.

parameters.earliest: after completion of the direct contract

rules.applies_to: Direct (prime/original) contractors on private works
rules.source: PDF page 77 of the 2026 CSLB Law Book
rules.quote: 1. Within 60 days of recording a Notice of Cessation or a Notice of Completion, the contractor must record a Claim of Lien.
rules.notes: Leginfo (leginfo.legislature.ca.gov) is behind a Cloudflare challenge and could not be fetched from this environment; quote is a search-engine excerpt of the official leginfo page, not a fetched copy. Verify exact wording before generating documents. Leginfo excerpt of 8412: record 'after the direct contractor completes the direct contract, and before the earlier of' 90 days after completion of the work of improvement or 60 days after the owner records a notice of completion or cessation. If owner fails to send 8190 copy, the 60-day period does not apply to that contractor.
rules.correction: Not refuted. Quote matches Law Book p.77. The 60/90-day figures match the CSLB page and Guide. The "earlier of" structure and the "after completion of the direct contract" start point come only from the original 8412 search excerpt.

rules.title: Subcontractor/supplier lien recording deadline (30/90 days)
rules.plain_english: Subcontractors, suppliers and other non-direct claimants must record their lien no later than 30 days after the owner records a notice of completion or cessation, or 90 days after completion if no valid notice is recorded - whichever is earlier.
rules.applies_to: Subcontractors, material suppliers, equipment lessors, laborers on private works
rules.source: PDF page 75-76 of the 2026 CSLB Law Book
rules.quote: (a) Within 30 days of the owner recording either a Notice of Cessation or Completion, the subcontractor must record a Claim of Lien with the county recorder.
rules.notes: Leginfo (leginfo.legislature.ca.gov) is behind a Cloudflare challenge and could not be fetched from this environment; quote is a search-engine excerpt of the official leginfo page, not a fetched copy. Verify exact wording before generating documents. Leginfo excerpt of 8414: claimant other than a direct contractor records after it ceases work and 'before the earlier of' 90 days after completion or 30 days after the owner records a notice of completion or cessation. Law Book (PDF page 79): 'If this notice is not filed in a timely manner, you have a 90-day period within which to record the claim.'
rules.correction: Not refuted. Quote matches Law Book p.75-76; it spans the page break. The 30/90-day figures match the CSLB page and Guide. The note's Law Book cite for the 90-day sentence is PDF p.79, not p.80: corrected. Civ. Code 8414 text not seen.

rules.title: No NOC recorded: 90 days after completion/use/acceptance
rules.plain_english: If no notice of completion or cessation is recorded, any claimant has 90 days after completion - including when labor ceases and the owner uses the improvement, or the owner accepts it - to record its lien.

triggers: labor ceases and owner/agent uses improvement

rules.applies_to: All private-works lien claimants
rules.quote: The potential lien claimant must record the mechanics lien within 90 days of: Completion of work; When the property owner began using the improvement;* or When the property owner accepted the improvement.
rules.notes: CSLB consumer page. Same rule appears in Law Book checklist (PDF page 76-77). Note completion also occurs automatically after 60 continuous days of no labor (Civ. Code 8180).
rules.correction: Quote matches the CSLB page verbatim and the 90-day figure is consistent across CSLB sources. FLAG, not applied because primary text not seen: the "owner/agent accepts improvement" trigger comes only from CSLB consumer narrative and looks like the former Civ. Code 3086 list. As recodified in 2012, Civ. Code 8180 is believed not to list owner acceptance for private works; acceptance is a public-works event under 9200. It is believed instead to include 60 days of continuous cessation and a notice of cessation after 30 days' cessation. The parameters omit the cessation triggers, which appear only in the notes. Verify 8180 before using these triggers.

rules.title: Lien foreclosure suit within 90 days of recording
rules.plain_english: After recording a mechanics lien, the claimant must file a lawsuit to foreclose it within 90 days (and record a lis pendens); otherwise the lien expires and is unenforceable.

parameters.trigger: date claim of lien recorded
parameters.also_record: lis pendens (notice of pendency of action)

rules.applies_to: All private-works lien claimants
rules.source: PDF page 76 of the 2026 CSLB Law Book
rules.quote: (b) File Lien Foreclosure Action within 90 days of recording a Claim of Lien and record a lis pendens at the same time. You must also file an action on the stop notice at this time, if applicable.
rules.notes: Leginfo (leginfo.legislature.ca.gov) is behind a Cloudflare challenge and could not be fetched from this environment; quote is a search-engine excerpt of the official leginfo page, not a fetched copy. Verify exact wording before generating documents. Leginfo excerpt of 8460 states that if no action is commenced the claim of lien 'expires and is unenforceable'. CSLB consumer page: 'The lien claimant must file a lien foreclosure action within 90 days of the date that he or she recorded the mechanics lien.'
rules.correction: Not refuted. Quote matches Law Book p.76. The 90-day period is confirmed by the CSLB page and Guide. "Record a lis pendens at the same time" is Law Book narrative; the statutory lis pendens requirement and its timing were not verified. "Expires and is unenforceable" comes only from the original 8460 excerpt.

rules.title: Credit extension can extend foreclosure deadline (max 1 year after completion)
rules.plain_english: If the owner and claimant agree to extend credit and record notice of the extension, the foreclosure suit is due within 90 days after the credit expires, but never later than one year after completion of the work.

parameters.absolute_limit: 1 year after completion of work of improvement

rules.applies_to: Private-works lien claimants granting credit to owner
rules.quote: the claimant shall commence an action to enforce the lien within 90 days after the expiration of the credit, but in no case later than one year after completion of the work of improvement
rules.notes: Leginfo (leginfo.legislature.ca.gov) is behind a Cloudflare challenge and could not be fetched from this environment; quote is a search-engine excerpt of the official leginfo page, not a fetched copy. Verify exact wording before generating documents. Excerpt also indicates the notice of credit extension may be recorded within 90 days after recording the claim of lien, or later before a good-faith purchaser/encumbrancer acquires an interest.
rules.correction: No official source reachable. The quote and the 90-day/1-year figures rest only on the original search excerpt.

rules.title: Claim of mechanics lien required contents
rules.plain_english: The claim of lien must be signed and verified and state: the amount owed after credits and offsets, the owner's name, the kind of work or materials furnished, who hired you, a site description, and your address, plus the Notice of Mechanics Lien and a proof of service affidavit.

fields: amount of demand after deducting credits and offsets
name of owner or reputed owner, if known
kind of labor, service, equipment or materials furnished
name of person who employed claimant or to whom work was furnished
description of site sufficient for identification
Notice of Mechanics Lien (statutory text, at least 10-point boldface)

rules.applies_to: All private-works lien claimants
rules.source: PDF page 78 of the 2026 CSLB Law Book
rules.quote: Claim of Lien (mechanics lien) is a written statement signed and verified by the claimant or by the claimant's agent that must state the following: 1. The amount of claimant's demand (after deducting credits and offsets). 2. The name of the owner or reputed owner, if known.
rules.notes: Law Book glossary (PDF page 78) also lists items 3-5 (kind of labor, person who employed claimant, site description). Claimant address, proof-of-service affidavit and Notice of Mechanics Lien come from Civ. Code 8416 per leginfo search excerpt and the CSLB 'If a Mechanics Lien Is Filed' page. Exact statutory Notice of Mechanics Lien text was not obtained verbatim; leginfo excerpt says it must be 'in at least 10-point boldface type' with the final sentence in uppercase except the CSLB web address. Copy text from leginfo Civ. Code 8416(a)(8) before generating.

rules.title: Serve lien + Notice of Mechanics Lien with proof of service affidavit
rules.plain_english: A copy of the recorded lien with the Notice of Mechanics Lien must be served on the owner (or, if the owner can't be served, on the construction lender or direct contractor), and the server must sign a proof of service affidavit. Failure makes the lien unenforceable.

serve_on: fallback: construction lender or original/direct contractor
affidavit_contents: date, place and manner of service
name and address of person served and capacity
parameters.consequence_of_failure: claim of lien unenforceable as a matter of law

rules.applies_to: All private-works lien claimants
rules.source: PDF page 78 of the 2026 CSLB Law Book
rules.quote: Failure to serve the mechanics lien and confirm a proof of service affidavit will cause the mechanics lien to be unenforceable.
rules.notes: Leginfo (leginfo.legislature.ca.gov) is behind a Cloudflare challenge and could not be fetched from this environment; quote is a search-engine excerpt of the official leginfo page, not a fetched copy. Verify exact wording before generating documents. Law Book (PDF page 78) attributes this to 'AB 457, which took effect in 2011'. Leginfo excerpt: failure to serve 'shall cause the claim of mechanics lien to be unenforceable as a matter of law'. Exact service methods (personal service, mail like preliminary notice, CCP 415.20) and timing relative to recording not verified.
rules.correction: Not refuted. Quote matches Law Book p.78. The Guide and CSLB page agree on service, proof of service affidavit and unenforceability. The required wording of the Notice of Mechanics Lien (8416(a)(7)) was not obtained, so do not generate that notice from this rule. Service methods and timing remain unverified.

rules.title: Lien only for work incorporated; supplier's supplier has no lien
rules.plain_english: To have a lien, your labor or materials must be incorporated (installed) in the improvement, and you must have been hired by the owner or someone in charge of the work; a supplier to a material supplier has no statutory lien.
rules.applies_to: Potential lien claimants on private works
rules.citation: Cal. Const. art. XIV, sec. 3; Civil Code 8400, 8404
rules.source: PDF page 73 of the 2026 CSLB Law Book
rules.quote: A material supplier is not the agent of the owner and, therefore, a material supplier's supplier is not entitled to a statutory lien. Further, to perfect your lien, the work and/or materials, etc. must be incorporated into the structure. That is to say, it has to be installed.
rules.notes: CSLB Law Book narrative. The statute (8400, 8404) not fetched; incorporation requirement is the Law Book's characterization.
rules.correction: Quote matches Law Book p.73. The constitutional text reproduced there was confirmed, but it contains neither the "incorporated/installed" requirement nor the bar on a supplier's supplier. Both are CSLB narrative. FLAG: "it has to be installed" is CSLB's simplification, and the statutory standard in Civ. Code 8400 et seq. may be broader. Do not use it as a hard eligibility gate until verified.

rules.title: Unlicensed contractor cannot enforce lien over $500
rules.plain_english: Anyone can record a lien, but an unlicensed contractor cannot foreclose a mechanics lien for work valued over $500 (B&P 7031 bars suits for compensation).

parameters.condition: work requiring a license performed while unlicensed

rules.applies_to: Contractors performing work requiring a CSLB license
rules.quote: Although anyone can record a mechanics lien, unlicensed contractors cannot foreclose on a mechanics lien if the work is valued at more than $500.
rules.notes: CSLB consumer page. The $500 figure corresponds to the minor-work exemption (B&P 7048); see license-domain research for 7031/7048 details.

rules.title: Lien release bond = 125% of claim
rules.plain_english: An owner, direct contractor or affected subcontractor can free the property from a recorded lien by recording a release bond from an admitted surety equal to 125% of the lien amount (or of the amount allocated to the property released).
rules.applies_to: Private works with recorded mechanics liens
rules.quote: 125 percent of the amount of the claim of lien or 125 percent of the amount allocated in the claim of lien to the real property to be released
rules.notes: Leginfo (leginfo.legislature.ca.gov) is behind a Cloudflare challenge and could not be fetched from this environment; quote is a search-engine excerpt of the official leginfo page, not a fetched copy. Verify exact wording before generating documents.
rules.correction: No official source reachable. The Law Book 1 1/4 figure (p.78, p.81) is for bonded stop notices, not lien release bonds, so it is not corroboration. The 125% figure rests only on the original search excerpt.

rules.title: Release-order petition: 10-day demand first
rules.plain_english: If the claimant has not filed a foreclosure suit within the 90-day period, the owner can petition the court to release the lien, but must first send the claimant a demand to release the lien at least 10 days before filing.

parameters.precondition: no enforcement action within Civ. Code 8460 period
parameters.demand_content: demand that claimant execute and record a release of the claim of lien

rules.applies_to: Owners of private property with expired/unenforced liens
rules.quote: unless at least 10 days before filing the petition the owner gives the claimant notice demanding that the claimant execute and record a release of the claim of lien
rules.notes: Leginfo (leginfo.legislature.ca.gov) is behind a Cloudflare challenge and could not be fetched from this environment; quote is a search-engine excerpt of the official leginfo page, not a fetched copy. Verify exact wording before generating documents. CSLB consumer page recommends sending the demand by certified, registered, or express mail and keeping proof.

rules.title: Prevailing party attorney fees on lien release petition (no cap)
rules.plain_english: In a court petition to release a lien, the prevailing party gets reasonable attorney's fees; the old $2,000 cap was removed effective July 1, 2012.
rules.applies_to: Owners and lien claimants in release-order proceedings
rules.quote: Civil Code section 8488 provides that if you use an attorney and you prevail, you are entitled to reasonable attorney's fees.
rules.notes: CSLB homeowner guide (PDF columns extracted with pdftotext; quote text read from guide). Leginfo excerpt of 8488: 'The prevailing party is entitled to reasonable attorney's fees.' 8488 also puts the burden of proof as to lien validity on the claimant.
rules.correction: Not refuted. Quote matches the Guide verbatim. Removal of the $2,000 cap effective July 1, 2012 (SB 189, Stats 2010 ch 697) is confirmed by both CSLB sources. Civ. Code 8488 text not seen.

rules.title: Notice of nonresponsibility: post and record within 10 days
rules.plain_english: An owner who did not order the work (e.g., a landlord whose tenant is remodeling) can avoid lien liability only by posting a signed, verified notice of nonresponsibility on the site and recording it within 10 days after learning of the work.

parameters.trigger: person gains knowledge of the work of improvement
actions: post in conspicuous place on site
fields: name and nature of title/interest of person giving notice
name of purchaser under contract or lessee, if known
statement that person is not responsible for claims arising from the work

rules.applies_to: Owners/interest holders who did not cause the work (landlords, vendors under contract of sale)
rules.source: PDF page 80 of the 2026 CSLB Law Book
rules.quote: Within 10 days of discovering the work of improvement, the person asserting non-responsibility must post this notice in a conspicuous place on the site and must record the notice in the Office of the County Recorder of the county in which the site is located.
rules.notes: Leginfo (leginfo.legislature.ca.gov) is behind a Cloudflare challenge and could not be fetched from this environment; quote is a search-engine excerpt of the official leginfo page, not a fetched copy. Verify exact wording before generating documents. Leginfo excerpt of 8444: notice 'is not effective unless, within 10 days after the person giving notice has knowledge of the work of improvement, the person both posts and records the notice'.
rules.correction: Not refuted. Quote and the four content fields match the Law Book glossary (p.79-80), which is CSLB narrative; Civ. Code 8444 text not seen.

rules.title: No mechanics lien on public works - use stop payment notice / bond
rules.plain_english: You cannot record a mechanics lien on public property; on public works your remedies are a stop payment notice to the public entity and a claim on the contractor's payment bond.

public_works_remedies: stop payment notice (Civ. Code 9350 et seq.)
payment bond claim (Civ. Code 9550 et seq.)

rules.applies_to: Subcontractors and suppliers on public works
rules.source: PDF page 74 of the 2026 CSLB Law Book
rules.quote: A mechanics lien is a lien on property. A stop notice is a lien on funds. You may use one or the other, or both. However, it should be noted that in public works, you cannot file a mechanics lien; therefore, your only remedy may be a stop notice.
rules.notes: CSLB Law Book narrative; uses pre-2012 term 'stop notice' (now 'stop payment notice').

rules.title: Stop payment notice contents
rules.plain_english: A stop payment notice is signed and verified by the claimant and states the kind of work furnished, who it was furnished to, and the value of work already furnished and of the whole work agreed to be done.

fields: kind of labor, service, equipment or materials furnished or agreed to be furnished
name of person to or for whom furnished
amount/value of work already done or furnished
amount of the whole work agreed to be done

rules.applies_to: Claimants giving stop payment notices (private and public works)
rules.source: PDF page 80 of the 2026 CSLB Law Book
rules.quote: Stop Notice is a written notice, signed and verified by the claimant or the claimant's agent, that puts a lender or anyone else holding construction funds on notice that there is money due and owed to the claimant.
rules.notes: Law Book glossary (PDF page 80) lists the three required statements. Current statutes call it a 'stop payment notice'; general contents also governed by Civ. Code 8102.

rules.title: Where to deliver a private-works stop payment notice
rules.plain_english: On private works, deliver the stop payment notice to the owner (or the owner's architect), and for a construction lender, to the manager or responsible officer at the office or branch administering the construction funds.

owner_delivery: left at residence/place of business with person in charge
parameters.lender_delivery: manager or other responsible person at office/branch administering or holding construction funds

rules.applies_to: Private-works claimants
rules.source: PDF page 80-81 of the 2026 CSLB Law Book
rules.quote: If involving a private work of improvement, the notice must be delivered to the owner personally or left at their residence or place of business with a person in charge or delivered to their architect, if any;
rules.notes: Leginfo (leginfo.legislature.ca.gov) is behind a Cloudflare challenge and could not be fetched from this environment; quote is a search-engine excerpt of the official leginfo page, not a fetched copy. Verify exact wording before generating documents. Leginfo excerpt of 8506: 'A stop payment notice to an owner shall be given to the owner or to the owner's architect, if any' and 'shall comply with the requirements of Chapter 2 (commencing with Section 8100) of Title 1.'

rules.title: Bonded stop payment notice to lender: bond = 125% of claim
rules.plain_english: To bind a construction lender, the stop payment notice must be accompanied by a bond equal to 125% (1.25x) of the claim.
rules.applies_to: Private-works claimants serving construction lenders
rules.source: PDF page 81 of the 2026 CSLB Law Book
rules.quote: To bind a construction lender, the stop notice must be bonded. The bond that accompanies a stop notice to any construction lender must be in the sum equal to 1 ¼ times the amount of the claim.
rules.notes: Leginfo (leginfo.legislature.ca.gov) is behind a Cloudflare challenge and could not be fetched from this environment; quote is a search-engine excerpt of the official leginfo page, not a fetched copy. Verify exact wording before generating documents. Leginfo excerpt of 8532: bond 'in an amount equal to 125 percent of the amount of the claim', conditioned on paying costs and damages if the defendant recovers judgment. Under 8536 (excerpt), a lender may elect not to withhold on an unbonded notice.
rules.correction: Not refuted. Quote matches Law Book p.81, and p.78 repeats "1 1/4 times the amount of the claim". Both are CSLB narrative using pre-2012 "stop notice" terminology. Civ. Code 8532/8536 text not seen.

rules.title: Lender objection to stop-notice bond sureties (20/10 days)
rules.plain_english: A lender that objects to the sureties on a bonded stop payment notice must notify the claimant within 20 days; the claimant then has 10 days to substitute a bond from an admitted surety or the lender may release the withheld funds.
rules.applies_to: Construction lenders and claimants on private works
rules.notes: Leginfo (leginfo.legislature.ca.gov) is behind a Cloudflare challenge and could not be fetched from this environment; quote is a search-engine excerpt of the official leginfo page, not a fetched copy. Verify exact wording before generating documents. Figures from leginfo search excerpt of 8534; exact wording not obtained.
rules.correction: No quote and no official source reachable. The 20-day and 10-day figures rest only on the original search excerpt.

rules.title: Holder of funds must withhold on stop payment notice
rules.plain_english: An owner or lender that receives a valid stop payment notice must withhold enough money from the contractor to cover the claim; if it does not, it can become directly liable to the claimant.

parameters.withhold_amount: sufficient to pay claim stated in notice
parameters.liability_if_not_withheld: may be liable to claimant directly

rules.applies_to: Owners and construction lenders on private works
rules.source: PDF page 81 of the 2026 CSLB Law Book
rules.quote: The stop notice obligates the person holding construction funds to withhold sufficient funds to satisfy the amount in the stop notice. If the person holding the funds does not withhold sufficient funds to satisfy the stop notice, then the lender or whoever else is holding the funds may be responsible to the claimant directly.
rules.notes: Leginfo (leginfo.legislature.ca.gov) is behind a Cloudflare challenge and could not be fetched from this environment; quote is a search-engine excerpt of the official leginfo page, not a fetched copy. Verify exact wording before generating documents. Leginfo excerpt of 8522: 'On receipt of a stop payment notice an owner shall withhold from the direct contractor ... a sufficient amount due or to become due to pay the claim stated in the notice.' Excerpt also indicates an owner with a recorded payment bond may elect not to withhold and must then notify the claimant within 30 days and give a bond copy - verify before automating.

rules.title: Only non-direct claimants may give owner a stop payment notice
rules.plain_english: On private works, a stop payment notice to the owner may be given by a claimant other than the direct contractor (subcontractors, suppliers, laborers).

parameters.eligible: claimant other than a direct contractor

rules.applies_to: Private works
rules.quote: A claimant other than a direct contractor may give the owner a stop payment notice.
rules.notes: Leginfo (leginfo.legislature.ca.gov) is behind a Cloudflare challenge and could not be fetched from this environment; quote is a search-engine excerpt of the official leginfo page, not a fetched copy. Verify exact wording before generating documents. The search excerpt also referenced forfeiture of lien rights tied to an owner's request for a stop payment notice; that sub-rule was not verified and is omitted.
rules.correction: Primary text not seen. The Law Book narrative is consistent: stop notices are served on the owner by subcontractors and suppliers. It does not state the direct-contractor exclusion.

rules.title: Suit on private stop payment notice: 10 days after / 90 days after window
rules.plain_english: A claimant must sue to enforce a private stop payment notice no earlier than 10 days after giving it and no later than 90 days after the time to give a stop payment notice expires; otherwise the notice lapses and the withheld funds are released.

parameters.notice_period: same as time to record claim of lien (8412/8414) - verify
parameters.consequence: notice ceases to be effective; funds released

rules.applies_to: Private-works claimants who gave stop payment notices
rules.quote: not later than 90 days after expiration of the time within which a stop payment notice must be given
rules.notes: Leginfo (leginfo.legislature.ca.gov) is behind a Cloudflare challenge and could not be fetched from this environment; quote is a search-engine excerpt of the official leginfo page, not a fetched copy. Verify exact wording before generating documents. Seen in SB 189 (2010) bill text that enacted the current code; codified subdivision lettering not verified. Law Book checklist (PDF page 76): 'File suit on the notice at the same time that you file a Lien Foreclosure Action.'
rules.correction: Primary text not seen. The Law Book says only to file suit on the notice with the lien foreclosure action, with no 10-day or 90-day figures. The notice-period parameter is still marked "verify".

rules.title: Payment bond recorded: serve notice on surety
rules.plain_english: If no mechanics lien has been recorded and a payment bond has been recorded, the notice must be served on the surety.

parameters.condition: no mechanics lien recorded AND payment bond recorded

rules.applies_to: Private-works claimants
rules.source: PDF page 76 of the 2026 CSLB Law Book
rules.quote: (b) If no mechanics lien has been recorded, and a surety payment bond has been recorded, then the notice must be served on the surety.
rules.notes: CSLB Law Book checklist. See private-bond-claim-notice for the statutory 15/75-day bond notice.

rules.title: Private payment bond claim notice (15/75 days) if no preliminary notice

rules.title: Home improvement downpayment: lesser of $1,000 or 10%
rules.plain_english: On a home improvement contract, any downpayment may not exceed $1,000 or 10% of the contract amount, whichever is less.
rules.applies_to: Home improvement contracts (B&P 7151.2) between owner/tenant and licensed or unlicensed contractor
rules.source: PDF page 410 of the 2026 CSLB Law Book
rules.quote: (3) If a downpayment will be charged, the downpayment shall not exceed one thousand dollars ($1,000) or 10 percent of the contract amount, whichever amount is less.
rules.notes: Contract must also print in 12-point boldface: 'THE DOWNPAYMENT MAY NOT EXCEED $1,000 OR 10 PERCENT OF THE CONTRACT PRICE, WHICHEVER IS LESS.' (B&P 7159(d)(8)(C), Law Book PDF page 400). Exempt if contractor furnishes qualifying bonds/joint control (7159.5(a)(8)).

rules.title: No payment exceeding value of work performed or materials delivered
rules.plain_english: Except for the downpayment, a home improvement contractor may not request or accept payment that exceeds the value of the work performed or materials delivered, including advance payments from a lender.

rules.title: Schedule of progress payments in dollars and cents
rules.plain_english: If any payments besides the downpayment are due before completion, the home improvement contract must include a 'Schedule of Progress Payments' stating each payment in dollars and cents tied to specific work, materials and equipment, with the statutory 12-point boldface warning.
rules.applies_to: Home improvement contracts with progress payments
rules.source: PDF page 400 of the 2026 CSLB Law Book
rules.quote: IT IS AGAINST THE LAW FOR A CONTRACTOR TO COLLECT PAYMENT FOR WORK NOT YET COMPLETED, OR FOR MATERIALS NOT YET DELIVERED. HOWEVER, A CONTRACTOR MAY REQUIRE A DOWNPAYMENT.
rules.notes: Full required statement begins: 'The schedule of progress payments must specifically describe each phase of work, including the type and amount of work or services scheduled to be supplied in each phase, along with the amount of each proposed progress payment.' (Law Book PDF page 400).

rules.title: Furnish unconditional lien releases on payment if requested
rules.plain_english: After each payment by the homeowner, the contractor must, if requested, obtain and give the owner full unconditional lien releases for the work paid for; the owner may withhold all further payments until it gets them.

parameters.trigger: any payment by owner + owner request
parameters.release_type: full and unconditional release (Civ. Code 8134/8138 forms)

rules.applies_to: Home improvement contractors
rules.source: PDF page 410 of the 2026 CSLB Law Book
rules.quote: (6) Upon any payment by the person contracting for home improvement, and prior to any further payment being made, the contractor shall, if requested, obtain and furnish to the person a full and unconditional release from any potential lien claimant claim or mechanics lien authorized pursuant to Sections 8400 and 8404 of the Civil Code for any portion of the work for which payment has been made.

rules.title: HIC must state contractor will furnish lien releases
rules.plain_english: Every home improvement contract must include a statement that, upon satisfactory payment for any portion of the work, the contractor will furnish a full and unconditional lien release for that portion before any further payment.

rules.notes: Quote truncated at 400 chars; statute continues 'authorized pursuant to Sections 8400 and 8404 of the Civil Code for that portion of the work for which payment has been made.'

rules.title: HIC must include the 'Mechanics Lien Warning' notice
rules.plain_english: Home improvement contracts must include the statutory 'Mechanics Lien Warning' explaining liens, preliminary notices, the 20-day timing, and joint checks (unless the contractor furnishes qualifying bonds or joint control).
rules.applies_to: Home improvement contracts
rules.source: PDF page 402 of the 2026 CSLB Law Book
rules.quote: Anyone who helps improve your property, but who is not paid, may record what is called a mechanics lien on your property. A mechanics lien is a claim, like a mortgage or home equity loan, made against your property and recorded with the county recorder.
rules.notes: Full text runs on Law Book PDF pages 402-403 (7159(e)(4)); generator should copy the entire warning verbatim from the Law Book including 'BE CAREFUL. The Preliminary Notice can be sent up to 20 days after the subcontractor starts work...' and the CSLB contact line. 7159(e) allows attachment only where a paragraph expressly authorizes it; paragraph (4) does not, so treat the warning as part of the contract form.

rules.title: Bond/joint-control exemption from HIC payment limits
rules.plain_english: A contractor that furnishes a performance and payment bond, lien and completion bond, CSLB-approved bond equivalent, or joint control covering full performance and payment is exempt from the downpayment cap, the payment-schedule and no-advance-payment rules, and need not include the contract's downpayment statement, the progress-payment details/statement, or the Mechanics Lien Warning; it may accept payment before completion. All other contract requirements still apply. A blanket bond application requires 2 years of active licensure.

parameters.still_required: all other 7159(c), (d) and (e) items, including the other 7159(e) notices

rules.source: PDF page 411 of the 2026 CSLB Law Book
rules.quote: (8) A contractor furnishing a performance and payment bond, lien and completion bond, or a bond equivalent or joint control approved by the registrar covering full performance and payment is exempt from paragraphs (3), (4), and (5), and need not include, as part of the contract, the statement regarding the downpayment specified in subparagraph (C) of paragraph (8) of subdivision (d) of Section 7159, the details and statement regarding progress payments specified in paragraph (9) of subdivision (d) of Section 7159, or the Mechanics Lien Warning specified in paragraph (4) of subdivision (e) of Section 7159.
rules.notes: Contractor furnishing joint control may not have a financial or other interest in the joint control.

Added both to exempt_from and plain_english. The quote is replaced with the operative exemption sentence. All other 7159(c)-(e) items still apply, including the rest of the 7159(e) notices.

rules.title: HIC payment violations are misdemeanors ($100-$5,000)

rules.title: New single-family dwelling contracts must include Mechanics Lien Warning
rules.plain_english: A contract to build a single-family home the owner will keep at least one year must be in writing, signed by both parties, and include the contractor's name/address/license number, approximate start and substantial-completion dates, the legal description, the 7164 version of the "Mechanics Lien Warning", and the CGL insurance statement and check box. Near the signatures it must state, in at least 10-point bold or all caps, that the owner may require a performance and payment bond at the owner's expense. The owner must get a contractor-signed copy before work starts.

rules.applies_to: Contracts between owner and contractor to construct a single-family dwelling retained by owner >= 1 year
rules.source: PDF pages 425-427 of the 2026 CSLB Law Book
rules.quote: (a) Notwithstanding Section 7044, every contract and any changes in a contract, between an owner and a contractor, for the construction of a single-family dwelling to be retained by the owner for at least one year shall be evidenced in writing signed by both parties.
rules.notes: The 7164(b)(4) warning differs from the 7159(e)(4) HIC warning: "if he or she is not paid" (7159: "if they are not paid"); "from your prime contractor or other persons you contract with directly or from laborers" (7159 omits the middle phrase); "visit CSLB's Web site at www.cslb.ca.gov or call CSLB at 800-321-CSLB (2752)" (7159: "internet website"). Copy the 7164 text verbatim from Law Book PDF p.425-426 for SFD contracts.
rules.correction: Two gaps where exact wording matters. (1) The 7164(b)(4) Mechanics Lien Warning is not identical to the 7159(e)(4) HIC warning. It says "if he or she is not paid" (7159: "if they are not paid") and "from your prime contractor or other persons you contract with directly or from laborers" (7159 omits the middle phrase). It also says "visit CSLB's Web site at www.cslb.ca.gov or call CSLB at 800-321-CSLB (2752)", where 7159 says "internet website" and splits the line. SFD contracts must use the 7164 text. (2) The rule omitted 7164(d): a notice near the owner and contractor signatures, in at least 10-point boldface or all capitals, that the owner has the right to require a performance and payment bond and that the owner may bear its expense. parts.2.5: California Residential Code (CRC), based on 2024 IRC
parts.7: (no longer published / vacant in recent editions)

Names of Parts 7-10 and 12 are from general knowledge of Title 24 structure, not read from a fetched source in this session; Part 7 status not verified. rules.title: Code edition is set by permit application date
rules.plain_english: The building standards that apply to a project are the ones in effect locally on the date the building permit application is submitted (plan-check submittal), not the date of issuance or construction.

parameters.trigger: date building permit application submitted

rules.applies_to: All permitted construction
rules.quote: (a) Only those building standards approved by the commission, and that are effective at the local level at the time an application for a building permit is submitted, shall apply to the plans and specifications for, and to the construction
rules.notes: Quote is from a 2009 Justia copy surfaced in a search excerpt; statute last amended Stats. 2025 ch. 22 sec. 40 per Counsel Stack - verify current wording. Exception: if the permit later expires (see permit-expiration rule), the new code applies to a re-application. Some building departments treat production-home plan review as the permit application (CALBO).

rules.title: Permit expiration and code lock-in: 12 months / 180 days
rules.plain_english: Under state law (H&S 18938.6, AB 2913) a building permit remains valid if work starts within 12 months after it is issued, unless the work is abandoned; the building official may grant written extensions of up to 180 days each on a written request showing justifiable cause. If work does not start within 12 months or is abandoned, the permit expires and the code edition in effect at application is lost. Locally adopted CBC/CRC Chapter 1 Section 105.5 adds a 180-day suspension/abandonment rule once work has started; check the local ordinance.

parameters.extension_request: written request by permittee showing justifiable cause; building official may grant one or more extensions in writing (H&S 18938.6)
parameters.code_edition_lock_lost_if: work not commenced within 12 months or abandoned

rules.applies_to: All building permits
rules.citation: Health & Safety Code 18938.5(b)(2)(B), 18938.6 (AB 2913, Stats. 2018 ch. 655); CBC (Part 2) Chapter 1 Div. II Sec. 105.5; CRC R105.5
rules.quote: Every permit shall remain valid for purposes of this part if the work on the site authorized by that permit is commenced within 12 months after its issuance, unless the permittee has abandoned the work authorized by the permit.
rules.notes: Statute text seen only through WebSearch excerpts of the DGS "California Building Standards Law" compilation (eff. 2026-01-01) and leginfo; dgs.ca.gov and leginfo cannot be fetched directly. H&S 18938.6(b): "A permittee may request an extension of a permit. The building official may grant, in writing, one or more extensions of time for periods of not more than 180 days per extension. The permittee shall request an extension pursuant to this subdivision in writing and demonstrate justifiable cause for the extension." BSC IB 19-03: AB 2913 "amended HSC Section 18938.5 (b)(2)(B) by changing the exception relative to the permit expiration time period from 180 days to 12 months" and DGS says HSC 18938.5/18938.6 take precedence over the administrative building standards on permit expiration. When work counts as "commenced" is not defined in these excerpts; local amendments still govern suspension/abandonment after start (e.g., 180 days between approved inspections).
rules.correction: 12-month figure confirmed, but the rule misstated the structure. Under H&S 18938.6 (added by AB 2913, eff. 2019-01-01), a permit stays valid if work is commenced within 12 months after issuance unless abandoned, and the building official may grant written extensions of up to 180 days each on a written request showing justifiable cause; under 18938.5(b)(2)(B) the code-edition lock-in is lost if work does not commence within 12 months of the permit date or is abandoned. DGS states that H&S 18938.5 and 18938.6 take precedence over the administrative building standards on permit expiration, so a locally adopted CBC 105.5 cannot impose a 180-day commencement period; the 180-day figure is the CBC 105.5 suspension/abandonment-after-start period and the statutory extension length. Parameters, plain_english and citation updated; effective date 2019-01-01 confirmed.

rules.title: Permit application abandoned after 180 days
rules.plain_english: A permit application that is not pursued in good faith or issued is deemed abandoned 180 days after it was filed (building official may grant extensions). Track plan-check corrections so the application does not lapse.

parameters.extension: building official may extend for justifiable cause (local)

rules.quote: An application for a permit for any proposed work shall be deemed to have been abandoned 180 days after the date of filing.
rules.notes: Quote from a city handout reproducing the model code text; section number 105.3.2 is from model-code knowledge, not read. Local amendments vary.
rules.correction: 2025 CBC Section 105.3.2 text was not visible. Model IBC 2021/2024 105.3.2 text matches the quote (180 days after filing unless pursued in good faith or permit issued); IBC 2021 allows extensions of up to 90 days each, IBC 2024 up to 180 days - the 2025 CBC extension length is unconfirmed.

rules.title: Common work exempt from a building permit
rules.plain_english: A building permit is required to construct, alter, repair, move, demolish or change occupancy of a building, but the code exempts minor work such as a one-story detached shed or playhouse up to 120 sq ft, fences up to 7 ft, and retaining walls up to 4 ft (measured bottom of footing to top of wall, not supporting a surcharge). Exempt work still has to meet code, and electrical/plumbing/mechanical work may still need its own permit.

parameters.retaining_wall_measurement: bottom of footing to top of wall
retaining_wall_exemption_void_if: impounds Class I, II or IIIA liquids
local_variations: some cities use 6 ft fence limit
some add total-height limits for sheds (e.g., 12-16 ft)

rules.applies_to: Owners and contractors deciding whether a permit is needed
rules.quote: One-story detached accessory structures, used as tool and storage sheds, playhouses, and similar uses, provided the floor area does not exceed 120 square feet
rules.notes: Thresholds from city handouts for the 2025 CBC/CRC (search excerpts), not the official Title 24 text. Many jurisdictions amend Section 105.2 (Atascadero and Fullerton use 6 ft fences). Always confirm with the local building department. The general rule that a permit is required for construct/alter/repair/move/demolish/change occupancy is model-code text not read here. [Verification 2026-11-25: corrected against official text - see verification.correction; earlier caveats in these notes are superseded where they conflict.]
rules.correction: 120 sq ft one-story shed, 7 ft fence and 4 ft retaining wall figures confirmed for the 2025 CBC, but the exemption conditions were incomplete: the fence exemption excludes swimming pool barriers, and the retaining-wall exemption is void if the wall supports a surcharge OR impounds Class I, II or IIIA liquids. Parameters updated. CRC R105.2 2025 text not checked.

rules.title: Permit applicant must sign license (or exemption) statement
rules.plain_english: Any city or county that requires a building permit must make the applicant sign a statement giving the contractor license number and stating it is in full force, or stating the basis for any exemption. A false or missing statement carries a civil penalty of up to $500.

statement_contents: licensed under Contractors State License Law
license is in full force and effect
parameters.timing: condition precedent to permit issuance

rules.applies_to: Every building permit applicant (contractor or owner-builder) for construction, alteration, improvement, demolition or repair
rules.source: PDF page 259-260 of the 2026 CSLB Law Book
rules.quote: giving the number of the license and stating that it is in full force and effect, or, if the applicant is exempt from the provisions of this chapter, the basis for the alleged exemption. Any violation of this section by any applicant for a permit shall be subject to a civil penalty of not more than five hundred dollars ($500).
rules.notes: Statute text starts on PDF p. 259 ("Each county or city which requires the issuance of a permit as a condition precedent to the construction, alteration, improvement, demolition or repair of any building or structure shall also require that each applicant for such a permit file ... a statement which he has prepared and") and continues on p. 260.

rules.title: Building department verifies license at permit issuance
rules.plain_english: Building departments are asked to check on the CSLB website that the license number used to pull a permit is valid and in good standing, and that the person signing is the licensee or an authorized agent. Keep license status current and have agent authorization on file before sending staff to pull permits.

parameters.owner_builder_permits: owner-builder verification required; CSLB owner-builder flyer distributed with every owner-builder permit

rules.applies_to: Contractors and agents pulling permits; building departments
rules.quote: As a condition of permit issuance, use the CSLB Web site (www.cslb.ca.gov) to verify that the contractor’s license number being used to pull the permit is valid and in good standing.
rules.notes: Guideline (cooperative CALBO/CSLB agreement), not a statute. The guideline also says owner-builder permits need verification "in accordance with Health and Safety Code Sections 19830, 19831 and 19832"; per search excerpts those sections were repealed by AB 2335 (2008) and the owner-builder notice requirement now sits in H&S 19825 - verify.

rules.title: Cities/counties may require plan approval before construction
rules.plain_english: The contractor license law does not limit a city or county from running its own permit and inspection system or from requiring plans and specifications to be submitted and approved before construction starts. Local building departments can also refer code-violating licensees to CSLB.

parameters.plan_approval_before_construction: may be required by local agency

rules.applies_to: All contractors working under local permits
rules.source: PDF page 260 of the 2026 CSLB Law Book
rules.quote: Nothing in this chapter shall limit the power of a city or county to adopt any system of permits requiring submission to and approval by the city or county of plans and specifications for an installation prior to the commencement of construction of the installation.

rules.title: Local business tax compliance may be required before permit
rules.plain_english: A city or county may require a contractor to prove it is current on local business tax before issuing any permit, and may deny the permit if it is not. Store each jurisdiction's business tax certificate with the permit packet.

parameters.document: local business tax certificate / proof of compliance
parameters.tax_cap: may not exceed license tax/fee authorized by Gov Code 37101 or B&P 16000

rules.applies_to: Licensed contractors applying for city/county permits
rules.source: PDF page 225 of the 2026 CSLB Law Book
rules.quote: Nothing in this code shall be interpreted to prohibit cities, counties, and cities and counties from requiring contractors to show proof that they are in compliance with local business tax requirements of the entity prior to issuing any city, county, or city and county permit.

rules.title: $1,000 minor-work exemption is lost if a permit is required
rules.plain_english: The license exemption for jobs under $1,000 (labor, materials and all other items) applies only if the work does not require a building permit. Any job needing a permit requires a licensed contractor, regardless of price, and jobs cannot be split into pieces under $1,000 to evade the law.
rules.applies_to: Handyman-scale work; any person bidding small jobs
rules.source: PDF page 268 of the 2026 CSLB Law Book
rules.quote: (a) This chapter does not apply to a work or operation on one undertaking or project by one or more contracts if the aggregate contract price for labor, materials, and all other items is less than one thousand dollars ($1,000), that work or operation being considered of casual, minor, or inconsequential nature, and the work or operation does not require a building permit.
rules.notes: CSLB owner-builder pamphlet (13P-060/1025) adds: "Note: Any project needing a permit or workers requires a licensed contractor."

rules.title: Work without a permit is presumed a willful violation
rules.plain_english: CSLB must discipline a license for willful and deliberate violation of state or local building-permit laws, and construction done without a permit is presumed willful. The only carve-out is equipment repair/maintenance/adjustment under $500 in labor or materials, or replacing a mechanical part with an identical part.

parameters.presumption: construction without permit = willful and deliberate (rebuttable)

rules.applies_to: All CSLB licensees
rules.source: PDF page 334 of the 2026 CSLB Law Book
rules.quote: For the purpose of this section, there shall be a rebuttable presumption affecting the burden of proof that construction performed without a permit is a willful and deliberate violation.
rules.notes: Same page: discipline applies where the licensee "has willfully and deliberately violated any state or local law relating to the issuance of building permits, other than failure to obtain a county or city permit for repair, maintenance, and adjustment of equipment where such repair, maintenance, or adjustment is valued at less than five hundred dollars ($500) for labor or materials".

rules.title: Violating building or permit laws is cause for discipline
rules.plain_english: Willfully disregarding state or local building laws, including permit-issuance laws and the 811 dig law, is grounds for CSLB disciplinary action.

causes: building laws of state or political subdivision
any state or local law relating to issuance of building permits (7110(h))
Gov Code 4216 et seq. excavation notification (7110(f))

rules.applies_to: All CSLB licensees
rules.source: PDF page 351 of the 2026 CSLB Law Book
rules.quote: Willful or deliberate disregard and violation of the building laws of the state, or of any political subdivision thereof, or of any of the following references to or provisions of law, constitutes a cause for disciplinary action against a licensee:
rules.notes: Subdivision (h) reads "(h) Any state or local law relating to the issuance of building permits." Amended by AB 1747 (Stats 2022 ch 757) effective Jan 1, 2023.

rules.title: Penalty range for failing to obtain permits
rules.plain_english: CSLB's disciplinary guidelines for failure to obtain building permits range from a stayed 60-day suspension with 1 year of probation up to license revocation, and probation may require submitting copies of building permits to the Registrar on demand.

possible_terms: actual suspension of 5 days or more
submit copies of building permits on demand during probation
retake trade exam if not taken within past 5 years

rules.applies_to: CSLB licensees found in violation of B&P 7090
rules.citation: Cal. Code Regs. tit. 16, 871 (CSLB Disciplinary Guidelines), item 7090
rules.source: PDF page 510 of the 2026 CSLB Law Book
rules.quote: Submit copies of building permits to the Registrar upon demand for projects undertaken during the probation period.
rules.notes: Heading on same page: "7090. Failure to Obtain Building Permits Minimum Penalty: 60 day suspension, stayed, 1 year probation Maximum Penalty: Revocation". Guideline citation 16 CCR 871 from general knowledge (the law book chapter 9 hosts the guidelines) - not verified on this page.

rules.title: Home improvement contract should identify permits and who pays
rules.plain_english: CSLB lists failure to identify the required building permits, or who is paying for them, as a common home improvement contract problem. Contract templates should list each required permit and state whether the contractor or owner obtains and pays for it.
rules.applies_to: Home improvement contracts (residential, including ADUs)
rules.citation: CSLB Law Book Section II guidance (Common Problems with Home Improvement Contracts)
rules.source: PDF page 36 of the 2026 CSLB Law Book
rules.quote: Failure to identify required building permits or indicate who is paying for them
rules.notes: CSLB guidance, not a specific statutory clause. CSLB ADU Fast Facts also warns owners to confirm permit costs with the building department before paying a contractor for "plans" or "permits".

rules.title: Loan-contingent HIC: only permit work before loan is final
rules.plain_english: When a home improvement contract depends on a loan that the contractor arranges or refers, the contractor may not deliver materials or do any work, other than getting building permits and similar non-lienable preliminary services, until the loan is approved, accepted and past its rescission period. Violating this makes the contract unenforceable.

allowed_before_loan_final: similar services preliminary to commencement for which no mechanics lien can be claimed
conditions: third party agrees to make loan
buyer accepts loan
TILA/Reg Z rescission period expires without rescission
parameters.consequence: contract unenforceable; contractor must return all money/property

rules.applies_to: Home improvement contractors whose contract is loan-contingent or who arrange/refer financing
rules.source: PDF page 424 of the 2026 CSLB Law Book
rules.quote: (1) Deliver any property or perform any services other than obtaining building permits or other similar services preliminary to the commencement of the home improvement for which no mechanic’s lien can be claimed.
rules.notes: Subdivision (b): "Until the requirements of paragraphs (1), (2), and (3) of subdivision (a) are satisfied, it shall be unlawful for the contractor to do any of the following:"

rules.title: Workers' comp declaration required on every permit
rules.plain_english: Before a city or county issues a permit for construction, alteration, improvement, demolition or repair, the applicant must sign, under penalty of perjury, a workers' compensation declaration: a certificate of consent to self-insure, or the insurance carrier and policy number, or a statement that no employees will be used. A permit cannot be issued without it.

options: certificate of consent to self-insure (Labor Code 3700)
exemption: no employees subject to WC

rules.applies_to: All building permit applicants
rules.notes: Content from search excerpts of code-mirror sites and city permit forms; leginfo blocked. AB 2335 (2008, eff. 1/1/2009) rewrote 19825 and folded the former owner-builder notice (old 19830-19832) into it. Lawbook only cross-references "Health and Safety Code Section 19825, Declaration of Worker’s Compensation Required on Building Permits" (appendix removed in 2026 edition).

rules.title: Owner-builder permit responsibilities and limits
rules.plain_english: An owner who signs the permit as owner-builder takes full responsibility for the project: pulling permits, requesting inspections, correcting failed work, paying workers and suppliers, and possibly acting as an employer. Home-improvement owner-builders must have lived in the home 12 months before completion and can use the exemption on no more than two structures in three years; new single-family owner-builders may sell no more than four structures per year unless a B contractor does the work.

parameters.sales_limit_waived_if: owner contracts with General Building (B) contractor
responsibilities: ensure workers and suppliers are paid

rules.applies_to: Property owners pulling owner-builder permits; contractors asked to work "under the owner's permit"
rules.quote: When you sign a building permit application as an owner-builder, you assume full responsibility for all phases of your project and its integrity. You may be considered an employer if you hire unlicensed contractors to do the work.
rules.notes: Owner-builder licensing exemption itself (B&P 7044) is in the lawbook PDF pp. 264-265; covered in more depth by licensing research. Pamphlet: consultants who bid or supervise hiring subcontractors must be licensed.

rules.title: Smoke and CO alarms required when residential permit work exceeds $1,000
rules.plain_english: When a permit is issued for an addition, alteration or repair to a dwelling and the work is valued over $1,000, smoke alarms and carbon monoxide alarms must be installed in the existing dwelling before final. Hard-wiring/interconnection is generally required only where finishes are removed.

devices: carbon monoxide alarms (if fuel-burning appliance or attached garage)
parameters.hardwire_interconnect_required_if: wall/ceiling finishes removed exposing structure (local practice)

rules.applies_to: Residential (R-3/one- and two-family and dwelling units) alteration, repair and addition permits
rules.citation: CRC R314.2.2, R315.2.2 (2025 numbering not verified); CBC 907.2.11.5/915; H&S 17926
rules.quote: Per California state law effective January 1, 2011, when building permits are issued for additions, alterations or repairs to residential buildings and the value of the work exceeds $1,000
rules.notes: Only city handouts read (search excerpts). Exact 2025 CRC section numbers for the retrofit trigger not verified (older handouts cite R314.6/R315.2). CO alarm trigger conditions (fuel-burning appliance, attached garage) from general code knowledge - verify.
rules.correction: Smoke-alarm $1,000 trigger traced to H&S 13113.7 (permits for alterations, repairs or additions exceeding $1,000; permit issuer may not sign off until alarms are SFM-listed) via a leginfo bill digest only; 2022 CRC R314.2.2 text shows the permit trigger with no dollar figure. The CO-alarm $1,000 trigger and 2025 CRC numbering were not seen. FLAG: add H&S 13113.7 to the citation once confirmed.

rules.title: Replace noncompliant plumbing fixtures on pre-1994 buildings
rules.plain_english: For buildings built on or before January 1, 1994, a permit for an addition, alteration or improvement triggers replacement of noncompliant (high-flow) plumbing fixtures with water-conserving fixtures before final approval. Single-family: all noncompliant fixtures in the house. Multifamily/commercial: fixtures in the altered area if permit valuation exceeds $150,000, and all fixtures in any altered room.

parameters.multifamily_commercial_scope: fixtures serving altered area; all fixtures in any altered room
parameters.timing: before final permit approval or certificate of occupancy

rules.applies_to: Permitted additions/alterations to residential and commercial buildings built on or before Jan 1, 1994
rules.quote: the permit applicant shall replace all noncompliant plumbing fixtures with water-conserving plumbing fixtures
rules.notes: From search excerpts of city summaries and code-mirror pages. Effective date 2014-01-01 for the permit trigger is from general knowledge of SB 407, not verified. Noncompliant fixture thresholds (toilets >1.6 gpf, urinals >1.0 gpf, showerheads >2.5 gpm, faucets >2.2 gpm) are from general knowledge and omitted from parameters.
rules.correction: Pre-1994 scope, single-family "replace all noncompliant plumbing fixtures" as a condition of final permit approval, and the multifamily/commercial $150,000 estimated-construction-cost trigger (fixtures serving the specific area of the improvement) matched leginfo bill text, but only in bill texts proposing amendments; the current codified wording, the 2014 operative date and the "all fixtures in any altered room" rule were not seen.

rules.title: New/remodeled residential pool: 2 of 7 drowning-prevention features
rules.plain_english: When a building permit is issued for a new pool or spa, or remodel of an existing one, at a private single-family home, it must have at least two of the seven listed drowning-prevention safety features, which the building official checks at final inspection.

example_features: enclosure per H&S 115923 isolating pool from home
removable mesh fencing with self-closing/latching gate
exit alarms on home doors to pool
self-closing, self-latching device on doors to pool
not_counted: exit alarm + self-closing latch on the same door counted as two

rules.applies_to: Pool/spa contractors and owners (private single-family homes)
rules.citation: Health & Safety Code 115922 (Swimming Pool Safety Act, 115920-115929)
rules.quote: spa at a private single-family home, the respective swimming pool or spa shall be equipped with at least two of the following seven drowning prevention safety features
rules.notes: From search excerpts only; full feature wording not read. Lawbook cross-references H&S 115920-115925 (appendix removed) and B&P 7195 requires home inspectors to report which of the 7 features exist (PDF p. 445).
rules.correction: None. Core rule (2 of 7, single-family, building permit trigger, 2018) confirmed. NOT confirmed: the "not_counted" combinations come from SB 552 (2023-24), whose enactment was not shown; AB 1237 (2025-26) would extend coverage to condominium units and its status is unknown.

rules.title: Required inspection sequence; do not cover work before approval
rules.plain_english: The permit holder must call for each required inspection and keep work exposed until it is approved. Typical residential sequence: foundation/footing (after excavation and rebar, before concrete), under-floor/slab, rough plumbing-mechanical-electrical, frame, lath/gypsum board, weather-exposed waterproofing, any special inspections, and final.
rules.applies_to: All permitted residential (CRC) and building (CBC) projects
rules.notes: Third-party code summaries only; official 2025 CRC text not read. Exact California sub-numbering (e.g., R109.1.4 frame, R109.1.6 final per a San Jose handbook) and the order of rough-ins vs. frame vary by jurisdiction. Energy (HERS) and CALGreen verifications are also needed before final.

rules.title: Statement of special inspections required for permit
rules.plain_english: Where special inspections are required (e.g., structural concrete, steel, masonry, high-strength bolting, deep foundations), the applicant must submit a statement of special inspections, prepared by the registered design professional, as a condition of permit issuance. The 2025 CBC removed the exception allowing a non-licensed person to prepare it.

parameters.timing: condition for permit issuance
parameters.prepared_by: registered design professional in responsible charge

rules.applies_to: Projects designed under the CBC requiring special inspections (most commercial/multifamily structural work)
rules.quote: The applicant shall submit a statement of special inspections in accordance with Section 107.1 as a condition for permit issuance. This statement shall be in accordance with Section 1704.3.
rules.notes: Quote from a third-party CBC summary. DGS 2025 change summary says the state does not permit the exception allowing non-licensed individuals to prepare the statement - confirm whether that applies to Chapter 17 (local) or only 17A (DSA/state agencies). "Owner hires special inspector" from model-code knowledge (CBC 1704.2), not read.

rules.title: Special inspection reports and final report before occupancy
rules.plain_english: Special inspectors/approved agencies keep records and send interim reports to the building official and the registered design professional; discrepancies must be reported and corrected. A final report documenting required special inspections and correction of discrepancies must be submitted before the certificate of occupancy (or final) is issued.

interim_reports_to: registered design professional in responsible charge
parameters.final_report_timing: before certificate of occupancy / final approval (or as agreed before work starts)
final_report_contents: documentation of required special inspections and tests

rules.applies_to: Projects with special inspections
rules.notes: From local agency forms and summaries; one summary says final report timing is agreed upon before work starts by the owner or owner's agent. Not read from official code text.

rules.title: Final inspection within 10 business days for small housing (AB 1308)
rules.plain_english: For qualifying new residential construction (buildings not exceeding 10 total units, including additions creating new units), the local building department must perform the final inspection within 10 business days after the builder gives notice the work is complete. Missing the deadline is a Housing Accountability Act violation, and the builder may use a qualified third-party inspector.

parameters.trigger: notice of completion / inspection request for final
remedy_if_missed: builder may retain qualified third-party inspector

rules.applies_to: Builders of new homes, ADU/duplex/small multifamily projects up to 10 units
rules.quote: Within 10 business days of receiving a notice of the completion of the permitted work authorized by a building permit issued for a project subject to this section, the building department of every city or county shall conduct an inspection of the permitted work.
rules.notes: From law-firm and CALBO summaries; statute text not read. Some summaries limit scope to 100-percent residential buildings and mention a 40-ft height limit; confirm scope, height and whether it covers only final or all inspections. [Verification 2026-11-25: corrected against official text - see verification.correction; earlier caveats in these notes are superseded where they conflict.]
rules.correction: Deadline confirmed: within 10 business days of receiving notice of completion of permitted work, the building department shall inspect; failure is a disapproval/violation under the Housing Accountability Act. The verbatim_quote was a law-firm paraphrase and was replaced with the statute text. NOT confirmed: the 10-unit scope limit and the third-party-inspector remedy (not in the excerpts); the statute says "an inspection of the permitted work", not only a final inspection.

rules.title: Private plan check option when city review is slow (AB 253)
rules.plain_english: Under the California Residential Private Permitting Review Act (AB 253), once a residential permit application is complete the city or county must give an estimated review timeframe. If that estimate exceeds 30 business days, or the agency has not determined compliance within 30 days, the applicant may hire a private professional provider (licensed engineer or architect with a residential plans examiner certification). The agency then has 10 business days to review the provider's report and either issue the permit or give written notice of noncompliance; if it does neither, the plans are deemed compliant. In effect until January 1, 2036.

parameters.provider_qualification: licensed professional engineer or architect with current residential plans examiner certification (e.g., ICC)
parameters.scope: residential projects (unit/height limits per summaries - not confirmed)

rules.applies_to: Residential permit applicants (small projects)
rules.notes: Summaries say AB 253 was an urgency measure effective immediately on signature (Oct 10, 2025). Whether "30 days" is calendar or business days, the code section number, and the unit/height limits were not verified against bill text. [Verification 2026-11-25: corrected against official text - see verification.correction; earlier caveats in these notes are superseded where they conflict.]
rules.correction: Citation was generic: AB 253 adds H&S 17960.3 and amends 17951 and 17960.1. Trigger is broader and the 30-day figure is mixed: the applicant may use a private professional provider if the agency's estimated compliance timeframe exceeds 30 business days or if no determination is made within 30 days of the application being deemed complete. After receiving the provider's report the agency has 10 business days to issue the permit or give written notice of noncompliance; if it does neither, the plans are deemed compliant. Provider = licensed engineer or architect with a current residential plans examiner certification (e.g., ICC). Operative until January 1, 2036. Unit/height scope not confirmed.

rules.title: Post-entitlement housing permit review deadlines (AB 2234)
rules.plain_english: For housing development projects, a local agency must decide whether a post-entitlement permit application (building, demolition, grading, minor off-site improvements) is complete and give written notice within 15 business days, then approve it or return a full set of comments within 30 business days of completeness (25 units or fewer) or 60 business days (26 or more units). Appeal decisions are due within 60/90 business days under existing law; AB 1621 (2026) shortens these to 30/45 business days.

parameters.tolling: while another public agency must review; notice to applicant within 3 business days

rules.applies_to: Housing development projects with entitlements
rules.quote: A local agency or state agency shall determine whether an application for a postentitlement phase permit is complete and provide written notice of this determination to the applicant not later than 15 business days after the local agency or state agency received the application.
rules.notes: Approval-deadline numbers and the 25-unit split were NOT confirmed in any source read; included only as a flagged lead. Do not compute deadlines from this rule without reading Gov Code 65913.3. [Verification 2026-11-25: corrected against official text - see verification.correction; earlier caveats in these notes are superseded where they conflict.]
rules.correction: Completeness determination is 15 BUSINESS days after receipt (written notice). Approval deadlines are now confirmed: 30 business days after the application is deemed complete for projects of 25 units or fewer, 60 business days for 26 or more units (full set of comments or approved permit). Added appeal deadlines: final written appeal determination within 60/90 business days under existing law, which AB 1621 (approved 2026-09-29) cuts to 30/45 business days (assumed operative 2027-01-01 - not confirmed). Timelines are tolled while another agency reviews (notice within 3 business days). AB 1114 scope claim not checked.

rules.title: 2025 Energy Code enforced from Jan 1, 2026
rules.plain_english: The 2025 Building Energy Efficiency Standards (Title 24 Part 6) apply to permit applications submitted on or after January 1, 2026; compliance forms carry the 2025 version and must match the code year of the permit application.
rules.applies_to: All newly constructed buildings, additions and alterations within Part 6 scope
rules.quote: Statewide enforcement of the 2025 Energy Code begins January 1, 2026.
rules.notes: energy.ca.gov blocked; quote from search excerpt. Energy Commission does not enforce directly; local building departments (AHJ) do. Verification 2026-11-25: CEC pages also require approved 2025 compliance software for permit applications on or after 2026-01-01; CEC software transition dates for later CBECC versions conflict between pages (2026-01-07 vs 2026-12-18) - check the software page.

rules.title: CF1R Certificate of Compliance at plan check (registered when HERS required)
rules.plain_english: The energy compliance documentation submitted with plans is the Certificate of Compliance (CF1R residential; NRCC nonresidential). For low-rise/single-family residential work that requires HERS field verification, the CF1R given to the building department must be a copy registered with an approved HERS data registry.

parameters.must_be_registered_if: HERS field verification or diagnostic testing required

rules.applies_to: Residential and nonresidential projects within Energy Code scope (new, additions, many alterations incl. HVAC changeouts)
rules.citation: Title 24 Part 6 Sec. 10-103(a)(1); Reference Joint Appendix JA7; CEC-400-2025-004 Data Registry Requirements Manual
rules.notes: Section 10-103 numbering from general knowledge. Search excerpt: the CF1R sent to the enforcement agency must be a copy registered with an approved HERS data registry for buildings needing field verification. 2025 forms reference an "ECC Registry" (HERS program renamed Energy Code Compliance) - naming not fully verified.

rules.title: CF2R Certificate of Installation by installer
rules.plain_english: The installing contractor completes and signs a Certificate of Installation (CF2R residential; NRCI nonresidential) for each energy feature installed. When HERS verification is required, the CF2R data must be submitted electronically to the same approved data registry, and the signed CF2R must be available at the job site for the building inspector.
rules.applies_to: Installing contractors (HVAC, insulation, windows, water heating, lighting, solar) on permitted work
rules.notes: From energycodeace (CEC-sponsored but third-party) excerpts; section number and job-site availability from general knowledge, not read.

rules.title: CF3R Certificate of Verification by HERS rater before final
rules.plain_english: Where the CF1R calls for field verification (e.g., duct leakage, fan efficacy, airflow, refrigerant charge, ventilation/IAQ, quality insulation), an independent certified HERS rater tests the installation and uploads a CF3R Certificate of Verification to the same registry used for the CF1R and CF2R. The building department should not final the permit until registered CF3Rs are received.
rules.applies_to: Residential new construction, additions and alterations with HERS-verified measures
rules.citation: Title 24 Part 6 Sec. 10-103(a)(5); Reference Residential Appendix RA2/RA3
rules.notes: "Not final until CF3R received" is standard enforcement practice from general knowledge; not read in official text this session.

rules.title: Solar PV required on new single-family homes
rules.plain_english: All newly constructed single-family residential buildings must have a solar PV system sized per Equation 150.1-C (five exceptions apply). If a battery energy storage system is installed with it, the required PV size may be reduced by 25 percent.
rules.applies_to: Builders of new single-family homes (including detached ADUs - check exceptions)
rules.quote: If installed in conjunction with a battery energy storage system (BESS), the solar PV size per Equation 150.1-C may be reduced by 25 percent.
rules.notes: CEC summary documents read only via search excerpt. The five exceptions (e.g., limited solar access, small roof area) not read. CEC FAQ addresses PV for newly constructed detached ADUs; not verified. Verification 2026-11-25: CEC says the 25% reduction applies only if the BESS meets JA12 with a minimum 7.5 kWh cycling capacity.
rules.correction: None. Caveat added to notes: the CEC page conditions the 25% reduction on a JA12-compliant battery (minimum 7.5 kWh cycling capacity). The count of five exceptions was not checked.

rules.title: Heat pumps are the 2025 prescriptive baseline for homes
rules.plain_english: The 2025 Energy Code uses heat pumps for both space heating and water heating as the prescriptive baseline for new single-family homes. Gas equipment is still allowed through the performance path but must make up the difference, and gas appliances trigger electric-ready requirements.

parameters.electric_ready_triggered_by: installation of certain natural gas/propane appliances

rules.applies_to: New single-family residential construction
rules.quote: For homes, use heat pumps for both space heating and water heating, expanding on the single heat pump baselines in the 2022 update.
rules.notes: Gas tankless water heaters removed from prescriptive options for single-family additions (150.2(a)1D) per search excerpt.

rules.title: Battery-storage-ready for new homes with >125 A service
rules.plain_english: Newly constructed one- or two-family dwellings with electrical service over 125 amps must be battery energy storage system (BESS) ready unless a battery is actually installed. Solar-ready rules apply to new single-family homes in subdivisions of 10 or more units.
rules.applies_to: New single-family one- and two-dwelling units
rules.notes: Section number 150.0(s) from general knowledge; requirement wording from CEC summary excerpts only.
