rules.quote: Wilful failure or refusal without legal excuse on the part of a licensee as a contractor to prosecute a construction project or operation with reasonable diligence causing material injury to another constitutes a cause for disciplinary action.
rules.notes: Daily logs and an updated schedule documenting delays and their causes are the practical defense.
rules.correction: None.

rules.title: Discipline for abandoning a project without legal excuse
rules.plain_english: Walking off a construction project without a legal excuse is grounds for CSLB discipline.

elements: abandonment
without legal excuse

rules.applies_to: All licensees
rules.source: PDF page 348 of the 2026 CSLB Law Book
rules.quote: Abandonment without legal excuse of any construction project or operation engaged in or undertaken by the licensee as a contractor constitutes a cause for disciplinary action.
rules.notes: Document stop-work reasons (e.g., nonpayment notices) in writing. Contract-rights exception on waiver forms preserves claims for 'rescission, abandonment, or breach of contract'.
rules.correction: None.

rules.title: Keep all project records at least 5 years after completion
rules.plain_english: Contractors must keep records of all contracts, documents, records, receipts and disbursements for every job and make them available to CSLB for at least five years after that project is completed. This covers change orders, pay apps, daily logs, RFIs, submittals and lien waivers.
rules.applies_to: All licensees
rules.source: PDF page 352 of the 2026 CSLB Law Book
rules.quote: (a) Failure to make and keep records showing all contracts, documents, records, receipts, and disbursements by a licensee of all of his or her transactions as a contractor, and failure to have those records available for inspection by the registrar or his or her duly authorized representative for a period of not less than five years after completion of any construction project
rules.notes: The 'practical_scope' list is an interpretation of 'all contracts, documents, records'. Longer retention is prudent given 10-year latent-defect exposure (CCP 337.15; B&P 7091(b)). Other laws impose their own periods (e.g., payroll 3-4 years; Cal/OSHA logs 5 years - see other research files).

rules.title: Daily log (daily report) contents
rules.plain_english: Keep a daily log for each job recording date, weather, crews and hours by trade/sub, work performed by location, equipment, deliveries, visitors and inspections, delays and their causes, safety incidents, instructions received, and photos. It is the main evidence for delay, change and defect disputes.

parameters.frequency: every working day (and non-working days with events)

rules.applies_to: All projects
rules.source: Industry practice; no official source fetched
rules.notes: Standard construction-management practice, not a legal requirement; not read from any primary legal text. CSLB Law Book (PDF page 70) generally advises: 'It is a good idea to document the progress of the project and keep your customer up to date.' Injuries recorded in the log may trigger Cal/OSHA/WC reporting deadlines covered in other research files.

rules.title: Request for Information (RFI) process
rules.plain_english: Use a numbered, logged RFI to ask the designer or owner to clarify conflicts or gaps in the plans and specs before doing the work; record the question, proposed solution, required-by date, response and whether it changes cost or time. If it does, issue a change order.

parameters.aging_metric: days_open = answered_date - sent_date (or today - sent_date if open)
parameters.if_cost_or_time_impact: convert to change order before performing changed work

rules.applies_to: All projects with plans/specs
rules.citation: Industry practice; B&P 7109(b) (no departure from plans without consent)
rules.source: Industry practice; no official source fetched
rules.notes: Standard construction-management practice, not a legal requirement; not read from any primary legal text. Response turnaround times are contractual (e.g., 'within X days' in the general conditions), not statutory in California private work.

rules.title: Submittals (shop drawings, product data, samples) process
rules.plain_english: Before ordering or installing specified items, send shop drawings, product data and samples through a logged submittal process for the design team's review; track required dates against the schedule's lead times and do not install until approved.
rules.applies_to: All projects with specifications
rules.citation: Industry practice; documents incorporated into HIC per B&P 7159(d)(12)
rules.source: Industry practice; no official source fetched
rules.notes: Standard construction-management practice, not a legal requirement; not read from any primary legal text. Substitutions that change significant materials/equipment described in an HIC (B&P 7159(d)(7)) should be documented by change order.

rules.title: HIC: list every document incorporated into the contract
rules.plain_english: If plans, specifications, bids or other documents are part of a home improvement contract, the contract must include the heading 'List of Documents to be Incorporated into the Contract' followed by the list.

parameters.heading: List of Documents to be Incorporated into the Contract
parameters.condition: if applicable
typical_documents: plans/drawings with dates and revision numbers

rules.applies_to: Home improvement contracts
rules.source: PDF page 401 of the 2026 CSLB Law Book
rules.quote: (12) If applicable, the heading: “List of Documents to be Incorporated into the Contract,” followed by the list of documents incorporated into the contract.
rules.notes: 'typical_documents' is practice. B&P 7164(c) similarly requires SFD contracts to 'clearly describe any other document which is to be incorporated into the contract.'
rules.correction: None.

rules.title: HIC: describe the project and significant materials/equipment
rules.plain_english: The contract must have the heading 'Description of the Project and Description of the Significant Materials to be Used and Equipment to be Installed' with an actual description; swimming pools also need a plan and scale drawing with dimensions and specs.

parameters.heading: Description of the Project and Description of the Significant Materials to be Used and Equipment to be Installed
parameters.swimming_pool_extra: plan and scale drawing showing shape, size, dimensions, construction and equipment specifications

rules.applies_to: Home improvement contracts
rules.source: PDF page 400 of the 2026 CSLB Law Book
rules.quote: (7) The heading: “Description of the Project and Description of the Significant Materials to be Used and Equipment to be Installed,” followed by a description of the project and a description of the significant materials to be used and equipment to be installed.
rules.notes: This scope description is the baseline for deciding whether later requests are 'extras' requiring a change order. CSLB lists 'Equipment to be used or installed is not detailed, and materials to be used not described specifically' as a common problem (Law Book PDF page 36).
rules.correction: None.

rules.title: CSLB checklist of HIC contract content (incl. permits and permissible delays)
rules.plain_english: CSLB tells contractors a home improvement contract should fully describe the work, materials and equipment, price, payment schedule, start and completion, permits and tests, permissible delays, extra work, required lien-release statements, and the owner's cancellation rights.

checklist: start and completion of work (dates and descriptions)
required release of mechanics' liens statements

rules.applies_to: Home improvement contracts
rules.citation: CSLB Law Book Ch. 2 summary of B&P 7159
rules.source: PDF page 35 of the 2026 CSLB Law Book
rules.quote: Contract must include full descriptions and information about the following: • Description of work • Description of materials and equipment • The contract price • Payment schedule • Start and completion of work (dates and descriptions) • Permits and tests • Permissible delays • Extra work
rules.notes: CSLB official summary, not statute text; 'permits and tests' and 'permissible delays' are not separately enumerated in the B&P 7159 text read on PDF pages 397-408, so treated as guidance (false). The list continues: 'Required release of mechanics' liens statements; Owner's applicable right to cancellation'.
rules.correction: None. This is a CSLB summary, not statute text, as the rule already says ("permits and tests" and "permissible delays" are not separate items in B&P 7159).

rules.title: Document progress and bill regularly
rules.plain_english: Keep the customer updated on progress in writing and invoice regularly; frequent billing reduces cash strain and keeps the customer informed.
rules.applies_to: All contractors
rules.source: PDF page 70 of the 2026 CSLB Law Book-71
rules.quote: It is a good idea to document the progress of the project and keep your customer up to date.
rules.notes: Quote is from the CSLB Law Book's non-binding business-management guidance chapter (official publication, but guidance, not law), so it is marked as a practice item. PDF page 71 continues: 'Closely allied with the communication of progress is frequent billing. By invoicing regularly, you will minimize your business's cash demands while keeping your customer informed.' On HIC jobs, billing frequency is still limited by work actually performed (B&P 7159.5(a)(5)).

rules.title: Punch lists and a pre-completion walk-through
rules.plain_english: Do frequent punch lists and a walk-through near the end of the job with the customer to list what remains, then fix deficiencies quickly.

parameters.timing: frequent during job + walk-through near end

rules.applies_to: All contractors
rules.source: PDF page 70 of the 2026 CSLB Law Book
rules.quote: Frequent “punch lists” are a good idea. A walk-through near the end of the job to determine the items that are left to be completed is recommended. Correct any deficiencies quickly.
rules.notes: Quote is from the CSLB Law Book's non-binding business-management guidance chapter (official publication, but guidance, not law), so it is marked as a practice item. Punch item fields are standard practice. Punch status should not be falsely certified as complete (B&P 7158).

rules.title: Using a false completion certificate is a misdemeanor ($500-$5,000)
rules.plain_english: Knowingly accepting and using a false completion certificate (or other proof the job is complete when it is not substantially complete) to assign or collect payment or obtain a loan is a misdemeanor punishable by a $500-$5,000 fine and/or 1 month to 1 year in county jail.

elements: accept/receive completion certificate or other evidence of completion
knowledge document is false and work not substantially completed
use in assignment/negotiation of right to payment or to obtain credit/loan

rules.applies_to: Any person (contractors, owners, lenders, salespersons) handling completion certificates
rules.source: PDF page 396 of the 2026 CSLB Law Book
rules.quote: shall be guilty of a misdemeanor and subject to a fine of not less than five hundred dollars ($500) nor more than five thousand dollars ($5,000), or to imprisonment in the county jail for a term of not less than one month nor more than one year, or both.
rules.notes: Closeout tool should require actual punch-list completion/inspection sign-off before generating any completion certificate or lender completion statement. Relevant to solar/financed HIC jobs where lenders pay on completion certificates.
rules.correction: None.

rules.title: Project closeout package
rules.plain_english: Before final payment, assemble: completed punch list signed off, final building inspection/permit final (and certificate of occupancy if applicable), final change order reconciliation and final pay app, conditional then unconditional final lien waivers from the GC and every sub and supplier, warranties and guarantees, O&M manuals, as-built drawings, attic stock and keys, and the notice of completion (owner records). Then release retention per the statutory deadlines.

checklist: final inspection / permit finaled (certificate of occupancy where applicable)
conditional waiver and release on final payment (Civ. Code 8136) from GC and each sub/supplier before final payment
unconditional waiver and release on final payment (Civ. Code 8138) after payment clears
written warranties (contractor and manufacturer), with start dates
recorded notice of completion (owner; Civ. Code 8182 per lien research)

rules.applies_to: GCs and owners at project completion
rules.citation: Industry practice; waiver forms per Civil Code 8132-8138; retention per Civil Code 8812 / PCC 7107
rules.source: Industry practice; legal items cross-referenced to other rules
rules.notes: Standard construction-management practice, not a legal requirement; not read from any primary legal text. Notice of completion recording deadlines and effects on lien periods are in web_lien-payment.json (noc-* rules). Warranty start dates matter for B&P 7091(e) (18 months after warranty expiration).

rules.title: Lien waivers must substantially follow the four statutory forms
rules.plain_english: A waiver and release of lien, stop payment notice and payment bond rights is effective only if it substantially follows one of the four statutory forms: conditional progress, unconditional progress, conditional final, unconditional final.
rules.applies_to: All claimants (GC, subs, suppliers, equipment lessors) and payers on private and public works
rules.quote: To be effective, the waiver and release forms must follow, substantially, one of the forms set forth in Civil Code sections 8132, 8134, 8136, and 8138.
rules.notes: Official CSLB page and the four CSLB form PDFs were read. B&P 7034(b) separately bars contractors from requiring lien waivers in violation of Civ. Code 8122 (see no-unlawful-lien-waiver-demands).

rules.title: Conditional waiver on progress payment - collect with every pay app
rules.plain_english: With each progress billing, get a Conditional Waiver and Release on Progress Payment from the GC and each sub/supplier being paid. It identifies claimant, customer, job, owner, a 'Through Date', and the check (maker, amount, payee), and only takes effect when the claimant is actually paid. It does not waive retentions, unpaid extras, earlier unpaid progress payments, or contract rights.

parameters.when: submitted with each progress pay application, before payment
exceptions_not_waived: extras for which claimant has not received payment
prior progress payments covered by conditional waivers but unpaid (dates and amounts listed)
contract rights incl. rescission, abandonment, breach, and compensation for work not covered by the payment
parameters.effective_on: claimant's receipt of payment from the financial institution on which the check is drawn
parameters.header_notice: NOTICE: THIS DOCUMENT WAIVES THE CLAIMANT'S LIEN, STOP PAYMENT NOTICE, AND PAYMENT BOND RIGHTS EFFECTIVE ON RECEIPT OF PAYMENT. A PERSON SHOULD NOT RELY ON THIS DOCUMENT UNLESS SATISFIED THAT THE CLAIMANT HAS RECEIVED PAYMENT.

rules.applies_to: All claimants and payers on progress payments
rules.quote: This document waives and releases lien, stop payment notice, and payment bond rights the claimant has for labor and service provided, and equipment and material delivered, to the customer on this job through the Through Date of this document.
rules.notes: Form text read from CSLB's PDF (dated 7/1/12). A generator should reproduce the statutory text verbatim; the field list above is the form's 'Identifying Information' and check fields.

rules.title: Unconditional progress waiver - only after payment actually received
rules.plain_english: After a progress payment clears, collect an Unconditional Waiver and Release on Progress Payment stating the amount received. Never sign or demand one before payment: it binds the claimant even if not paid.

parameters.when: after the progress payment has cleared (commonly collected with the next pay app)
exceptions_not_waived: extras for which claimant has not received payment
contract rights incl. rescission, abandonment, breach, and compensation for work not covered by the payment
parameters.header_notice: NOTICE TO CLAIMANT: THIS DOCUMENT WAIVES AND RELEASES LIEN, STOP PAYMENT NOTICE, AND PAYMENT BOND RIGHTS UNCONDITIONALLY AND STATES THAT YOU HAVE BEEN PAID FOR GIVING UP THOSE RIGHTS. THIS DOCUMENT IS ENFORCEABLE AGAINST YOU IF YOU SIGN IT, EVEN IF YOU HAVE NOT BEEN PAID. IF YOU HAVE NOT BEEN PAID, USE A CONDITIONAL WAIVER AND RELEASE FORM.

rules.applies_to: All claimants and payers
rules.quote: THIS DOCUMENT IS ENFORCEABLE AGAINST YOU IF YOU SIGN IT, EVEN IF YOU HAVE NOT BEEN PAID. IF YOU HAVE NOT BEEN PAID, USE A CONDITIONAL WAIVER AND RELEASE FORM.
rules.notes: CSLB consumer guidance (companion research) advises owners they may withhold the next payment until unconditional releases for the previous payment are received.

rules.title: Final waivers: conditional before final payment, unconditional after
rules.plain_english: For the final payment, collect a Conditional Waiver and Release on Final Payment (with check details) before paying, then an Unconditional Waiver and Release on Final Payment stating the claimant has been paid in full. The only exception on the final forms is a stated dollar amount of disputed claims for extras.

sequence: conditional final waiver (Civ. Code 8136) before final payment
unconditional final waiver (Civ. Code 8138) after payment clears
parameters.unconditional_final_statement: The claimant has been paid in full.
parameters.only_exception: Disputed claims for extras in the amount of: $

rules.applies_to: GC, every sub and supplier at closeout; owners/lenders releasing final payment and retention
rules.quote: This document does not affect any of the following: Disputed claims for extras in the amount of: $
rules.notes: Because final forms waive everything except listed disputed extras, a closeout tool should require the claimant to enter any open change-order claims before signing.

rules.title: Waivers release rights on change orders fully signed before the waiver date
rules.plain_english: Every statutory waiver form waives rights for work done under any written change order that was fully signed before the claimant signs the waiver, unless that change order is listed as an exception. Unpaid extras remain protected on progress waivers; on final waivers only the listed disputed-extras amount is preserved.

parameters.rule: rights under change orders fully executed before waiver signature date are waived unless listed as an exception
parameters.progress_waiver_preserves: extras for which the claimant has not received payment
parameters.final_waiver_preserves: only disputed claims for extras in the stated amount
parameters.check: for each CO with executed_date < waiver_signed_date and unpaid: confirm listed as exception or covered by 'extras not paid' exception (progress) / disputed-extras amount (final)

rules.applies_to: Anyone signing or collecting lien waivers on jobs with change orders
rules.quote: Rights based upon labor or service provided, or equipment or material delivered, pursuant to a written change order that has been fully executed by the parties prior to the date that this document is signed by the claimant, are waived and released by this document, unless listed as an Exception below.
rules.notes: Same sentence appears on all four CSLB form PDFs. Ties change-order log to waiver generation.

rules.title: Conditional waiver binds only on evidence of payment
rules.plain_english: A conditional waiver only becomes binding when there is evidence the claimant was paid: the claimant's endorsement on a single or joint check that the bank has paid, or the claimant's written acknowledgment of payment.

evidence_of_payment: claimant's endorsement on a single or joint check paid by the drawee bank
written acknowledgment of payment by claimant

rules.applies_to: Owners, GCs and lenders relying on conditional waivers
rules.quote: In the case of a conditional release, the release is only binding if there is evidence of payment to the claimant.
rules.notes: CSLB official page; continues 'Evidence of payment may be demonstrated by: The claimant's endorsement on a single check or a joint check that has been paid by the bank upon which it was drawn; or Written acknowledgment of payment given by the claimant.' Exact Civil Code subsection not verified.

rules.title: HIC: furnish unconditional lien releases for each paid portion (contract must say so)
rules.plain_english: A home improvement contract must state that after each satisfactory payment, and before any further payment, the contractor will furnish a full unconditional lien release for the paid portion; on request the contractor must obtain and deliver releases, and the owner may withhold further payments until it does.

parameters.trigger: each satisfactory payment for any portion of the work, before further payment
parameters.release_type: full and unconditional release (Civ. Code 8134/8138 form)
release_from: potential lien claimants for the paid portion (subs, suppliers)

rules.applies_to: Home improvement and swimming pool contracts
rules.source: PDF page 398 of the 2026 CSLB Law Book; PDF page 410 of the 2026 CSLB Law Book
rules.quote: (4) The contract shall include a statement that, upon satisfactory payment being made for any portion of the work performed, the contractor, prior to any further payment being made, shall furnish to the person contracting for the home improvement or swimming pool work a full and unconditional release from any potential lien claimant claim or mechanics lien
rules.notes: Duplicates hic-lien-release-on-payment / hic-contract-lien-release-clause in web_lien-payment.json; kept here because it drives per-payment waiver generation.
rules.correction: None. Note: the statute describes the release as one "from any potential lien claimant claim or mechanics lien authorized pursuant to Sections 8400 and 8404 of the Civil Code"; the "Civ. Code 8134/8138 form" in parameters is the rule's interpretation, not statute text. The contract statement (7159(c)(4)) is unconditional; the duty to obtain sub/supplier releases (7159.5(a)(6)) applies "if requested".

rules.title: Do not put void indemnity clauses in subcontracts or demand unlawful lien waivers
rules.plain_english: A licensed contractor may not include in a subcontract any clause that is void under Civil Code 2782 (construction indemnity limits), and may not require a sub, employee or supplier to waive lien rights in violation of Civil Code 8122 (no waivers except by the statutory forms).

parameters.prohibited_subcontract_clauses: provisions void or unenforceable under Civil Code 2782
parameters.prohibited_demand: waiver of lien rights in violation of Civil Code 8122

rules.applies_to: Licensed contractors drafting subcontracts and payment conditions
rules.source: PDF page 261 of the 2026 CSLB Law Book
rules.quote: (a) No contractor that is required to be licensed under this chapter shall insert in any contract, or be a party, with a subcontractor that is licensed under this chapter to any contract which contains, a provision, clause, covenant, or agreement which is void or unenforceable under Section 2782 of the Civil Code.
rules.notes: 7034(b): 'No contractor that is required to be licensed under this chapter shall require a waiver of lien rights from any subcontractor, employee, or supplier in violation of Section 8122 of the Civil Code.' The substance of Civil Code 2782/2782.05 (e.g., no indemnity for indemnitee's active negligence/sole negligence; residential and private-subcontract limits) and of 8122 was NOT read (leginfo blocked; not reproduced in the Law Book, which refers to an Appendix not included in the PDF).

rules.title: Required statement on all non-HIC prime contracts (CSLB 4-year/10-year complaint limits)
rules.plain_english: Every written contract where the licensee is the prime contractor (other than home improvement and service-and-repair contracts, which use a different CSLB notice) must include, in at least 10-point type, the statutory statement that CSLB complaints must be filed within 4 years for patent defects and 10 years for latent structural defects.

parameters.applies_when: licensee is prime contractor on a written contract
parameters.statement_text: Contractors are required by law to be licensed and regulated by the Contractors State License Board which has jurisdiction to investigate complaints against contractors if a complaint regarding a patent act or omission is filed within four years of the date of the alleged violation. A complaint regarding a latent act or omission pertaining to structural defects must be filed within 10 years of the date of the alleged violation. Any questions concerning a contractor may be referred to the Registrar, Contractors State License Board, P.O. Box 26000, Sacramento, CA 95826.
parameters.hic_alternative: B&P 7030(b) 'Information about the Contractors State License Board (CSLB)' notice in 12-point type

rules.applies_to: Licensed prime contractors (commercial, new construction, and other non-HIC contracts)
rules.source: PDF page 256 of the 2026 CSLB Law Book
rules.quote: “Contractors are required by law to be licensed and regulated by the Contractors State License Board which has jurisdiction to investigate complaints against contractors if a complaint regarding a patent act or omission is filed within four years of the date of the alleged violation.
rules.notes: Full statement text is in parameters.statement_text (read from PDF page 256). HIC version text is on PDF page 257 and in B&P 7159(e)(5).
rules.correction: None.

rules.title: CSLB complaint deadline for patent (visible) defects: 4 years
rules.plain_english: A complaint to CSLB about a patent (reasonably visible) act or omission must be filed within 4 years after it occurred; CSLB must file discipline within 4 years of the act or 18 months after the complaint, whichever is later.

parameters.trigger: date of the act or omission
parameters.disciplinary_filing_deadline: later of 4 years after act or 18 months after complaint filed
parameters.calc: complaint_deadline = act_date + 4 years; discipline_deadline = max(act_date + 4 years, complaint_date + 18 months)

rules.applies_to: Owners filing CSLB complaints; contractors tracking exposure
rules.source: PDF page 336 of the 2026 CSLB Law Book
rules.quote: (a) (1) A complaint against a licensee alleging commission of any patent acts or omissions that may be grounds for legal action shall be filed in writing with the registrar within four years after the act or omission alleged as the ground for the disciplinary action.
rules.notes: This is the CSLB administrative deadline, not the civil statute of limitations (see ccp-337-1-patent-defects-4-years).
rules.correction: None. Detail: the 4-year/18-month limit in 7091(a)(2) also governs a referral to CSLB arbitration under B&P 7085, not only the filing of a disciplinary action.

rules.title: CSLB complaint deadline for latent structural defects: 10 years
rules.plain_english: A CSLB complaint about a latent (not visible on reasonable inspection) structural defect must be filed within 10 years after the act or omission; discipline must be filed within 10 years or 18 months after the complaint, whichever is later.

parameters.scope: latent acts or omissions re structural defects (B&P 7109(a)); see 16 CCR 861.5
parameters.disciplinary_filing_deadline: later of 10 years after act or 18 months after complaint filed
parameters.latent_definition: act or omission not apparent by reasonable inspection

rules.applies_to: Owners filing CSLB complaints; contractors tracking exposure
rules.source: PDF page 336 of the 2026 CSLB Law Book-337
rules.quote: (b) (1) A complaint against a licensee alleging commission of any latent acts or omissions that may be grounds for legal action pursuant to subdivision (a) of Section 7109 regarding structural defects, as defined by regulation, shall be filed in writing with the registrar within 10 years after the act or omission alleged as the ground for the disciplinary action.
rules.notes: PDF page 337: 'As used in this subdivision "latent act or omission" means an act or omission that is not apparent by reasonable inspection.'
rules.correction: None.

rules.title: CSLB action on breach of a written warranty: within 18 months after warranty expires
rules.plain_english: CSLB must file a disciplinary action for breach of a contractor's express written warranty no later than 18 months after the warranty expires. Track warranty end dates.

parameters.applies_to_warranty_type: express, written warranty issued by the contractor

rules.applies_to: Contractors issuing written warranties; owners
rules.source: PDF page 337 of the 2026 CSLB Law Book
rules.quote: (e) A disciplinary action regarding an alleged breach of an express, written warranty issued by the contractor shall be filed not later than 18 months from the expiration of the warranty.
rules.notes: Warranty-tracking tools should store start date, term and expiration for each contractor warranty issued at closeout.
rules.correction: None.

rules.title: 'Structural defect' defined for CSLB 10-year complaints
rules.plain_english: A structural defect is a failure (or condition likely to cause failure) in load-bearing parts that were not built to the codes in effect at the time, which makes that part of the structure unusable for its intended purpose.

elements_all_required: failure or condition that would probably result in failure in load-bearing portions
those portions not constructed in compliance with codes in effect at the time for the location
results in inability to reasonably use the affected portion for its intended purpose

rules.applies_to: CSLB latent-defect complaints under B&P 7091(b)
rules.source: PDF page 491 of the 2026 CSLB Law Book
rules.quote: (1) A failure or condition that would probably result in a failure in the load bearing portions of a structure, (2) which portions of the structure are not constructed in compliance with the codes in effect at the time for the location of the structure, provided that, (3) such failure or condition results in the inability to reasonably use the affected portion of the structure
rules.notes: Regulatory definition for CSLB purposes only; civil defect claims use other standards (e.g., SB 800 Civil Code 896 for new homes).

rules.title: Civil suits for latent construction defects: 10 years after substantial completion
rules.plain_english: A lawsuit against a developer, designer, contractor or others for a latent (hidden) deficiency in design or construction, or resulting property damage, cannot be brought more than 10 years after substantial completion of the improvement.

parameters.trigger: substantial completion of the development or improvement
parameters.latent_deficiency: deficiency not apparent by reasonable inspection
substantial_completion_start_no_later_th: final inspection by the public agency
recordation of a valid notice of completion
use or occupation of the improvement
one year after termination or cessation of work
parameters.calc: repose_date = min(substantial_completion, final_inspection, noc_recorded, use_or_occupancy, cessation_date + 1 year) + 10 years
not_applicable_to: willful misconduct or fraudulent concealment (per statute; verify)

rules.applies_to: Contractors, developers, design professionals, owners (statute of repose)
rules.notes: leginfo.legislature.ca.gov could not be fetched from this environment (Cloudflare 403 via curl; host not allowed for WebFetch) and the session's WebSearch budget was exhausted, so the statute text was NOT read. The 10-year period and the four-event start rule are stated from general knowledge of CCP 337.15 (subdivisions (a), (b) and (g)), not read here; verify exact text before use. The 10-year concept is corroborated only indirectly by the CSLB 10-year latent structural complaint rule (B&P 7091(b), read). For new homes sold under SB 800, Civil Code 941 also sets a 10-year limit.
rules.correction: None for the encoded figures. Excerpts confirm the 10-year period, the start at substantial completion but no later than the first of final inspection, recordation of a valid notice of completion, use or occupation, or one year after termination or cessation of work (337.15(g)), and the willful-misconduct/fraudulent-concealment exclusion, which is subdivision (f). Added caution (not applied): Civil Code 941(d) says CCP 337.15 and 337.1 do not apply to actions under the SB 800 title, so for SB 800 new-home claims use Civil Code 941. rules.title: Civil suits for patent construction defects: 4 years after substantial completion
rules.plain_english: A lawsuit for a patent (reasonably visible) deficiency in design or construction must be brought within 4 years after substantial completion; if an injury occurs in the fourth year, the suit may be filed within 1 year after the injury but no more than 5 years after substantial completion.

parameters.trigger: substantial completion of the improvement
parameters.injury_in_fourth_year_extension: 1 year after injury, max 5 years after substantial completion

rules.applies_to: Contractors, developers, design professionals, owners

Separate general limitation periods (e.g., written contract) may also apply.

rules.title: SB 800 Right to Repair Act: applies to new residential construction sold on/after 2003
rules.plain_english: California's Right to Repair Act (Civil Code 895-945.5) sets building standards and a mandatory pre-lawsuit claim process for defects in newly built residential units; it applies to new residential construction where the purchase agreement was signed on or after January 1, 2003, and not to condominium conversions.

excluded: remodels/home improvement on existing homes (not 'new residential' - verify)

parties.builder: entity in the business of selling residential units to the public (Civ. Code 911)

rules.title: SB 800 builder must give at least a 1-year fit and finish warranty
rules.plain_english: Builders of new homes covered by SB 800 must provide a written limited warranty of at least one year for fit and finish items such as cabinets, mirrors, flooring, interior and exterior walls, countertops, paint finishes and trim.

rules.applies_to: SB 800 builders

rules.title: SB 800 builder duties: produce plans/reports within 30 days of request; designate claim agent; give maintenance info
rules.plain_english: On a written request from a homeowner that states it relates to the structural, fire safety or soils provisions of SB 800, the builder must provide copies of the relevant plans, specifications, mass or rough grading plans, final soils reports, public reports and available engineering calculations within 30 days, with copying costs paid by the requester. Within 30 days of a written request, and also at the initial sale, the builder must provide maintenance recommendations, product maintenance and warranty information, and its limited warranties. The builder must keep an agent for notice of claims.

documents: Department of Real Estate public reports
other_duties: designate agent for receipt of notices of claim
provide maintenance obligations/recommendations and warranty information to homeowner
parameters.copying_costs_borne_by: requesting party (builder may require onsite copying; homeowner may use bonded and insured offsite copy facility)
other_30_day_documents_on_written_reques: manufactured products maintenance, preventive maintenance and limited warranty information (912(c))
builder's limited contractual warranties in effect at original sale (912(d))
parameters.agent_for_notice: name and address maintained with the Secretary of State, or a third party noticed to the homeowner in writing (912(e))

rules.applies_to: SB 800 builders
rules.source: https://www.cslb.ca.gov/Resources/GuidesAndPublications/LawReferenceBook2022.pdf (PDF pages 695-696, Civil Code 912 as of 2022-01-01); https://leginfo.legislature.ca.gov/faces/codes_displaySection.xhtml?lawCode=CIV&sectionNum=912 (not fetchable)
rules.quote: (a) Within 30 days of a written request by a homeowner or his or her legal representative, the builder shall provide copies of all relevant plans, specifications, mass or rough grading plans, final soils reports, Bureau of Real Estate public reports, and available engineering calculations, that pertain to a homeowner's residence specifically or as part of a larger development tract. The request shall be honored if it states that it is made relative to structural, fire safety, or soils provisions of this title.
rules.notes: leginfo.legislature.ca.gov could not be fetched from this environment (Cloudflare 403 via curl; host not allowed for WebFetch) and the session's WebSearch budget was exhausted, so the statute text was NOT read. 30-day figure and document list from general knowledge of Civil Code 912(a); verify before relying. Failure to follow SB 800 procedures can release the homeowner from them (Civ. Code 915) - not verified. [Verification 2026-11-25: corrected against official text - see verification.correction; earlier caveats in these notes are superseded where they conflict.]
rules.correction: The 30-day document duty is confirmed, but the rule omitted its conditions. Under 912(a) the request must state that it relates to the structural, fire safety or soils provisions of the title; the requester bears reasonable copying costs; and the builder may require onsite copying (or the homeowner may use a bonded and insured copy service). The 2022 text names "Bureau of Real Estate public reports". Maintenance and preventive-maintenance recommendations (912(b)), manufactured-product maintenance and warranty information (912(c)) and the builder's limited warranties (912(d)) are also due within 30 days of a written request, at the homeowner's expense, and must be given at the initial sale. The agent for notice is kept with the Secretary of State or a noticed third party (912(e)). Parameters updated. Checked against the official 2022 reprint; amendments after 2022 could not be checked (leginfo not fetchable).

rules.title: SB 800 pre-litigation claim timeline (acknowledge 14 days, inspect 14 days, offer repair 30 days)
rules.plain_english: Before suing a builder, a homeowner must give written notice of the claim. The builder must acknowledge it in writing within 14 days, may complete an initial inspection and testing within 14 days after acknowledging, and may make a written offer to repair within 30 days after the inspection. The homeowner then has 30 days to accept the repair offer, and an accepted repair should start within about 14 days and be completed (every effort) within 120 days.

parameters.step_1_claim_notice: homeowner written notice of claim to builder's designated agent (Civ. Code 910)
parameters.step_2_trigger: builder's receipt of notice of claim (Civ. Code 913)
parameters.step_4_trigger: initial or (if requested) second inspection/testing (Civ. Code 917)
parameters.step_5_trigger: receipt of offer to repair (Civ. Code 918)
parameters.builder_failure_consequence: homeowner may proceed to file action (Civ. Code 915) - verify

rules.applies_to: SB 800 builders, their subcontractors (often tendered claims) and homeowners
rules.source: WebSearch excerpts of secondary sources summarizing Civil Code 913, 916, 917 (leginfo not fetched)

The 14/14/30-day figures for 913, 916 and 917 were confirmed only by search-result summaries of secondary sources (e.g., 'Section 913 requires a builder or his or her representative to acknowledge, in writing, receipt of the notice of the claim within 14 days after receipt of the notice of the claim.'). The 918 (30 days), 921 (14 days to start / 120 days to complete) figures are from general knowledge and are less certain; verify all before building a deadline calculator. Second-inspection timing and mediation options (Civ. Code 916, 919) omitted as unverified.

rules.title: SB 800 claims: 10-year outer limit; repair process can extend time to sue
rules.plain_english: SB 800 actions cannot be brought more than 10 years after substantial completion of the improvement, with the 10 years starting no later than recordation of a valid notice of completion (some standards have shorter limits). If a limitations period would otherwise run during the claim and repair process, the time to sue extends to 100 days after the repair is completed. If the builder does not acknowledge the claim, opts out of the process or does not timely request an inspection, the extension is to 45 days after its response time expired.

parameters.outer_limit_start: substantial completion, but not later than recordation of a valid notice of completion
parameters.calc_outer: deadline = min(substantial_completion_date, noc_recorded_date if any) + 10 years
parameters.tolling_alternative_trigger: builder fails to acknowledge claim in time, elects not to use the statutory process, or fails to request inspection in time: extended to 45 days after the builder's response time expired

rules.applies_to: SB 800 builders and homeowners
rules.source: https://www.cslb.ca.gov/Resources/GuidesAndPublications/LawReferenceBook2022.pdf (PDF pages 703 and 707, Civil Code 927 and 941 as of 2022-01-01); https://leginfo.legislature.ca.gov/faces/codes_displaySection.xhtml?lawCode=CIV&sectionNum=941 (not fetchable)
rules.quote: (a) Except as specifically set forth in this title, no action may be brought to recover under this title more than 10 years after substantial completion of the improvement but not later than the date of recordation of a valid notice of completion.
rules.notes: leginfo.legislature.ca.gov could not be fetched from this environment (Cloudflare 403 via curl; host not allowed for WebFetch) and the session's WebSearch budget was exhausted, so the statute text was NOT read. Figures from general knowledge of Civil Code 941(a) and 927; verify text (including how 'substantial completion' and notice-of-completion recordation interact in 941) before use. [Verification 2026-11-25: corrected against official text - see verification.correction; earlier caveats in these notes are superseded where they conflict.]
rules.correction: The 10-year outer limit and the 100-day post-repair extension are confirmed, but the calculation needed two fixes. (1) 941(a) starts the 10 years at substantial completion "but not later than the date of recordation of a valid notice of completion", so the clock is capped at NOC recordation. (2) Under 927 the 100-day extension runs from the original claim to 100 days after the repair is completed. If the builder fails to acknowledge the claim in time, elects not to use the process, or fails to request an inspection in time, the extension instead runs to 45 days after the time to respond to the notice of claim expired. Also: 941(d) says CCP 337.15 and 337.1 do not apply; 941(e) says SB 800 repairs do not restart the B&P 7091 CSLB complaint periods. Checked against the official 2022 reprint; amendments after 2022 not checked.

rules.title: SB 800 standards with shorter claim periods (e.g., plumbing/electrical 4 years, irrigation/noise 1 year)
rules.plain_english: Some SB 800 building standards carry shorter claim periods. From close of escrow: plumbing and sewer systems 4 years, electrical systems 4 years, exterior hardscape cracking 4 years, untreated steel fences 4 years, paint and stains 5 years, untreated wood posts 2 years, landscaping 2 years, dryer ducts 2 years, and irrigation and drainage 1 year. Noise transmission between attached units: 1 year from the original occupancy of the adjacent unit.

parameters.measured_from: close of escrow, except noise transmission (original occupancy of the adjacent unit)

rules.applies_to: SB 800 builders (warranty/claims tracking by system)

Under 896(g)(6) the 1-year limit runs "from the original occupancy of the adjacent unit", not from close of escrow, and that standard applies only to attached structures with an applicable noise code. Plumbing and sewer (896(e), 4 years), electrical (896(f), 4 years) and irrigation and drainage (896(g)(7), 1 year) from close of escrow are confirmed. Added the other periods the rule left blank, all from close of escrow: hardscape cracking 4 years (g)(1); untreated wood posts 2 years (g)(8); untreated steel fences 4 years (g)(9); paint and stains 5 years (g)(10); landscaping 2 years, and it must survive at least 1 year (g)(12); dryer ducts 2 years (g)(14). rules.title: SB 800 builder defenses include homeowner maintenance failures and alterations
rules.plain_english: SB 800 lets builders defend claims where damage was caused by things like acts of nature, the homeowner's unreasonable failure to minimize damage, failure to follow the builder's or manufacturer's maintenance recommendations, normal wear and tear, or alterations/repairs by others. Builders should give homeowners written maintenance schedules at closeout.

alterations, repairs or modifications by others
builder's prior repair or claimant refusal of repair (verify)

rules.title: Home roof warranties pass to later owners unless clearly limited
rules.plain_english: For home roofing contracts entered on or after January 1, 1994, the roofing warranty automatically benefits and can be enforced by later buyers of the house, unless the contract clearly and conspicuously limits transferability.

parameters.to_limit_transfer: clear and conspicuous provision in the contract limiting transferability

rules.notes: Read as quoted in the Law Book (Ch. 2), which also notes 'Home warranties generally are not transferable, except as provided for home roof warranties.' Other provisions of Civil Code 1797.90-1797.96 were not read.

rules.title: Report $1M+ multifamily construction-defect judgments/settlements to CSLB within 90 days
rules.plain_english: A licensee must report to CSLB in writing within 90 days after learning of a final judgment, signed settlement or final arbitration award of $1 million or more in a construction-defect case involving load-bearing failures of a multifamily rental building (designated a complex case). Contractors assigned less than $15,000 of liability need not report; SB 800 residential construction is excluded.

rules.title: HIC/service contract notice: Commercial General Liability Insurance (CGL)
rules.plain_english: Home improvement (and service and repair) contracts must include a notice headed 'Commercial General Liability Insurance (CGL)' with the one correct statement: no CGL; carries CGL (insurer name and phone to verify); self-insured; or LLC carrying liability insurance/other security as required by law. It may be an attachment if the contract says so.

You may call (the insurance company or trust company or bank) at ____ to check on the contractor's insurance coverage or security.

rules.title: LLC licensees: liability insurance $1M aggregate (+$100k per person over 5, max $5M)
rules.plain_english: A licensed LLC must carry liability insurance with at least a $1 million aggregate limit if it has five or fewer people on its personnel of record, plus $100,000 more per additional person, up to $5 million. A Certificate of Liability Insurance signed by the insurer must be filed with CSLB, and if the limit is exhausted it must be restored by the next policy period or the license is suspended.

parameters.also_required: $100,000 LLC worker-protection surety bond (B&P 7071.6.5) in addition to $25,000 license bond

Formula follows the CSLB narrative; the literal reading (100,000 x all persons) would give a higher figure - flag for legal review. Non-LLC licensees are not required by license law to carry CGL (PDF page 43).

rules.title: Arbitration clause in residential (1-4 unit) contracts: required title, type and notice

Otherwise it may not be enforceable against anyone but the licensee.

rules.title: CSLB arbitration: mandatory at or below $25,000 (contract price or damages); voluntary above $25,000 and under $50,000
rules.plain_english: CSLB must refer an eligible complaint to its free arbitration program, without the parties' consent, when the contract price or the damages demanded is $25,000 (the license bond amount) or less. Above that and below $50,000 in damages, CSLB may refer it only if both the contractor and the complainant agree. Eligibility: the licensee has no history of repeated or similar violations, was in good standing at the time, has no outstanding disciplinary actions, arbitration serves the public interest better than discipline, and the parties did not already agree to private arbitration.

covered_violations: any complaint arising from a contract involving works of improvement
eligibility_criteria_mandatory_7085a2_to: public interest better served by arbitration than discipline
no history of repeated or similar violations
licensee in good standing at time of alleged violation
no outstanding disciplinary actions against licensee
parties have not previously agreed to private arbitration

rules.applies_to: Contractors and owners in CSLB complaint disputes
rules.source: PDF page 324 of the 2026 CSLB Law Book-325; PDF page 295 of the 2026 CSLB Law Book; PDF page 72 of the 2026 CSLB Law Book
rules.quote: (b) In all cases in which a possible violation of the sections set forth in paragraph (1) of subdivision (a) exists and the contract price, or the demand for damages is equal to or less than the amount of the bond required under Section 7071.6, but, regardless of the contract price, the complaint shall be referred to arbitration, utilizing the criteria set forth in paragraphs (2) to (6), inclusive, of subdivision (a).
rules.notes: Read from the Law Book narrative (B&P 7085 statute text itself not reviewed here). [Verification 2026-11-25: corrected against official text - see verification.correction; earlier caveats in these notes are superseded where they conflict.]
rules.correction: The Law Book narrative gets the tier edges and criteria wrong. B&P 7085(b): referral is mandatory (no consent needed) when the contract price OR the demand for damages is "equal to or less than" the 7071.6 bond amount ($25,000), so exactly $25,000 is mandatory, not voluntary. Voluntary referral under 7085(a) needs both parties to agree and covers "material damages" greater than the bond amount and less than $50,000. Eligibility is not "no record of prior violations": 7085(a) requires no history of repeated or similar violations, good standing at the time of the alleged violation, no outstanding disciplinary actions, a registrar finding that arbitration serves the public interest better than discipline, no prior agreement to private arbitration, and (voluntary only) advice on Civil Code 2855. The scope is complaints alleging violations of B&P 7107, 7109, 7110, 7113, 7119 or 7120, or complaints arising from a contract for works of improvement. Parameters, plain_english, citation and quote replaced with the statute.

rules.title: Small claims: money judgments up to $12,500 (no lien foreclosure)
rules.plain_english: A contractor owed money can sue in small claims court for up to $12,500 if it is a natural person or sole proprietor; a corporation, partnership, LLC or other entity is limited to $6,250. A mechanics lien cannot be foreclosed there, neither side may use a lawyer, a losing defendant can appeal within 30 days, and no more than two claims over $2,500 may be filed statewide per calendar year.
rules.applies_to: Contractors collecting small balances (e.g., unpaid change orders)
rules.citation: CCP 116.220(a)(1), 116.221 (as cited in CSLB Law Book and court self-help pages); two-claims-over-$2,500 limit per court self-help pages
rules.source: PDF page 71 of the 2026 CSLB Law Book
rules.quote: Although you cannot foreclose on a mechanics lien in small claims court, you may get a monetary judgment of up to $12,500 (see CCP §116.221).
rules.notes: CCP 116.221's $12,500 limit applies to natural persons; lower limits for entities (CCP 116.220) are from general knowledge, not read - a corporation/LLC contractor may be limited to a lower amount. Verify before advising entity contractors. [Verification 2026-11-25: corrected against official text - see verification.correction; earlier caveats in these notes are superseded where they conflict.]
rules.correction: The $12,500 limit applies only to natural persons, including a sole proprietor. Corporations, partnerships, LLCs and other entities are capped at $6,250 (CCP 116.220(a)(1); the 2022 reprint read $5,000/$10,000, since raised). The plain_english "a contractor ... can sue for up to $12,500" was wrong for entity contractors. Also added: no more than two claims over $2,500 per calendar year statewide. The CCP text itself was not read on leginfo.

rules.title: Unlicensed (or improperly licensed) contractors cannot sue for payment and may have to return payments

rules.title: HIC: give buyer a fully signed and dated copy before work starts

rules.title: Contract types: lump sum, cost-plus, unit price, GMP
rules.plain_english: Know which contract type you are using - lump sum, cost-plus, unit price, or guaranteed maximum price - because each changes how you bill, track costs, handle changes and share savings.

rules.title: What counts as 'public works'

also_covers: street, sewer or other improvement work under public authority
tree removal in execution of a covered project
excludes: work done directly by a public utility company under PUC order

rules.applies_to: Any contractor or subcontractor working on publicly funded projects in California
rules.quote: As used in this chapter, “public works” means all of the following: (1) Construction, alteration, demolition, installation, or repair work done under contract and paid for in whole or in part out of public funds, except work done directly by a public utility company pursuant to order of the Public Utilities Commission or other public authority.
rules.notes: Statute text read from the official CSLB 2022 Law Book appendix (statutes as published Jan. 2022); leginfo.legislature.ca.gov could not be reached to confirm later amendments. Also see DIR summary at https://www.dir.ca.gov/Public-Works/PublicWorks.html (maintenance is also covered per LC 1771).

rules.title: Pre- and post-construction work is 'construction'
rules.plain_english: Design-phase site assessment, feasibility, inspection and land surveying work, and post-construction cleanup at the jobsite count as covered 'construction', even if no further construction happens.

parameters.installation_includes: assembly/disassembly of freestanding and affixed modular office systems

rules.applies_to: Surveyors, inspectors, cleanup crews and other pre/post-construction workers on public projects
rules.quote: “construction” includes work performed during the design, site assessment, feasibility study, and other preconstruction phases of construction, including, but not limited to, inspection and land surveying work, regardless of whether any further construction work is conducted, and work performed during the postconstruction phases of construction, including, but not limited to
rules.notes: Statute text read from the official CSLB 2022 Law Book appendix (statutes as published Jan. 2022); leginfo.legislature.ca.gov could not be reached to confirm later amendments.

rules.title: 'Paid for out of public funds' includes indirect subsidies
rules.plain_english: A project is publicly funded not only when a public agency pays cash, but also when it does construction work, transfers property below market value, waives or reduces fees, rents, loans or interest, makes contingent loans, or gives credits.

forms: payment of money or equivalent to or on behalf of contractor/developer
construction work performed by the public entity
transfer of asset for less than fair market price
fees/costs/rents/insurance/bond premiums/loans/interest paid, reduced, below market, waived or forgiven
money loaned repayable on a contingent basis
credits against repayment obligations

rules.applies_to: Developers and contractors on private projects that receive public assistance
rules.quote: (3) Transfer by the state or political subdivision of an asset of value for less than fair market price. (4) Fees, costs, rents, insurance or bond premiums, loans, interest rates, or other obligations that would normally be required in the execution of the contract, that are paid, reduced, charged at less than fair market value, waived, or forgiven by the state or political subdivision.
rules.notes: Statute text read from the official CSLB 2022 Law Book appendix (statutes as published Jan. 2022); leginfo.legislature.ca.gov could not be reached to confirm later amendments. If a project is later found to be public work, see rule pw-1784-recover-increased-costs.

rules.title: De minimis public subsidy exception ($600,000 and 2%)
rules.plain_english: A private development does not become a public work because of a small public subsidy: the subsidy must be both under $600,000 and under 2% of total project cost (for all-single-family projects, only the under-2% test applies).
rules.applies_to: Private developers and their contractors receiving public subsidies
rules.quote: For purposes of subparagraph (A), a public subsidy is de minimis if it is both less than six hundred thousand dollars ($600,000) and less than 2 percent of the total project cost. (ii) Notwithstanding clause (i), for purposes of subparagraph (A), a public subsidy for a project that consists entirely of single-family dwellings is de minimis if it is less than 2 percent of the total project cost.
rules.notes: Statute text read from the official CSLB 2022 Law Book appendix (statutes as published Jan. 2022); leginfo.legislature.ca.gov could not be reached to confirm later amendments. Subdivision (c)(3)(A) also excludes reimbursement of costs normally borne by the public.

rules.title: Private residential projects on private property excluded
rules.plain_english: Private residential projects built on private property are not public works unless built under an agreement with a state agency, redevelopment agency (or successor), or local public housing authority.

parameters.excluded: private residential projects on private property

rules.applies_to: Residential builders
rules.quote: (1) Private residential projects built on private property are not subject to this chapter unless the projects are built pursuant to an agreement with a state agency, a redevelopment agency, a successor agency to a redevelopment agency when acting in that capacity, or a local public housing authority.
rules.notes: Statute text read from the official CSLB 2022 Law Book appendix (statutes as published Jan. 2022); leginfo.legislature.ca.gov could not be reached to confirm later amendments. Other residential exclusions in 1720(c)(5) (self-help housing with >=500 buyer hours, homeless shelters, etc.) and 1720(d).

rules.title: Definition of 'maintenance' (lower $15,000 small-project threshold)
rules.plain_english: Maintenance means routine, recurring work to keep a public facility in safe, usable condition, including craft repair work; routine janitorial and security guard services are not covered maintenance.

includes: routine, recurring and usual preservation work on publicly owned/operated facilities
carpentry, electrical, plumbing, glazing, touchup painting and other craft work

rules.applies_to: Contractors on public maintenance contracts
rules.quote: (1) Routine, recurring and usual work for the preservation, protection and keeping of any publicly owned or publicly operated facility (plant, building, structure, ground facility, utility system or any real property) for its intended purposes in a safe and continually usable condition for which it has been designed, improved, constructed, altered or repaired.
rules.notes: Used to decide whether the $15,000 (maintenance) or $25,000 (construction) small-project threshold applies.

rules.title: Prevailing wage required on public works over $1,000
rules.plain_english: Every worker on a public works project over $1,000 must be paid at least the prevailing wage, including holiday and overtime rates. It applies to maintenance contracts, but not to a public agency's own employees.
rules.applies_to: All contractors/subcontractors on public works
rules.quote: Except for public works projects of one thousand dollars ($1,000) or less, not less than the general prevailing rate of per diem wages for work of a similar character in the locality in which the public work is performed, and not less than the general prevailing rate of per diem wages for holiday and overtime work fixed as provided in this chapter
rules.notes: Statute text read from the official CSLB 2022 Law Book appendix (statutes as published Jan. 2022); leginfo.legislature.ca.gov could not be reached to confirm later amendments. DIR FAQ notes some LCP-enforcing awarding bodies historically had higher exemption thresholds ($25,000/$15,000) under LC 1771.5.

rules.title: No splitting projects to dodge thresholds
rules.plain_english: Jobs may not be split or parceled into smaller work orders to get under the $1,000 prevailing wage threshold or the $25,000/$15,000 small-project thresholds. If yearly work with the same vendor will exceed the threshold, the vendor must register and the contract must be registered.
rules.applies_to: Awarding bodies and contractors on recurring/small public jobs
rules.quote: Prevailing wage requirements apply to public works projects over $1,000. The law does not permit jobs to be parceled in order to avoid the $1,000 threshold. If the awarding body knows that total yearly project costs or projects awarded to the same vendor will exceed $1,000, that vendor must be registered with the DIR as a public works contractor
rules.notes: 8 CCR 16100(b)(6): awarding body must 'Ensure that public works projects are not split or separated into smaller work orders or projects for the purpose of evading the applicable provisions of Labor Code Section 1771.'

rules.title: Prime and every subcontractor must pay prevailing rates to all workers
rules.plain_english: The prime contractor and every subcontractor must pay at least the specified prevailing rates to every worker employed in executing the contract, regardless of the worker's title (owner, partner, foreman, independent contractor).

parameters.who_is_covered: all workers employed in the execution of the contract

rules.applies_to: All public works contractors
rules.source: https://www.cslb.ca.gov/Resources/GuidesAndPublications/LawReferenceBook2022.pdf PDF page 977 (Appendix, Labor Code §1774); PDF page 967 (§1772)
rules.quote: The contractor to whom the contract is awarded, and any subcontractor under him, shall pay not less than the specified prevailing rates of wages to all workmen employed in the execution of the contract.
rules.notes: Statute text read from the official CSLB 2022 Law Book appendix (statutes as published Jan. 2022); leginfo.legislature.ca.gov could not be reached to confirm later amendments. LC 1772: workers employed by contractors or subcontractors in the execution of any contract for public work are deemed employed upon public work.

rules.title: Sole proprietors/owner-operators must earn at least the prevailing wage
rules.plain_english: An owner who does the work must show that the labor portion of the contract (contract price minus materials, overhead and other costs, divided by hours worked) is at least the prevailing rate, and must still submit eCPRs. Salaried corporate officers doing covered work are annualized and topped up if below the rate.

parameters.corporate_officer_salary: annualize to hourly; pay difference if below prevailing rate

rules.applies_to: Sole proprietors, partners and owner-operators doing covered work
rules.quote: Divide profit before labor costs (the amount of the contract, less fixed and variable costs) by the total number of hours worked on the public works site. If labor profit falls below the prevailing wage rate, the contractor could be subject to public works penalties for failing to pay the correct prevailing wage rate.
rules.notes: Use SSN or ITIN when reporting if no FEIN. Owners cannot underbid labor cost.

rules.title: Ask DIR for a coverage determination when unsure
rules.plain_english: If you are unsure whether a job is a public work, the awarding body or any interested party (contractor, union, worker) can request a written coverage determination from DIR's Director.

parameters.request_to: pwcoverage@dir.ca.gov (DIR Office of the Director, Legal Unit)

rules.applies_to: Contractors and owners on projects with public money
rules.quote: If you need assistance determining whether a project constitutes a public work, you may request a coverage determination with the DIR Office of the Director, Legal Unit, at pwcoverage@dir.ca.gov.
rules.notes: Past determinations: https://www.dir.ca.gov/oprl/PWDecision.asp

rules.title: Recovering prevailing wage costs when a private job is later ruled public work
rules.plain_english: If a private job is later ruled a public work and nobody told you it was, you can sue your hiring party for the extra wages and penalties, but you must notify the hiring party and owner/developer within 30 days of the DIR/LWDA decision or court filing, by registered/certified mail, express mail or overnight carrier.

parameters.trigger: receipt of DIR/LWDA decision or initiation of court action alleging public work
not_available_if: owner/hiring party expressly advised it was public work

rules.applies_to: CSLB-licensed contractors with a direct contract on a private project later deemed public work
rules.quote: the contractor shall notify the hiring party and the owner or developer within 30 days after receipt of the notice of a decision by the Department of Industrial Relations or the Labor and Workforce Development Agency, or the initiation of any action in a court alleging, that the work covered by the project, or any portion thereof, is a “public work,” as defined in this chapter.
rules.notes: Statute text read from the official CSLB 2022 Law Book appendix (statutes as published Jan. 2022); leginfo.legislature.ca.gov could not be reached to confirm later amendments. Also (c): such violations need not be listed on prequalification questionnaires.

rules.title: DIR public works contractor registration required
rules.plain_english: A contractor or subcontractor cannot bid, be listed in a bid, or work on a public works contract unless currently registered with DIR under Labor Code 1725.5 (unless the small-project exemption applies).

required_for: being listed as a subcontractor in a bid
parameters.exception: small-project exemption (see rule small-project-exemption-25000-15000)

rules.applies_to: All prime contractors and subcontractors (any tier) on public works
rules.quote: (a) A contractor or subcontractor shall not be qualified to bid on, be listed in a bid proposal, subject to the requirements of Section 4104 of the Public Contract Code, or engage in the performance of any contract for public work, as defined in this chapter, unless currently registered and qualified to perform public work pursuant to Section 1725.5.
rules.notes: Statute text read from the official CSLB 2022 Law Book appendix (statutes as published Jan. 2022); leginfo.legislature.ca.gov could not be reached to confirm later amendments. Per FindLaw snippets a new version of LC 1725.5 became operative July 1, 2026 (with interim LC 1725.6 sunsetting); text not read. SB 909 (Ch. 660, Stats. 2026, chaptered 9/27/2026) amends LC 1725.5, 1771.3, 1775, 1776 and 1777.7 and PCC 2603 per its chaptered title on leginfo (LC 1741 and 1813 appeared only in earlier versions). Final amounts and operative date NOT verified - re-check before 2027.

rules.title: Who must register (separate licenses, joint employers, sole proprietors)
rules.plain_english: Each separately licensed business entity, every independent contractor doing prevailing wage work, joint employers such as temp staffing agencies and labor contractors, brokers who sub out the actual work, and owner-operator sole proprietors must each register.

must_register: each separately CSLB-licensed entity/name bidding or working on public works
independent contractors performing prevailing wage work
joint employers incl. temp staffing agencies, PEOs, labor contractors
entities that contract and then subcontract all the actual work
parameters.employee_test: not an employee of a registered contractor unless that contractor carries workers' comp for the person

rules.applies_to: Contractors, staffing agencies, owner-operators
rules.quote: (1) Each business entity or name that is separately licensed by the Contractors State License Board or other licensing entity and intends to bid or work on public works through that separate license, irrespective of whether the separately licensed entities or business names share a common ownership.
rules.notes: DIR FAQ: registration not required for projects under complete control of the federal government (Davis-Bacon only).

rules.title: Registration fee: $400 per fiscal year (1-3 years)
rules.plain_english: Registration or renewal costs $400 per fiscal year; you can register for one, two or three years at once ($400, $800 or $1,200). Fees are nonrefundable and registration is not complete until payment is processed.
rules.applies_to: All public works contractors and subcontractors
rules.quote: (6) The fees specified in paragraphs (1), (2), and (3) are for registration or renewal for a single fiscal year, as determined in accordance with section 16410(b). A contractor or subcontractor may apply to register or renew for one, two, or three years by paying the fee specified in paragraphs (1), (2), or (3) for each year of registration or renewal
rules.notes: CSLB Summer 2026 newsletter also states $400 per fiscal year. SB 909 (Ch. 660, Stats. 2026, chaptered 9/27/2026) amends LC 1725.5, 1771.3, 1775, 1776 and 1777.7 and PCC 2603 per its chaptered title on leginfo (LC 1741 and 1813 appeared only in earlier versions). Final amounts and operative date NOT verified - re-check before 2027. (SB 909 analyses describe letting the DIR Director set/CPI-adjust the fee.)
rules.correction: None. LC 1725.5(a)(1) lets the Director adjust the fees by posting them on the DIR website, and the DIR page (April 2026) still shows $400/$800/$1,200. FLAG: SB 909 (Ch. 660, Stats. 2026, chaptered 9/27/2026) amends LC 1725.5, 1771.3, 1775, 1776 and 1777.7 and PCC 2603, per its chaptered title as shown in leginfo search excerpts. The chaptered text and its operative date were not read. The amount here is current law as of 2026-11-25. Re-check it against Ch. 660 before 2027.

rules.title: Registration runs July 1 - June 30; renew by June 30
rules.plain_english: Registration covers the July 1 to June 30 fiscal year (or the remainder of it), no matter when you register. Renew before June 30 to avoid penalties.
rules.applies_to: All registered public works contractors
rules.quote: (b) All registrations shall be for the July 1 to June 30 fiscal year or any part of the fiscal year that remains following the date of registration.
rules.notes: dir.ca.gov/pw: 'Your registration must be valid each year by June 30 to prevent penalties.'

rules.title: $2,000 penalty to register after working/bidding unregistered
rules.plain_english: If you worked on, bid on, or were listed on a bid for a public works project in the past 12 months while unregistered, you must pay an extra $2,000 penalty (plus the $400 fee) to register. For a single violation in 12 months you can still register by paying it.
rules.applies_to: Contractors registering for the first time or reactivating
rules.quote: (4) Additional penalty to apply for registration if contractor or subcontractor has worked, bid, or been listed on a bid in violation of the requirements of Labor Code Section 1725.5(a) within the preceding twelve months - $2000
rules.notes: DIR may refund the penalty on clear and convincing proof it did not apply (16412(d)). SB 909 (Ch. 660, Stats. 2026, chaptered 9/27/2026) amends LC 1725.5, 1771.3, 1775, 1776 and 1777.7 and PCC 2603 per its chaptered title on leginfo (LC 1741 and 1813 appeared only in earlier versions). Final amounts and operative date NOT verified - re-check before 2027.
rules.correction: None. Leginfo search excerpts show the current LC 1725.5, operative July 1, 2026, keeps the $2,000 penalty registration fee. FLAG: SB 909 (Ch. 660, Stats. 2026, chaptered 9/27/2026) amends LC 1725.5, 1771.3, 1775, 1776 and 1777.7 and PCC 2603, per its chaptered title as shown in leginfo search excerpts. The chaptered text and its operative date were not read. The amount here is current law as of 2026-11-25. Re-check it against Ch. 660 before 2027.

rules.title: Late renewal: 90-day grace with $400 penalty
rules.plain_english: If your registration lapses and you keep working or bidding, you can renew retroactively within 90 days after expiration (July 1 - Sept 30) by paying a $400 penalty plus the renewal fee if the lapse was accidental ($2,000 if not accidental). Renewing after September 30 (or reactivating) costs a $2,000 penalty if you bid, were awarded or worked on public works while unregistered in the past 12 months.
rules.applies_to: Registered contractors who miss the June 30 renewal
rules.citation: 8 CCR 16412(a)(5); DIR FAQ; DIR registration page
rules.quote: Registered contractors who inadvertently fail to renew by June 30, but continue to work on public works after that date, have a 90-day grace period to renew retroactively by paying a $400 penalty in addition to the registration renewal fee.
rules.notes: Accidental vs. non-accidental split ($400 vs $2,000) is from DIR registration page dated April 2026. 8 CCR 16412(a)(5) text: '$400' during first ninety days for inadvertent lapse.

rules.title: Registration eligibility requirements
rules.plain_english: To register you must: carry workers' comp for any employees and use only registered subcontractors; hold a CSLB license if your trade requires one; owe no delinquent unpaid wage or penalty assessments; not be debarred; and not have prior registration violations (first violation in 12 months can be cured with the penalty).

requirements: no prior registration violation (first in 12 months curable by penalty)

rules.applies_to: Applicants for DIR registration
rules.quote: Have workers' compensation coverage for any employees and only use subcontractors who are registered public works contractors. Have Contractors State License Board license if applicable to trade. Not have any delinquent unpaid wage or penalty assessments owed to any employee or enforcement agency. Not be under federal or state debarment.
rules.notes: Workers' comp evidence (per secondary snippets of LC 1725.5): certificate of insurance or self-insurance under B&P 7125.

rules.title: Pay by credit card: registration posts in about 24 hours
rules.plain_english: Credit card registrations are processed within about 24 hours; other payment methods can delay registration up to eight weeks. Plan ahead of bid dates.
rules.applies_to: Contractors registering before a bid
rules.quote: Please note: credit card payments can be processed within 24 hours while other forms of payment may delay registration up to eight weeks.
rules.notes: Since May 24, 2024 contractors must create accounts on the modernized Public Works Website Services.

rules.title: Two registration violations in 12 months: up to 12 months disqualification
rules.plain_english: Contractors found violating the registration requirement twice within 12 months can be barred from public works for up to 12 months at a time.
rules.applies_to: Contractors with repeat registration violations
rules.quote: Contractors who are found to be in violation of the registration requirement twice in 12 months can be disqualified from working in public works for up to 12 months at a time.

rules.title: Appeal of registration denial within 60 days
rules.plain_english: If DIR denies your registration on the merits, you can appeal in writing within 60 days; a hearing is set within 30 days of the appeal.
rules.applies_to: Contractors denied registration
rules.quote: (c) Within sixty (60) days following the issuance of any notice of denial pursuant to subsection (b), including a notification of denial provided at the conclusion of the online registration process or any written notice of denial that is subsequently transmitted, mailed, or delivered to the applicant for registration
rules.notes: Denial for incomplete application is without prejudice to reapplying (16413(a)).

rules.title: Registration revocation: 10 days to stay, 60 days to appeal; 30 days-24 months disqualification
rules.plain_english: DIR can revoke registration (e.g., no longer qualified, false certification, or knowingly hiring unregistered subs). Revocation takes effect at 11:59 p.m. on the 10th day after notice unless you appeal within those 10 days; you may still appeal up to 60 days, but a late appeal does not stop the revocation. Disqualification is 30 days to 24 months.
rules.applies_to: Registered contractors
rules.quote: (d) Except as provided in section 16417, revocation shall be effective at 11:59 p.m. on the tenth day following the date the Labor Commissioner sends the written notice of revocation specified in subsections (b) and (c), unless prior to that deadline the Department receives the contractor or subcontractor's written appeal under subsection (e).
rules.notes: 16414(b): 'The period of disqualification shall be no less than 30 days and no greater than 24 months following the effective date of revocation.' Decision within 5 days (stayed) or 10 days of hearing; writ within 45 days (16416).

rules.title: Working unregistered: $100/day up to $8,000
rules.plain_english: A contractor or subcontractor who works on a public works contract without registration owes $100 for each day of work, up to $8,000, on top of the $2,000 registration penalty fee.
rules.applies_to: Unregistered contractors/subcontractors
rules.quote: shall forfeit, as a civil penalty to the state, one hundred dollars ($100) for each day of work performed in violation of the registration requirement, not to exceed an aggregate penalty of eight thousand dollars ($8,000) in addition to any penalty registration fee assessed pursuant to clause (ii) of subparagraph (E) of paragraph (2) of subdivision (a) of Section 1725.5.
rules.notes: Statute text read from the official CSLB 2022 Law Book appendix (statutes as published Jan. 2022); leginfo.legislature.ca.gov could not be reached to confirm later amendments. SB 909 (Ch. 660, Stats. 2026, chaptered 9/27/2026) amends LC 1725.5, 1771.3, 1775, 1776 and 1777.7 and PCC 2603 per its chaptered title on leginfo (LC 1741 and 1813 appeared only in earlier versions). Final amounts and operative date NOT verified - re-check before 2027.

rules.title: Hiring an unregistered sub: $100/day up to $10,000; no indemnity
rules.plain_english: A prime or higher-tier sub that subcontracts with an unregistered lower-tier sub owes $100 for each day the unregistered sub works, up to $10,000. You cannot make the sub indemnify you for this penalty. No liability if the sub's registration was later revoked; first-time unintentional violations may be waived.

parameters.exception: lower-tier registration revoked
parameters.waivable: first-time, unintentional, did not hinder enforcement

rules.applies_to: Prime contractors and upper-tier subcontractors
