rules.quote: shall be subject to forfeiture, as a civil penalty to the state, of one hundred dollars ($100) for each day the unregistered lower tier subcontractor performs work in violation of the registration requirement, not to exceed an aggregate penalty of ten thousand dollars ($10,000).
rules.notes: Statute text read from the official CSLB 2022 Law Book appendix (statutes as published Jan. 2022); leginfo.legislature.ca.gov could not be reached to confirm later amendments. Check sub registration at https://services.dir.ca.gov/pw before signing subcontracts.

rules.title: Stop order against unregistered contractors; idled workers paid up to 10 days
rules.plain_english: The Labor Commissioner must issue a stop order barring an unregistered contractor from all public works until it registers. Workers idled by the stop order must be paid their regular prevailing rate for up to 10 days.
rules.applies_to: Unregistered contractors and those who hire them
rules.source: https://www.cslb.ca.gov/Resources/GuidesAndPublications/LawReferenceBook2022.pdf PDF pages 957-958 (Appendix, Labor Code §1771.1(j)); current text: DIR 'California Prevailing Wage Laws' (rev. Feb. 1, 2025) https://www.dir.ca.gov/public-works/CaliforniaPrevailingWageLaws.pdf PDF p.152
rules.quote: (4) Any employee of an unregistered contractor or subcontractor who is affected by a work stoppage ordered by the commissioner pursuant to this subdivision shall be paid at their regular hourly prevailing wage rate by that employer for any hours the employee would have worked but for the work stoppage, not to exceed 10 days.
rules.notes: Statute text read from the official CSLB 2022 Law Book appendix (statutes as published Jan. 2022); leginfo.legislature.ca.gov could not be reached to confirm later amendments.
rules.correction: Quote only. The current text of LC 1771.1(j)(4) reads 'at their regular hourly prevailing wage rate' where the 2022 reprint read 'his or her'. The quote now uses the current wording. The substance (stop order effective on service; up to 10 days' pay for idled workers) is unchanged.

rules.title: Ignoring a stop order: misdemeanor, up to 60 days jail / $10,000
rules.plain_english: A contractor, owner, director, officer or managing agent who fails to observe a served stop order is guilty of a misdemeanor punishable by up to 60 days in county jail, a fine up to $10,000, or both.
rules.applies_to: Unregistered contractors served with stop orders
rules.source: https://www.cslb.ca.gov/Resources/GuidesAndPublications/LawReferenceBook2022.pdf PDF page 958 (Appendix, Labor Code §1771.1(k)); current text: DIR 'California Prevailing Wage Laws' (rev. Feb. 1, 2025) https://www.dir.ca.gov/public-works/CaliforniaPrevailingWageLaws.pdf PDF p.152
rules.quote: (k) Failure of a contractor or subcontractor, owner, director, officer, or managing agent of the contractor or subcontractor to observe a stop order issued and served upon them pursuant to subdivision (j) is guilty of a misdemeanor punishable by imprisonment in county jail not exceeding 60 days or by a fine not exceeding ten thousand dollars ($10,000), or both.
rules.notes: Statute text read from the official CSLB 2022 Law Book appendix (statutes as published Jan. 2022); leginfo.legislature.ca.gov could not be reached to confirm later amendments.
rules.correction: Quote only. The current text of LC 1771.1(k) reads 'served upon them' where the 2022 reprint read 'upon him or her'. The quote now uses the current wording. The 60-day jail and $10,000 fine maximums are unchanged.

rules.title: Inadvertently listing an unregistered sub: cure options
rules.plain_english: Listing an unregistered subcontractor by mistake does not make the bid nonresponsive if the sub registered before bid opening, registers and pays the penalty fee within 24 hours after bid opening, or is replaced with a registered sub under PCC 4107.

cure_options: sub registers and pays penalty fee within 24 hours after bid opening

rules.applies_to: Prime contractors submitting bids
rules.quote: (c) An inadvertent error in listing a subcontractor who is not registered pursuant to Section 1725.5 in a bid proposal shall not be grounds for filing a bid protest or grounds for considering the bid nonresponsive, provided that any of the following apply: (1) The subcontractor is registered prior to the bid opening. (2) Within 24 hours after the bid opening
rules.notes: Statute text read from the official CSLB 2022 Law Book appendix (statutes as published Jan. 2022); leginfo.legislature.ca.gov could not be reached to confirm later amendments.

rules.title: Proof of registration before accepting bids or signing subcontracts
rules.plain_english: Bid invitations and public works contracts must give notice of the registration requirement, and no bid may be accepted and no contract or subcontract signed without proof of the contractor's or subcontractor's current DIR registration.
rules.applies_to: Awarding bodies, prime contractors, subcontractors
rules.quote: (b) Notice of the requirement described in subdivision (a) shall be included in all bid invitations and public works contracts, and a bid shall not be accepted nor any contract or subcontract entered into without proof of the contractor or subcontractor’s current registration to perform public work pursuant to Section 1725.5.
rules.notes: Statute text read from the official CSLB 2022 Law Book appendix (statutes as published Jan. 2022); leginfo.legislature.ca.gov could not be reached to confirm later amendments. A tool can verify PWCR numbers against DIR's public contractor search before subcontract execution.

rules.title: Small project exemption: $25,000 construction / $15,000 maintenance
rules.plain_english: On public works of $25,000 or less (construction, alteration, demolition, installation or repair) or $15,000 or less (maintenance), contractors need not register with DIR or file eCPRs, and the awarding body need not file the PWC-100. Prevailing wages (over $1,000) and certified payroll records still apply; keep the records at least 3 years.
rules.applies_to: Contractors working exclusively on small public works projects
rules.source: https://www.cslb.ca.gov/Resources/GuidesAndPublications/LawReferenceBook2022.pdf PDF page 958 (Appendix, Labor Code §1771.1(n)); PDF page 961 (§1771.4(a)(4))
rules.quote: (n) This section shall not apply to work performed on a public works project of twenty-five thousand dollars ($25,000) or less when the project is for construction, alteration, demolition, installation, or repair work or to work performed on a public works project of fifteen thousand dollars ($15,000) or less when the project is for maintenance work.
rules.notes: Statute text read from the official CSLB 2022 Law Book appendix (statutes as published Jan. 2022); leginfo.legislature.ca.gov could not be reached to confirm later amendments. LC 1771.4(a)(4): unregistered small-project contractors 'shall retain the records specified in Section 1776 for at least three years after completion of the work.'

rules.title: Small-project exemption is measured on the whole prime contract
rules.plain_english: The $25,000/$15,000 test uses the entire contract between the awarding body and the prime contractor, not the size of your subcontract. A $10,000 subcontract on a $500,000 job is not exempt.

parameters.measure: awarding body to prime contractor contract amount

rules.applies_to: Subcontractors on public works
rules.quote: Keep in mind that this amount is for the entire contract between the Awarding Body and the Prime Contractor. If the subcontract is less than this amount but the master contract is more than this amount then it would not fall under the small project exemption.

rules.title: Joint venture and federal-aid bids: register by contract award
rules.plain_english: An unregistered contractor may submit a joint-venture bid (B&P 7029.1) or a bid on a federally funded project (PCC 10164/20103.5) as long as it is registered when the contract is awarded.
rules.applies_to: Joint ventures and bidders on federally funded projects
rules.quote: It is not a violation of this section for an unregistered contractor to submit a bid that is authorized by Section 7029.1 of the Business and Professions Code or by Section 10164 or 20103.5 of the Public Contract Code, provided the contractor is registered to perform public work pursuant to Section 1725.5 at the time the contract is awarded.
rules.notes: Statute text read from the official CSLB 2022 Law Book appendix (statutes as published Jan. 2022); leginfo.legislature.ca.gov could not be reached to confirm later amendments.

rules.title: Awarding body must register project (PWC-100) within 30 days of award
rules.plain_english: The awarding body must electronically notify DIR of each public works contract within 30 days after award and no later than the first day any contractor has workers on the job. Contractors cannot file eCPRs until the project is registered.

parameters.latest: first day contractor has workers employed
parameters.jobs_under_PCC_10122_20113_20654_22050: within 30 days after award but no later than last day workers employed

rules.applies_to: Awarding bodies; contractors should confirm project is registered
rules.quote: (a) (1) An awarding body shall provide notice to the Department of Industrial Relations of any public works contract subject to the requirements of this chapter, within 30 days of the award, but in no event later than the first day in which a contractor has workers employed upon the public work.
rules.notes: Statute text read from the official CSLB 2022 Law Book appendix (statutes as published Jan. 2022); leginfo.legislature.ca.gov could not be reached to confirm later amendments. Development proponents (Gov. Code 65852.24, 65912.130, 65913.4) also register projects with DIR.

rules.title: Project registration contents
rules.plain_english: The DIR project notice must include the prime contractor's and listed subcontractors' names and DIR registration numbers, bid and award dates, contract amount, estimated start and completion dates and jobsite location.

parameters.format: electronic via DIR Public Works Website Services

rules.applies_to: Awarding bodies (contractors supply data)
rules.quote: (3) The notice shall be transmitted electronically in a format specified by the department and shall include the name and registration number issued by the Department of Industrial Relations pursuant to Section 1725.5 of the contractor, the name and registration number issued by the Department of Industrial Relations pursuant to Section 1725.5 of any subcontractor listed on the successful bid
rules.notes: Statute text read from the official CSLB 2022 Law Book appendix (statutes as published Jan. 2022); leginfo.legislature.ca.gov could not be reached to confirm later amendments. Unlisted subs can request to join the project in the DIR portal (DIR FAQ).

rules.title: Awarding body penalty: $100/day up to $10,000 per project; contractors cannot be charged
rules.plain_english: An awarding body that fails to register the project, or contracts with/permits an unregistered contractor, faces $100 per day up to $10,000 per project. Contractors are not liable for these penalties and cannot be required to indemnify the awarding body.
rules.applies_to: Awarding bodies; contract reviewers (reject indemnity clauses)
rules.quote: (h) A contractor or subcontractor shall not be liable for any penalties assessed against an awarding body pursuant to this section. An awarding body may not require a contractor or subcontractor to indemnify or otherwise be liable for any penalties assessed against an awarding body pursuant to this section.
rules.notes: Statute text read from the official CSLB 2022 Law Book appendix (statutes as published Jan. 2022); leginfo.legislature.ca.gov could not be reached to confirm later amendments. Two or more willful violations in 12 months: awarding body loses state construction funding for one year (1773.3(g)).

rules.title: Final payment withheld until 30 days after full subcontractor list submitted
rules.plain_english: The awarding body must hold the prime's final payment until at least 30 days after all required project information, including a complete subcontractor list, has been submitted to DIR. Paying early and later finding an unregistered sub exposes it to $100/day up to 100 days per unregistered contractor.
rules.applies_to: Prime contractors (final payment timing) and awarding bodies
rules.quote: (d) An awarding body shall withhold final payment due to the contractor until at least 30 days after all of the required information in paragraph (2) of subdivision (a) has been submitted, including, but not limited to, providing a complete list of all subcontractors.
rules.notes: Statute text read from the official CSLB 2022 Law Book appendix (statutes as published Jan. 2022); leginfo.legislature.ca.gov could not be reached to confirm later amendments. Cash-flow planning: final payment cannot be expected sooner than 30 days after a complete sub list is in DIR's system.

rules.title: Bid and contract documents must state DIR compliance monitoring
rules.plain_english: Calls for bids and contract documents must state that the project is subject to compliance monitoring and enforcement by DIR.

parameters.required_statement: project is subject to compliance monitoring and enforcement by the Department of Industrial Relations

rules.applies_to: Awarding bodies; contractors drafting subcontracts
rules.quote: (1) The call for bids and contract documents shall specify that the project is subject to compliance monitoring and enforcement by the Department of Industrial Relations.
rules.notes: Statute text read from the official CSLB 2022 Law Book appendix (statutes as published Jan. 2022); leginfo.legislature.ca.gov could not be reached to confirm later amendments. Applies to contracts awarded on or after Jan. 1, 2015 (1771.4(c)).

rules.title: Required public works job site postings
rules.plain_english: Each job site must have posted: the Director's prevailing wage determinations for the crafts on the job (one location OK if multiple sites), the DIR compliance monitoring notice, and the payday notice (Labor Code 207). The awarding body posts or requires the prime to post.

postings: DIR prevailing wage rate determination(s) for each craft
DIR/DLSE compliance monitoring (CMU) notice per 8 CCR 16451(d)
notice of paydays and time/place of payment (LC 207)
parameters.who_posts: awarding body or prime contractor if required
parameters.multiple_worksites: may post at one location readily available to all workers

rules.applies_to: Prime contractors and awarding bodies
rules.quote: “This public works project is subject to monitoring and investigative activities by the Compliance Monitoring Unit (CMU) of the Division of Labor Standards Enforcement, Department of Industrial Relations, State of California. This Notice is intended to provide information to all workers employed in the execution of the contract for public work
rules.notes: Full CMU notice text (including blank for local DLSE office phone) is in 8 CCR 16451(d) - a tool can generate it verbatim. LC 1773.2: awarding body 'shall also cause a copy of the determination of the director of the prevailing rate of per diem wages to be posted at each job site.'
rules.correction: None. The quote matches the CMU notice text in 8 CCR 16451(d) verbatim.

rules.title: Prevailing rates must be in (or referenced by) the bid call and contract
rules.plain_english: The awarding body must state the prevailing per diem wage rates for each craft in the call for bids, bid specifications and contract, or state that copies are on file at its principal office and available on request.

parameters.alternative: statement that rates are on file at principal office and available on request

rules.applies_to: Awarding bodies; primes flowing down to subs
rules.quote: The body awarding any contract for public work, or otherwise undertaking any public work, shall specify in the call for bids for the contract, and in the bid specifications and in the contract itself, what the general rate of per diem wages is for each craft, classification, or type of worker needed to execute the contract.
rules.notes: Statute text read from the official CSLB 2022 Law Book appendix (statutes as published Jan. 2022); leginfo.legislature.ca.gov could not be reached to confirm later amendments.

rules.title: Electronic certified payroll (eCPR) to DIR at least every 30 days
rules.plain_english: Every contractor and subcontractor must upload certified payroll records directly to the Labor Commissioner through DIR's portal at least once every 30 days while working, and within 30 days after the last day of work (or more often if the contract says so). Best practice is weekly.

parameters.format: online form or XML upload (V2 schema)

rules.applies_to: All contractors/subcontractors on non-exempt public works
rules.quote: (i) At least monthly or more frequently if specified in the contract with the awarding body. For purposes of this clause, “monthly” means that a submission of records shall be made at least once every 30 days while work is being performed on the project and within 30 days after the final day of work performed on the project.
rules.notes: Statute text read from the official CSLB 2022 Law Book appendix (statutes as published Jan. 2022); leginfo.legislature.ca.gov could not be reached to confirm later amendments. Applies to all contracts, new or ongoing, on or after Jan. 1, 2016 (1771.4(d)).

rules.title: Late eCPRs: $100/day up to $5,000 per project (after 14-day grace)
rules.plain_english: A contractor that fails to submit eCPRs is subject to $100 per day of violation, up to $5,000 per project. The penalty cannot be levied until the records are 14 days past due, and only the contractor that failed to file is liable.

parameters.liable_party: only the contractor/subcontractor that failed to furnish

rules.applies_to: All contractors/subcontractors filing eCPRs
rules.quote: (C) The Labor Commissioner shall not levy a penalty pursuant to subparagraph (B) until a contractor or subcontractor fails to furnish the records pursuant to subparagraph (A) 14 days after the requirement set forth in clause (i) of subparagraph (A).
rules.notes: Statute text read from the official CSLB 2022 Law Book appendix (statutes as published Jan. 2022); leginfo.legislature.ca.gov could not be reached to confirm later amendments. 14-day grace added by AB 1023 (Stats 2021 ch 326), effective 1/1/2022. Penalty amount per (B): 'one hundred dollars ($100) per each day ... not to exceed a total penalty of five thousand dollars ($5,000) per project.'

rules.title: eCPR exemptions: legacy LCPs and qualifying PLAs only
rules.plain_english: Only projects monitored by the four legacy labor compliance programs (Caltrans, City of Los Angeles, LAUSD, County of Sacramento) or covered by a qualifying project labor agreement with a wage dispute mechanism, plus small projects, are exempt from filing eCPRs with DIR.

parameters.exempt_pla: awarding body CBA binding all contractors with wage dispute mechanism

rules.applies_to: Contractors deciding whether eCPRs are needed
rules.citation: Labor Code 1771.4(b); DIR eCPR exemptions page
rules.quote: Only projects monitored and enforced by an approved labor compliance program (LCP) or covered by a qualifying project labor agreement may be exempted from the requirement to submit certified payroll records to DIR.
rules.notes: Exempt contractors still keep CPRs and produce them on request (LC 1776).

rules.title: Sending CPRs to the prime, union, awarding body or LCP does not replace eCPR
rules.plain_english: Each company must submit its own eCPRs directly to DIR; giving payrolls to the prime contractor, a union, the awarding body or an LCP does not satisfy the DIR requirement.
rules.applies_to: All contractors/subcontractors
rules.quote: Yes. Submitting certified payroll records to other agencies does not fulfill the requirement to submit certified payroll records to the Labor Commissioner/DIR.
rules.notes: Prop 84 projects: submit to both DIR and the LCP (DIR FAQ).

rules.title: eCPR filing does not excuse answering a written CPR request (and vice versa)
rules.plain_english: Uploading eCPRs is a separate duty from responding within 10 days to a written request for certified payroll records under LC 1776; eCPRs lack some required A-1-131 information (gross weekly earnings, itemized deductions, etc.).

separate_duties: certified copies on written request within 10 days (LC 1776(d))
parameters.form_for_requests: DIR Form A-1-131 or equivalent with all LC 1776 info

rules.applies_to: All contractors/subcontractors
rules.quote: Thus, a contractor that has electronically furnished eCPRs is not excused from timely furnishing to the Labor Commissioner “a certified copy of all payroll records” within 10 days after receipt of such a written request.
rules.notes: Public Works Manual is an official Labor Commissioner training publication, not binding law.

rules.title: Mark the final eCPR; file Statements of Non-Performance for weeks with no work
rules.plain_english: When filing the last eCPR for a job, answer 'Yes' to the final eCPR question. For payroll weeks with no work, submit a Statement of Non-Performance (statementOfNP=true). Submitted records cannot be deleted; correct them by submitting an amended record for the same period, which takes precedence.

parameters.amendments: new record for same period supersedes; original stays visible

rules.applies_to: All eCPR filers
rules.citation: Labor Code 1771.4; DIR FAQ; eCPR XML Guidelines V2 §5.4-5.5
rules.source: https://www.dir.ca.gov/Public-Works/PublicWorksSB854FAQ.html (Viewing, Correcting, and Amending Records; Completing the Payroll Information Fields); https://www.dir.ca.gov/Public-Works/CPR/eCPR-XML-Guidelines-V2.pdf
rules.quote: Yes. When submitting the final eCPR for a job, select Yes on the submission form’s final eCPR question.
rules.notes: FAQ: 'You cannot change or delete payroll records that have already been submitted (except for non-performance submissions). However, you may correct errors by submitting a new record for the same pay period.'

rules.title: How to report fringes, deductions and mixed public/private pay on eCPRs
rules.plain_english: Report the pre-tax hourly rate. Fringes paid directly to the worker go into the hourly rate; fringes paid to a fund are reported as hourly contribution rates (same for ST/OT/DT). Deductions and payments (e.g., travel/subsistence) are reported as period totals; enter 0 in required fields with no withholding. If a check covers public and private work, report this-project gross and all-work gross.

parameters.fringe_paid_to_plan: report as hourly contribution per classification

rules.applies_to: eCPR preparers / payroll software
rules.citation: DIR FAQ (Completing the Payroll Information Fields)
rules.quote: Whether fringe benefits are included in the hourly rate depends on how they are paid to employees. If paid directly to the worker, include them in the hourly rate. If paid into a fund or to a committee, do not include them in the hourly rate. Indicate them in the contribution section instead.
rules.notes: Notes field is publicly visible - no personal information.

rules.title: eCPR XML V2: PWCR number (10 digits) and DIR project ID are mandatory
rules.plain_english: Every eCPR XML file must carry the contractor's 10-digit PWCR registration number and the numeric DIR project ID exactly as on file; a mismatch is a hard failure. The version element must be 2.0; payrollNum and amendmentNum are left empty.
rules.applies_to: Payroll software generating eCPR XML
rules.citation: Labor Code 1771.4(a)(3)(A)(ii); DIR eCPR XML Guidelines V2 (Nov. 2026)
rules.quote: contractorPWCR is now required and must be exactly 10 numeric digits, matching the PWCR number on file with DIR. The option to enter “NA” has been removed.
rules.notes: Element order must match the XSD exactly or validation fails.

rules.title: eCPR XML V2: weekly structure and hour limits
rules.plain_english: Each payroll week ends on forWeekEnding and covers that date plus the six prior days. Each classification needs exactly seven day elements (id 1-7, id 7 = week-ending date), hours >=0 and <100 with two decimals, and an employee's ST+OT+DT across all classifications may not exceed 24 hours in a day. totHrs must equal the daily sums.
rules.applies_to: Payroll software generating eCPR XML
rules.quote: Each classification must include exactly seven-day elements, one for each day of the payroll week, even if the employee did not work on a given day.

rules.title: eCPR XML V2: preparer-calculated totals (not recalculated by DIR)
rules.plain_english: Total hourly rates must equal the base ST/OT/DT rate plus the sum of fringe amounts for that classification; totalDeductions must equal the sum of fedTax, FICA, stateTax, SDI, fundAdmin, savings, dues and other (excluding travelSubs and fringes). grossThisProject, grossAllWork and netWagePaidWeek are stored as entered.

parameters.totalHrlyPayRate_X: hrlyPayRate_X + healthWelfare + vacationHoliday + pension + training + other
parameters.totalDeductions: fedTax + FICA + stateTax + SDI + fundAdmin + savings + dues + other

rules.applies_to: Payroll software generating eCPR XML
rules.quote: totalDeductions is a source-of-truth field - it is stored directly and is not recalculated by the system. It must equal the sum of all deduction fields above and must not include travelSubs or fringe amounts.
rules.notes: Validation checks a tool should run before upload.

rules.title: eCPR XML V2: employee and classification fields
rules.plain_english: Each employee needs first and last name, street/city/2-letter state/ZIP, and a unique 9-digit SSN or ITIN. Each classification needs the official classification and craft names, employeeLevel ('journeyman' or 'apprentice'), apprenticeLevel 1-10 for apprentices, fringePaid flags (at least one true) and all five fringe amounts (0.0 if none).
rules.applies_to: Payroll software generating eCPR XML
rules.quote: SSN takes priority when both ssn and itin are provided. At least one of ssn or itin must be populated. Each SSN must be unique within the submission - duplicate SSNs will cause the affected employees to be rejected.

rules.title: Certified payroll record contents and declaration
rules.plain_english: Each contractor and subcontractor must keep accurate payroll records showing each worker's name, address, Social Security number, work classification, straight-time and overtime hours each day and week, and actual per diem wages paid, verified under penalty of perjury that it is true and that LC 1771, 1811 and 1815 were complied with.

fields: straight time hours each day and week
overtime hours each day and week
parameters.form: DIR A-1-131 or equivalent printout with same info

rules.applies_to: All public works contractors and subcontractors
rules.quote: (a) Each contractor and subcontractor shall keep accurate payroll records, showing the name, address, social security number, work classification, straight time and overtime hours worked each day and week, and the actual per diem wages paid to each journeyman, apprentice, worker, or other employee employed by the contractor or subcontractor in connection with the public work.
rules.notes: Statute text read from the official CSLB 2022 Law Book appendix (statutes as published Jan. 2022); leginfo.legislature.ca.gov could not be reached to confirm later amendments. Also attach Statement of Employer Payments (DLSE Form PW 26) for fringe credits.

rules.title: Required certification wording for payroll copies
rules.plain_english: Certified payroll copies must carry a signed certification under penalty of perjury that the records are the originals or true, full and correct copies depicting actual disbursements to each worker.

parameters.template: I, [name], the undersigned, am [position] with the authority to act for and on behalf of [business], certify under penalty of perjury that the records or copies thereof submitted and consisting of [description, no. of pages] are the originals or true, full and correct copies of the originals which depict the payroll record(s) of the actual disbursements by way of cash, check, or whatever form to the individual or individuals named. Date: Signature:

rules.applies_to: Contractors furnishing CPR copies
rules.quote: certify under penalty of perjury that the records or copies thereof submitted and consisting of ________________ (description, no. of pages) are the originals or true, full and correct copies of the originals which depict the payroll record(s) of the actual disbursements by way of cash, check, or whatever form to the individual or individuals named.
rules.notes: A public entity may require stricter certification. Electronic CPRs must be non-modifiable with e-signature or printed with original signature (8 CCR 16404(c)).
rules.correction: None. The template wording matches 8 CCR 16401(b).

rules.title: CPRs must use the Director's classification title and full SSNs
rules.plain_english: Payroll records must name the worker's classification exactly as titled in DIR's prevailing wage determination (e.g., 'Laborer Group 1'), not just 'journeyman' or 'apprentice', and must include the full Social Security number (a separate sworn SSN report is accepted).
rules.applies_to: Payroll preparers
rules.source: https://www.dir.ca.gov/dlse/PWManualCombined.pdf (Public Works Manual Oct 2023, §3.1 and §3.1.13, manual pp. 13, 21)
rules.quote: Payroll records which do not identify the Director’s specified title (e.g., records which only identify a worker by status, such as “journeyperson” or “apprentice” or “partner,” and do not refer to the Director’s published classification, such as “Laborer Group 1” or “Carpenter”) are inadequate.
rules.notes: Unlike LC 226 wage statements (last 4 SSN digits), LC 1776 requires the full SSN.

rules.title: Produce certified payroll within 10 days of a written request
rules.plain_english: When the awarding body, DLSE or DAS asks in writing, you must file certified copies of your payroll records within 10 days (calendar) of receiving the request. Workers can also request their own records.

requesters: public via awarding body or DLSE

rules.applies_to: All public works contractors and subcontractors
rules.quote: (d) A contractor or subcontractor shall file a certified copy of the records enumerated in subdivision (a) with the entity that requested the records within 10 days after receipt of a written request.
rules.notes: Statute text read from the official CSLB 2022 Law Book appendix (statutes as published Jan. 2022); leginfo.legislature.ca.gov could not be reached to confirm later amendments.

rules.title: Late payroll records: $100 per worker per calendar day
rules.plain_english: If you miss the 10-day deadline for requested payroll records, you forfeit $100 for each calendar day (or part) for each worker until you fully comply; DLSE can have it withheld from progress payments. A prime is not penalized for its sub's failure.
rules.applies_to: All public works contractors and subcontractors
rules.quote: In the event that the contractor or subcontractor fails to comply within the 10-day period, the contractor or subcontractor shall, as a penalty to the state or political subdivision on whose behalf the contract is made or awarded, forfeit one hundred dollars ($100) for each calendar day, or portion thereof, for each worker, until strict compliance is effectuated.
rules.notes: Statute text read from the official CSLB 2022 Law Book appendix (statutes as published Jan. 2022); leginfo.legislature.ca.gov could not be reached to confirm later amendments. 8 CCR 16400(d)(2)(B) still recites an older $25/day figure; statute ($100) controls. SB 909 (Ch. 660, Stats. 2026, chaptered 9/27/2026) amends LC 1725.5, 1771.3, 1775, 1776 and 1777.7 and PCC 2603 per its chaptered title on leginfo (LC 1741 and 1813 appeared only in earlier versions). Final amounts and operative date NOT verified - re-check before 2027.
rules.correction: None. FLAG: SB 909 (Ch. 660, Stats. 2026, chaptered 9/27/2026) amends LC 1725.5, 1771.3, 1775, 1776 and 1777.7 and PCC 2603, per its chaptered title as shown in leginfo search excerpts. The chaptered text and its operative date were not read. The amount here is current law as of 2026-11-25. Re-check it against Ch. 660 before 2027. (An earlier version of SB 909 proposed $140; the chaptered amount was not seen.)

rules.title: Tell the awarding body where payroll records are kept (5 working days for changes)
rules.plain_english: The contractor must tell the awarding body the street address, city and county where its payroll records are kept and give notice of any change of location within five working days.
rules.applies_to: Prime contractors
rules.quote: (g) The contractor shall inform the body awarding the contract of the location of the records enumerated under subdivision (a), including the street address, city, and county, and shall, within five working days, provide a notice of a change of location and address.
rules.notes: Statute text read from the official CSLB 2022 Law Book appendix (statutes as published Jan. 2022); leginfo.legislature.ca.gov could not be reached to confirm later amendments.

rules.title: Public requests for payroll: redaction and copying fees
rules.plain_english: Public requests for certified payroll go through the awarding body or DLSE, never directly to the contractor's office. Copies given to the public must black out workers' names, addresses and SSNs (not the contractor's name). The requester prepays $1 for the first page, $0.25 per additional page, plus $10 handling to the contractor.

parameters.taft_hartley_trust: redact only to last 4 SSN digits

rules.applies_to: Contractors receiving public CPR requests
rules.quote: Such cost shall be $1 for the first page of the payroll record and 25 cents for each page thereafter, plus $10 to the contractor or subcontractor for handling costs. Payment in the form of cash, check or certified money order shall be made prior to release of the documents to cover the actual costs of preparation.
rules.notes: Public entity keeps received records at least 6 months after project completion and acceptance (16403(a)).

rules.title: Payroll record retention
rules.plain_english: Unregistered small-project contractors must keep certified payroll records at least 3 years after completing the work. For other projects the prevailing wage law sets no specific period; DLSE advises keeping them for the full limitations period (e.g., 18 months after notice of completion for assessments) and complying with general Labor Code/IWC record rules.
rules.applies_to: All public works contractors
rules.source: https://www.dir.ca.gov/dlse/PWManualCombined.pdf (Public Works Manual Oct 2023, §3.1.14, manual p. 22); https://www.cslb.ca.gov/Resources/GuidesAndPublications/LawReferenceBook2022.pdf PDF page 961
rules.quote: There is no provision in the prevailing wage laws which specifies a records retention period for CPRs or all of the types of “payroll records” as defined and listed at 8 CCR § 16000. The limitations period for legally recognized wage underpayment remedies available against public works contractors, however, vary depending upon the remedy available.
rules.notes: CSLB B&P 7111 separately requires keeping project records 5 years after completion (see lawbook research). General Labor Code payroll records: 3 years (see labor-hr research).

rules.title: Failing to produce payroll within 30 days of debarment notice: 1-3 year debarment
rules.plain_english: If you don't respond to a payroll request, the Labor Commissioner will notify you that you face debarment unless the records are produced within 30 days of receiving that notice; failing that (absent circumstances beyond your control), you are barred from public works for 1 to 3 years.
rules.applies_to: Contractors who ignore CPR requests
rules.quote: the Labor Commissioner shall notify the contractor or subcontractor that, in addition to any other penalties provided by law, the contractor or subcontractor will be subject to debarment under this section if the certified payroll records are not produced within 30 days after receipt of the written notice.
rules.notes: Statute text read from the official CSLB 2022 Law Book appendix (statutes as published Jan. 2022); leginfo.legislature.ca.gov could not be reached to confirm later amendments.

rules.title: Statement of Employer Payments (Form PW 26) for fringe credits
rules.plain_english: If you take credit for fringe benefit payments against the prevailing wage, document them on DLSE Form PW 26 (Statement of Employer Payments) along with the A-1-131 payroll form; accurate completion of both is presumptive compliance on CMU-monitored projects.

parameters.companion_form: DIR Form A-1-131 Public Works Payroll Reporting Form

rules.applies_to: Contractors claiming fringe/employer payment credits
rules.quote: Payroll records shall be furnished in a format prescribed by section 16401 of Title 8 of the California Code of Regulations, with use of the current version of DIR’s “Public Works Payroll Reporting Form” (A-1-131) and “Statement of Employer Payments” (DLSE Form PW26) constituting presumptive compliance with this requirement
rules.notes: 16461 applies to CMU-fee projects; DLSE also encloses A-1-131 and PW 26 with every written CPR request (Manual §3.1.5).

rules.title: Ready-mix concrete haulers: written subcontract requiring prevailing wage compliance
rules.plain_english: A company hauling/delivering ready-mixed concrete to a public works project must have a written subcontract agreement with whoever engaged it that requires compliance with the prevailing wage chapter; it is a subcontractor only for prevailing wage purposes (must register, pay prevailing wages, file eCPRs).

parameters.must_require: compliance with Labor Code Part 7, Chapter 1 (public works)
parameters.status: subcontractor solely for prevailing wage chapter

rules.applies_to: Ready-mix suppliers and the contractors who order from them
rules.quote: (e) The entity hauling or delivering ready-mixed concrete to carry out a public works contract shall enter into a written subcontract agreement with the party that engaged the entity to supply the ready-mixed concrete. The written agreement shall require compliance with the requirements of this chapter.
rules.notes: Statute text read from the official CSLB 2022 Law Book appendix (statutes as published Jan. 2022); leginfo.legislature.ca.gov could not be reached to confirm later amendments. DIR FAQ: an invoice or purchase order with the required statutory language may suffice.

rules.title: Ready-mix: certified payroll to engaging party and GC within 5 working days
rules.plain_english: The ready-mix hauler must give certified payroll copies to the party that engaged it and to the general contractor within five working days after the employee is paid, with a time record certified by each driver.
rules.applies_to: Ready-mix concrete suppliers on public works
rules.quote: (f) The entity hauling or delivering ready-mixed concrete to carry out a public works contract shall submit a certified copy of the payroll records required by subdivision (a) of Section 1776 to the party that engaged the entity and to the general contractor within five working days after the employee has been paid, accompanied by a written time record that shall be certified by each driver
rules.notes: Statute text read from the official CSLB 2022 Law Book appendix (statutes as published Jan. 2022); leginfo.legislature.ca.gov could not be reached to confirm later amendments. DIR FAQ: no statutory penalty for missing the 5 days; contract may impose one.

rules.title: Ready-mix: rate from the plant's area; covers loading through return trip
rules.plain_english: Ready-mix drivers are paid the 'Driver - Mixer Trucks' prevailing rate for the area where the plant is located, from receiving concrete at the plant until returning to the plant (intermediate private stops included).

parameters.covered_time: receipt of concrete at plant through return to plant

rules.applies_to: Ready-mix suppliers
rules.quote: (d) For purposes of this section, the applicable prevailing wage rate shall be the current prevailing wage, as determined by the director, for the geographic area in which the factory or batching plant is located.
rules.notes: Statute text read from the official CSLB 2022 Law Book appendix (statutes as published Jan. 2022); leginfo.legislature.ca.gov could not be reached to confirm later amendments.

rules.title: Prevailing wage determinations: issued Feb 22 / Aug 22, effective 10 days later
rules.plain_english: DIR issues general prevailing wage determinations twice a year, on February 22 and August 22. Each takes effect 10 days after its issue date (generally March 4 (March 3 in leap years) and September 1).
rules.applies_to: Bidders, estimators, payroll
rules.quote: General determinations are issued twice a year on February 22 and August 22.
rules.notes: FAQ A10: effective date 'is 10 days after the issue date of the determination.' Rates: https://www.dir.ca.gov/OPRL/DPreWageDetermination.htm

rules.title: Which rates apply: those in effect on the bid advertisement date
rules.plain_english: Use the determination in effect on the date the awarding body first advertised for bids (or, if not bid, the first written agreement/funding contract). A later change in the Director's rates does not apply to a contract whose notice to bidders was already published (but see predetermined increases and the 2027 large-project rule).

parameters.rate_lock_event: bid advertisement date (first published notice inviting bids)
parameters.fallback_event_if_not_bid: first written memorialization of agreement or funding contract

rules.applies_to: Estimators and payroll on public works
rules.citation: Labor Code 1773.6; 8 CCR 16000 ('Date of Notice or Call for Bids')
rules.quote: For the Labor Commissioner’s enforcement purposes, if the effective date of a determination is on or after the bid advertisement date but before the listed expiration date, the rates listed on that particular determination constitute the prevailing wage rates for work performed under that public works contract.
rules.notes: Statute text read from the official CSLB 2022 Law Book appendix (statutes as published Jan. 2022); leginfo.legislature.ca.gov could not be reached to confirm later amendments. LC 1773.6: a Director's change 'shall not be effective as to any contract for which the notice to bidders has been published.' See rule ab1198-mid-project-rate-changes-35m (not verified).

rules.title: Double-asterisk determinations: pay scheduled increases mid-project
rules.plain_english: If a determination's expiration date has two asterisks (**), predetermined increases to base rates, overtime, holiday pay and employer payments must be paid for work after that date - build them into bids. A single asterisk (*) means the rates stay in effect for the life of the project.

parameters.double_asterisk: predetermined increases must be paid after expiration date; new rate effective day after expiration date
parameters.single_asterisk: rates in effect at bid advertisement apply for life of project

rules.applies_to: Estimators and payroll
rules.citation: 8 CCR 16000 ('Predetermined Changes'); DIR Prevailing Wage FAQ
rules.quote: Prevailing wage determinations with double asterisks after the expiration date indicate that the basic hourly wage rate, overtime, holiday pay rates and employers' payments for work performed after this date have been predetermined. If work is to extend past this date, the new rates must be paid and should be incorporated in contracts entered into now.
rules.notes: Predetermined increases are posted on DIR's OD-Research pages.

rules.title: Special wage determination request: 45 days before bid advertisement
rules.plain_english: If a needed craft or classification is not covered by a general determination, the awarding body should request a special determination at least 45 days before the bid advertisement date.
rules.applies_to: Awarding bodies; contractors spotting missing classifications
rules.quote: (B) If a wage rate for a craft, classification or type of worker is not published in the Director's general prevailing wage determinations, a request for a special determination should be made by the awarding body to Chief, Division of Labor Statistics and Research, P.O. Box 420603, San Francisco, CA 94142, at least 45 days prior to the project bid advertisement date.

rules.title: Petition to review a wage rate within 20 days after bid advertising starts
rules.plain_english: A prospective bidder, union representative or the awarding body may file a verified petition with the DIR Director within 20 days after bid advertising begins, copying the awarding body within 2 days. The Director decides within 20 days, and the bid closing is extended until 5 days after the determination.
rules.applies_to: Prospective bidders
rules.quote: Any prospective bidder or his representative, any representative of any craft, classification or type of workman involved, or the awarding body may, within 20 days after commencement of advertising of the call for bids by the awarding body, file with the Director of Industrial Relations a verified petition to review the determination of any such rate or rates
rules.notes: Statute text read from the official CSLB 2022 Law Book appendix (statutes as published Jan. 2022); leginfo.legislature.ca.gov could not be reached to confirm later amendments. AB 1198 (2026) reportedly creates a new 20-day petition process - not verified.
rules.correction: None. FLAG: leginfo search excerpts show that AB 1198 (Ch. 513, Stats. 2026) adds a separate 20-day verified-petition process for newly published determinations. That chaptered text was not read.

rules.title: Large projects ($35M+): mid-project prevailing wage changes from July 1, 2027 (reported)
rules.plain_english: Reported new law: starting July 1, 2027, changes in prevailing wage rates apply mid-project to public works prime contracts awarded at $35 million or more, instead of staying fixed at bid-time rates. Who bears the cost is not addressed.
rules.applies_to: Contractors bidding very large public works
rules.citation: Labor Code 1773.6 et seq. as amended by AB 1198 (2026) - unverified
rules.notes: From web-search summary of a law-firm alert and bill trackers; chaptered text not read (leginfo unreachable). Do not rely on threshold or date until verified against Ch. 513, Stats. 2026.
rules.correction: Not refuted. Leginfo excerpts report that the bill was chaptered as Ch. 513, Stats. 2026 (approved 9/27/2026). Starting July 1, 2027, a new determination applies to contracts awarded or advertised after that date with an awarded value of $35,000,000 or more. This matches the rule's parameters, but the chaptered text was not read, so the rule stays unverifiable.

rules.title: Public works overtime: over 8 hours/day or 40 hours/week at 1.5x
rules.plain_english: Work on public works over 8 hours in a day or 40 hours in a week must be paid at least 1.5 times the basic rate, or the higher overtime rate in the wage determination (some crafts trigger overtime sooner, e.g., 7/35).
rules.applies_to: All public works employers
rules.quote: Labor Code § 1815 requires that work performed on public works projects in excess of 8 hours per day, or 40 hours per week, must be compensated at not less than time and one-half the basic rate of pay. Failure to pay the appropriate overtime rates subject the contractor to penalties pursuant to Labor Code § 1813.
rules.notes: LC 1810, 1811 and 1815 text read in the DIR compilation (rev. Feb. 1, 2025) PDF pp.194-195. LC 1815 expressly requires 1.5x for hours over 8 per day; the weekly 40-hour trigger is stated in 8 CCR 16100(b)(8) and the DLSE Public Works Manual (and LC 1811/1813).
rules.correction: None. LC 1815 itself expressly requires 1.5x only for hours over 8 per day. The 40-hour weekly trigger rests on 8 CCR 16100(b)(8), LC 1811/1813 and the DLSE Manual, all of which state it.

rules.title: Limited exceptions to weekend overtime
rules.plain_english: No overtime is owed for the first 8 hours on Saturday or Sunday only if (1) a non-Monday-Friday workweek is a fixed business practice on all your jobs or required by the awarding body, (2) the CBA allows straight-time weekend work, or (3) the awarding body finds off-hours work necessary; otherwise follow the determination.

exceptions: fixed business practice/awarding body requires non Mon-Fri workweek: first 8 hrs Sat/Sun straight time
CBA provides Sat/Sun straight time: first 8 hrs
awarding body determines off-hours work necessary: no OT first 8 hrs/day and 40 hrs/week
no OT under 8/day or 40/week unless CBA basis requires

rules.applies_to: Public works employers scheduling weekend work
rules.quote: If a workweek other than Monday through Friday is a fixed business practice or is required by the awarding body, no overtime payment is required for the first eight hours on Saturday or Sunday.
rules.notes: Saturday make-up day exceptions apply only if written into the determination itself (Manual §4.1.9).

rules.title: Alternative workweek schedules don't avoid daily overtime on public works
rules.plain_english: Even workers on a 4/10 alternative workweek or under a CBA must get overtime for hours over 8 in a day on public works.
rules.applies_to: Contractors using 4/10 or other AWS schedules
rules.citation: Labor Code 1810, 1811, 1815; Cal. Const. art. XIV §2
rules.quote: Accordingly, no worker may be employed on a public works project for more than eight hours a day unless the worker receives the overtime compensation specified by the applicable prevailing wage determination.

rules.title: Overtime when a worker works two classifications or projects in a day
rules.plain_english: All hours in a day count toward overtime; overtime hours are paid at the overtime rate for the classification being worked during those hours. For mixed public/private days, public-work overtime uses the higher of the prevailing rate or weighted average.

parameters.ot_rate: classification worked during the OT hours
parameters.public_private_mix: higher of weighted-average regular rate or prevailing rate
parameters.example: 4h Inside Wireman ST + 4h Painter ST + 2h Painter OT

rules.applies_to: Payroll for multi-craft or mixed public/private crews
rules.citation: Labor Code 1815; DLSE Public Works Manual
rules.quote: In the situation where a worker performs work during the same workday in two or more different classifications with different rates of pay, the worker must be paid the overtime rate in effect for the type of work he or she is performing during those overtime hours.

rules.title: Travel time is paid at the prevailing rate; travel/subsistence payments per determination
rules.plain_english: Employer-required travel after the first reporting place (yard to site, site to site) is hours worked paid at the prevailing rate for the work performed. Separately, many determinations require fixed daily travel and/or subsistence payments - check the footnotes.

parameters.travel_time_rate: prevailing rate for work performed at site unless determination sets lower travel rate
parameters.travel_subsistence_payments: fixed daily amounts per CBA footnotes on determination

rules.applies_to: Public works employers
rules.citation: Labor Code 1773.1(a)(4)-(5); DLSE Public Works Manual
rules.quote: All such compensable travel time must be paid at the same prevailing wage rate required for the work actually performed by the worker at the public works site.
rules.notes: Report travel/subsistence on eCPR as travelSubs (not a deduction).

rules.title: Fringe credits cannot reduce the basic hourly rate
rules.plain_english: Employer payments (health, pension, vacation, training, etc.) count toward the total prevailing wage package, but they can never reduce the straight-time or overtime basic hourly rate shown in the determination; no credit for benefits required by other law.

no_credit_for: benefits required by other state/federal law
industry advancement fees not under obligated CBA

rules.applies_to: Contractors paying fringes to plans
rules.quote: (c) Employer payments are a credit against the obligation to pay the general prevailing rate of per diem wages. However, credit shall not be granted for benefits required to be provided by other state or federal law,
rules.notes: Statute text read from the official CSLB 2022 Law Book appendix (statutes as published Jan. 2022); leginfo.legislature.ca.gov could not be reached to confirm later amendments. Same subdivision: 'Credits for employer payments also shall not reduce the obligation to pay the hourly straight time or overtime wages found to be prevailing.'

rules.title: Fringe credit allowed if contributions are made at least quarterly
rules.plain_english: You may take credit for employer payments even if they are not paid in the same pay period, as long as you regularly make the contributions at least quarterly.
rules.applies_to: Contractors claiming fringe credits
rules.quote: (d) An employer may take credit for an employer payment specified in subdivision (b), even if contributions are not made, or costs are not paid, during the same pay period for which credit is taken, if the employer regularly makes the contributions, or regularly pays the costs, for the plan, fund, or program on no less than a quarterly basis.
rules.notes: Statute text read from the official CSLB 2022 Law Book appendix (statutes as published Jan. 2022); leginfo.legislature.ca.gov could not be reached to confirm later amendments.

rules.title: Annualize fringe credits when public-job contributions exceed private-job ones
rules.plain_english: If you pay higher benefit contributions on public jobs than on private jobs, the credit must be annualized: divide annual plan cost by total hours worked on all jobs (DLSE accepts 2,080 hours unless the worker worked more). Exceptions: enforceable obligation for future private work, PLA requirement, CAC payments, or Director waiver.

exceptions: enforceable obligation to pay higher rate on future private work
required by project labor agreement
payments to California Apprenticeship Council
Director determination

rules.applies_to: Open-shop contractors claiming health/pension credits
rules.quote: (e) The credit for employer payments shall be computed on an annualized basis when the employer seeks credit for employer payments that are higher for public works projects than for private construction performed by the same employer,
rules.notes: Statute text read from the official CSLB 2022 Law Book appendix (statutes as published Jan. 2022); leginfo.legislature.ca.gov could not be reached to confirm later amendments. Manual: 'It is not considered a violation if the contractor uses the full year equivalent of 2,080 (40 hours x 52 weeks) hours ... unless ... the affected employee worked more than 2,080 hours'.

rules.title: Underpaying prevailing wages: up to $200 per worker per day
rules.plain_english: For each worker paid less than the prevailing rate, the contractor and sub forfeit up to $200 per calendar day (or part). Minimums: $40 (unless a good-faith mistake promptly corrected), $80 if penalized in the prior 3 years, $120 if willful. Back wages are also owed and wages are satisfied before penalties.

parameters.plus: difference between prevailing and paid wages to each worker

rules.applies_to: Prime contractors and subcontractors
rules.quote: forfeit not more than two hundred dollars ($200) for each calendar day, or portion thereof, for each worker paid less than the prevailing wage rates as determined by the director for the work or craft in which the worker is employed for any public work done under the contract by the contractor or, except as provided in subdivision (b), by any subcontractor under the contractor.
rules.notes: Statute text read from the official CSLB 2022 Law Book appendix (statutes as published Jan. 2022); leginfo.legislature.ca.gov could not be reached to confirm later amendments. SB 909 (Ch. 660, Stats. 2026, chaptered 9/27/2026) amends LC 1725.5, 1771.3, 1775, 1776 and 1777.7 and PCC 2603 per its chaptered title on leginfo (LC 1741 and 1813 appeared only in earlier versions). Final amounts and operative date NOT verified - re-check before 2027. (SB 909 analyses mention raising $200/$120 maximum/minimums - e.g., to $280/$168 - unverified.)
rules.correction: None. $200 max and $40/$80/$120 minimums match current text. FLAG: SB 909 (Ch. 660, Stats. 2026, chaptered 9/27/2026) amends LC 1725.5, 1771.3, 1775, 1776 and 1777.7 and PCC 2603, per its chaptered title as shown in leginfo search excerpts. The chaptered text and its operative date were not read. The amount here is current law as of 2026-11-25. Re-check it against Ch. 660 before 2027. The chaptered LC 1775 excerpt shows a $56 minimum, which implies roughly 1.4x increases (for example $280/$112/$168).

rules.title: Overtime violations: $25 per worker per day (mandatory)
rules.plain_english: For each worker each calendar day the worker is required or permitted to work over 8 hours in a day or 40 in a week without proper overtime, the contractor forfeits $25. The Labor Commissioner cannot waive or reduce it.

parameters.trigger: work over 8 hrs/day or 40 hrs/week without required OT pay

rules.applies_to: Public works employers
rules.quote: The dollar amount of this penalty is fixed at $25.00 for each worker for each calendar day during which the worker is required or permitted to work more than eight hours in any one calendar day or 40 hours in any one calendar week.
rules.notes: LC 1813 text read in the DIR compilation (rev. Feb. 1, 2025) PDF p.194; matches the DLSE Public Works Manual (Oct 2023). SB 909 (Ch. 660, Stats. 2026, chaptered 9/27/2026) amends LC 1725.5, 1771.3, 1775, 1776 and 1777.7 and PCC 2603 per its chaptered title on leginfo (LC 1741 and 1813 appeared only in earlier versions). Final amounts and operative date NOT verified - re-check before 2027. (An earlier SB 909 version proposed $25 -> $35; the chaptered title does not list LC 1813, so $25 appears unchanged - chaptered text not read.)
rules.correction: None to parameters. The $25 per worker per day figure matches the statute text. The note was corrected: SB 909's chaptered title does not list LC 1813. The $25 to $35 change appeared only in an earlier version, so $25 appears unchanged (chaptered text not read).

rules.title: Subcontracts must include LC 1771, 1775, 1776, 1777.5, 1813 and 1815
rules.plain_english: To avoid penalties for a sub's prevailing wage underpayment, the prime must meet all of LC 1775(b). Its written subcontract must include a copy of Labor Code sections 1771, 1775, 1776, 1777.5, 1813 and 1815. It must also monitor the sub's certified payrolls periodically and take diligent corrective action when it learns of underpayment, including retaining funds due the sub. Before final payment it must get the sub's affidavit, under penalty of perjury, that prevailing wages and any 1813 amounts were paid. The safe harbor is lost if the prime knew of the underpayment.

parameters.where: contract between prime and each subcontractor
other_safe_harbor_conditions: periodic review of the sub's certified payroll records (1775(b)(2))
diligent corrective action on becoming aware of underpayment, including retaining sufficient funds due the sub (1775(b)(3))
before final payment, sub's affidavit under penalty of perjury that prevailing wages and LC 1813 amounts were paid (1775(b)(4))

rules.applies_to: Prime contractors (and upper-tier subs)
rules.quote: (1) The contract executed between the contractor and the subcontractor for the performance of work on the public works project shall include a copy of the provisions of this section and Sections 1771, 1776, 1777.5, 1813, and 1815.
rules.notes: Statute text read from the official CSLB 2022 Law Book appendix (statutes as published Jan. 2022); leginfo.legislature.ca.gov could not be reached to confirm later amendments. Safe harbor does not apply if prime knew of the underpayment; prime remains jointly liable for wages, 1813 penalties and liquidated damages.
rules.correction: Incomplete. Under LC 1775(b), the prime escapes penalties for a sub's underpayment only if it meets all four requirements: (1) the clauses; (2) periodic review of the sub's CPRs; (3) diligent corrective action, including retaining funds; and (4) the sub's affidavit under penalty of perjury before final payment. The safe harbor is lost if the prime had knowledge. The rule implied the clauses alone suffice. The missing conditions were added to parameters and plain_english. The section list (1771, 1775, 1776, 1777.5, 1813, 1815) is confirmed.

rules.title: Prime must monitor sub payroll, act on violations, and get a sworn affidavit before final payment
rules.plain_english: The prime must periodically review each sub's certified payroll, take corrective action (including withholding funds) on discovering underpayment, and before final payment obtain the sub's affidavit under penalty of perjury that it paid prevailing wages and any 1813 amounts.

steps: periodic review of sub certified payrolls
diligent corrective action incl. retaining sufficient funds
affidavit under penalty of perjury before final payment
affidavit_contents: sub paid general prevailing rate of per diem wages to employees on the project
sub paid any amounts due under LC 1813
parameters.timing: prior to final payment to subcontractor

rules.applies_to: Prime contractors
rules.quote: (4) Prior to making final payment to the subcontractor for work performed on the public works project, the contractor shall obtain an affidavit signed under penalty of perjury from the subcontractor that the subcontractor has paid the specified general prevailing rate of per diem wages to his or her employees on the public works project and any amounts due pursuant to Section 1813.
rules.notes: Statute text read from the official CSLB 2022 Law Book appendix (statutes as published Jan. 2022); leginfo.legislature.ca.gov could not be reached to confirm later amendments. A tool can generate this affidavit and block final sub payment until it is on file.

rules.title: DLSE notifies the prime within 15 days of a complaint about a sub
rules.plain_english: When DLSE receives a complaint that a subcontractor is underpaying prevailing wages, it must notify the prime contractor within 15 days - a trigger for the prime's corrective-action duty.

parameters.trigger: DLSE receipt of complaint about subcontractor underpayment

rules.applies_to: Prime contractors
rules.quote: (c) The Division of Labor Standards Enforcement shall notify the contractor on a public works project within 15 days of the receipt by the Division of Labor Standards Enforcement of a complaint of the failure of a subcontractor on that public works project to pay workers the general prevailing rate of per diem wages.
rules.notes: Statute text read from the official CSLB 2022 Law Book appendix (statutes as published Jan. 2022); leginfo.legislature.ca.gov could not be reached to confirm later amendments.

rules.title: Prime and subs are jointly and severally liable for unpaid prevailing wages
rules.plain_english: Contractors and subcontractors share responsibility for all money due from a violation; even a prime that meets the 1775(b) safe harbor remains liable for its subs' unpaid wages, 1813 penalties and liquidated damages.
rules.applies_to: Prime contractors
rules.quote: Contractors and subcontractors share monetary responsibility (known as joint and several liability) for all monies due as a result of a violation.
rules.notes: LC 1784 lets a private-job contractor recover costs from its hiring party in limited cases.

rules.title: No wage kickbacks or fees for hiring/registration on public works
rules.plain_english: Contractors may not take back any part of workers' wages (kickbacks) or charge fees for registering anyone for public work or filling work orders.

prohibited: taking/receiving any portion of workers' wages (LC 1778)
fees for registering persons for public work (LC 1779)
fees for filling work orders (LC 1780)

rules.applies_to: All public works contractors
rules.quote: (6) The prohibition against accepting or extracting kickback from employee wages under Labor Code Section 1778; (7) The prohibition against accepting fees for registering any person for public work under Labor Code Section 1779; or for filling work orders on public works under Labor Code Section 1780;
rules.notes: Statute text not read; prohibition confirmed by DIR regulation checklist. DIR lists 'Demands that worker pay wage kickbacks' as a common violation.

rules.title: Workers' compensation: required clause and signed certification before starting work
rules.plain_english: Every public works contract must require the contractor to secure workers' compensation for employees (LC 3700), and the contractor must sign and file a certification with the awarding body before starting work.

parameters.certification_text_reported: I am aware of the provisions of Section 3700 of the Labor Code which require every employer to be insured against liability for workers' compensation or to undertake self-insurance in accordance with the provisions of that code, and I will comply with such provisions before commencing the performance of the work of this contract.

rules.applies_to: All public works contractors
rules.source: DIR 'California Prevailing Wage Laws' (rev. Feb. 1, 2025) https://www.dir.ca.gov/public-works/CaliforniaPrevailingWageLaws.pdf PDF p.195 (LC 1860, 1861); https://www.dir.ca.gov/t8/16100.html (c)(3)
rules.quote: Each contractor to whom a public works contract is awarded shall sign and file with the awarding body the following certification prior to performing the work of the contract: “I am aware of the provisions of Section 3700 of the Labor Code which require every employer to be insured against liability for workers' compensation or to undertake self-insurance in accordance with the provisions of that code, and I will comply with such provisions before commencing the performance of the work of this contract.”
rules.notes: LC 1861 wording verified on 2026-11-25 against the DIR compilation of prevailing wage laws (rev. Feb. 1, 2025) and safe to generate verbatim. LC 1860 requires the awarding body to insert a workers' comp clause (LC 3700) in every public works contract. Also 8 CCR 16100(c)(3).
rules.correction: None. The reported certification wording matches LC 1861 verbatim. The statute text was added as verbatim_quote, read_from_primary_text was set to true, and the source was updated. LC 1861 says 'prior to performing the work of the contract'.

rules.title: Prejob conference labor-law checklist and subcontractor acknowledgment
rules.plain_english: Awarding bodies (especially with labor compliance programs) review a standard list of labor requirements at the prejob conference and may have each subcontractor sign an acknowledgment that it was informed of them.

parameters.acknowledgment: I acknowledge that I have been informed and am aware of the foregoing requirements and that I am authorized to make this certification on behalf of [name of subcontractor].

rules.applies_to: Prime contractors and subcontractors at prejob meetings
rules.quote: I acknowledge that I have been informed and am aware of the foregoing requirements and that I am authorized to make this certification on behalf of [name of subcontractor].
rules.notes: Labeled 'Suggested Checklist'; useful template for document generation.

rules.title: Apprenticeship duties apply on public works of $30,000 or more
rules.plain_english: On public works contracts of $30,000 or more, every contractor and subcontractor employing workers in an apprenticeable craft must meet the apprenticeship requirements, even if its own subcontract is under $30,000. General contractors (and specialty primes) with contracts under $30,000 are exempt.

exempt_when: federal project with no state/local funds not administered by state agency
sole proprietor who worked alone with no employees

rules.applies_to: All contractors/subcontractors on public works
rules.quote: (o) This section does not apply to contracts of general contractors or to contracts of specialty contractors not bidding for work through a general or prime contractor when the contracts of general contractors or those specialty contractors involve less than thirty thousand dollars ($30,000).
rules.notes: Statute text read from the official CSLB 2022 Law Book appendix (statutes as published Jan. 2022); leginfo.legislature.ca.gov could not be reached to confirm later amendments. DAS FAQ: training fund contributions are still owed on projects under $30,000 (paid to employee only if exempt).
rules.correction: None. The federal-funds exemption matches the DAS FAQ. The sole-proprietor item is not an enumerated exemption; it follows from LC 1777.5(d), which applies only when the contractor 'employs workers'.

rules.title: DAS 140 contract award information: within 10 days of contract execution
rules.plain_english: Send contract award information (DAS 140 or equivalent written notice) to the applicable apprenticeship committee(s) within 10 days after your prime contract or subcontract is executed, and no later than the first day you have workers on the job. Failure is a continuing violation until the notice of completion.

parameters.latest: first day contractor has workers employed on the public work
parameters.dlse_enforcement_deadline: first day a journeyperson in that craft works for the contractor
parameters.continuing_violation_until: awarding body files Notice of Completion

rules.applies_to: All contractors/subcontractors on public works >= $30,000
rules.quote: The information shall be provided to the applicable apprenticeship committee within ten (10) days of the date of the execution of the prime contract or subcontract, but in no event later than the first day in which the contractor has workers employed upon the public work.
rules.notes: DAS FAQ: sending DAS 140/142 after the project ends does not eliminate penalties. Exempt contractors under 1777.5(j)/(k) certificates still must send DAS 140.

rules.title: Who gets the DAS 140
rules.plain_english: If you are already approved to train apprentices, send it to your apprenticeship committee for the craft; if not, send it to every apprenticeship committee whose area covers the job site, for each craft you will use. Do not send it to DAS.

parameters.approved_to_train: your committee(s) for each craft in area
parameters.not_approved: ALL applicable committees in geographic area for each craft

form_boxes.2: comply with a committee's standards for this job only
form_boxes.3: follow California Apprenticeship Council regulations (1:5 min and max)

rules.applies_to: All contractors/subcontractors on covered public works
rules.quote: Contractors who are not already approved to train by an apprenticeship program sponsor shall provide contract award information to all of the applicable apprenticeship committees whose geographic area of operation includes the area of the public works project.

rules.title: DAS 140 required contents
rules.plain_english: The contract award notice must state: contractor name, address, phone and license number; awarding body name and address; exact job location; contract award date; expected start date; estimated journeyman hours; number of apprentices to be employed; and approximate dates they will be employed.

fields: awarding body full name and address
exact location of public work site
number of apprentices to be employed
approximate dates apprentices will be employed

rules.applies_to: Contractors preparing DAS 140
rules.quote: (1) the contractor's name, address, telephone number and state license number; (2) full name and address of the public work awarding body; (3) the exact location of the public work site; (4) date of the contract award; (5) expected start date of the work; (6) estimated journeyman hours; (7) number of apprentices to be employed; (8) approximate dates apprentices will be employed;
rules.notes: DAS 140 is not a dispatch request; a separate DAS 142 is required.

rules.title: DAS 142 apprentice dispatch request: written, at least 72 hours ahead
rules.plain_english: If you don't already employ enough registered apprentices, request dispatch in writing (first-class mail, fax or email) from the apprenticeship committees for the craft at least 72 hours (excluding Saturdays, Sundays and holidays) before you need them. If one committee doesn't dispatch, request from each other committee in the area.

parameters.escalation: request from every committee in area (consecutively or simultaneously) until all asked
parameters.frequency: once per project per craft (DAS FAQ)

rules.applies_to: Contractors needing apprentices
rules.quote: must request the dispatch of required apprentices from the apprenticeship committees providing training in the applicable craft or trade and whose geographic area of operation includes the site of the public work by giving the committee written notice of at least 72 hours (excluding Saturdays, Sundays and holidays) before the date on which one or more apprentices are required.
rules.notes: Requests must be unconditional (no circumventing duty to pay for preemployment processes). Contractor need not sign DAS 7 or other conditions (DAS FAQ).

rules.title: Dispatch requests: at least an 8-hour day or 20% of apprentice hours
rules.plain_english: Except on jobs with under 40 journeyman hours, each dispatch request must be for at least an 8-hour day per apprentice or 20% of the estimated apprentice hours for that craft, whichever is greater.
rules.applies_to: Contractors requesting apprentices
rules.quote: Except for projects with less than 40 hours of journeyman work, each request for apprentice dispatch shall be for not less than an 8 hour day per each apprentice, or 20% of the estimated apprentice hours to be worked for an employer in a particular craft or trade on a project, whichever is greater,

rules.title: DAS 142 required contents
rules.plain_english: A dispatch request must include: request date; committee name, address, phone and fax/email; contractor name, address, CSLB license number, phone and fax/email; project name and address; DIR project number, contract number, total contract and subcontract amounts; number of apprentices, craft, report date (72-hour notice), report time, person and address to report to.

fields: name of person to report to
parameters.form: DAS 142 (Rev. 6/24) optional; one craft per form

rules.applies_to: Contractors preparing DAS 142
rules.quote: 5) PWC Project Number, Contract Number, Total Contract Amount, Sub-Contract Amount for projects which have been registered with the Department of Industrial Relations in accordance with Labor Code section 1773.3; 6) Dispatch Request Information: Number of Apprentice(s) Needed, Craft or Trade, Date Apprentice(s) to Report (72 hrs. notice required), Time to Report, Name of Person to Report to

rules.title: Minimum ratio: 1 apprentice hour per 5 journeyman hours, per craft, by end of contract
rules.plain_english: By the end of your contract or subcontract, apprentice hours in each apprenticeable craft must be at least 20% of the straight-time journeyman hours in that craft (1:5). Hours over 8/day or 40/week don't count, crafts can't be combined, and you should try to employ apprentices while journeymen are on site.

parameters.max_ratio: per committee standards if contractor bound by them; CAC rules: max = min = 1:5

rules.applies_to: All contractors/subcontractors employing apprenticeable crafts on covered public works
rules.quote: However, except as otherwise provided in this section, in no case shall the ratio be less than one hour of apprentice work for every five hours of journeyman work.
rules.notes: Statute text read from the official CSLB 2022 Law Book appendix (statutes as published Jan. 2022); leginfo.legislature.ca.gov could not be reached to confirm later amendments. DAS FAQ example: 100 journeyman hours -> 20 apprentice hours. Manual example: 750 ST journeyman hrs -> 150 apprentice hrs.

rules.title: Ratio shortfall defense: proper DAS 142 requests
rules.plain_english: If you fall short of the 1:5 ratio, you avoid penalties only by proving you made timely written dispatch requests (72-hour notice) to every committee in the area, early enough to meet the ratio, kept proof of sending, and employed every apprentice dispatched.

must_prove: requested from each committee in area
copy of each written request with proof sent by mail/fax/email
at least 72 hours notice excl. weekends/holidays
requested in time to meet ratio

rules.applies_to: Contractors short of apprentice hours
rules.quote: To do so, it is the contractor's burden to establish that all of the regulation's request-to-dispatch requirements have been satisfied.
rules.notes: Retain DAS 142 transmittal proofs (fax confirmations, email receipts, certified mail receipts).

rules.title: Only DAS-registered apprentices may be paid apprentice rates
rules.plain_english: Only workers registered in a DAS-approved apprenticeship program, with a written apprentice agreement, may be paid apprentice rates. Anyone else doing the craft's work must be paid the journeyman rate, and does not count toward the ratio.

parameters.eligible: apprentices under DAS-approved standards with written agreement (LC 3077)

rules.applies_to: Contractors employing apprentices
rules.quote: (c) Only apprentices, as defined in Section 3077, who are in training under apprenticeship standards that have been approved by the Chief of the Division of Apprenticeship Standards and who are parties to written apprentice agreements under Chapter 4 (commencing with Section 3070) of Division 3 are eligible to be employed at the apprentice wage rate on public works.
rules.notes: Statute text read from the official CSLB 2022 Law Book appendix (statutes as published Jan. 2022); leginfo.legislature.ca.gov could not be reached to confirm later amendments. Helpers may never replace statutorily required apprentices (8 CCR 16000).

rules.title: Apprentices: apprentice prevailing rate, own craft only, journeyperson supervision
rules.plain_english: Apprentices must be paid the apprentice prevailing rate for their trade, may only do work of the craft they are registered in, and (under CAC rules / DAS 140 box 3) must always work with or under direct supervision of a journeyperson - otherwise the journeyman rate is owed.

parameters.pay: apprentice prevailing per diem rate for registered trade
parameters.work_scope: only craft/work processes in apprenticeship standards
parameters.supervision: at all times with or under direct supervision of journeyworker (CAC rules)

rules.applies_to: Contractors employing apprentices
rules.quote: Where an employer employs apprentices under the rules and regulations of the California Apprenticeship Council, as set forth in Labor Code Section 1777.5(c)(2), apprentices employed on public works must at all times work with or under the direct supervision of a journeyworker.
rules.notes: Apprentice rates: https://www.dir.ca.gov/OPRL/pwappwage/PWAppWageStart.asp

rules.title: Pay apprentices for required pre-employment testing/training time
